`BUILD-MKW.bat`:

```bat
@echo off
setlocal EnableExtensions
cd /d "%~dp0"

if not defined MKW_GAME (
  echo [ERROR] Set MKW_GAME to your legally dumped 1.8.0 folder containing exefs\ and romfs\.
  exit /b 1
)
if not exist "%MKW_GAME%\exefs\main" (
  echo [ERROR] Missing %MKW_GAME%\exefs\main
  exit /b 1
)
if not defined NUMBER_OF_PROCESSORS set "NUMBER_OF_PROCESSORS=4"

if not exist ".venv\Scripts\python.exe" py -3 -m venv .venv || exit /b 1
.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r tools\requirements.txt zstandard || exit /b 1

.venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\mkw_cli.py prepare --repo . --dump "%MKW_GAME%" --i-confirm-update-180 || exit /b 1
if not exist "build\xlate\totk_xlate.exe" .venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\mkw_cli.py xlate --repo . || exit /b 1
if not exist "generated\mkw180\layout.json" .venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\mkw_cli.py generate --repo . --dump "%MKW_GAME%" --jobs %NUMBER_OF_PROCESSORS% || exit /b 1

if defined MKW_PACKED_ROMFS (
  .venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\mkw_select_romfs.py --repo . --packed "%MKW_PACKED_ROMFS%" || exit /b 1
) else (
  .venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\mkw_cli.py pack --repo . --dump "%MKW_GAME%" || exit /b 1
)

.venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\mkw_cli.py build --repo . --dump "%MKW_GAME%" --jobs %NUMBER_OF_PROCESSORS% || exit /b 1
echo.
echo Built build\mkw180\mkw.exe from your local dump.
echo Run RUN-MKW.bat to start it.
exit /b 0

```

`README.md`:

```md
# MKW-THWOMP: Mario Kart World PC

A static recompilation of **Mario Kart World** (Nintendo Switch 2, update 1.8.0) to native Windows with Vulkan.

**No game files are included.** You need your own legally dumped copy of the game (exefs and romfs of the 1.8.0
update). This repository holds only the recompiler, the runtime and the build tools.

> Status: work in progress. The intro, title screen and menus render and races load; graphical issues remain
> (see *Known issues*). Not yet fully playable.

## What it is

- `recomp/`: lifts the game's ARM64 code to C (`gen.py`).
- `runtime/`: the host side: the NVN 2 graphics API on Vulkan, the Switch 2 services, input, audio, the file system
  and the in-game settings menu.
- `tools/`: build, packing and diagnostic scripts.

## Build

Requirements: Windows 10/11, [MSYS2](https://www.msys2.org/) UCRT64 (clang, ninja, Vulkan headers, SDL3, Opus),
Python 3.12, a Vulkan 1.3 GPU.

```bat
set MKW_GAME=D:\path\to\your\mkw-1.8.0-dump
BUILD-MKW.bat
RUN-MKW.bat
```

Or build the runtime directly into a folder of your choice:

```bat
python tools\build_game.py --version mkw180 --out build\mkw
```

## Settings

Press **F1** or **Esc** (Minus + Plus on a controller) in game for the settings menu: Display, Sound, Controls,
System and Advanced, in a light (Switch 2 style) or dark theme. Settings are saved to `mkw.ini` next to `mkw.exe`.
Any setting can also be set as an environment variable with the `MKW_` prefix (for example `MKW_MEMORY=import`).

The game renders at its own resolution, as on the console. There are no upscalers or frame generation.

## Known issues

- Foliage (trees, bushes, cacti) pops in and flickers between levels of detail.
- The terrain arrays are reduced to 1024² on the host (the full 8192² × 68 layers does not fit in VRAM).
- The `mirror` GPU memory mode can corrupt game memory (crashes, flicker); `import` is the default.

## Credits

Built on the open-source recompiler runtime lineage (TotK Recomp and its contributors), Eden / Eglantine
(shader recompiler), Dear ImGui, Ryujinx and others. See `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` and the licence files.

Mario Kart World is a trademark of Nintendo. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo.

```

`RUN-MKW.bat`:

```bat
@echo off
setlocal EnableExtensions
cd /d "%~dp0"

if not defined MKW_GAME (
  echo [ERROR] Set MKW_GAME to the same legally dumped folder used for the build.
  exit /b 1
)
if not exist "build\mkw180\mkw.exe" (
  echo [ERROR] No build\mkw180\mkw.exe. Run BUILD-MKW.bat first.
  exit /b 1
)

set "TOTK_ASTC=gpu"
set "TOTK_ASTC_BC=1"
set "TOTK_MEMORY=auto"
set "TOTK_LANG=en-US"
if not defined TOTK_TRACE set "TOTK_TRACE=perf"

.venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\mkw_cli.py run --repo . --dump "%MKW_GAME%" --mode game --timeout 0 --trace "%TOTK_TRACE%"
exit /b %ERRORLEVEL%

```

## Compiler runtime in a source build

A build with the MSYS2 UCRT64 toolchain of `docs/building.md` links these into `totk.exe`. The installer release builds with llvm-mingw instead (its row below).

| Component | Version | License | How it is used |
|---|---|---|---|
| GCC runtime (`libstdc++`) | 16.2.0 | GPL-3.0 with the GCC Runtime Library Exception | linked into `totk.exe` |
| winpthreads (mingw-w64) | 14.0.0 | MIT / BSD | linked into `totk.exe` |
| libiconv | 1.19 | LGPL-2.1+ | `libiconv-2.dll`, unmodified, next to `totk.exe`: MSYS2's `SDL3.dll` imports it |

`recomp/flags.py`:

```py
"""Function-local NZCV for recomp/gen.py.

The lifter writes flags the way the guest does: every flag-setting instruction packs N, Z, C and V into c->nzcv
(subs64() and friends in runtime/cpu.h) and every reader unpacks them (COND_xx(c)). Compilers keep NZCV inside a
function, and AAPCS64 neither passes it to a callee nor preserves it across a call. So a generated function keeps its
flags in a local `Flags F` (runtime/cpu.h), which clang holds in registers, and writes c->nzcv only where it leaves
for another function other than by a call or a return (see plan()).

A flag-setting instruction of a known kind (subtract, add or logic result; 32 or 64 bits) stores its operands in F.a
and F.b. A reader all of whose reaching definitions are of one kind computes its condition from those operands, so
`cmp x1, x2; b.lt` becomes a signed compare in C. Instructions whose result is only known packed (CCMP, FCMP, MSR
NZCV, ADCS) write F.nz, the packed form; a reader whose definitions are of several kinds reads F.nz, and those
definitions then also write it.

A read that can see flags a callee left reads the caller's flags from before the call instead. AAPCS64 code never
reads a callee's flags, so such a read only sits on a path that does not run: in TotK it follows calls to noreturn
functions (asserts) that the compiler placed before another branch's target. Plan.after_call counts them.
"""
import re

KIND_DEF = re.compile(r'\b(subs|adds|logic)(32|64)\(c, ')
CARRY_DEF = re.compile(r'\b(adcs|sbcs)(32|64)\(c, ')
CARRY_USE = re.compile(r'\b(adc|sbc)(32|64)\(c, ')
COND = re.compile(r'COND_([A-Z]{2})\(c\)')
NZ_DEF = 'c->nzcv = '
NZ_USE = '(c->nzcv)'
KIND_NAME = {'subs': 'sub', 'adds': 'add', 'logic': 'logic'}

ENTRY, CALL = 'entry', 'call'


class FlagError(Exception):
    pass


def effect(code):
    """(reads flags, kind of the flags written or None) of one instruction's C."""
    reads = bool(COND.search(code) or CARRY_USE.search(code) or CARRY_DEF.search(code) or NZ_USE in code)
    if NZ_DEF in code or CARRY_DEF.search(code):
        return reads, 'nz'
    defs = KIND_DEF.findall(code)
    if len(defs) > 1:
        raise FlagError(f'several flag definitions in one instruction: {code}')
    if defs:
        op, size = defs[0]
        return reads, KIND_NAME[op] + size
    return reads, None


class Plan:
    """Per instruction: the kind its flag reads use, whether its flag definition also writes F.nz, and what it writes
    to c->nzcv before it leaves for another function."""

    def __init__(self, n):
        self.reader = [None] * n
        self.pack = [False] * n
        self.exit = [None] * n      # kind of the flags to publish in c->nzcv at a tail exit, or None
        self.entry = False          # F.nz starts as c->nzcv: flags from the entry reach a read or an exit
        self.entry_read = False     # they reach a read, not only an exit
        self.after_call = 0         # reads that can see flags a callee left (see the module docstring)
        self.used = False

    def decl(self):
        """Declaration of F at the top of the function."""
        return 'Flags F = {.nz = c->nzcv};' if self.entry else 'Flags F = {0};'

    def publish(self, i):
        """Statement writing the flags to c->nzcv at instruction i's tail exit ('' when it need not)."""
        k = self.exit[i]
        return f'c->nzcv = fnz_{k}(&F); ' if k else ''

    def rewrite(self, i, code):
        """code of instruction i with its flag reads and writes on F."""
        rk = self.reader[i]
        _, dk = effect(code)
        if rk:
            code = COND.sub(lambda m: f'fc_{rk}(&F, CC_{m.group(1)})', code)
            code = CARRY_DEF.sub(lambda m: f'{m.group(1)}{m.group(2)}f(&F, fc_{rk}(&F, CC_CS), ', code)
            code = CARRY_USE.sub(lambda m: f'{m.group(1)}{m.group(2)}f(fc_{rk}(&F, CC_CS), ', code)
            code = code.replace(NZ_USE, f'(fnz_{rk}(&F))')
        if dk == 'nz':
            code = code.replace(NZ_DEF, 'F.nz = ')
            code = re.sub(r'\(void\)(subs|adds)(32|64)\(c, ', lambda m: f'F.nz = nz_{KIND_NAME[m.group(1)]}{m.group(2)}(',
                          code)
        elif dk:
            code = KIND_DEF.sub(lambda m: f'f{KIND_NAME[m.group(1)]}{m.group(2)}(&F, ', code)
            if self.pack[i]:
                code += f' F.nz = fnz_{dk}(&F);'
        if 'c->nzcv' in code or COND.search(code) or KIND_DEF.search(code) or CARRY_USE.search(code):
            raise FlagError(f'flag access left after the rewrite: {code}')
        return code


def plan(effects, succ, calls, exits):
    """effects[i]: (reads, kind or None); succ[i]: successor indices inside the function; calls: indices of calls,
    whose callee may leave any flags; exits: indices that can leave for another function other than by a call or a
    return (a tail branch, falling into the next function, a br through rt_dispatch).

    Discovery can start a function inside another one (a branch target, a materialised address), and the code
    before it then falls or branches into it with live flags. So a tail exit publishes the flags in c->nzcv, and a
    function whose reads can see its entry flags starts F.nz from c->nzcv. Calls and returns publish nothing: AAPCS64
    code neither passes flags to a callee nor reads a callee's, so a call's flags count as no definition."""
    n = len(effects)
    p = Plan(n)
    if not any(r or k for r, k in effects):
        return p
    p.used = True
    reach = [set() for _ in range(n)]
    reach[0].add(ENTRY)
    work = [0]
    while work:
        i = work.pop()
        out = {i} if effects[i][1] else ({CALL} if i in calls else reach[i])
        for s in succ[i]:
            if not out <= reach[s]:
                reach[s] |= out
                work.append(s)

    def kind(d):
        return 'nz' if d == ENTRY else effects[d][1]

    def use(r):
        """Kind a use of the definitions r reads; several kinds read the packed form, which they then all write."""
        kinds = {kind(d) for d in r}
        if ENTRY in r:
            p.entry = True
        if len(kinds) == 1:
            return kinds.pop()
        for d in r:
            if d != ENTRY:
                p.pack[d] = True
        return 'nz'   # several kinds, or none (unreachable)

    for i, (reads, _) in enumerate(effects):
        if reads:
            p.after_call += CALL in reach[i]
            p.reader[i] = use(reach[i] - {CALL})
            p.entry_read |= ENTRY in reach[i]
    for i in exits:
        # Entry flags alone are still in c->nzcv.
        r = reach[i] - {CALL}
        if r and r != {ENTRY}:
            p.exit[i] = use(r)
    return p

```

`recomp/gen.py`:

```py
# Adapted from LAS Recomp tools/gen.py @ da35b83 (MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 Peiikai).
"""Generate C for the ExeFS modules: function discovery, then parallel emission into chunked C files.

Usage: gen.py --exefs build/extracted/v121/exefs --out generated/v121 [--modules main,subsdk0,sdk] [--jobs N]
              [--limit N] [--chunk-fns N] [--chunk-bytes B] [--big-fn B] [--patches FILE]

Output, under --out:
  layout.h, layout.json        module bases (recomp/layout.py)
  <mod>/<mod>_NNNN.c           one `void f_<addr>(Cpu *c)` per guest function, about --chunk-bytes of C per file
  <mod>/<mod>_table.c          sorted <mod>_fn_addrs[] / <mod>_fn_ptrs[] / <mod>_fn_count for rt_dispatch
  <mod>/manifest.json          chunk list, function count, statistics and timings
  patches.h                    code patch sets for the runtime (recomp/patches.py; no sets without --patches)

Function discovery runs in this process, vectorised over the module's .text words. Function starts are the module
seeds (.eh_frame_hdr, exported FUNC symbols, RELATIVE relocation targets), every BL target, and code addresses
materialised by ADR or ADRP+ADD (except an ADR that anchors a jump table: one with a `br` in the next 16
instructions, or one an ADD register form uses as its base right after). A function is [start, next start). A direct branch whose target lies outside its
function makes the target a new start, until no new start appears.

Emission runs in worker processes, one chunk per task. Each worker loads the modules itself, lifts one function at a
time and resolves its jump tables (recomp/jumptables.py), so memory per worker does not grow with the module.
Chunks are sized from a per-instruction estimate of the C they produce, so their names and contents only depend on
the input; a chunk whose text did not change is not rewritten and keeps its mtime.
"""
import argparse
import json
import multiprocessing as mp
import os
import re
import sys
import time
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / 'tools'))
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / 'recomp'))

import flags  # noqa: E402
import hostmem  # noqa: E402
import jumptables  # noqa: E402
import patches  # noqa: E402
import regs  # noqa: E402
from check_content import GENERATED_MARKER  # noqa: E402
from layout import layout, write as write_layout  # noqa: E402
from lifter import hx  # noqa: E402
from module import Module  # noqa: E402

TERMINATORS = ('b', 'br', 'ret', 'trap')
MUSTTAIL = '__attribute__((musttail)) return'

# Estimated bytes of C per instruction, by class, for chunking (estimate_sizes()).
# Least squares over every function of main, subsdk0 and sdk (1.2.1) gives 62 / 75 / 48 bytes per instruction, 38
# per function and 4.5 per instruction of a function with a `br` (switches; the all-label fallback costs about 60
# per instruction but is rare); the median error per function is 7 %.
EST_INT = 62
EST_SIMD = 75
EST_SIMD_LDST = 48
EST_FN = 38          # per function: signature, FN_ENTER, closing brace
EST_BR_LABELS = 10   # per instruction of a function with a `br`: switch cases, or labels if it falls back


def fname(a):
    return f'f_{a:x}'


def header(what):
    return f'// {GENERATED_MARKER}: {what}, generated by recomp/gen.py from game code. Do not edit or commit.\n'


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ discovery

def _sext(v, n):
    v = v.astype(np.int64)
    return np.where(v & (1 << (n - 1)), v - (1 << n), v)


def discover(mod):
    """Function starts of mod as a sorted int64 array of word indices into mod.words, plus discovery statistics."""
    w = mod.words
    n = len(w)

    def idx(mask):
        return np.flatnonzero(mask).astype(np.int64)

    seeds = (np.asarray(mod.seeds(), dtype=np.int64) - mod.lo) >> 2

    # B and BL: imm26. BL targets are function starts; B targets join the fixpoint below.
    b_all = idx((w & 0x7C000000) == 0x14000000)
    imm = _sext(w[b_all] & 0x03FFFFFF, 26)
    is_bl = (w[b_all] >> 31).astype(bool)
    bl_tgt = b_all[is_bl] + imm[is_bl]
    br_src, br_tgt = [b_all[~is_bl]], [b_all[~is_bl] + imm[~is_bl]]
    # B.cond (the lifter accepts o1 = 1 too), CBZ/CBNZ: imm19 at bit 5. TBZ/TBNZ: imm14 at bit 5.
    for mask, val, nb in ((0xFE000010, 0x54000000, 19), (0x7E000000, 0x34000000, 19), (0x7E000000, 0x36000000, 14)):
        s = idx((w & mask) == val)
        br_src.append(s)
        br_tgt.append(s + _sext((w[s] >> 5) & ((1 << nb) - 1), nb))
    br_src, br_tgt = np.concatenate(br_src), np.concatenate(br_tgt)
    ok = (br_tgt >= 0) & (br_tgt < n)
    br_src, br_tgt = br_src[ok], br_tgt[ok]

    # ADR: pc + imm21. ADRP: page + (imm21 << 12), then ADD (imm, 64-bit, unshifted) of the same register within
    # 8 instructions. Targets must be aligned and in .text.
    def imm21(s):
        v = w[s]
        return _sext(((v >> 5) & 0x7FFFF) << 2 | ((v >> 29) & 3), 21)

    pc0 = np.int64(mod.lo)
    adr = idx((w & 0x9F000000) == 0x10000000)
    # Clang's jump tables add a table entry to an ADR anchor, the first case block, then `br`. That anchor is not a
    # function (it would split the switch): an ADR with a `br` in the next 16 instructions is not a seed, nor is one
    # whose register is the base of an ADD (shifted or extended register) in the next 4 instructions
    # (`adr xA, L; ldrb wO, [..]; add xA, xA, wO, lsl #2`), however far the scheduler moved the `br`.
    br = idx((w & 0xFFFFFC1F) == 0xD61F0000)
    nxt = np.searchsorted(br, adr)
    has_br = nxt < len(br)
    near = np.zeros(len(adr), dtype=bool)
    near[has_br] = br[nxt[has_br]] - adr[has_br] <= 16
    rd = w[adr] & 31
    for k in range(1, 5):
        x = w[np.minimum(adr + k, n - 1)]
        near |= (((x & 0xFF200000) == 0x8B000000) | ((x & 0xFFE00000) == 0x8B200000)) & (((x >> 5) & 31) == rd)
    adr = adr[~near]
    adr_bytes = pc0 + adr * 4 + imm21(adr)
    is_adrp = (w & 0x9F000000) == 0x90000000
    add = idx((w & 0xFFC00000) == 0x91000000)
    rn = ((w[add] >> 5) & 31).astype(np.int64)
    found = np.full(len(add), -1, dtype=np.int64)
    for k in range(1, 9):
        p = add - k
        cand = (found < 0) & (p >= 0)
        pc = np.where(cand, p, 0)
        cand &= is_adrp[pc] & ((w[pc] & 31).astype(np.int64) == rn)
        found[cand] = p[cand]
    hit = found >= 0
    p = found[hit]
    page = ((pc0 + p * 4) & ~np.int64(0xFFF)) + (imm21(p) << 12)
    add_bytes = page + ((w[add[hit]] >> 10) & 0xFFF).astype(np.int64)
    mat = np.concatenate([adr_bytes, add_bytes])
    mat = mat[(mat >= mod.lo) & (mat < mod.hi) & (mat % 4 == 0)]
    mat = (mat - pc0) >> 2

    bl_tgt = bl_tgt[(bl_tgt >= 0) & (bl_tgt < n)]
    starts = np.unique(np.concatenate([seeds, bl_tgt, mat]))
    stats = {'seeds': int(len(seeds)), 'bl_targets': int(len(np.unique(bl_tgt))),
             'materialised_targets': int(len(np.unique(mat))), 'initial_starts': int(len(starts))}

    rounds = 0
    while True:
        rounds += 1
        f = np.searchsorted(starts, br_src, side='right') - 1
        live = f >= 0
        f = np.where(live, f, 0)
        lo = starts[f]
        hi = np.where(f + 1 < len(starts), starts[np.minimum(f + 1, len(starts) - 1)], n)
        out = live & ((br_tgt < lo) | (br_tgt >= hi))
        new = np.setdiff1d(br_tgt[out], starts, assume_unique=False)
        if not len(new):
            break
        starts = np.union1d(starts, new)
    stats['rounds'] = rounds
    stats['functions'] = int(len(starts))
    return starts, stats


def estimate_sizes(mod, starts):
    """Estimated bytes of C per function (for chunking only; the manifest records the real sizes)."""
    w = mod.words
    cost = np.full(len(w), EST_INT, dtype=np.int64)
    cost[(w & 0x0E000000) == 0x0E000000] = EST_SIMD                    # FP/AdvSIMD data processing
    cost[((w & 0x0A000000) == 0x08000000) & (((w >> 26) & 1) == 1)] = EST_SIMD_LDST  # FP/SIMD load/store
    has_br = np.zeros(len(w), dtype=np.int64)
    has_br[np.flatnonzero((w & 0xFFFFFC1F) == 0xD61F0000)] = 1           # BR Xn
    csum = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(cost)])
    bsum = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(has_br)])
    ends = np.append(starts[1:], len(w))
    size = csum[ends] - csum[starts] + EST_FN
    with_br = (bsum[ends] - bsum[starts]) > 0
    size[with_br] += (ends[with_br] - starts[with_br]) * EST_BR_LABELS
    return size


def partition(est, max_fns, max_bytes, big_fn):
    """Contiguous [i0, i1) function ranges: at most max_fns functions and about max_bytes of C each; a function
    estimated above big_fn gets a file of its own so large functions compile in parallel."""
    chunks, i0, size = [], 0, 0
    for i, s in enumerate(est.tolist()):
        if s > big_fn:
            if i > i0:
                chunks.append((i0, i))
            chunks.append((i, i + 1))
            i0, size = i + 1, 0
            continue
        if i > i0 and (i - i0 >= max_fns or size + s > max_bytes):
            chunks.append((i0, i))
            i0, size = i, 0
        size += s
    if len(est) > i0:
        chunks.append((i0, len(est)))
    return chunks


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ emission

class Emitter:
    """C for the functions of one module. starts is the set of every function start of the module."""

    def __init__(self, mod, starts, patched=None, reg_locals=regs.LOCALS, callee_saved=True, spins=None):
        self.mod = mod
        self.starts = starts
        self.patched = patched or {}   # {address: (set index, [replacement words])} (recomp/patches.py)
        self.spins = spins or {}       # {spin wait back-edge: its head} (recomp/patches.py `spin`)
        self.reg_locals = reg_locals   # recomp/regs.py: registers per function in C locals
        self.kept = regs.CALLEE_SAVED if callee_saved else frozenset()   # not reloaded after a call
        self.uses_patches = False
        self.stats = Counter()
        self.unsupported = Counter()

    def scan(self, insns, entry, end):
        """Labels and jump tables of one function: {pc: sorted targets} for resolved tables, 'all' for an
        unresolved computed br."""
        mod, labels, tables = self.mod, set(), {}
        for i, ins in enumerate(insns):
            k = ins.kind
            if k in ('b', 'bcond'):
                if entry <= ins.target < end:
                    labels.add(ins.target)
            elif k == 'br':
                a = entry + 4 * i
                jt = jumptables.resolve(mod, a, entry, end)
                if jt:
                    tables[a] = jt
                    labels.update(jt)
                    self.stats['jump_tables'] += 1
                    self.stats['jump_table_targets'] += len(jt)
                elif jumptables.is_computed(mod, a, entry):
                    tables[a] = 'all'
                    self.stats['all_label_fallbacks'] += 1
                else:
                    self.stats['br_dispatch'] += 1
            elif k == 'trap':
                self.stats['traps'] += 1
                c = ins.code
                if c.startswith('rt_udf') and '/*' in c:
                    self.stats['unsupported'] += 1
                    msg = c[c.index('/*') + 2:c.rindex('*/')].strip()
                    self.unsupported[re.sub(r'\b[0-9a-f]{8}\b', '', msg).strip()] += 1
            elif k == 'asm':
                raise ValueError(f'{entry + 4 * i:#x}: asm instruction from the portable lifter')
        return labels, tables

    def replacements(self, a):
        """Lifted replacement words of the patched site a."""
        return [self.mod.lifter.lift(w, a) for w in self.patched[a][1]]

    @staticmethod
    def flow(insns, entry, end, tables):
        """Successors of each instruction inside the function [entry, end). Index len(insns) stands for falling
        through into the next function and has none."""
        def idx(t):
            return [(t - entry) // 4] if entry <= t < end else []

        succ = []
        for i, ins in enumerate(insns):
            k = ins.kind
            if k in ('op', 'bl', 'blr'):
                succ.append([i + 1])
            elif k == 'b':
                succ.append(idx(ins.target))
            elif k == 'bcond':
                succ.append(idx(ins.target) + [i + 1])
            elif k == 'br':
                jt = tables.get(entry + 4 * i)
                succ.append([t for x in jt for t in idx(x)] if jt and jt != 'all' else [])
            else:   # ret, trap
                succ.append([])
        succ.append([])
        return succ

    def flag_plan(self, insns, entry, end, tables, succ):
        """recomp/flags.py plan for the function: each instruction's flag use over the flow succ (flow())."""
        n = len(insns)
        calls, effects, exits = set(), [], {n}
        for i, ins in enumerate(insns):
            k, a = ins.kind, entry + 4 * i
            if k in ('bl', 'blr'):
                calls.add(i)
            elif k in ('b', 'bcond') and not entry <= ins.target < end:
                exits.add(i)
            elif k == 'br':
                exits.add(i)   # through rt_dispatch, also a table's default
            if a in self.patched:
                effects.append(self.patched_effect(ins, a))
                if any(r.kind == 'bl' for r in self.replacements(a)):
                    calls.add(i)
            else:
                effects.append(flags.effect(ins.cond if k == 'bcond' else ins.code or ''))
        effects.append((False, None))
        return flags.plan(effects, succ, calls, exits)

    def patched_effect(self, ins, a):
        """Flag effect of a patched site: both alternatives must have the same one, in at most one word each."""
        alts = []
        for words in ([ins], self.replacements(a)):
            fx = [flags.effect(w.code or '') for w in words if w.kind == 'op']
            fx = [e for e in fx if e[0] or e[1]]
            if len(fx) > 1:
                raise patches.PatchError(f'{a:#x}: several flag-using words in one alternative')
            alts.append(fx[0] if fx else (False, None))
        if alts[0][1] != alts[1][1]:
            raise patches.PatchError(f'{a:#x}: the alternatives write different flags ({alts[0][1]}, {alts[1][1]})')
        if (alts[0][1] or alts[0][0] or alts[1][0]) and ins.kind == 'bl':
            raise patches.PatchError(f'{a:#x}: a patched call that uses flags')
        return alts[0][0] or alts[1][0], alts[0][1]

    def function(self, entry, end):
        """(lines of C, referenced function starts) for the guest function [entry, end)."""
        mod, starts = self.mod, self.starts
        insns = [mod.lift(a) for a in range(entry, end, 4)]
        labels, tables = self.scan(insns, entry, end)
        refs = set()
        all_labels = 'all' in tables.values()
        if all_labels:
            labels = set(range(entry, end, 4))
        # An unresolved computed br re-enters the function through fb_<entry>, a C function of its own, which local
        # flags would not survive; such functions keep NZCV in c->nzcv.
        # The same holds for registers in locals (recomp/regs.py): fb_<entry> keeps them in the Cpu too.
        local = not all_labels
        spill, reload, reload_call = (regs.SPILL, regs.RELOAD, regs.RELOAD_CALL) if local else ('', '', '')
        succ = self.flow(insns, entry, end, tables) if local else None
        fp = self.flag_plan(insns, entry, end, tables, succ) if local else None
        if fp and fp.used:
            self.stats['local_flag_functions'] += 1
            self.stats['flag_reads_direct'] += sum(1 for k in fp.reader if k and k != 'nz')
            self.stats['flag_reads_packed'] += sum(1 for k in fp.reader if k == 'nz')
            self.stats['flag_entry_functions'] += fp.entry
            self.stats['flag_entry_reads'] += fp.entry_read
            self.stats['flag_reads_after_call'] += fp.after_call
            self.stats['flag_publishing_exits'] += sum(1 for k in fp.exit if k)

        def fx(i, code):
            return fp.rewrite(i, code) if fp and fp.used else code

        def publish(i):
            return fp.publish(i) if fp and fp.used else ''

        def jump(t, i):
            if entry <= t < end:
                return f'goto L_{t:x};'
            if t in starts:
                refs.add(t)
                return f'{publish(i)}{spill}{MUSTTAIL} {fname(t)}(c);'
            self.stats['external_branches'] += 1
            return f'{publish(i)}{spill}c->pc = {hx(t)}; {MUSTTAIL} rt_dispatch(c);'

        if all_labels:
            # An unresolved computed br re-enters the function through fb_<entry>, which switches on c->pc to any
            # instruction. A goto to a shared dispatch block inside the body instead turns every instruction into
            # a loop header, and clang's loop passes then take tens of seconds on one function.
            fb = f'fb_{entry:x}'
            cases = ' '.join(f'case {hx(t)}: goto L_{t:x};' for t in range(entry, end, 4))
            redispatch = f'{MUSTTAIL} {fb}(c);'
            out = [f'static void {fb}(Cpu *c);',
                   f'void {fname(entry)}(Cpu *c) {{', f'    FN_ENTER({hx(entry)});', f'    c->pc = {hx(entry)};',
                   f'    {redispatch}', '}',
                   f'static void {fb}(Cpu *c) {{', f'    switch (c->pc) {{ {cases} default: break; }}',
                   f'    {MUSTTAIL} rt_dispatch(c);']
        else:
            redispatch = f'{MUSTTAIL} rt_dispatch(c);'
            out = [f'void {fname(entry)}(Cpu *c) {{', f'    FN_ENTER({hx(entry)});']
            if fp.used:
                out.append('    ' + fp.decl())

        def call(t, a):
            if t in starts:
                refs.add(t)
                return f'c->x[30] = {hx(a + 4)}; {spill}{fname(t)}(c);{reload_call}'
            self.stats['external_calls'] += 1
            return f'c->x[30] = {hx(a + 4)}; {spill}c->pc = {hx(t)}; rt_dispatch(c);{reload_call}'

        def op(i, code):
            code = fx(i, code)
            return f'{spill}{code}{reload}' if regs.ESCAPE.search(code) else code

        def patch(i, ins, a):
            """if (switch) { replacement } else { original } for a patched site (recomp/patches.py)."""
            k, words = self.patched[a]
            if ins.kind not in ('op', 'bl'):
                raise patches.PatchError(f'{a:#x}: patched instruction is a {ins.kind}')
            repl = []
            for j, (w, r) in enumerate(zip(words, self.replacements(a))):
                if r.kind == 'op':
                    repl.append(op(i, r.code))
                elif r.kind == 'bl' and j == len(words) - 1:
                    repl.append(call(r.target, a))
                else:
                    raise patches.PatchError(f'{a:#x}: replacement word {w:08x} is a {r.kind}')
            orig = op(i, ins.code) if ins.kind == 'op' else call(ins.target, a)
            self.uses_patches = True
            self.stats['patched_sites'] += 1
            return f'    if (rt_patch_on[{k}]) {{ {" ".join(repl)} }} else {{ {orig} }}'

        body = []   # (instruction index or None for a label, line); a line belongs to the instruction it lifts

        def emit(i, line):
            body.append((i, line))

        k = None
        for i, ins in enumerate(insns):
            a = entry + 4 * i
            if a in labels:
                emit(None, f'L_{a:x}:;')
            k = ins.kind
            if a in self.patched:
                emit(i, patch(i, ins, a))
            elif k == 'op':
                emit(i, '    ' + op(i, ins.code))
            elif k == 'trap':
                emit(i, f'    {spill}{fx(i, ins.code)}')
            elif k in ('b', 'bcond'):
                j = jump(ins.target, i)
                if self.spins.get(a) == ins.target and entry <= ins.target < end:
                    j = f'rt_spin_gate(c, {hx(ins.target)}); {j}'   # a pass of a spin wait
                    self.stats['spin_gates'] += 1
                emit(i, '    ' + j if k == 'b' else f'    if ({fx(i, ins.cond)}) {{ {j} }}')
            elif k == 'bl':
                emit(i, '    ' + call(ins.target, a))
            elif k == 'blr':
                emit(i, f'    c->pc = {ins.target}; c->x[30] = {hx(a + 4)}; {spill}rt_dispatch(c);{reload_call}')
            elif k == 'br':
                jt = tables.get(a)
                if jt == 'all':
                    emit(i, f'    c->pc = {ins.target}; {redispatch}')
                elif jt:
                    cases = ' '.join(f'case {hx(t)}: goto L_{t:x};' for t in jt)
                    emit(i, f'    switch ({ins.target}) {{ {cases} default: break; }}')
                    emit(i, f'    {publish(i)}{spill}c->pc = {ins.target}; {redispatch}')
                else:
                    emit(i, f'    {publish(i)}{spill}c->pc = {ins.target}; {MUSTTAIL} rt_dispatch(c);')
            elif k == 'ret':
                emit(i, f'    {spill}return;')
            else:
                raise ValueError(f'{a:#x}: unknown instruction kind {k!r}')
        n = len(insns)
        if k not in TERMINATORS:  # falls through into the next function
            if end < mod.hi:
                emit(n, '    ' + jump(end, n))
            else:
                emit(n, f'    {spill}rt_udf(c, {hx(end)});')
        if local:
            texts = [''] * (n + 1)
            for i, line in body:
                if i is not None:
                    texts[i] += line
            clean = {i for i, ins in enumerate(insns) if entry + 4 * i not in self.patched
                     and (ins.kind in ('bl', 'blr') or (ins.kind == 'op' and regs.RELOAD in texts[i]))}
            rp = regs.plan(texts, succ, clean, self.reg_locals, self.kept)
            if rp.regs:
                out.append('    ' + rp.decl())
            self.stats['local_reg_functions'] += bool(rp.regs)
            self.stats['reg_spills'] += sum(len(s) for s in rp.spill)
            out += [line if i is None else rp.resolve(i, line) for i, line in body]
        else:
            out += [line for _, line in body]
        out.append('}')
        self.stats['functions'] += 1
        self.stats['instructions'] += len(insns)
        return out, refs


def chunk_text(name, number, emitter, fns):
    """C text of one chunk. fns: [(entry, end)]."""
    body, refs = [], set()
    emitter.uses_patches = False
    for entry, end in fns:
        lines, r = emitter.function(entry, end)
        body.append('\n'.join(lines))
        refs |= r
    # Every referenced function gets a prototype, including ones defined later in this chunk.
    protos = ''.join(f'void {fname(r)}(Cpu *c);\n' for r in sorted(refs))
    if emitter.uses_patches:
        protos += 'extern uint8_t rt_patch_on[];\n'
    return (header(f'{name} chunk {number:04d}') + '#include "cpu.h"\n#include "simd.h"\n\n' + protos + '\n'
            + '\n\n'.join(body) + '\n')


def write_if_changed(path, text):
    """Returns True if the file was written. An unchanged file keeps its mtime, so the build skips it. A changed one
    is written under a temporary name and renamed into place, so a reader never sees it half written."""
    data = text.encode()
    try:
        if path.stat().st_size == len(data) and path.read_bytes() == data:
            return False
    except FileNotFoundError:
        pass
    tmp = path.with_name(f'.{path.name}.{os.getpid()}.tmp')
    tmp.write_bytes(data)
    try:
        _retry(os.replace, tmp, path)
    except OSError:
        tmp.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        raise
    return True


def _retry(fn, *args):
    """Windows refuses to rewrite or delete a file another process has open or mapped (clang maps its sources, so a
    build running on the output holds them; so can a scanner or an editor). Waits up to 30 s for it."""
    for i in range(120):
        try:
            return fn(*args)
        except OSError as e:
            if i == 119 or isinstance(e, FileNotFoundError):
                raise
            time.sleep(0.25)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ workers

_W = {}  # worker state: 'mods' {name: (path, base)}, 'starts' {name: sorted array}, 'emitters' {name: Emitter}


def _worker_init(mods, starts, table, opts):
    _W['mods'] = mods
    _W['starts'] = starts
    _W['patches'] = table
    _W['opts'] = opts   # Emitter keyword arguments
    _W['emitters'] = {}


def _emitter(name):
    e = _W['emitters'].get(name)
    if e is None:
        path, base = _W['mods'][name]
        mod = Module(name, path, base, 'c')
        e = _W['emitters'][name] = Emitter(mod, set(_W['starts'][name].tolist()),
                                           _W['patches'].for_module(name, base),
                                           spins=_W['patches'].spins_for(name, base), **_W['opts'])
    return e


def _emit_chunk(task):
    """Worker: write one chunk. Returns its statistics."""
    name, number, path, fns = task
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    e = _emitter(name)
    e.stats.clear()
    e.unsupported.clear()
    text = chunk_text(name, number, e, fns)
    error = None
    try:
        written = write_if_changed(Path(path), text)
    except OSError as ex:
        written, error = False, f'{path}: {ex}'
    return {'module': name, 'number': number, 'file': Path(path).name, 'functions': len(fns), 'bytes': len(text),
            'written': written, 'error': error, 'seconds': time.perf_counter() - t0, 'stats': dict(e.stats),
            'unsupported': dict(e.unsupported)}


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ driver

def table_text(name, addrs):
    lines = [header(f'{name} function table'), '#include "cpu.h"\n\n']
    lines += [f'void {fname(a)}(Cpu *c);\n' for a in addrs]
    lines.append(f'\nconst uint64_t {name}_fn_addrs[] = {{\n')
    lines.append(',\n'.join(hx(a) for a in addrs))
    lines.append(f'\n}};\nconst GuestFn {name}_fn_ptrs[] = {{\n')
    lines.append(',\n'.join(fname(a) for a in addrs))
    lines.append(f'\n}};\nconst uint64_t {name}_fn_count = {len(addrs)};\n')
    return ''.join(lines)


def remove_stale(moddir, name, nchunks, errors):
    """Delete chunks an earlier run wrote beyond this run's count, and temporary files an interrupted run left."""
    pat = re.compile(re.escape(name) + r'_(\d{4})\.c')
    removed = 0
    for p in moddir.iterdir():
        m = pat.fullmatch(p.name)
        if (m and int(m.group(1)) >= nchunks) or (p.name.startswith('.') and p.name.endswith('.tmp')):
            try:
                _retry(p.unlink)
                removed += 1
            except OSError as ex:
                errors.append(f'{p}: {ex}')
    return removed


# Peak memory of one emit worker on 1.4.3 is 1.3 GiB (1.5 GiB with margin); the parent holds about 0.7 GiB.
WORKER_MEM = 1536 << 20
MEM_SHARE = 0.8  # of the free memory the workers may take, the rest is for the system and other programs


def pick_jobs(requested):
    """Worker count and the reason for it: --jobs if given, else the CPU count capped by the free memory."""
    if requested:
        return requested, '--jobs'
    cpus = os.cpu_count() or 4
    free = hostmem.available_ram()
    if free is None:
        return cpus, f'{cpus} CPUs, free memory unknown'
    by_mem = max(1, int(free * MEM_SHARE) // WORKER_MEM)
    return min(cpus, by_mem), f'{cpus} CPUs, {free / 2**30:.1f} GiB free memory allows {by_mem}'


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument('--exefs', type=Path, required=True)
    ap.add_argument('--out', type=Path, required=True)
    ap.add_argument('--modules', default='main,subsdk0,sdk')
    ap.add_argument('--jobs', type=int, help='emit workers (default: by free memory and CPU count)')
    ap.add_argument('--limit', type=int, default=0, help='emit only the first N functions of each module')
    ap.add_argument('--chunk-fns', type=int, default=3000, help='functions per chunk at most')
    ap.add_argument('--chunk-bytes', type=int, default=3000000, help='estimated bytes of C per chunk')
    ap.add_argument('--big-fn', type=int, default=300000, help='estimated bytes of C from which a function gets '
                                                               'its own chunk')
    ap.add_argument('--patches', type=Path, help='code patch table (recomp/patches.py)')
    ap.add_argument('--reg-locals', type=int, default=regs.LOCALS,
                    help=f'guest registers per function kept in C locals (recomp/regs.py; default {regs.LOCALS}, 0: none)')
    ap.add_argument('--no-callee-saved-trust', action='store_true',
                    help='reload X19-X29 and SP after every call too, instead of trusting AAPCS64 (slower; for '
                         'telling a broken callee from a generator bug)')
    args = ap.parse_args()
    opts = {'reg_locals': args.reg_locals, 'callee_saved': not args.no_callee_saved_trust}

    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    mods = layout(args.exefs)
    write_layout(mods, args.out)
    table = patches.load(args.patches, mods) if args.patches else patches.Table()
    write_if_changed(args.out / 'patches.h', patches.header_text(table, GENERATED_MARKER))
    want = args.modules.split(',')
    unknown = set(want) - {n for n, _, _ in mods}
    if unknown:
        raise SystemExit(f'not in {args.exefs}: {", ".join(sorted(unknown))}')

    paths, starts_abs, info, tasks = {}, {}, {}, []
    for name, base, _ in mods:
        if name not in want:
            continue
        t = time.perf_counter()
        path = args.exefs / name
        mod = Module(name, path, base, 'c')
        patches.check(table, mod, name)
        starts, dstats = discover(mod)
        est = estimate_sizes(mod, starts)
        abs_starts = mod.lo + starts * 4
        n = len(starts) if not args.limit else min(args.limit, len(starts))
        ends = np.append(abs_starts[1:], mod.hi)
        chunks = partition(est[:n], args.chunk_fns, args.chunk_bytes, args.big_fn)
        moddir = args.out / name
        moddir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        for number, (i0, i1) in enumerate(chunks):
            fns = list(zip(abs_starts[i0:i1].tolist(), ends[i0:i1].tolist()))
            tasks.append((int(est[i0:i1].sum()), (name, number, str(moddir / f'{name}_{number:04d}.c'), fns)))
        paths[name] = (str(path), base)
        starts_abs[name] = abs_starts
        info[name] = {'base': base, 'lo': mod.lo, 'hi': mod.hi, 'emitted': abs_starts[:n].tolist(),
                      'chunks': len(chunks), 'discover': dstats, 'discover_seconds': time.perf_counter() - t,
                      'moddir': moddir}
        print(f'{name}: {dstats["functions"]} functions ({dstats["seeds"]} seeds, {dstats["rounds"]} rounds), '
              f'{len(chunks)} chunks, discovery {time.perf_counter() - t:.1f}s', file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
        del mod

    # Largest chunks first, so the pool does not end on a long tail.
    tasks.sort(key=lambda t: -t[0])
    results = {name: [] for name in info}
    done_at, errors = {}, []
    t_emit = time.perf_counter()
    ctx = mp.get_context('spawn')
    jobs, why = pick_jobs(args.jobs)
    print(f'emitting with {jobs} workers ({why})', file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
    with ctx.Pool(jobs, initializer=_worker_init, initargs=(paths, starts_abs, table, opts)) as pool:
        for i, r in enumerate(pool.imap_unordered(_emit_chunk, [t for _, t in tasks], chunksize=1)):
            results[r['module']].append(r)
            if r['error']:
                errors.append(r['error'])
            done_at[r['module']] = time.perf_counter() - t_emit
            if (i + 1) % 200 == 0 or i + 1 == len(tasks):
                print(f'emitted {i + 1}/{len(tasks)} chunks, {time.perf_counter() - t_emit:.0f}s', file=sys.stderr,
                      flush=True)

    for name, d in info.items():
        rs = sorted(results[name], key=lambda r: r['number'])
        moddir = d['moddir']
        stats, unsupported = Counter(), Counter()
        for r in rs:
            stats.update(r['stats'])
            unsupported.update(r['unsupported'])
        t = time.perf_counter()
        table_written = write_if_changed(moddir / f'{name}_table.c', table_text(name, d['emitted']))
        removed = remove_stale(moddir, name, d['chunks'], errors)
        manifest = {
            'module': name,
            'marker': GENERATED_MARKER,
            'base': f'{d["base"]:#x}',
            'text': [f'{d["lo"]:#x}', f'{d["hi"]:#x}'],
            'function_count': len(d['emitted']),
            'chunks': [r['file'] for r in rs],
            'table': f'{name}_table.c',
            'chunk_info': [{'file': r['file'], 'functions': r['functions'], 'bytes': r['bytes'],
                            'seconds': round(r['seconds'], 2)} for r in rs],
            'stats': {
                **d['discover'],
                'emitted_functions': stats['functions'],
                'instructions': stats['instructions'],
                'jump_tables': stats['jump_tables'],
                'jump_table_targets': stats['jump_table_targets'],
                'all_label_fallbacks': stats['all_label_fallbacks'],
                'br_dispatch': stats['br_dispatch'],
                'traps': stats['traps'],
                'patched_sites': stats['patched_sites'],
                'local_flag_functions': stats['local_flag_functions'],
                'flag_reads_direct': stats['flag_reads_direct'],
                'flag_reads_packed': stats['flag_reads_packed'],
                'flag_entry_functions': stats['flag_entry_functions'],
                'flag_entry_reads': stats['flag_entry_reads'],
                'flag_reads_after_call': stats['flag_reads_after_call'],
                'flag_publishing_exits': stats['flag_publishing_exits'],
                'spin_gates': stats['spin_gates'],
                'unsupported': stats['unsupported'],
                'external_branches': stats['external_branches'],
                'external_calls': stats['external_calls'],
                'c_bytes': sum(r['bytes'] for r in rs),
                'largest_chunk_bytes': max((r['bytes'] for r in rs), default=0),
                'chunks_written': sum(r['written'] for r in rs) + table_written,
                'stale_chunks_removed': removed,
            },
            'unsupported_census': dict(unsupported.most_common(50)),
            'timings': {
                'discover_s': round(d['discover_seconds'], 2),
                'emit_wall_s': round(done_at.get(name, 0.0), 2),
                'emit_worker_s': round(sum(r['seconds'] for r in rs), 2),
                'table_s': round(time.perf_counter() - t, 2),
            },
        }
        write_if_changed(moddir / 'manifest.json', json.dumps(manifest, indent=1) + '\n')
        s = manifest['stats']
        print(f'{name}: {s["emitted_functions"]} functions, {len(rs)} chunks, {s["c_bytes"] / 1e6:.0f} MB of C, '
              f'{s["jump_tables"]} jump tables, {s["all_label_fallbacks"]} all-label fallbacks, '
              f'{s["br_dispatch"]} br via dispatch, {s["traps"]} traps ({s["unsupported"]} unsupported)',
              file=sys.stderr)
    print(f'total {time.perf_counter() - t0:.0f}s', file=sys.stderr)
    if errors:
        print(f'{len(errors)} files could not be written or removed (held open by another process?):',
              file=sys.stderr)
        for e in errors:
            print(f'  {e}', file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())

```

`recomp/jumptables.py`:

```py
"""Static jump-table resolution for computed `br`.

Clang lowers a dense switch to a bounds check (`cmp wI, #N; b.hi default`, or `b.ls` to a dispatch block placed
elsewhere), a table load (`ldrb/ldrh/ldrsw wO, [xT, xI, lsl #s]`) and an add to an anchor (`adr xB, L;
add xB, xB, wO, sxtb #2`, or the table address itself). The resolver walks back from the `br` over its block and the
predecessor blocks (_explore), evaluates each path forward symbolically (_run), and enumerates the values the path
conditions (bounds checks, ccmp chains, cbz/tbz) or the construction (masks, bit inserts, selects of constants)
allow for the unknowns the target depends on (_solve). Table entries come from .text/.rodata of the unrelocated
image. Anything it cannot prove is rejected.

Values are expression tuples over the registers at the top of the path. 32/64-bit views are normalised
(`lo(zx(e)) = e`, `uxtw`, `and #0xffffffff`, ...) so that the copies and extensions clang inserts compare equal.
Registers at a path top come from a function-wide must-analysis (_facts): constants, small constant sets, terms
over named values, zero-extension. That carries table bases clang hoists out of loops and index copies made
before them.

A function is resolved as a whole (_function): table targets are blocks and edges for the facts and the paths, and
the tables and the facts are iterated to a common fixpoint. Assumptions: control enters [entry, end) only at the
entry, at targets of direct branches (seen module-wide), at exception landing pads (.eh_frame LSDAs) and through
its own table jumps; an unresolved table never enters another switch between its bounds check and its `br`.
Work per function is capped (MAX_STEPS); past the cap nothing in the function is resolved.
"""
import bisect
import itertools
import weakref
from operator import is_not

import numpy as np

from lifter import bits, decode_bit_masks, sext

MAX_BLOCK = 64       # instructions in one block
MAX_DEPTH = 4        # predecessor blocks above the dispatch block
MAX_PATHS = 32       # paths explored per br
MAX_COUNT = 4096     # table entries
MAX_CANDS = 8        # candidates combined in pairs and triples
MAX_SET = 8          # constants a register fact may hold
MAX_STEPS = 1 << 19  # work units per function (instructions evaluated, blocks met, assignments tried)
MAX_ROUNDS = 8       # rounds of the per-function table/fact iteration

M32, M64 = 0xFFFFFFFF, 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF
HS, LO, HI, LS = 2, 3, 8, 9

_REGS = range(31)
_INDEX = weakref.WeakKeyDictionary()
_FUNCS = weakref.WeakKeyDictionary()
_PADS = weakref.WeakKeyDictionary()


def _mask(sz):
    return M32 if sz == 32 else M64


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- expressions

def C(v, sz=64):
    return ('c', v & _mask(sz))


def lo(e):
    """Low 32 bits of a 64-bit value."""
    k = e[0]
    if k == 'c':
        return ('c', e[1] & M32)
    if k in ('zx', 'sx'):
        return e[1]
    if k == 'oneof' and max(e[2]) <= M32:
        return e
    return ('lo', e)


def zx(e):
    return e if e[0] in ('c', 'oneof') else ('zx', e)


def sx(e):
    return C(sext(e[1], 32)) if e[0] == 'c' else ('sx', e)


def binop(op, sz, a, b):
    if a[0] == 'c' and b[0] == 'c':
        return C(_BIN[op](a[1], b[1], sz), sz)
    if op in ('add', 'orr', 'eor') and a[0] == 'c' and a[1] == 0:
        return b
    if op in ('add', 'sub', 'orr', 'eor') and b[0] == 'c' and b[1] == 0:
        return a
    if op == 'and' and b[0] == 'c' and sz == 64 and b[1] <= M32:
        return zx(binop('and', 32, lo(a), b)) if b[1] != M32 else zx(lo(a))
    if op == 'and' and b[0] == 'c' and b[1] == _mask(sz):
        return a
    return (op, sz, a, b)


def shift(op, sz, a, n):
    n %= sz
    if n == 0:
        return a
    if a[0] == 'c':
        return C(_SH[op](a[1], n, sz), sz)
    return (op, sz, a, n)


def bfm(sz, signed, immr, imms, x):
    """UBFM/SBFM of the sz-bit value x."""
    if not signed and immr == 0 and imms == 31 and sz == 64:
        return zx(lo(x))
    if signed and immr == 0 and imms == 31 and sz == 64:
        return sx(lo(x))
    if imms == sz - 1:
        return shift('asr' if signed else 'lsr', sz, x, immr)
    if not signed and imms + 1 == immr:
        return shift('lsl', sz, x, sz - immr)
    if not signed and immr == 0:
        return binop('and', sz, x, C((1 << (imms + 1)) - 1))
    if not signed and sz == 64 and immr <= imms < 32:
        return zx(bfm(32, False, immr, imms, lo(x)))
    e = ('bfm', sz, signed, immr, imms, x)
    return C(_bfm(sz, signed, immr, imms, x[1]), sz) if x[0] == 'c' else e


def bfi(sz, immr, imms, dst, src):
    """BFM (bfi, bfxil): bits of src inserted into dst."""
    if dst[0] == 'c' and src[0] == 'c':
        return C(_bfi(sz, immr, imms, dst[1], src[1]), sz)
    return ('bfi', sz, immr, imms, dst, src)


def _bfi(sz, immr, imms, d, v):
    wmask, tmask = decode_bit_masks(1 if sz == 64 else 0, imms, immr, sz, False)
    m = _mask(sz)
    bot = (d & ~wmask & m) | (_SH['ror'](v, immr, sz) if immr else v) & wmask
    return (d & ~tmask & m) | (bot & tmask)


def extend(e, option, sz):
    """Extended-register operand: option applied to the 64-bit register value e, result sz bits."""
    if option in (3, 7):
        return e if sz == 64 else lo(e)
    if option == 2:
        return zx(lo(e)) if sz == 64 else lo(e)
    if option == 6:
        return sx(lo(e)) if sz == 64 else lo(e)
    b, signed = 8 if option & 3 == 0 else 16, option >= 4
    v = lo(e)
    if v[0] == 'c':
        x = v[1] & ((1 << b) - 1)
        return C(sext(x, b) if signed else x, sz)
    return ('xt', b, signed, sz, v)


def _bfm(sz, signed, immr, imms, v):
    m = _mask(sz)
    if imms >= immr:
        w = imms - immr + 1
        f = (v >> immr) & ((1 << w) - 1)
        return (sext(f, w) if signed else f) & m
    f = v & ((1 << (imms + 1)) - 1)
    if signed:
        f = sext(f, imms + 1)
    return (f << (sz - immr)) & m


_BIN = {
    'add': lambda a, b, sz: (a + b) & _mask(sz),
    'sub': lambda a, b, sz: (a - b) & _mask(sz),
    'and': lambda a, b, sz: a & b,
    'orr': lambda a, b, sz: a | b,
    'eor': lambda a, b, sz: a ^ b,
    'bic': lambda a, b, sz: a & ~b & _mask(sz),
    'orn': lambda a, b, sz: (a | ~b) & _mask(sz),
    'eon': lambda a, b, sz: (a ^ ~b) & _mask(sz),
}
_SH = {
    'lsl': lambda a, n, sz: (a << n) & _mask(sz),
    'lsr': lambda a, n, sz: a >> n,
    'asr': lambda a, n, sz: (sext(a, sz) >> n) & _mask(sz),
    'ror': lambda a, n, sz: ((a >> n) | (a << (sz - n))) & _mask(sz),
}
_SHIFT_NAMES = ('lsl', 'lsr', 'asr', 'ror')


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- symbolic execution of one path

class _State:
    __slots__ = ('regs', 'flags', 'epoch', 'mem', 'conds', 'fresh')

    def __init__(self):
        self.regs = [('r', r) for r in range(32)]  # 31 is SP
        self.flags = None
        self.epoch = 0   # memory version: loads of different versions are different values
        self.mem = []    # [(base, offset, size, value)] stores of this version, disjoint
        self.conds = []   # conditions the branches on the path prove (see _edge)
        self.fresh = 0

    def unknown(self):
        self.fresh += 1
        return ('u', self.fresh)

    def get(self, r, sz, sp=False):
        if r == 31 and not sp:
            return C(0)
        e = self.regs[r]
        return e if sz == 64 else lo(e)

    def set(self, r, sz, e, sp=False):
        if r == 31 and not sp:
            return
        self.regs[r] = e if sz == 64 else zx(e)

    def kill(self, r, sz=64, sp=False):
        """r gets an unknown value; a 32-bit write leaves the upper half zero."""
        if r != 31 or sp:
            self.regs[r] = self.unknown() if sz == 64 else ('zx', self.unknown())

    def clobber(self):
        """Memory changed in an unknown way."""
        self.epoch += 1
        self.mem = []

    def kill_all(self):
        for r in range(32):
            self.regs[r] = self.unknown()
        self.flags = None
        self.clobber()

    def call(self):
        for r in list(range(19)) + [30]:
            self.regs[r] = self.unknown()
        self.flags = None
        self.clobber()

    def store(self, addr, size, value):
        """value (64-bit for 8 bytes, else 32-bit) stored at addr. Stores that may overlap are forgotten: same base
        and overlapping offsets, or a different base."""
        base, off = _split(addr)
        self.epoch += 1
        self.mem = [m for m in self.mem if m[0] == base and (m[1] + m[2] <= off or off + size <= m[1])]
        self.mem.append((base, off, size, value))

    def load(self, size, signed, sz, addr):
        """sz-bit value of the size-byte load at addr, forwarded from a store when the same bytes were stored."""
        base, off = _split(addr)
        for b, o, n, v in self.mem:
            if b == base and o == off and n == size:
                if size == 8:
                    return v
                if size == 4:
                    return sx(v) if signed and sz == 64 else v
                if signed and v[0] == 'c':
                    return C(sext(v[1] & ((1 << (8 * size)) - 1), 8 * size), sz)
                if signed:
                    return ('xt', 8 * size, True, sz, v)
                return binop('and', 32, v, C((1 << (8 * size)) - 1))
        return ('ld', size, signed, sz, addr, self.epoch)


def _split(addr):
    if addr[0] == 'add' and addr[3][0] == 'c':
        return addr[2], addr[3][1]
    if addr[0] == 'c':
        return ('c', 0), addr[1]
    return addr, 0


def _addr_imm(st, w, scale):
    """Base and offset of the load/store register (immediate and register offset) forms."""
    rn = bits(w, 5, 5)
    base = st.get(rn, 64, sp=True)
    if bits(w, 24, 1):  # unsigned offset
        return base, binop('add', 64, base, C(bits(w, 10, 12) << scale)), None
    if bits(w, 21, 1):  # register offset
        if bits(w, 10, 2) != 2:
            return None
        off = extend(st.get(bits(w, 16, 5), 64), bits(w, 13, 3), 64)
        if bits(w, 12, 1):
            off = shift('lsl', 64, off, scale)
        return base, binop('add', 64, base, off), None
    imm = sext(bits(w, 12, 9), 9)
    mode = bits(w, 10, 2)
    new = binop('add', 64, base, C(imm))
    if mode == 1:  # post-index
        return base, base, new
    if mode == 3:  # pre-index
        return base, new, new
    return base, new, None


def _ldst(st, w, pc):
    rt, rn = bits(w, 0, 5), bits(w, 5, 5)
    if (w & 0x3B000000) == 0x18000000:  # load literal
        opc, v = bits(w, 30, 2), bits(w, 26, 1)
        if not v and opc != 3:
            a = C(pc + sext(bits(w, 5, 19), 19) * 4)
            st.set(rt, 64, st.load(8 if opc == 1 else 4, opc == 2, 64, a) if opc else zx(st.load(4, False, 32, a)))
        return
    if (w & 0x3A000000) == 0x28000000:  # pair
        mode, load, v, opc = bits(w, 23, 2), bits(w, 22, 1), bits(w, 26, 1), bits(w, 30, 2)
        scale = 2 + (bits(w, 31, 1) if not v else opc)
        base = st.get(rn, 64, sp=True)
        new = binop('add', 64, base, C(sext(bits(w, 15, 7), 7) << scale))
        addr = base if mode == 1 else new
        rt2 = bits(w, 10, 5)
        if load and not v:
            sz = 64 if opc else 32
            st.kill(rt, sz)
            st.kill(rt2, sz)
        elif not load and not v and opc != 1:
            n = 1 << scale
            a, b = st.get(rt, 8 * n), st.get(rt2, 8 * n)
            st.store(addr, n, a)
            st.store(binop('add', 64, addr, C(n)), n, b)
        elif not load:
            st.clobber()
        if mode in (1, 3):
            st.set(rn, 64, new, sp=True)
        return
    if (w & 0x3B200C00) in (0x38000000, 0x38000400, 0x38000C00, 0x38200800) or (w & 0x3B000000) == 0x39000000:
        size, v, opc = bits(w, 30, 2), bits(w, 26, 1), bits(w, 22, 2)
        if v:
            scale = size | (bits(w, 23, 1) << 2)
            r = _addr_imm(st, w, scale)
            if r is None:
                st.kill_all()
                return
            if not (opc & 1):
                st.clobber()
            if r[2] is not None:
                st.set(rn, 64, r[2], sp=True)
            return
        r = _addr_imm(st, w, size)
        if r is None:
            st.kill_all()
            return
        _, addr, new = r
        if opc == 0:
            st.store(addr, 1 << size, st.get(rt, 64 if size == 3 else 32))
        elif opc == 1:
            st.set(rt, 64, zx(st.load(1 << size, False, 32, addr)) if size < 3 else st.load(8, False, 64, addr))
        elif size == 3:  # prfm
            pass
        elif opc == 2:
            st.set(rt, 64, st.load(1 << size, True, 64, addr))
        elif size < 2:
            st.set(rt, 32, st.load(1 << size, True, 32, addr))
        else:
            st.kill_all()
            return
        if new is not None:
            st.set(rn, 64, new, sp=True)
        return
    if (w & 0xBE000000) == 0x0C000000:  # SIMD structures (multiple and single)
        if not bits(w, 22, 1):
            st.clobber()
        if bits(w, 23, 1):
            st.kill(rn, sp=True)
        return
    sz = 64 if bits(w, 30, 2) == 3 else 32
    if (w & 0x3F000000) == 0x08000000:  # exclusives, acquire/release
        st.kill(rt, sz)
        st.kill(bits(w, 16, 5), 32)
        st.kill(bits(w, 10, 5), sz)
        st.clobber()
        return
    if (w & 0x3B200C00) == 0x38200000:  # LSE atomics
        st.kill(rt, sz)
        st.clobber()
        return
    st.kill_all()


def _dp_imm(st, w, pc):
    sf, rd, rn = bits(w, 31, 1), bits(w, 0, 5), bits(w, 5, 5)
    sz = 64 if sf else 32
    op = bits(w, 23, 3)
    if op in (0, 1):  # ADR, ADRP
        imm = sext((bits(w, 5, 19) << 2) | bits(w, 29, 2), 21)
        st.set(rd, 64, C((pc & ~0xFFF) + (imm << 12) if sf else pc + imm))
    elif op == 2:  # add/sub imm
        opc, s = bits(w, 30, 1), bits(w, 29, 1)
        imm = C(bits(w, 10, 12) << (12 if bits(w, 22, 1) else 0), sz)
        a = st.get(rn, sz, sp=True)
        r = binop('sub' if opc else 'add', sz, a, imm)
        if s:
            st.flags = ('sub' if opc else 'add', sz, a, imm)
        st.set(rd, sz, r, sp=not s)
    elif op == 4:  # logical imm
        opc, n = bits(w, 29, 2), bits(w, 22, 1)
        if not sf and n:
            st.kill_all()
            return
        imm, _ = decode_bit_masks(n, bits(w, 10, 6), bits(w, 16, 6), sz, True)
        r = binop(('and', 'orr', 'eor', 'and')[opc], sz, st.get(rn, sz), C(imm, sz))
        if opc == 3:
            st.flags = ('logic', sz, r)
        st.set(rd, sz, r, sp=opc != 3)
    elif op == 5:  # move wide
        opc, hw = bits(w, 29, 2), bits(w, 21, 2)
        imm = bits(w, 5, 16) << (hw * 16)
        if opc == 0:
            st.set(rd, sz, C(~imm, sz))
        elif opc == 2:
            st.set(rd, sz, C(imm, sz))
        elif opc == 3:
            old = st.get(rd, sz)
            st.set(rd, sz, C((old[1] & ~(0xFFFF << (hw * 16))) | imm, sz) if old[0] == 'c' else st.unknown())
        else:
            st.kill_all()
    elif op == 6:  # bitfield
        opc = bits(w, 29, 2)
        if opc == 1:  # BFM: bfi, bfxil
            st.set(rd, sz, bfi(sz, bits(w, 16, 6), bits(w, 10, 6), st.get(rd, sz), st.get(rn, sz)))
        elif opc == 3:
            st.kill(rd, sz)
        else:
            st.set(rd, sz, bfm(sz, opc == 0, bits(w, 16, 6), bits(w, 10, 6), st.get(rn, sz)))
    elif bits(w, 16, 5) == rn:  # ROR (EXTR with Rn = Rm)
        st.set(rd, sz, shift('ror', sz, st.get(rn, sz), bits(w, 10, 6)))
    else:
        st.kill(rd, sz)


def _dp_reg(st, w):
    sf, rd, rn, rm = bits(w, 31, 1), bits(w, 0, 5), bits(w, 5, 5), bits(w, 16, 5)
    sz = 64 if sf else 32
    if (w & 0x1F000000) == 0x0A000000:  # logical shifted register
        opc, n = bits(w, 29, 2), bits(w, 21, 1)
        b = shift(_SHIFT_NAMES[bits(w, 22, 2)], sz, st.get(rm, sz), bits(w, 10, 6))
        name = (('and', 'orr', 'eor', 'and'), ('bic', 'orn', 'eon', 'bic'))[n][opc]
        r = binop(name, sz, st.get(rn, sz), b)
        if opc == 3:
            st.flags = ('logic', sz, r)
        st.set(rd, sz, r)
    elif (w & 0x1F200000) == 0x0B000000:  # add/sub shifted register
        opc, s, typ = bits(w, 30, 1), bits(w, 29, 1), bits(w, 22, 2)
        if typ == 3:
            st.kill_all()
            return
        a = st.get(rn, sz)
        b = shift(_SHIFT_NAMES[typ], sz, st.get(rm, sz), bits(w, 10, 6))
        if s:
            st.flags = ('sub' if opc else 'add', sz, a, b)
        st.set(rd, sz, binop('sub' if opc else 'add', sz, a, b))
    elif (w & 0x1F200000) == 0x0B200000:  # add/sub extended register
        opc, s = bits(w, 30, 1), bits(w, 29, 1)
        a = st.get(rn, sz, sp=True)
        b = shift('lsl', sz, extend(st.get(rm, 64), bits(w, 13, 3), sz), bits(w, 10, 3))
        if s:
            st.flags = ('sub' if opc else 'add', sz, a, b)
        st.set(rd, sz, binop('sub' if opc else 'add', sz, a, b), sp=not s)
    elif (w & 0x1FE00000) == 0x1A400000 and bits(w, 29, 1):  # ccmp, ccmn
        b = C(rm, sz) if bits(w, 11, 1) else st.get(rm, sz)
        st.flags = ('ccmp', sz, st.get(rn, sz), b, not bits(w, 30, 1), bits(w, 12, 4), bits(w, 0, 4), st.flags)
    elif (w & 0x1FE00000) == 0x1A000000 and (w & 0xFC00):
        st.flags = None  # rmif, setf
    elif (w & 0x1FE00800) == 0x1A800000 and not bits(w, 29, 1):  # csel, csinc, csinv, csneg
        x, y = st.get(rn, sz), st.get(rm, sz)
        if bits(w, 10, 1):
            y = binop('add', sz, y, C(1)) if not bits(w, 30, 1) else binop('sub', sz, C(0), y)
        elif bits(w, 30, 1):
            y = binop('eor', sz, y, C(_mask(sz)))
        # Equal expressions are equal values, so a select carries what picks the arm: the condition and the flags
        # record, or a fresh unknown when the flags are not known (two `cset wN, ne` on different compares differ).
        sel = st.flags if st.flags is not None else st.unknown()
        st.set(rd, sz, x if x == y else ('csel', sz, x, y, bits(w, 12, 4), sel))
    else:  # adc, sbc, csel, 1/2/3-source
        st.kill(rd, sz)
        if bits(w, 29, 1):
            st.flags = None


def _fp_simd(st, w):
    if (w & 0x5F203C00) == 0x1E202000 or (w & 0x5F200C00) == 0x1E200400:  # fcmp, fccmp
        st.flags = None
    elif (w & 0x5F200000) == 0x1E000000 or (w & 0x5F20FC00) == 0x1E200000:  # conversions with a general register
        if bits(w, 16, 3) in (0, 1, 4, 5, 6):  # to a general register (fcvt*, fmov Rd, Vn)
            st.kill(bits(w, 0, 5), 64 if bits(w, 31, 1) else 32)
    elif (w & 0x9FE08400) == 0x0E000400 and bits(w, 11, 4) in (5, 7):  # smov, umov
        st.kill(bits(w, 0, 5), 64 if bits(w, 30, 1) else 32)


def _step(st, w, pc):
    """Effect of one non-branch instruction."""
    op0 = bits(w, 25, 4)
    if (op0 & 0b1110) == 0b1000:
        _dp_imm(st, w, pc)
    elif (op0 & 0b0101) == 0b0100:
        _ldst(st, w, pc)
    elif (op0 & 0b0111) == 0b0101:
        _dp_reg(st, w)
    elif (op0 & 0b0111) == 0b0111:
        _fp_simd(st, w)
    elif (w & 0xFC000000) == 0x94000000 or (w & 0xFFFFFC1F) == 0xD63F0000:  # bl, blr
        st.call()
    elif (w & 0xFFFFF01F) in (0xD503201F, 0xD503301F):  # hints, barriers
        pass
    elif (w & 0xFFF00000) == 0xD5300000:  # mrs
        st.kill(bits(w, 0, 5))
    elif (w & 0xFFF00000) == 0xD5100000:  # msr (system register): may write NZCV
        st.flags = None
    elif (w & 0xFFF80000) == 0xD5080000:  # sys: dc, ic, tlbi
        st.clobber()
    else:
        st.kill_all()


def _edge(st, w, taken):
    """Record the condition a conditional branch edge proves."""
    if (w & 0xFF000010) == 0x54000000:
        cond = bits(w, 0, 4)
        if cond < 14 and st.flags is not None:
            st.conds.append(('flags', st.flags, cond, taken))
    elif (w & 0x7E000000) == 0x34000000:  # cbz, cbnz
        sz = 64 if bits(w, 31, 1) else 32
        st.conds.append(('zero', sz, st.get(bits(w, 0, 5), sz), taken != bool(bits(w, 24, 1))))
    elif (w & 0x7E000000) == 0x36000000:  # tbz, tbnz
        bit = (bits(w, 31, 1) << 5) | bits(w, 19, 5)
        st.conds.append(('bit', st.get(bits(w, 0, 5), 64), bit, taken == bool(bits(w, 24, 1))))


def _init(st, facts):
    """Registers at the top of a path from the function-wide facts (see _facts)."""
    for r, v in facts.items():
        st.regs[r] = ('zx', ('lo', ('r', r))) if v == 'z' else ('oneof', r, v[1]) if v[0] == 'set' else v


class _Exhausted(Exception):
    """The per-function step budget ran out."""


_budget = [0]


def _spend(n):
    _budget[0] -= n
    if _budget[0] < 0:
        raise _Exhausted


def _run(mod, path, rn, facts, spend=True):
    """Symbolic state at the br that ends path [(start, last, taken)] (top block first) and the br register value.

    taken says which edge of a conditional branch at `last` the path follows; None for any other block end
    (fall-through, unconditional branch, table jump).
    """
    if spend:
        _spend(sum(last - start >> 2 for start, last, _ in path) + 1)
    st = _State()
    if facts:
        _init(st, facts)
    for start, last, taken in path[:-1]:
        for a in range(start, last, 4):
            _step(st, mod.word(a), a)
        w = mod.word(last)
        if taken is not None:
            _edge(st, w, taken)
        elif _branch_target(w, last) is None and not _is_br(w):
            _step(st, w, last)
    start, last, _ = path[-1]
    for a in range(start, last, 4):
        _step(st, mod.word(a), a)
    return st, st.get(rn, 64)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- control flow

def _branch_target(w, pc):
    """Target of a direct branch (b, b.cond, cbz/cbnz, tbz/tbnz), else None."""
    if (w & 0xFC000000) == 0x14000000:
        return pc + sext(w & 0x3FFFFFF, 26) * 4
    if (w & 0xFF000010) == 0x54000000 or (w & 0x7E000000) == 0x34000000:
        return pc + sext(bits(w, 5, 19), 19) * 4
    if (w & 0x7E000000) == 0x36000000:
        return pc + sext(bits(w, 5, 14), 14) * 4
    return None


def _no_fallthrough(w):
    """b, b.al, br/ret/eret (branch-register forms other than blr), udf, brk, hlt."""
    return ((w & 0xFC000000) == 0x14000000 or (w & 0xFF00001E) == 0x5400000E
            or (w & 0xFE000000) == 0xD6000000 and (w & 0x01E00000) != 0x00200000
            or (w >> 16) == 0 or (w & 0xFFE0001F) in (0xD4200000, 0xD4400000))


def _ends_block(w):
    return _no_fallthrough(w) or (w & 0xFF000010) == 0x54000000 or (w & 0x7C000000) == 0x34000000


def _ends_block_np(w):
    return (((w & 0xFC000000) == 0x14000000) | ((w & 0xFF000010) == 0x54000000) | ((w & 0x7C000000) == 0x34000000)
            | (((w & 0xFE000000) == 0xD6000000) & ((w & 0x01E00000) != 0x00200000)) | ((w >> 16) == 0)
            | ((w & 0xFFE0001F) == 0xD4200000) | ((w & 0xFFE0001F) == 0xD4400000))


def _is_br(w):
    return (w & 0xFFFFFC1F) == 0xD61F0000


def _is_call(w):
    return (w & 0xFC000000) == 0x94000000 or (w & 0xFFFFFC1F) == 0xD63F0000


def _branch_index(mod):
    """(targets, sources) of every direct branch in .text, sorted by target; cached per module."""
    r = _INDEX.get(mod)
    if r is None:
        w = mod.words.astype(np.int64)
        pc = mod.lo + 4 * np.arange(len(w), dtype=np.int64)
        b = (w & 0xFC000000) == 0x14000000
        c = ((w & 0xFF000010) == 0x54000000) | ((w & 0x7E000000) == 0x34000000)
        t = (w & 0x7E000000) == 0x36000000
        off = np.zeros(len(w), dtype=np.int64)
        off[b] = ((w[b] & 0x3FFFFFF) ^ 0x2000000) - 0x2000000
        off[c] = (((w[c] >> 5) & 0x7FFFF) ^ 0x40000) - 0x40000
        off[t] = (((w[t] >> 5) & 0x3FFF) ^ 0x2000) - 0x2000
        m = b | c | t
        src, dst = pc[m], pc[m] + 4 * off[m]
        order = np.argsort(dst, kind='stable')
        r = _INDEX[mod] = (dst[order], src[order])
    return r


def branch_sources(mod, entry, end):
    """{target: [sources]} of the direct branches anywhere in .text that land in [entry, end)."""
    dst, src = _branch_index(mod)
    i, j = np.searchsorted(dst, [entry, end])
    out = {}
    for d, s in zip(dst[i:j].tolist(), src[i:j].tolist()):
        out.setdefault(d, []).append(s)
    return out


class _Cfg:
    """Basic blocks of [entry, end) with direct, fall-through and table edges.

    tables maps each table-shaped br to its targets so far, or None when it is unresolved and may reach any block.
    Leaders are the entry, direct branch targets, landing pads, table targets and the instruction after each
    block-ending instruction. `unknown` holds the blocks entered in ways the function does not show: the entry and
    targets of branches from other functions.
    """

    def __init__(self, mod, entry, end, tables, pads):
        self.mod, self.entry, self.end, self.pads = mod, entry, end, pads
        labels = branch_sources(mod, entry, end)
        words = mod.words[(entry - mod.lo) >> 2:(end - mod.lo) >> 2].astype(np.int64)
        after = (entry + 4 * np.nonzero(_ends_block_np(words))[0] + 4).tolist()
        targets = {t for ts in tables.values() if ts for t in ts if entry <= t < end}
        self.leaders = sorted({entry} | set(labels) | set(pads) | targets | {a for a in after if a < end})
        self.stops = self.leaders[1:] + [end]
        self.unknown = {entry} | {t for t, srcs in labels.items() if any(not entry <= a < end for a in srcs)}
        self.everywhere = [br for br, ts in tables.items() if ts is None]
        self.preds = {b: [] for b in self.leaders}  # [(last instruction of the predecessor, taken)]
        for b, stop in zip(self.leaders, self.stops):
            last = stop - 4
            w = mod.word(last)
            t = _branch_target(w, last)
            cond = (w & 0xFF000010) == 0x54000000 and (w & 0xE) != 0xE or (w & 0x7C000000) == 0x34000000
            if t is not None and entry <= t < end:
                self.preds[t].append((last, True if cond and t != stop else None))
            if not _no_fallthrough(w) and stop < end and t != stop:
                self.preds[stop].append((last, False if cond else None))
        for br, ts in tables.items():
            for t in ts or ():
                if entry <= t < end:
                    self.preds[t].append((br, None))

    def block(self, a):
        """Start of the block holding a."""
        return self.leaders[bisect.bisect_right(self.leaders, a) - 1]

    def path_preds(self, b):
        """[(start, last, taken)] predecessor segments of block b, or None if some entry is not visible.

        Unresolved table jumps are not counted: a table is assumed never to enter another switch's dispatch path
        after its bounds check.
        """
        if b in self.unknown or b in self.pads or not self.preds[b]:
            return None
        return [(self.block(src), src, taken) for src, taken in self.preds[b]]


def _facts(cfg):
    """{block start: {reg: fact}} for the registers whose value is known the same way on every path into the block.

    A fact is a constant, a small set of constants ('set', values), a term, or 'z' (a zero-extended 32-bit value).
    Terms are expressions over names ('v', A, r) / ('vw', A, r): the 64-bit / 32-bit value the most recent execution
    of instruction A wrote to r.
    They keep copies and extensions of one value equal across blocks (`mov w12, w8` before a loop, the check on w8
    inside it). A name dies when its instruction executes again.

    A forward must-analysis over cfg, optimistic for blocks not yet reached. An exception landing pad is entered from
    the calls of its call-site ranges with the caller-saved registers clobbered; an unresolved table jump may enter
    any block. None if the analysis does not settle.
    """
    mod, out, ins, calls, names = cfg.mod, {}, {}, {}, set()
    for _ in range(64):
        _spend(len(cfg.leaders))
        changed = False
        anywhere = None
        for br in cfg.everywhere:
            anywhere = _meet(anywhere, out.get(br))
        for b, stop in zip(cfg.leaders, cfg.stops):
            if b in cfg.unknown:
                d = {}
            else:
                d = None
                for src, _ in cfg.preds[b]:
                    d = _meet(d, out.get(src))
                for lo_, hi_ in cfg.pads.get(b, ()):
                    for a, c in calls.items():
                        if lo_ <= a < hi_:
                            d = _meet(d, c)
                d = _meet(d, anywhere)
                if d is None:
                    continue
            if ins.get(b) == d and stop - 4 in out:
                continue  # same input as last round: the transfer gives the same output
            ins[b] = d
            _spend(stop - b >> 2)
            st = _State()
            _init(st, d)
            regs = st.regs
            for a in range(b, stop, 4):
                w = mod.word(a)
                if _is_call(w):
                    c = {r: v for r, v in _facts_of(st).items() if 19 <= r < 30}
                    if calls.get(a) != c:
                        calls[a] = c
                        changed = True
                if a == stop - 4 and (_is_br(w) or _branch_target(w, a) is not None):
                    break
                before = regs[:31]
                _step(st, w, a)
                for r in itertools.compress(_REGS, map(is_not, regs, before)):
                    e = regs[r]
                    if e[0] != 'oneof' and not _clean(e):
                        regs[r] = ('zx', ('vw', a, r)) if e[0] == 'zx' else ('v', a, r)
                        names.add(a)
                if a in names:
                    for r in range(31):
                        if regs[r] is before[r] and _names(regs[r], a):
                            regs[r] = st.unknown()
            d = _facts_of(st)
            if out.get(stop - 4) != d:
                out[stop - 4] = d
                changed = True
        if not changed:
            return ins
    return None


def _clean(e, depth=8):
    """e is built from constants and names only, and is small (larger values get a name)."""
    k = e[0]
    if k in ('c', 'v', 'vw'):
        return True
    if k in ('r', 'u', 'ld', 'oneof') or not depth:
        return False
    return all(_clean(x, depth - 1) for x in e[1:] if isinstance(x, tuple))


def _names(e, a):
    """e mentions a name written by instruction a."""
    k = e[0]
    if k in ('v', 'vw'):
        return e[1] == a
    if k in ('c', 'r', 'u'):
        return False
    return any(_names(x, a) for x in e[1:] if isinstance(x, tuple))


def _facts_of(st):
    out = {}
    for r, e in enumerate(st.regs[:31]):
        if _clean(e):
            out[r] = e
        elif e[0] == 'oneof':
            out[r] = ('set', e[2])
        elif e[0] == 'zx':
            out[r] = 'z'
    return out


def _values(v):
    return frozenset((v[1],)) if v[0] == 'c' else v[1] if v[0] == 'set' else None


def _zext(v):
    return v == 'z' or v[0] == 'zx' or _values(v) is not None and max(_values(v)) <= M32


def _meet(a, b):
    if a is None:
        return b
    if b is None:
        return a
    out = {}
    for r, v in a.items():
        u = b.get(r)
        if u is None:
            continue
        if u == v:
            out[r] = v
            continue
        if u != 'z' and v != 'z':
            a_, b_ = _values(u), _values(v)
            if a_ is not None and b_ is not None and len(a_ | b_) <= MAX_SET:
                out[r] = ('set', a_ | b_)
                continue
        if _zext(u) and _zext(v):
            out[r] = 'z'
    return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- enumeration

class _Unknown(Exception):
    """The value depends on something the assignment does not fix (a register, or memory other than .text and
    .rodata)."""


def _eval(mod, e, env):
    """Value of e with the subexpressions in env [(expr, value)] fixed."""
    for x, v in env:
        if e is x:
            return v
    k = e[0]
    if k == 'c':
        return e[1]
    for x, v in env:
        if e == x:
            return v
    if k == 'lo':
        return _eval(mod, e[1], env) & M32
    if k == 'zx':
        return _eval(mod, e[1], env)
    if k == 'sx':
        return sext(_eval(mod, e[1], env), 32) & M64
    if k in _BIN:
        return _BIN[k](_eval(mod, e[2], env), _eval(mod, e[3], env), e[1])
    if k in _SH:
        return _SH[k](_eval(mod, e[2], env), e[3], e[1])
    if k == 'xt':
        _, b, signed, sz, x = e
        v = _eval(mod, x, env) & ((1 << b) - 1)
        return (sext(v, b) if signed else v) & _mask(sz)
    if k == 'bfm':
        return _bfm(e[1], e[2], e[3], e[4], _eval(mod, e[5], env))
    if k == 'bfi':
        return _bfi(e[1], e[2], e[3], _eval(mod, e[4], env), _eval(mod, e[5], env))
    if k == 'ld':
        _, size, signed, sz, addr, _ = e
        a = _eval(mod, addr, env)
        if not _const_mem(mod, a, size):
            raise _Unknown
