`runtime/cfg.h`:

```h
// Settings: the TOTK_* environment variables, with totk.ini next to totk.exe behind them.
#pragma once

// getenv for a setting: the environment variable when set, else the totk.ini key (the name without "TOTK_", any
// case), else the device profile's default (cfg.c: the Steam Deck), else NULL. Same string semantics as getenv; the pointer stays valid for the process (a value cfg_set replaces
// is kept). A name without the TOTK_ prefix goes to getenv unchanged. Safe from any thread once cfg_init has returned.
const char *cfg_get(const char *name);

// Reads totk.ini once, from mem_init after the address space is claimed and before any setting is read. Logs the file, its key count, unknown keys and environment overrides.
void cfg_init(void);

// Replaces the loaded keys with those of the file at path (tests). 1 when the file was read, 0 when missing.
// Not thread-safe: nothing else may call cfg_get meanwhile.
int cfg_load(const char *path);

// Live settings (the in-game menu). cfg_set stores value as the totk.ini value of name (TOTK_ prefixed), marks it for
// cfg_save and bumps cfg_version. cfg_get returns it unless the environment sets name. Any thread.
void cfg_set(const char *name, const char *value);
// Bumped by every cfg_set. A consumer that keeps a parsed value compares this with the number it last saw (one atomic
// load) and parses again when it changed.
unsigned cfg_version(void);
// 1 when the environment sets name: cfg_set cannot change what cfg_get returns (the menu greys the setting out).
int cfg_from_env(const char *name);
// 1 when the player set name (the environment or totk.ini), 0 when cfg_get gives a device profile's default or NULL.
int cfg_is_set(const char *name);
// The device profile in use, "deck" or "desktop" (TOTK_DEVICE_PROFILE, else what the machine is).
const char *cfg_device_profile(void);
// Writes the keys cfg_set changed since the last save into totk.ini next to totk.exe (cfg_save_to: the file at path).
// Only those lines change: the last line of a changed key gets the new value, a missing key goes under its section
// (after the commented example line of the key when the section has one; the section is added at the end of the file
// when missing), comments and every other line stay byte for byte. 1 on success or with nothing to write.
int cfg_save(void);
int cfg_save_to(const char *path);

// Reset (the menu's "Reset all settings to defaults"). Removes the active line of each key (names without TOTK_, any
// case) from totk.ini at the next cfg_save and its value from memory, so the consumer's own default applies again; the
// commented example lines stay. Keys the environment sets are skipped. Bumps cfg_version. Returns how many it reset.
int cfg_reset(const char *const *keys, int n);
// 0 when the last cfg_save / cfg_save_to failed to write (the values stay set in memory, the next save tries again).
int cfg_last_save_ok(void);
// Every setting with a value, for a bug report ("Copy system info"): the totk.ini and cfg_set keys (name without
// TOTK_, upper case; from_env 0), then the known TOTK_ variables the environment sets (from_env 1).
void cfg_each_active(void (*cb)(const char *key, const char *value, int from_env, void *ctx), void *ctx);

// What the menu knows about a setting. key: without TOTK_, upper case. def: what the consumer uses when the key is
// unset ("" = no fixed default, the consumer picks per machine). values: "0|1", "mailbox|fifo|immediate", a range
// "0..300", or NULL for free text. live: applies at once; the others are read at start.
typedef struct { const char *key, *def, *values; int live; } CfgMeta;
// The row of key (prefix and case ignored); NULL for a key the menu does not show.
const CfgMeta *cfg_meta(const char *key);
// The i-th row (0-based, table order); NULL past the last.
const CfgMeta *cfg_meta_at(int i);

// The setting's value for consumers: the environment or totk.ini value, else the CfgMeta default. name has the TOTK_
// prefix, like cfg_get; a name without a row is a bug (rt_fatal). A row with an empty default has no fixed value: its
// consumer reads cfg_get and keeps its own "unset" branch. An empty value counts as unset.
const char *cfg_value(const char *name);
// cfg_value parsed. A set value that does not parse (int: whole string; double: strtod) gives the default's number.
// cfg_bool: "0" is false, anything else true.
int cfg_int(const char *name);
double cfg_double(const char *name);
int cfg_bool(const char *name);

```

`runtime/cfg_probe.c`:

```c
// --probe-cfg: totk.ini parsing, the environment override, the MKW_ names and a missing file (cfg.c). Needs no game
// files.
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "cfg.h"
#include "host.h"
#include "input.h"
#include "input_map.h"
#include "platform/platform.h"

static int fails;
#define CHECK(c, what) do { if (!(c)) { fails++; fprintf(stderr, "FAIL cfg: %s\n", what); } } while (0)
#define EQ(a, b) ((a) && !strcmp((a), (b)))

int probe_cfg(void) {
    char path[1024];
    if (!plat_exe_path(path, sizeof path)) return 1;
    char *cut = plat_last_sep(path);
    if (!cut) return 1;
    strcpy(cut + 1, "cfg-probe.ini");
    static const char ini[] =
        "\xEF\xBB\xBF# comment\r\n"
        "; another comment\r\n"
        "[frame rate]\r\n"
        "  fps60 = 0  \r\n"
        "Realtime=0\r\n"
        "[Display]\r\n"
        "GPU_name = \"My GPU 1\"\r\n"
        "TOTK_Locale = de-DE\r\n"
        "lang =\r\n"
        "trace = a\r\n"
        "trace = b\r\n"
        "no_such_setting = 1\r\n"
        "no equals sign\r\n"
        "last = no newline at the end";
    plat_setenv("TOTK_LOCALE", NULL);
    plat_setenv("TOTK_FPS60", NULL);
    CHECK(plat_file_write(path, ini, sizeof ini - 1), "write the probe ini");
    CHECK(cfg_load(path) == 1, "load the probe ini");
    CHECK(EQ(cfg_get("TOTK_FPS60"), "0"), "value read, whitespace trimmed, lower-case key");
    CHECK(EQ(cfg_get("TOTK_REALTIME"), "0"), "key without spaces, mixed case");
    CHECK(EQ(cfg_get("TOTK_GPU_NAME"), "My GPU 1"), "quoted value, section ignored");
    CHECK(EQ(cfg_get("TOTK_LOCALE"), "de-DE"), "TOTK_ prefix accepted in the file");
    CHECK(cfg_get("TOTK_LANG") == NULL, "empty value is unset");
    CHECK(EQ(cfg_get("TOTK_TRACE"), "b"), "later line wins");
    CHECK(cfg_get("TOTK_CLOTH_REALTIME") == NULL, "absent key is NULL");
    CHECK(cfg_get("TOTK_comment") == NULL, "comment is not a key");
    CHECK(EQ(cfg_get("TOTK_NO_SUCH_SETTING"), "1"), "unknown key is still readable");
    plat_setenv("TOTK_FPS60", "1");
    CHECK(EQ(cfg_get("TOTK_FPS60"), "1"), "environment overrides the file");
    plat_setenv("TOTK_FPS60", NULL);
    CHECK(EQ(cfg_get("TOTK_FPS60"), "0"), "file value returns when the variable is removed");
    plat_setenv("MKW_FPS60", "1");
    CHECK(EQ(cfg_get("TOTK_FPS60"), "1") && cfg_from_env("TOTK_FPS60"), "MKW_ name stands for the TOTK_ one");
    plat_setenv("TOTK_FPS60", "0");
    CHECK(EQ(cfg_get("TOTK_FPS60"), "1"), "MKW_ name wins over the TOTK_ one");
    plat_setenv("MKW_FPS60", NULL);
    plat_setenv("TOTK_FPS60", NULL);
    plat_file_delete(path);
    CHECK(cfg_load(path) == 0, "missing file is not an error");
    CHECK(cfg_get("TOTK_FPS60") == NULL, "missing file leaves no keys");

    // cfg_set / cfg_save: only changed lines move, comments stay, a missing key goes under its section
    static const char before[] =
        "\xEF\xBB\xBF# my settings\r\n"
        "[frame rate]\r\n"
        "  FPS60 = 1\r\n"
        "; keep this\r\n"
        "\r\n"
        "[input]\r\n"
        "# Gamepad motion controls (0 = off) and vibration (0 = off).\r\n"
        "# motion = 1\r\n"
        "# rumble = 1\r\n"
        "rumble_curve = 0.6\r\n"
        "\r\n"
        "[files]\r\n"
        "romfs_mods = C:\\mods";
    static const char after[] =
        "\xEF\xBB\xBF# my settings\r\n"
        "[frame rate]\r\n"
        "  FPS60 = 0\r\n"
        "; keep this\r\n"
        "\r\n"
        "[input]\r\n"
        "# Gamepad motion controls (0 = off) and vibration (0 = off).\r\n"
        "# motion = 1\r\n"
        "motion = 0\r\n"
        "# rumble = 1\r\n"
        "rumble_curve = 0.6\r\n"
        "rumble_strength = 80\r\n"
        "\r\n"
        "[files]\r\n"
        "romfs_mods = C:\\mods\r\n"
        "\r\n"
        "[audio]\r\n"
        "volume = 40\r\n";
    plat_setenv("TOTK_MOTION", NULL);
    plat_setenv("TOTK_VOLUME", NULL);
    plat_setenv("TOTK_RUMBLE_STRENGTH", NULL);
    CHECK(plat_file_write(path, before, sizeof before - 1), "write the save ini");
    CHECK(cfg_load(path) == 1, "load the save ini");
    unsigned v0 = cfg_version();
    cfg_set("TOTK_FPS60", "0");
    cfg_set("TOTK_MOTION", "0");
    cfg_set("TOTK_RUMBLE_STRENGTH", "80");
    cfg_set("TOTK_VOLUME", "40");
    CHECK(cfg_version() == v0 + 4, "cfg_set bumps the version");
    CHECK(EQ(cfg_get("TOTK_FPS60"), "0") && EQ(cfg_get("TOTK_VOLUME"), "40"), "cfg_set values are read back at once");
    CHECK(cfg_save_to(path) == 1, "cfg_save_to writes");
    uint64_t got_n = 0;
    uint8_t *got = plat_file_read(path, &got_n);
    CHECK(got && got_n == sizeof after - 1 && !memcmp(got, after, got_n),
          "saved file: changed line replaced, comments kept, missing keys under their sections");
    if (got && (got_n != sizeof after - 1 || memcmp(got, after, got_n))) fprintf(stderr, "---- saved:\n%s\n----\n", got);
    free(got);
    CHECK(cfg_save_to(path) == 1, "a save with nothing changed");
    got = plat_file_read(path, &got_n);
    CHECK(got && got_n == sizeof after - 1 && !memcmp(got, after, got_n), "a save with nothing changed keeps the file");
    free(got);
    CHECK(cfg_load(path) == 1 && EQ(cfg_get("TOTK_FPS60"), "0") && EQ(cfg_get("TOTK_MOTION"), "0") &&
          EQ(cfg_get("TOTK_RUMBLE_STRENGTH"), "80") && EQ(cfg_get("TOTK_VOLUME"), "40") &&
          EQ(cfg_get("TOTK_ROMFS_MODS"), "C:\\mods"), "the saved file reads back");
    const char *held = cfg_get("TOTK_VOLUME");
    plat_setenv("TOTK_VOLUME", "70");
    cfg_set("TOTK_VOLUME", "90");
    CHECK(cfg_from_env("TOTK_VOLUME") && EQ(cfg_get("TOTK_VOLUME"), "70"), "environment wins over cfg_set");
    CHECK(EQ(held, "40"), "a pointer cfg_get handed out stays valid after cfg_set");
    plat_setenv("TOTK_VOLUME", NULL);
    CHECK(!cfg_from_env("TOTK_VOLUME") && EQ(cfg_get("TOTK_VOLUME"), "90"), "cfg_set value returns without the variable");
    plat_file_delete(path);
    CHECK(cfg_save_to(path) == 1, "cfg_save_to creates a missing file");
    got = plat_file_read(path, &got_n);
    CHECK(got && !strcmp((const char *)got, "[audio]\nvolume = 90\n"), "new file: the section and the key");
    free(got);

    // Defaults table: the menu's "default" marks and Reset
    const CfgMeta *m = cfg_meta("FPS60");
    CHECK(m && EQ(m->def, "1") && m->live, "meta: fps60 defaults to 1 and is live");
    m = cfg_meta("ASYNC_PREEMPT");
    CHECK(m && EQ(m->values, "0|1|2") && !m->live, "meta: async_preempt takes 0|1|2 and needs a restart");
    m = cfg_meta("totk_vk_present");
    CHECK(m && EQ(m->key, "VK_PRESENT") && EQ(m->values, "mailbox|fifo|immediate") && m->live,
          "meta: prefix and case are accepted");
    m = cfg_meta("RUMBLE_STRENGTH");
    CHECK(m && EQ(m->def, "130") && EQ(m->values, "0..300"), "meta: rumble strength 130 in 0..300");
    m = cfg_meta("PERF_OVERLAY");
    CHECK(m && EQ(m->def, "off") && EQ(m->values, "off|fps|full") && m->live, "meta: perf_overlay is live, off by default");
    CHECK(cfg_meta("BIND_A") == NULL && cfg_meta("FPS_COUNTER") == NULL && cfg_meta("NO_SUCH") == NULL,
          "meta: keys the menu does not show are NULL");

    // cfg_reset: the key's active lines leave totk.ini, the commented example stays
    static const char rbase[] = "[audio]\n# volume = 100\n[input]\nmotion = 0\n";
    static const char *const vol[] = {"VOLUME"};
    plat_setenv("TOTK_VOLUME", NULL);
    CHECK(plat_file_write(path, rbase, sizeof rbase - 1), "write the reset ini");
    CHECK(cfg_load(path) == 1, "load the reset ini");
    cfg_set("TOTK_VOLUME", "40");
    CHECK(cfg_save_to(path) == 1 && cfg_last_save_ok(), "reset: volume saved");
    got = plat_file_read(path, &got_n);
    CHECK(got && strstr((const char *)got, "\nvolume = 40\n"), "reset: the active line is in the file");
    free(got);
    unsigned v1 = cfg_version();
    CHECK(cfg_reset(vol, 1) == 1, "reset: one key reset");
    CHECK(cfg_version() > v1 && cfg_get("TOTK_VOLUME") == NULL, "reset: the value is gone in memory, the version moved");
    CHECK(cfg_reset(vol, 1) == 0, "reset: a key already reset counts 0");
    CHECK(cfg_save_to(path) == 1, "reset: save");
    got = plat_file_read(path, &got_n);
    CHECK(got && got_n == sizeof rbase - 1 && !memcmp(got, rbase, got_n) && strstr((const char *)got, "# volume = 100"),
          "reset: no active volume line, the commented example and the other keys stay");
    if (got && (got_n != sizeof rbase - 1 || memcmp(got, rbase, got_n))) fprintf(stderr, "---- saved:\n%s\n----\n", got);
    free(got);
    cfg_set("TOTK_VOLUME", "55");
    CHECK(cfg_reset(vol, 1) == 1 && cfg_get("TOTK_VOLUME") == NULL, "reset: a value set after a save resets too");
    cfg_set("TOTK_VOLUME", "60");
    CHECK(cfg_save_to(path) == 1 && EQ(cfg_get("TOTK_VOLUME"), "60"), "reset then set before the save: the set wins");
    got = plat_file_read(path, &got_n);
    CHECK(got && strstr((const char *)got, "\nvolume = 60\n"), "reset then set: the new line is written");
    free(got);

    // an active line with an empty value has no entry in memory; Reset still removes it from the file
    static const char rempty[] = "[audio]\n# volume = 100\nvolume =\n[input]\nmotion = 0\n";
    CHECK(plat_file_write(path, rempty, sizeof rempty - 1) && cfg_load(path) == 1 && cfg_get("TOTK_VOLUME") == NULL,
          "reset: load an ini with an empty value");
    CHECK(cfg_reset(vol, 1) == 0 && cfg_save_to(path) == 1, "reset: an empty-valued key saves");
    got = plat_file_read(path, &got_n);
    CHECK(got && got_n == sizeof rbase - 1 && !memcmp(got, rbase, got_n), "reset: the empty-valued line is gone");
    free(got);
    cfg_set("TOTK_VOLUME", "60");
    CHECK(cfg_save_to(path) == 1, "reset: volume 60 again for the environment case");

    // a key the environment sets is skipped and keeps its file line
    CHECK(cfg_load(path) == 1 && EQ(cfg_get("TOTK_VOLUME"), "60"), "reset: reload");
    plat_setenv("TOTK_VOLUME", "70");
    CHECK(cfg_reset(vol, 1) == 0, "reset: an environment-set key is skipped");
    plat_setenv("TOTK_VOLUME", NULL);
    CHECK(EQ(cfg_get("TOTK_VOLUME"), "60"), "reset: the skipped key keeps its value");
    CHECK(cfg_save_to(path) == 1, "reset: save after a skip");
    got = plat_file_read(path, &got_n);
    CHECK(got && strstr((const char *)got, "\nvolume = 60\n"), "reset: the skipped key keeps its file line");
    free(got);

    // a failed save: the call fails, cfg_last_save_ok says so, the value stays set and a later save works
    CHECK(cfg_last_save_ok() == 1, "save status: ok after a good save");
    cfg_set("TOTK_VOLUME", "20");
    char bad[1100];
    snprintf(bad, sizeof bad, "%s", path);
    strcpy(plat_last_sep(bad) + 1, "no-such-dir/cfg-probe.ini");
    CHECK(cfg_save_to(bad) == 0 && cfg_last_save_ok() == 0 && EQ(cfg_get("TOTK_VOLUME"), "20"),
          "save status: an unwritable path fails, the value stays");
    cfg_set("TOTK_VOLUME", "21");
    CHECK(plat_file_write(path, rbase, sizeof rbase - 1), "write the read-only ini");
    CHECK(plat_file_set_readonly(path, 1), "set the file read-only");
    CHECK(cfg_save_to(path) == 0 && cfg_last_save_ok() == 0 && EQ(cfg_get("TOTK_VOLUME"), "21"),
          "save status: a read-only file fails, cfg_get returns the new value");
    plat_file_set_readonly(path, 0);
    CHECK(cfg_save_to(path) == 1 && cfg_last_save_ok() == 1, "save status: the retry after the failure works");
    got = plat_file_read(path, &got_n);
    CHECK(got && strstr((const char *)got, "\nvolume = 21\n"), "save status: the retried save wrote the value");
    free(got);
    plat_file_delete(path);
    cfg_load(path);
    CHECK(rumble_motor(0, 0.6f, 1.3f) == 0 && rumble_motor(0.5f, 0.6f, 0) == 0, "rumble: zero amplitude or strength is silent");
    CHECK(rumble_motor(1, 0.6f, 3) == 65535 && rumble_motor(5, 1, 1) == 65535, "rumble: saturates at 65535");
    CHECK(rumble_motor(0.25f, 1, 1) > 16000 && rumble_motor(0.25f, 1, 1) < 16800, "rumble: curve 1, strength 100% is linear");
    CHECK(rumble_motor(0.1f, 0.6f, 1.3f) > rumble_motor(0.1f, 1, 1.3f), "rumble: curve lifts weak values");
    CHECK(rumble_motor(0.3f, 0.6f, 1.3f) > rumble_motor(0.3f, 0.6f, 1), "rumble: strength scales");
    // Keyboard and mouse bindings (input_map.c)
    uint8_t dn[KEY_COUNT] = {0};
    int32_t st[2];
    CHECK(input_map_buttons(dn) == 0, "keys: nothing held, no buttons");
    dn[KEY_MOUSE_L] = 1;
    CHECK(input_map_buttons(dn) == 1ull << B_Y, "keys: left mouse button is Y");
    dn[KEY_MOUSE_R] = dn[KEY_Z] = 1;
    CHECK(input_map_buttons(dn) == (1ull << B_Y | 1ull << B_ZL), "keys: right mouse button and Z both press ZL");
    memset(dn, 0, sizeof dn);
    dn[KEY_X] = dn[KEY_TAB] = dn[KEY_M] = dn[KEY_LCTRL] = dn[KEY_3] = 1;
    CHECK(input_map_buttons(dn) == (1ull << B_ZR | 1ull << B_PLUS | 1ull << B_MINUS | 1ull << B_STICK_L | 1ull << B_RIGHT),
          "keys: X ZR, Tab Plus, M Minus, Left Ctrl stick click, 3 D-pad right");
    memset(dn, 0, sizeof dn);
    dn[KEY_W] = 1;
    input_map_stick(dn, 0, st);
    CHECK(st[0] == 0 && st[1] == 32767, "keys: W is left stick up");
    dn[KEY_A] = 1;
    input_map_stick(dn, 0, st);
    CHECK(st[0] == -23170 && st[1] == 23170, "keys: W A is a diagonal on the unit circle");
    dn[KEY_W] = dn[KEY_A] = dn[KEY_S] = 1;
    dn[KEY_D] = 1;
    input_map_stick(dn, 0, st);
    CHECK(st[0] == 0 && st[1] == 0, "keys: opposite keys cancel");
    memset(dn, 0, sizeof dn);
    dn[KEY_LEFT] = 1;
    input_map_stick(dn, 1, st);
    CHECK(st[0] == -32767 && st[1] == 0, "keys: left arrow is right stick left");
    input_map_stick(dn, 0, st);
    CHECK(st[0] == 0 && st[1] == 0, "keys: arrows leave the left stick alone");
    input_mouse_stick(30, 0, 1.0 / 60, 1, st);
    CHECK(st[0] == 32767 * 1800 / 3000 && st[1] == 0, "mouse: 30 counts in 1/60 s is 60% right");
    input_mouse_stick(0, -10, 1.0 / 60, 1, st);
    CHECK(st[0] == 0 && st[1] > 0, "mouse: moving up is stick up");
    input_mouse_stick(30, 0, 1.0 / 30, 1, st);
    CHECK(st[0] == 32767 * 900 / 3000, "mouse: the same counts over twice the time are half the deflection");
    input_mouse_stick(15, 0, 1.0 / 60, 2, st);
    CHECK(st[0] == 32767 * 1800 / 3000, "mouse: doubling sensitivity halves the counts needed (15 counts at 2 = 30 at 1)");
    input_mouse_stick(1000, 1000, 1.0 / 60, 1, st);
    CHECK((int64_t)st[0] * st[0] + (int64_t)st[1] * st[1] <= 32768ll * 32768, "mouse: clamped to the unit circle");
    input_mouse_stick(30, 0, 1.0 / 60, 0, st);
    CHECK(st[0] == 0 && st[1] == 0, "mouse: sensitivity 0 is off");
    input_pad_stick(3000, -2000, 0.15f, st);
    CHECK(st[0] == 0 && st[1] == 0, "pad stick: an 11% drift inside a 15% dead zone reads centred");
    input_pad_stick(4000, -3000, 0, st);
    CHECK(st[0] == 4000 && st[1] == -3000, "pad stick: dead zone 0 passes the stick unchanged");
    input_pad_stick(32767, 0, 0.15f, st);
    CHECK(st[0] == 32767 && st[1] == 0, "pad stick: full deflection still reaches full");
    input_pad_stick(-32768, -32768, 0.15f, st);
    CHECK(st[0] < 0 && st[1] < 0 && st[0] >= -32767 && (int64_t)st[0] * st[0] + (int64_t)st[1] * st[1] <= 32768ll * 32768,
          "pad stick: a square gate's corner stays on the unit circle");
    input_pad_stick(0, 32767 / 2 + 1, 0.2f, st);
    CHECK(abs(st[1] - 32767 * 3 / 8) <= 3, "pad stick: half deflection past a 20% zone is (0.5 - 0.2) / 0.8 of full");
    // Gamepad layouts (input_map.c)
    CHECK(input_pad_layout_pick("auto", 1) == PAD_LAYOUT_NINTENDO && input_pad_layout_pick(NULL, 0) == PAD_LAYOUT_XBOX,
          "pad layout: automatic is Nintendo for an east button labelled A, Xbox otherwise");
    CHECK(input_pad_layout_pick("Xbox", 1) == PAD_LAYOUT_XBOX && input_pad_layout_pick("nintendo", 0) == PAD_LAYOUT_NINTENDO,
          "pad layout: a set layout wins over the labels");
    CHECK(input_pad_layout_pick("xbox_prompts", 0) == PAD_LAYOUT_NINTENDO &&
              input_pad_layout_pick("Xbox_Prompts", 1) == PAD_LAYOUT_NINTENDO,
          "pad layout: Xbox prompts keep the Nintendo positions (only the prompts change, romfs.c overlay_init)");
    uint8_t pd[PAD_COUNT] = {0};
    pd[PAD_SOUTH] = pd[PAD_NORTH] = 1;
    CHECK(input_map_pad_buttons(pd, PAD_LAYOUT_NINTENDO) == (1ull << B_B | 1ull << B_X) &&
          input_map_pad_buttons(pd, PAD_LAYOUT_XBOX) == (1ull << B_A | 1ull << B_Y),
          "pad layout: south and north are B and X by position, A and Y on Xbox");
    pd[PAD_SOUTH] = pd[PAD_NORTH] = 0;
    pd[PAD_START] = pd[PAD_ZR] = 1;
    CHECK(input_map_pad_buttons(pd, PAD_LAYOUT_XBOX) == (1ull << B_PLUS | 1ull << B_ZR), "pad layout: Xbox keeps the other buttons");
    CHECK(input_map_bind("A", "pad:west") && input_map_pad_buttons((uint8_t[PAD_COUNT]){[PAD_WEST] = 1}, PAD_LAYOUT_XBOX) ==
                                                 (1ull << B_A | 1ull << B_X),
          "pad layout: a bind line adds its physical button in every layout");
    CHECK(input_map_pad_buttons((uint8_t[PAD_COUNT]){[PAD_SOUTH] = 1}, PAD_LAYOUT_XBOX) == 0,
          "pad layout: a bind line replaces the layout's own button");
    input_map_reset();
    CHECK(input_map_pad_buttons((uint8_t[PAD_COUNT]){[PAD_RPADDLE1] = 1}, PAD_LAYOUT_XBOX) == 0,
          "pad layout: a back paddle is unbound by default");
    CHECK(input_map_bind("ZL", "pad:default, pad:rpaddle1") &&
              input_map_pad_buttons((uint8_t[PAD_COUNT]){[PAD_RPADDLE1] = 1}, PAD_LAYOUT_NINTENDO) == 1ull << B_ZL &&
              input_map_pad_buttons((uint8_t[PAD_COUNT]){[PAD_ZL] = 1}, PAD_LAYOUT_NINTENDO) == 1ull << B_ZL,
          "bind: pad:rpaddle1 adds a back paddle, pad:default keeps the trigger");
    input_map_reset();
    // Bind lines for stick directions and default parts; the remapping rows' edits (input_map.c)
    memset(dn, 0, sizeof dn);
    dn[KEY_I] = 1;
    CHECK(input_map_bind("LSTICK_UP", "key:i, pad:south") == 1, "bind: a stick direction takes keys, skips pad entries");
    input_map_stick(dn, 0, st);
    CHECK(st[1] == 32767, "bind: I moves forward after bind_LSTICK_UP = key:i");
    dn[KEY_I] = 0, dn[KEY_W] = 1;
    input_map_stick(dn, 0, st);
    CHECK(st[1] == 0, "bind: W no longer moves forward");
    CHECK(input_map_bind("A", "key:default, pad:north") == 1, "bind: key:default with a pad entry");
    memset(dn, 0, sizeof dn);
    dn[KEY_E] = 1;
    CHECK(input_map_buttons(dn) == 1ull << B_A &&
              input_map_pad_buttons((uint8_t[PAD_COUNT]){[PAD_NORTH] = 1}, PAD_LAYOUT_XBOX) == (1ull << B_A | 1ull << B_Y),
          "bind: key:default keeps E, pad:north adds the top button in every layout");
    CHECK(input_map_bind("B", "key:j, pad:default") == 1 &&
              input_map_pad_buttons((uint8_t[PAD_COUNT]){[PAD_EAST] = 1}, PAD_LAYOUT_XBOX) == 1ull << B_B &&
              input_map_pad_buttons((uint8_t[PAD_COUNT]){[PAD_SOUTH] = 1}, PAD_LAYOUT_NINTENDO) == 1ull << B_B,
          "bind: pad:default keeps each layout's own button");
    input_map_reset();
    InputMap mp = input_map;
    char line[256];
    input_map_line(&mp, B_ZR, line, sizeof line);
    CHECK(!line[0], "edit: an action at its defaults needs no line");
    CHECK(input_map_set_key(&mp, B_A, 0, KEY_F) == B_ZR, "edit: F taken from ZR");
    input_map_line(&mp, B_A, line, sizeof line);
    CHECK(!strcmp(line, "key:f, pad:default"), "edit: A's line is key:f, pad:default");
    input_map_line(&mp, B_ZR, line, sizeof line);
    CHECK(!strcmp(line, "key:x, pad:default"), "edit: ZR keeps X");
    CHECK(input_map_set_key(&mp, B_ZL, 1, KEY_NONE) == -1, "edit: clearing a key takes from no one");
    uint8_t ks[8];
    CHECK(input_map_keys_of(&mp, B_ZL, ks, 8) == 1 && ks[0] == KEY_MOUSE_R, "edit: ZL keeps its first key only");
    mp = input_map;
    CHECK(input_map_set_pad(&mp, B_X, PAD_LAYOUT_XBOX, PAD_SOUTH) == B_A, "edit: south swaps X with A (Xbox layout)");
    uint8_t ps[8];
    CHECK(input_map_pads_of(&mp, B_A, PAD_LAYOUT_XBOX, ps, 8) == 1 && ps[0] == PAD_WEST, "edit: A takes X's west button");
    CHECK(input_map_pads_of(&mp, B_A, PAD_LAYOUT_NINTENDO, ps, 8) == 1 && ps[0] == PAD_WEST &&
              input_map_pads_of(&mp, B_B, PAD_LAYOUT_NINTENDO, ps, 8) == 1 && ps[0] == PAD_EAST,
          "edit: the face buttons are pinned in every layout after a gamepad edit");
    input_map_line(&mp, B_X, line, sizeof line);
    CHECK(!strcmp(line, "key:default, pad:south"), "edit: X's line is key:default, pad:south");
    input_map_set_pad(&mp, B_X, PAD_LAYOUT_XBOX, PAD_WEST);   // and back
    input_map_line(&mp, B_A, line, sizeof line);
    CHECK(!line[0] && input_map_pads_of(&mp, B_A, PAD_LAYOUT_NINTENDO, ps, 8) == 1 && ps[0] == PAD_EAST,
          "edit: swapping back restores every layout's defaults");
    mp = input_map;
    input_map_set_key(&mp, B_SL_UP, 0, KEY_NONE);
    input_map_line(&mp, B_SL_UP, line, sizeof line);
    CHECK(!strcmp(line, "none"), "edit: a stick direction without keys is none");
    // defaults live in the CfgMeta table: cfg_value and the typed accessors fall back to it
    cfg_load("cfg-probe-missing.ini");
    plat_setenv("TOTK_FPS60", NULL);
    plat_setenv("TOTK_MOUSE_SENS", NULL);
    plat_setenv("TOTK_FREE_CORES", NULL);
    CHECK(cfg_bool("TOTK_FPS60") == 1, "default: unset FPS60 is on");
    CHECK(EQ(cfg_value("TOTK_VK_PRESENT"), "mailbox") && cfg_int("TOTK_SPLIT_DRAWS") == 64, "default: text and integer");
    plat_setenv("TOTK_MOUSE_SENS", "2.5");
    CHECK(cfg_double("TOTK_MOUSE_SENS") == 2.5, "double: the environment value");
    plat_setenv("TOTK_MOUSE_SENS", "fast");
    CHECK(cfg_double("TOTK_MOUSE_SENS") == 1.0, "double: a value that does not parse gives the default");
    plat_setenv("TOTK_MOUSE_SENS", NULL);
    cfg_set("TOTK_MOUSE_SENS", "3");
    CHECK(cfg_double("TOTK_MOUSE_SENS") == 3.0 && cfg_int("TOTK_MOUSE_SENS") == 3, "a cfg_set value beats the default");
    CHECK(cfg_bool("TOTK_FREE_CORES") == 0, "free_cores unset: off");
    plat_setenv("TOTK_FREE_CORES", "0");
    CHECK(cfg_bool("TOTK_FREE_CORES") == 0, "free_cores 0 gives the same as unset");
    plat_setenv("TOTK_FREE_CORES", "1");
    CHECK(cfg_bool("TOTK_FREE_CORES") == 1, "free_cores 1: on");
    plat_setenv("TOTK_FREE_CORES", NULL);
    cfg_load("cfg-probe-missing.ini");
    int listed = 0;
    for (int i = 0; cfg_meta_at(i); i++) {
        const CfgMeta *m = cfg_meta_at(i);
        if (!*m->def) continue;
        listed++;
        char name[96];
        snprintf(name, sizeof name, "TOTK_%s", m->key);
        plat_setenv(name, "");
        CHECK(EQ(cfg_value(name), m->def), "cfg_value returns the table default");
        int ok = 0;
        if (!m->values) ok = 1;
        else if (strstr(m->values, "..")) {
            long lo = strtol(m->values, NULL, 10), hi = strtol(strstr(m->values, "..") + 2, NULL, 10);
            double d = strtod(m->def, NULL);
            ok = d >= (double)lo && d <= (double)hi;
        } else {
            size_t dl = strlen(m->def);
            for (const char *v = m->values; *v;) {
                size_t n = strcspn(v, "|");
                ok |= n == dl && !strncmp(v, m->def, n);
                v += n + (v[n] == '|');
            }
        }
        if (!ok) fprintf(stderr, "FAIL cfg: default '%s' of %s is not one of its values '%s'\n", m->def, m->key, m->values), fails++;
    }
    CHECK(listed >= 30, "the defaults table was walked");
    printf("probe-cfg: %s\n", fails ? "FAIL" : "ok");
    return fails ? 1 : 0;
}
```

`runtime/cpu.h`:

```h
// Adapted from LAS Recomp runtime/cpu.h @ da35b83 (MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 Peiikai).
// Guest CPU state and helpers used by recompiled code.
#pragma once
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <string.h>

typedef struct __attribute__((aligned(16))) Cpu {
    uint64_t x[32];          // x0-x30 (x[31] unused; sp is separate)
    uint64_t sp;             // 256
    uint64_t pc;             // 264: target for indirect dispatch
    uint64_t nzcv;           // 272: flags in bits 31..28
    uint64_t tpidr;          // 280
    uint64_t tpidrro;        // 288
    uint64_t excl_addr;      // 296
    uint64_t excl_val;       // 304
    void *thread;            // 312: runtime thread object
    uint64_t fpcr;           // 320: guest FPCR/FPSR (portable FP/SIMD lowering only; the asm path uses the host's)
    uint64_t fpsr;           // 328
    uint64_t excl_val_hi;    // 336: upper half of a 128-bit exclusive pair (LDXP/LDAXP of two X registers)
    uint8_t _pad[512 - 344];
    __uint128_t v[32];       // 512
} Cpu;

_Static_assert(offsetof(Cpu, sp) == 256, "sp");
_Static_assert(offsetof(Cpu, pc) == 264, "pc");
_Static_assert(offsetof(Cpu, nzcv) == 272, "nzcv");
_Static_assert(offsetof(Cpu, fpcr) == 320, "fpcr");
_Static_assert(offsetof(Cpu, fpsr) == 328, "fpsr");
_Static_assert(offsetof(Cpu, v) == 512, "v");

typedef void (*GuestFn)(Cpu *);

// ---- runtime services (runtime/*.c)
void rt_dispatch(Cpu *c);                 // call function at c->pc
void rt_spin_gate(Cpu *c, uint64_t head);  // a pass of a spin wait loop (kernel.c, recomp/patches.py `spin`)
void rt_svc(Cpu *c, uint32_t imm, uint64_t pc);
void rt_brk(Cpu *c, uint32_t imm, uint64_t pc) __attribute__((noreturn));
void rt_udf(Cpu *c, uint64_t pc) __attribute__((noreturn));
uint64_t rt_ticks(void);
uint32_t rt_tick_hz(void);   // the guest counter rate: 19.2 MHz (Switch), 31.25 MHz (Switch 2)
uint64_t rt_ticks_to_ns(uint64_t ticks);
uint64_t rt_ns_to_ticks(uint64_t ns);

#if defined(__aarch64__)
static inline uint64_t rt_get_fpcr(void) { uint64_t v; __asm__ volatile("mrs %0, fpcr" : "=r"(v)); return v; }
static inline uint64_t rt_get_fpsr(void) { uint64_t v; __asm__ volatile("mrs %0, fpsr" : "=r"(v)); return v; }
static inline void rt_set_fpcr(uint64_t v) { __asm__ volatile("msr fpcr, %0" :: "r"(v)); }
static inline void rt_set_fpsr(uint64_t v) { __asm__ volatile("msr fpsr, %0" :: "r"(v)); }
static inline void rt_fpcr_sync(const Cpu *c) { (void)c; }
#else
// Host FP state is not the guest's here: code lifted with --simd=c keeps FPCR/FPSR in Cpu (c->fpcr, zeroed
// with the Cpu), so the host-side reset in thread start-up has nothing to do.
static inline uint64_t rt_get_fpcr(void) { return 0; }
static inline uint64_t rt_get_fpsr(void) { return 0; }
static inline void rt_set_fpcr(uint64_t v) { (void)v; }
static inline void rt_set_fpsr(uint64_t v) { (void)v; }
// The MXCSR of a host thread running guest code mirrors c->fpcr: FTZ|DAZ = FPCR.FZ, RC = nearest (FPCR.RMode takes
// the slow paths of runtime/simd.h, which switch RC around one operation). The FP helpers rely on it without checking,
// so it is set wherever FPCR or the host FP context changes: MSR FPCR (recomp/lifter.py), rt_call (thread and fiber
// entry, host code calling guest code), fiber resume (runtime/kernel.c fiber_resumed; fibers keep their own MXCSR).
static inline void rt_fpcr_sync(const Cpu *c) {
    unsigned cur = __builtin_ia32_stmxcsr();
    unsigned want = (cur & ~0xE040u) | (c->fpcr & (1u << 24) ? 0x8040u : 0);   // FTZ 0x8000, DAZ 0x40, RC 0x6000
    if (cur != want) __builtin_ia32_ldmxcsr(want);
}
#endif

// ---- memory: guest addresses are host addresses
typedef uint16_t __attribute__((aligned(1), may_alias)) u16u;
typedef uint32_t __attribute__((aligned(1), may_alias)) u32u;
typedef uint64_t __attribute__((aligned(1), may_alias)) u64u;
typedef uint8_t __attribute__((may_alias)) u8a;

// Function-entry profiler (runtime/fnprof.c, LARECOMP_FNPROF): one predictable branch per call when off.
extern volatile int g_fnprof;
void fnprof_hit(uint64_t addr, uint64_t lr, uint64_t x0);
#define FN_ENTER(a) do { if (__builtin_expect(g_fnprof, 0)) fnprof_hit(a, c->x[30], c->x[0]); } while (0)

#define LD8(a)  (*(const volatile u8a *)(uintptr_t)(a))
#define LD16(a) (*(const volatile u16u *)(uintptr_t)(a))
#define LD32(a) (*(const volatile u32u *)(uintptr_t)(a))
#define LD64(a) (*(const volatile u64u *)(uintptr_t)(a))
#define ST8(a, v)  (*(volatile u8a *)(uintptr_t)(a) = (uint8_t)(v))
#define ST16(a, v) (*(volatile u16u *)(uintptr_t)(a) = (uint16_t)(v))
#define ST32(a, v) (*(volatile u32u *)(uintptr_t)(a) = (uint32_t)(v))
#define ST64(a, v) (*(volatile u64u *)(uintptr_t)(a) = (uint64_t)(v))

// ---- exclusive monitor (emulated with compare-and-swap)
#define EXCL(N, T)                                                                         \
    static inline uint64_t ldx##N(Cpu *c, uint64_t a) {                                    \
        T v = __atomic_load_n((T *)(uintptr_t)a, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);                        \
        c->excl_addr = a;                                                                  \
        c->excl_val = v;                                                                   \
        return v;                                                                          \
    }                                                                                      \
    static inline uint32_t stx##N(Cpu *c, uint64_t a, uint64_t v) {                        \
        if (c->excl_addr != a) return 1;                                                   \
        c->excl_addr = ~0ull;                                                              \
        T expected = (T)c->excl_val;                                                       \
        return !__atomic_compare_exchange_n((T *)(uintptr_t)a, &expected, (T)v, 0,         \
                                            __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST, __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST);           \
    }                                                                                      \
    static inline uint64_t lda##N(uint64_t a) {                                            \
        return __atomic_load_n((T *)(uintptr_t)a, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);                       \
    }                                                                                      \
    static inline void stl##N(uint64_t a, uint64_t v) {                                    \
        __atomic_store_n((T *)(uintptr_t)a, (T)v, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);                       \
    }
EXCL(8, uint8_t)
EXCL(16, uint16_t)
EXCL(32, uint32_t)
EXCL(64, uint64_t)

// Exclusive pair of two X registers: one 16-byte-aligned 128-bit access (cmpxchg16b; x86-64-v3 has CX16).
// A pair of two W registers is a 64-bit exclusive and uses ldx64/stx64.
static inline __uint128_t ldxp128(Cpu *c, uint64_t a) {
    __uint128_t v = __atomic_load_n((__uint128_t *)(uintptr_t)a, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
    c->excl_addr = a;
    c->excl_val = (uint64_t)v;
    c->excl_val_hi = (uint64_t)(v >> 64);
    return v;
}
static inline uint32_t stxp128(Cpu *c, uint64_t a, uint64_t lo, uint64_t hi) {
    if (c->excl_addr != a) return 1;
    c->excl_addr = ~0ull;
    __uint128_t expected = ((__uint128_t)c->excl_val_hi << 64) | c->excl_val;
    __uint128_t v = ((__uint128_t)hi << 64) | lo;
    return !__atomic_compare_exchange_n((__uint128_t *)(uintptr_t)a, &expected, v, 0, __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST,
                                        __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST);
}

// ---- LSE atomics (ARMv8.1; the A57 lacks them, the SDK carries them behind a CPU feature check).
// Add, clear, xor, set and swap map to __atomic builtins in the lifter; min/max need a CAS loop. Return the old value.
#define ATOMIC_MINMAX(N, T, S)                                                             \
    static inline T atomic_smax##N(uint64_t a, T v) {                                      \
        T o = __atomic_load_n((T *)(uintptr_t)a, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);                        \
        while (!__atomic_compare_exchange_n((T *)(uintptr_t)a, &o, (S)o > (S)v ? o : v, 1, \
                                            __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST, __ATOMIC_RELAXED)) {}        \
        return o;                                                                          \
    }                                                                                      \
    static inline T atomic_smin##N(uint64_t a, T v) {                                      \
        T o = __atomic_load_n((T *)(uintptr_t)a, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);                        \
        while (!__atomic_compare_exchange_n((T *)(uintptr_t)a, &o, (S)o < (S)v ? o : v, 1, \
                                            __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST, __ATOMIC_RELAXED)) {}        \
        return o;                                                                          \
    }                                                                                      \
    static inline T atomic_umax##N(uint64_t a, T v) {                                      \
        T o = __atomic_load_n((T *)(uintptr_t)a, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);                        \
        while (!__atomic_compare_exchange_n((T *)(uintptr_t)a, &o, o > v ? o : v, 1,       \
                                            __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST, __ATOMIC_RELAXED)) {}        \
        return o;                                                                          \
    }                                                                                      \
    static inline T atomic_umin##N(uint64_t a, T v) {                                      \
        T o = __atomic_load_n((T *)(uintptr_t)a, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);                        \
        while (!__atomic_compare_exchange_n((T *)(uintptr_t)a, &o, o < v ? o : v, 1,       \
                                            __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST, __ATOMIC_RELAXED)) {}        \
        return o;                                                                          \
    }
ATOMIC_MINMAX(8, uint8_t, int8_t)
ATOMIC_MINMAX(16, uint16_t, int16_t)
ATOMIC_MINMAX(32, uint32_t, int32_t)
ATOMIC_MINMAX(64, uint64_t, int64_t)

// ---- flags (packed NZCV in bits 31..28)
#define FLAG_N(c) (((c)->nzcv >> 31) & 1)
#define FLAG_Z(c) (((c)->nzcv >> 30) & 1)
#define FLAG_C(c) (((c)->nzcv >> 29) & 1)
#define FLAG_V(c) (((c)->nzcv >> 28) & 1)
#define COND_EQ(c) (FLAG_Z(c))
#define COND_NE(c) (!FLAG_Z(c))
#define COND_CS(c) (FLAG_C(c))
#define COND_CC(c) (!FLAG_C(c))
#define COND_MI(c) (FLAG_N(c))
#define COND_PL(c) (!FLAG_N(c))
#define COND_VS(c) (FLAG_V(c))
#define COND_VC(c) (!FLAG_V(c))
#define COND_HI(c) (FLAG_C(c) && !FLAG_Z(c))
#define COND_LS(c) (!(FLAG_C(c) && !FLAG_Z(c)))
#define COND_GE(c) (FLAG_N(c) == FLAG_V(c))
#define COND_LT(c) (FLAG_N(c) != FLAG_V(c))
#define COND_GT(c) (!FLAG_Z(c) && FLAG_N(c) == FLAG_V(c))
#define COND_LE(c) (!(!FLAG_Z(c) && FLAG_N(c) == FLAG_V(c)))

#define MKFLAGS(n, z, cy, v) \
    (((uint64_t)(n) << 31) | ((uint64_t)(z) << 30) | ((uint64_t)(cy) << 29) | ((uint64_t)(v) << 28))

static inline uint64_t adds64(Cpu *c, uint64_t a, uint64_t b) {
    uint64_t r = a + b;
    c->nzcv = MKFLAGS(r >> 63, r == 0, r < a, ((a ^ r) & (b ^ r)) >> 63);
    return r;
}
static inline uint64_t subs64(Cpu *c, uint64_t a, uint64_t b) {
    uint64_t r = a - b;
    c->nzcv = MKFLAGS(r >> 63, r == 0, a >= b, ((a ^ b) & (a ^ r)) >> 63);
    return r;
}
static inline uint32_t adds32(Cpu *c, uint32_t a, uint32_t b) {
    uint32_t r = a + b;
    c->nzcv = MKFLAGS(r >> 31, r == 0, r < a, ((a ^ r) & (b ^ r)) >> 31);
    return r;
}
static inline uint32_t subs32(Cpu *c, uint32_t a, uint32_t b) {
    uint32_t r = a - b;
    c->nzcv = MKFLAGS(r >> 31, r == 0, a >= b, ((a ^ b) & (a ^ r)) >> 31);
    return r;
}
static inline uint64_t logic64(Cpu *c, uint64_t r) { c->nzcv = MKFLAGS(r >> 63, r == 0, 0, 0); return r; }
static inline uint32_t logic32(Cpu *c, uint32_t r) { c->nzcv = MKFLAGS(r >> 31, r == 0, 0, 0); return r; }

#define ADC_IMPL(N, S)                                                                     \
    static inline uint##N##_t adc##N(Cpu *c, uint##N##_t a, uint##N##_t b) {               \
        return a + b + (uint##N##_t)FLAG_C(c);                                             \
    }                                                                                      \
    static inline uint##N##_t sbc##N(Cpu *c, uint##N##_t a, uint##N##_t b) {               \
        return a - b - 1 + (uint##N##_t)FLAG_C(c);                                         \
    }                                                                                      \
    static inline uint##N##_t adcs##N(Cpu *c, uint##N##_t a, uint##N##_t b) {              \
        uint##N##_t cin = FLAG_C(c), r = a + b + cin;                                      \
        int carry = cin ? r <= a : r < a;                                                  \
        c->nzcv = MKFLAGS(r >> (N - 1), r == 0, carry, ((a ^ r) & (b ^ r)) >> (N - 1));    \
        return r;                                                                          \
    }                                                                                      \
    static inline uint##N##_t sbcs##N(Cpu *c, uint##N##_t a, uint##N##_t b) {              \
        return adcs##N(c, a, (uint##N##_t)~b);                                             \
    }
ADC_IMPL(64, )
ADC_IMPL(32, )

// ---- function-local flags (recomp/flags.py)
// Generated functions keep NZCV in a local Flags F, never in c->nzcv. A definition of a known kind stores its
// operands (a - b, a + b, or a logic result in a); fc_<kind>(&F, CC_xx) computes a condition from them, so a compare
// and its branch become one host compare. F.nz holds the packed form for definitions only known packed (CCMP, FCMP,
// MSR, ADCS) and for readers that several kinds of definition reach. Every helper is always inlined with a constant
// condition, so F stays in registers and only the condition's own arithmetic remains.
typedef struct { uint64_t a, b, nz; } Flags;
enum { CC_EQ, CC_NE, CC_CS, CC_CC, CC_MI, CC_PL, CC_VS, CC_VC, CC_HI, CC_LS, CC_GE, CC_LT, CC_GT, CC_LE };
#define CPU_FL static inline __attribute__((always_inline))

CPU_FL int fl_cond(int cc, int n, int z, int cy, int v) {
    switch (cc) {
    case CC_EQ: return z;
    case CC_NE: return !z;
    case CC_CS: return cy;
    case CC_CC: return !cy;
    case CC_MI: return n;
    case CC_PL: return !n;
    case CC_VS: return v;
    case CC_VC: return !v;
    case CC_HI: return cy && !z;
    case CC_LS: return !cy || z;
    case CC_GE: return n == v;
    case CC_LT: return n != v;
    case CC_GT: return !z && n == v;
    default: return z || n != v;
    }
}

// Subtract (SUBS, CMP): conditions as host compares of the operands.
#define FL_SUB(N, U, S)                                                                    \
    CPU_FL U fsub##N(Flags *f, U a, U b) { f->a = a; f->b = b; return (U)(a - b); }            \
    CPU_FL int fc_sub##N(const Flags *f, int cc) {                                             \
        U a = (U)f->a, b = (U)f->b, r = (U)(a - b);                                        \
        switch (cc) {                                                                      \
        case CC_EQ: return a == b;                                                         \
        case CC_NE: return a != b;                                                         \
        case CC_CS: return a >= b;                                                         \
        case CC_CC: return a < b;                                                          \
        case CC_MI: return (S)r < 0;                                                       \
        case CC_PL: return (S)r >= 0;                                                      \
        case CC_VS: return (S)((a ^ b) & (a ^ r)) < 0;                                     \
        case CC_VC: return (S)((a ^ b) & (a ^ r)) >= 0;                                    \
        case CC_HI: return a > b;                                                          \
        case CC_LS: return a <= b;                                                         \
        case CC_GE: return (S)a >= (S)b;                                                   \
        case CC_LT: return (S)a < (S)b;                                                    \
        case CC_GT: return (S)a > (S)b;                                                    \
        default: return (S)a <= (S)b;                                                      \
        }                                                                                  \
    }                                                                                      \
    CPU_FL uint64_t nz_sub##N(U a, U b) {                                                      \
        U r = (U)(a - b);                                                                  \
        return MKFLAGS((S)r < 0, r == 0, a >= b, (S)((a ^ b) & (a ^ r)) < 0);              \
    }                                                                                      \
    CPU_FL uint64_t fnz_sub##N(const Flags *f) { return nz_sub##N((U)f->a, (U)f->b); }
FL_SUB(64, uint64_t, int64_t)
FL_SUB(32, uint32_t, int32_t)

// Add (ADDS, CMN) and logic results (ANDS, TST, BICS): conditions from N, Z, C, V.
#define FL_ADD(N, U, S)                                                                    \
    CPU_FL U fadd##N(Flags *f, U a, U b) { f->a = a; f->b = b; return (U)(a + b); }            \
    CPU_FL uint64_t nz_add##N(U a, U b) {                                                      \
        U r = (U)(a + b);                                                                  \
        return MKFLAGS((S)r < 0, r == 0, r < a, (S)((a ^ r) & (b ^ r)) < 0);               \
    }                                                                                      \
    CPU_FL int fc_add##N(const Flags *f, int cc) {                                             \
        U a = (U)f->a, b = (U)f->b, r = (U)(a + b);                                        \
        return fl_cond(cc, (S)r < 0, r == 0, r < a, (S)((a ^ r) & (b ^ r)) < 0);           \
    }                                                                                      \
    CPU_FL uint64_t fnz_add##N(const Flags *f) { return nz_add##N((U)f->a, (U)f->b); }         \
    CPU_FL U flogic##N(Flags *f, U r) { f->a = r; return r; }                                  \
    CPU_FL int fc_logic##N(const Flags *f, int cc) {                                           \
        U r = (U)f->a;                                                                     \
        return fl_cond(cc, (S)r < 0, r == 0, 0, 0);                                        \
    }                                                                                      \
    CPU_FL uint64_t fnz_logic##N(const Flags *f) { return MKFLAGS((S)f->a < 0, (U)f->a == 0, 0, 0); }
FL_ADD(64, uint64_t, int64_t)
FL_ADD(32, uint32_t, int32_t)

// Packed flags.
CPU_FL int fc_nz(const Flags *f, int cc) {
    return fl_cond(cc, f->nz >> 31 & 1, f->nz >> 30 & 1, f->nz >> 29 & 1, f->nz >> 28 & 1);
}
CPU_FL uint64_t fnz_nz(const Flags *f) { return f->nz; }

// ADC, SBC, ADCS, SBCS with the carry in from F.
#define FL_ADC(N, U)                                                                       \
    CPU_FL U adc##N##f(int cin, U a, U b) { return (U)(a + b + (U)cin); }                      \
    CPU_FL U sbc##N##f(int cin, U a, U b) { return (U)(a - b - 1 + (U)cin); }                  \
    CPU_FL U adcs##N##f(Flags *f, int cin, U a, U b) {                                         \
        U r = (U)(a + b + (U)cin);                                                         \
        int carry = cin ? r <= a : r < a;                                                  \
        f->nz = MKFLAGS(r >> (N - 1), r == 0, carry, ((a ^ r) & (b ^ r)) >> (N - 1));      \
        return r;                                                                          \
    }                                                                                      \
    CPU_FL U sbcs##N##f(Flags *f, int cin, U a, U b) { return adcs##N##f(f, cin, a, (U)~b); }
FL_ADC(64, uint64_t)
FL_ADC(32, uint32_t)
#undef CPU_FL

// ---- bit ops
#define ROR64(v, r) ((uint64_t)(v) >> ((r) & 63) | (uint64_t)(v) << ((64 - ((r) & 63)) & 63))
#define ROR32(v, r) ((uint32_t)(v) >> ((r) & 31) | (uint32_t)(v) << ((32 - ((r) & 31)) & 31))
static inline uint64_t clz64(uint64_t v) { return v ? __builtin_clzll(v) : 64; }
static inline uint32_t clz32(uint32_t v) { return v ? __builtin_clz(v) : 32; }
static inline uint64_t cls64(uint64_t v) { return clz64(v ^ (uint64_t)((int64_t)v >> 1)) - 1; }
static inline uint32_t cls32(uint32_t v) { return clz32(v ^ (uint32_t)((int32_t)v >> 1)) - 1; }
static inline uint64_t rbit64(uint64_t v) { return __builtin_bitreverse64(v); }
static inline uint32_t rbit32(uint32_t v) { return __builtin_bitreverse32(v); }
static inline uint32_t rev16_32(uint32_t v) { return ((v & 0x00ff00ffu) << 8) | ((v >> 8) & 0x00ff00ffu); }
static inline uint64_t rev16_64(uint64_t v) {
    return ((v & 0x00ff00ff00ff00ffull) << 8) | ((v >> 8) & 0x00ff00ff00ff00ffull);
}
static inline uint64_t rev32_64(uint64_t v) {
    return ((uint64_t)__builtin_bswap32((uint32_t)v)) | ((uint64_t)__builtin_bswap32((uint32_t)(v >> 32)) << 32);
}
static inline uint64_t udiv64(uint64_t a, uint64_t b) { return b ? a / b : 0; }
static inline uint32_t udiv32(uint32_t a, uint32_t b) { return b ? a / b : 0; }
static inline uint64_t sdiv64(uint64_t a, uint64_t b) {
    if (!b) return 0;
    if ((int64_t)a == INT64_MIN && (int64_t)b == -1) return a;
    return (uint64_t)((int64_t)a / (int64_t)b);
}
static inline uint32_t sdiv32(uint32_t a, uint32_t b) {
    if (!b) return 0;
    if ((int32_t)a == INT32_MIN && (int32_t)b == -1) return a;
    return (uint32_t)((int32_t)a / (int32_t)b);
}

// Portable FP/SIMD helpers for code lifted with --simd=c (default off AArch64; gen.py includes simd.h itself
// in that mode, so AArch64 hosts can build it too).
#if !defined(__cplusplus) && !defined(__aarch64__)
#include "simd.h"
#endif
```

`runtime/dispatch.c`:

```c
// Indirect-branch dispatch: guest address -> lifted function, O(1).
//
// Layout of the table: one uint32_t slot per 4-byte guest instruction over [lo, hi), where lo is the lowest function
// start of any module and hi is past the highest. A slot is 0 when no function starts there, else the host function's
// address minus `anchor` (an address just below the lowest host function), so 4 bytes are enough as long as all lifted
// code lies within 4 GiB, which a single PE image guarantees. Memory: 4 bytes per 4 guest bytes, i.e. the size of the
// guest range covered. The gaps between code ranges (rodata, data, bss, alignment) are reserved but never written, so
// the OS never backs them with RAM; resident memory is about the total .text size of the modules.
//
// The table is filled once by rt_dispatch_init and then made read-only, so any number of threads read it without
// locks or per-thread caches. Host (HLE) functions at addresses outside the modules live in a small hash table that
// is also fixed at init; they are looked up only after the flat table misses.
#include "dispatch.h"
#include "host.h"
#include "platform/platform.h"

#include <stdarg.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>


#define TABLE_SPAN_LIMIT (1ull << 30)   // guest bytes covered by the table, and its size in bytes
#define HOST_CAP 8192                   // host function registry, power of two
#define MAX_MODULES 16

// Hot data read by every rt_dispatch: one cache line.
static struct __attribute__((aligned(64))) {
    const uint32_t *slot;
    uintptr_t anchor;
    uint64_t lo;
    uint64_t slots;
} D;

static const RtModule *g_mods[MAX_MODULES];   // sorted by base
static int g_nmods;
static bool g_ready;
static uint64_t g_table_bytes, g_functions;

static struct { uint64_t addr; GuestFn fn; } g_host[HOST_CAP];
static uint64_t g_nhost;

void rt_fatal(const char *fmt, ...) {
    va_list ap;
    va_start(ap, fmt);
    rt_log_raw("FATAL: ", 7);
    rt_vlogf(fmt, ap);
    rt_log_raw("\n", 1);
    va_end(ap);
    // A failed allocation (malloc, realloc, VirtualAlloc) means the commit limit was reached: this line tells a leak of
    // ours (process private bytes near the limit) from a machine short of page file.
    double proc, used, limit;
    plat_commit_info(&proc, &used, &limit);
    rt_log("fatal: memory commit: this process %.0f MB, the system %.0f of %.0f MB", proc, used, limit);
    fflush(stdout);
    fflush(stderr);
    _Exit(70);
}

static const RtModule *module_at(uint64_t pc) {
    for (int i = 0; i < g_nmods; i++)
        if (pc - g_mods[i]->base < g_mods[i]->size) return g_mods[i];
    return NULL;
}

const char *rt_guest_name(uint64_t pc, char *buf, int size) {
    const RtModule *m = module_at(pc);
    if (m) snprintf(buf, size, "%#llx (%s+%#llx)", (unsigned long long)pc, m->name, (unsigned long long)(pc - m->base));
    else snprintf(buf, size, "%#llx", (unsigned long long)pc);
    return buf;
}

static uint64_t host_hash(uint64_t addr) { return (addr >> 2) * 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15ull >> 51; }   // 13 bits

static GuestFn host_lookup(uint64_t addr) {
    for (uint64_t h = host_hash(addr), n = 0; n < HOST_CAP; h = (h + 1) & (HOST_CAP - 1), n++) {
        if (g_host[h].addr == addr) return g_host[h].fn;
        if (!g_host[h].addr) return NULL;
    }
    return NULL;
}

void rt_register_host(uint64_t addr, GuestFn fn) {
    if (g_ready) rt_fatal("rt_register_host(%#llx) after rt_dispatch_init", (unsigned long long)addr);
    if (!addr || (addr & 3) || !fn) rt_fatal("rt_register_host: bad entry %#llx", (unsigned long long)addr);
    if (g_nhost >= HOST_CAP / 2) rt_fatal("rt_register_host: more than %d host functions", HOST_CAP / 2);
    uint64_t h = host_hash(addr);
    while (g_host[h].addr && g_host[h].addr != addr) h = (h + 1) & (HOST_CAP - 1);
    if (g_host[h].addr) rt_fatal("rt_register_host: %#llx registered twice", (unsigned long long)addr);
    g_host[h].addr = addr;
    g_host[h].fn = fn;
    g_nhost++;
}

static void *table_alloc(uint64_t bytes) {
    return plat_mem_alloc(bytes);   // zero pages, backed on first write
}

static void table_seal(void *p, uint64_t bytes) {
    if (!plat_mem_protect((uint64_t)(uintptr_t)p, bytes, PLAT_PROT_READ)) rt_fatal("dispatch: sealing the table failed");
}

void rt_dispatch_init(const RtModule *mods, int count) {
    if (g_ready) rt_fatal("rt_dispatch_init called twice");
    if (count <= 0 || count > MAX_MODULES) rt_fatal("rt_dispatch_init: %d modules", count);

    // Modules by base, checked for overlap.
    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        int j = g_nmods++;
        while (j > 0 && g_mods[j - 1]->base > mods[i].base) { g_mods[j] = g_mods[j - 1]; j--; }
        g_mods[j] = &mods[i];
    }
    for (int i = 1; i < g_nmods; i++)
        if (g_mods[i - 1]->base + g_mods[i - 1]->size > g_mods[i]->base)
            rt_fatal("dispatch: modules %s and %s overlap", g_mods[i - 1]->name, g_mods[i]->name);

    // Function tables: sorted, aligned, inside their module. Range of guest starts and of host functions.
    uint64_t lo = UINT64_MAX, hi = 0;
    uintptr_t host_lo = UINTPTR_MAX, host_hi = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < g_nmods; i++) {
        const RtModule *m = g_mods[i];
        for (uint64_t k = 0; k < m->count; k++) {
            uint64_t a = m->addrs[k];
            uintptr_t f = (uintptr_t)m->fns[k];
            if ((a & 3) || a - m->base >= m->size)
                rt_fatal("dispatch: %s_fn_addrs[%llu] = %#llx is misaligned or outside the module", m->name,
                         (unsigned long long)k, (unsigned long long)a);
            if (k && a <= m->addrs[k - 1])
                rt_fatal("dispatch: %s_fn_addrs is not strictly ascending at [%llu] = %#llx", m->name,
                         (unsigned long long)k, (unsigned long long)a);
            if (!f) rt_fatal("dispatch: %s_fn_ptrs[%llu] is NULL", m->name, (unsigned long long)k);
            if (f < host_lo) host_lo = f;
            if (f > host_hi) host_hi = f;
        }
        if (m->count) {
            if (m->addrs[0] < lo) lo = m->addrs[0];
            if (m->addrs[m->count - 1] + 4 > hi) hi = m->addrs[m->count - 1] + 4;
        }
    }
    if (hi <= lo) rt_fatal("dispatch: no functions in any module");
    if (hi - lo > TABLE_SPAN_LIMIT)
        rt_fatal("dispatch: modules span %#llx guest bytes, over the %#llx the flat table allows",
                 (unsigned long long)(hi - lo), TABLE_SPAN_LIMIT);
    uintptr_t anchor = (host_lo & ~(uintptr_t)15) - 16;
    if (host_hi - anchor > UINT32_MAX)
        rt_fatal("dispatch: lifted code spans %#llx host bytes; slots hold 32-bit offsets (4 GiB)",
                 (unsigned long long)(host_hi - anchor));

    for (uint64_t h = 0; h < HOST_CAP; h++)
        if (g_host[h].addr && module_at(g_host[h].addr))
            rt_fatal("dispatch: host function at %#llx lies inside module %s", (unsigned long long)g_host[h].addr,
                     module_at(g_host[h].addr)->name);

    uint64_t slots = (hi - lo) >> 2, bytes = (slots * 4 + 0xFFFF) & ~0xFFFFull;
    uint32_t *slot = table_alloc(bytes);
    if (!slot) rt_fatal("dispatch: cannot allocate a %llu-byte table", (unsigned long long)bytes);
    for (int i = 0; i < g_nmods; i++) {
        const RtModule *m = g_mods[i];
        for (uint64_t k = 0; k < m->count; k++)
            slot[(m->addrs[k] - lo) >> 2] = (uint32_t)((uintptr_t)m->fns[k] - anchor);
        g_functions += m->count;
    }
    table_seal(slot, bytes);

    g_table_bytes = bytes;
    D.slot = slot;
    D.anchor = anchor;
    D.lo = lo;
    D.slots = slots;
    __atomic_store_n(&g_ready, true, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
}

GuestFn rt_dispatch_lookup(uint64_t pc) {
    uint64_t i = __builtin_rotateright64(pc - D.lo, 2);   // a misaligned pc lands far above D.slots
    if (i < D.slots && D.slot[i]) return (GuestFn)(D.anchor + D.slot[i]);
    return g_ready ? host_lookup(pc) : NULL;
}

__attribute__((noinline, noreturn, cold)) static void dispatch_fail(Cpu *c) {
    char at[64], lr[64];
    uint64_t pc = c->pc;
    if (!g_ready) rt_fatal("rt_dispatch to %#llx before rt_dispatch_init", (unsigned long long)pc);
    const char *why = (pc & 3) ? "misaligned address"
                    : module_at(pc) ? "not a function start"
                    : "outside every module, no host function registered";
    rt_fatal("rt_dispatch: no function at guest pc %s: %s (lr %s)", rt_guest_name(pc, at, sizeof at), why,
             rt_guest_name(c->x[30], lr, sizeof lr));
}

// Host functions, and the fatal error. A separate tail call keeps the fast path below free of a stack frame.
__attribute__((noinline)) static void dispatch_slow(Cpu *c) {
    // Poison pcs: null / near-null / float-bit-pattern / truncated low-4GiB / misaligned, or a
    // guest heap pointer used as code. Cap heap skips so a tight corrupt loop cannot spin forever
    // (n22: 1M skips, black title). n35: pc 0xbf800101 (IEEE float as code) is misaligned low-4GiB.
    // n178: 0x100000001 sat just above the 4GiB floor and was misaligned — soft-skip before budgets.
    if (!c->pc || c->pc < 0x100000000ull || (c->pc & 3)) {
        static int logged;
        if (logged++ < 16)
            rt_log("rt_dispatch: bad pc %#llx skipped (lr %#llx)", (unsigned long long)c->pc,
                   (unsigned long long)c->x[30]);
        return;
    }
    // Guest heap and other non-code high addresses used as pc (n119: 0x9c41de45f3 past the
    // old 0x70_0000_0000 ceiling). Soft-skip anything below the NSO/module window.
    if (c->pc >= 0x100000000ull && c->pc < 0x7000000000ull) {
        static int heap_skips;
        // Overnight: n173 exhausted 256 and then wild_skips → FATAL at 0x2573e35f8 mid-title.
        if (heap_skips < 8192) {
            if (heap_skips < 16)
                rt_log("rt_dispatch: heap pc %#llx skipped (lr %#llx)", (unsigned long long)c->pc,
                       (unsigned long long)c->x[30]);
            heap_skips++;
            return;
        }
        // fall through to dispatch_fail after the budget
    }
    GuestFn f = g_ready ? host_lookup(c->pc) : NULL;
    if (!f) {
        // n31: pc landed on a vtable/data address inside main (0x700363a2e0, "not a function start").
        // Skip a budget of those overnight; past the budget still FATAL.
        if (module_at(c->pc)) {
            static int data_skips;
            if (data_skips < 2048) {
                if (data_skips < 16)
                    rt_log("rt_dispatch: data pc %#llx skipped (lr %#llx)", (unsigned long long)c->pc,
                           (unsigned long long)c->x[30]);
                data_skips++;
                return;
            }
        }
        // Outside every module (n119 float/garbage pc 0x9c41de45f3): soft-skip a budget so
        // overnight keeps producing title shots instead of FATAL aborting the series.
        static int wild_skips;
        if (wild_skips < 2048) {
            if (wild_skips < 16)
                rt_log("rt_dispatch: wild pc %#llx skipped (lr %#llx)", (unsigned long long)c->pc,
                       (unsigned long long)c->x[30]);
            wild_skips++;
            return;
        }
        dispatch_fail(c);
    }
    __attribute__((musttail)) return f(c);
}

// A pending preempt request at an indirect call (a safe point: the guest state is all in Cpu). Out of line, so
// rt_dispatch keeps no stack frame.
static __attribute__((noinline)) void dispatch_preempt(Cpu *c) {
    kern_checkpoint();
    __attribute__((musttail)) return rt_dispatch(c);
}

// Jump to the guest address in c->pc. Always a tail call, so chains of indirect jumps keep the host stack flat. A
// pending preempt request costs two loads and a branch to check.
void rt_dispatch(Cpu *c) {
    if (__builtin_expect(c->thread && kern_preempt_pending(c->thread), 0))
        __attribute__((musttail)) return dispatch_preempt(c);
    uint64_t i = __builtin_rotateright64(c->pc - D.lo, 2);
    uint32_t off = i < D.slots ? D.slot[i] : 0;
    if (__builtin_expect(!off, 0)) __attribute__((musttail)) return dispatch_slow(c);
    GuestFn f = (GuestFn)(D.anchor + off);
    __attribute__((musttail)) return f(c);
}

RtDispatchStats rt_dispatch_stats(void) {
    return (RtDispatchStats){D.lo, D.lo + D.slots * 4, D.slots, g_table_bytes, g_functions, g_nhost};
}

```

`runtime/dispatch.h`:

```h
// Guest address -> host function lookup for indirect branches (rt_dispatch, declared in cpu.h).
//
// One flat table covers every module's code range: slot (pc - lo) >> 2 holds the host function for a guest
// function start, as a 32-bit offset from an anchor address. Lookup is one range check and one load. The table is
// built once by rt_dispatch_init and never written again, so threads read it without locks.
#pragma once
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdint.h>

#include "cpu.h"

// A lifted module: its place in the guest layout and the generator's sorted function table.
typedef struct RtModule {
    const char *name;
    uint64_t base, size;      // guest image (layout.h MOD_<NAME>_BASE / _SIZE)
    const uint64_t *addrs;    // <mod>_fn_addrs: guest function starts, strictly ascending
    const GuestFn *fns;       // <mod>_fn_ptrs: the lifted function for each start
    uint64_t count;           // <mod>_fn_count
} RtModule;

// The module glue that tools/build_game.py writes for each build (build/<version>/modules.c), from layout.json and
// layout.h: every module of the layout, and the modules linked into this executable.
typedef struct RtLayoutEntry { const char *name; uint64_t base, size; } RtLayoutEntry;
extern const RtLayoutEntry rt_layout[];
extern const int rt_layout_count;
int rt_linked_modules(RtModule *out, int max);

// Register a host function at a guest address outside every module (HLE entry points). Allowed only before
// rt_dispatch_init; the registry is fixed afterwards.
void rt_register_host(uint64_t addr, GuestFn fn);

// Build the table from the modules (kept by pointer; they must outlive the process). Call it once, before any guest
// thread starts: thread creation publishes the table to the threads. Fatal on a malformed table:
// unsorted or duplicate starts, a start outside its module, overlapping modules, host code spread over 4 GiB.
void rt_dispatch_init(const RtModule *mods, int count);

// The host function for a guest address, or NULL when nothing is there. Does not run guest code.
GuestFn rt_dispatch_lookup(uint64_t pc);

// "0x7000001234 (main+0x1234)" for a guest address inside a module, else the bare address. Returns buf.
const char *rt_guest_name(uint64_t pc, char *buf, int size);

typedef struct RtDispatchStats {
    uint64_t lo, hi;          // guest range the table covers
    uint64_t slots;           // (hi - lo) / 4
    uint64_t table_bytes;     // reserved for the table
    uint64_t functions;       // filled slots
    uint64_t host_fns;        // rt_register_host entries
} RtDispatchStats;
RtDispatchStats rt_dispatch_stats(void);

// Runtime fatal error: message to stderr, then exit. Used by the dispatcher and the stubs.
void rt_fatal(const char *fmt, ...) __attribute__((noreturn, format(printf, 1, 2)));

```

`runtime/dpi_probe_win.c`:

```c
// --probe-dpi: the process DPI awareness that totk.manifest declares, and what the primary monitor reports under it.
// A DPI-unaware process gets every window and monitor size scaled down by the display scale and its output stretched
// back up by Windows; the probe fails unless the process is per-monitor aware (v2). Needs no game files and no GPU.
#include <stdio.h>
#include <windows.h>

#include "host.h"

static const char *awareness_name(DPI_AWARENESS_CONTEXT ctx) {
    if (AreDpiAwarenessContextsEqual(ctx, DPI_AWARENESS_CONTEXT_PER_MONITOR_AWARE_V2)) return "per-monitor aware v2";
    switch (GetAwarenessFromDpiAwarenessContext(ctx)) {
    case DPI_AWARENESS_UNAWARE: return "unaware";
    case DPI_AWARENESS_SYSTEM_AWARE: return "system aware";
    case DPI_AWARENESS_PER_MONITOR_AWARE: return "per-monitor aware v1";
    default: return "invalid";
    }
}

int probe_dpi(void) {
    DPI_AWARENESS_CONTEXT ctx = GetThreadDpiAwarenessContext();
    MONITORINFO mi = {sizeof mi};
    HMONITOR mon = MonitorFromPoint((POINT){0, 0}, MONITOR_DEFAULTTOPRIMARY);
    int have = GetMonitorInfoW(mon, &mi);
    printf("dpi: awareness %s\n", awareness_name(ctx));
    printf("dpi: system dpi %u (scale %u%%)\n", GetDpiForSystem(), GetDpiForSystem() * 100 / 96);
    if (have)
        printf("dpi: primary monitor %ldx%ld at %ld,%ld; screen metrics %dx%d\n", mi.rcMonitor.right - mi.rcMonitor.left,
               mi.rcMonitor.bottom - mi.rcMonitor.top, mi.rcMonitor.left, mi.rcMonitor.top, GetSystemMetrics(SM_CXSCREEN),
               GetSystemMetrics(SM_CYSCREEN));
    int ok = AreDpiAwarenessContextsEqual(ctx, DPI_AWARENESS_CONTEXT_PER_MONITOR_AWARE_V2) && have;
    printf("probe-dpi: %s\n", ok ? "PASS" : "FAIL (the process is not per-monitor aware v2)");
    return ok ? 0 : 1;
}
```
