`runtime/ov_codec.c`:

```c
// nn::codec video decoding (the Switch 2 SDK's VP9 path) on the host with libvpx, for the NVN 2 reference title's tutorial
// guide movies (Movie/Guide*.webm, 960x540). The SDK's nn::codec::video::Initialize opens the console's video service
// over IPC, which the host does not serve (the first guide movie crashed in nn::codec::video::detail::ipc::Initialize),
// so the decoder calls are host functions. The demuxer (nn::movie::MediaExtractor) stays guest code.
// What the game's movie player (main+0xdfb8xx..0xdfe9xx) expects, read from its code:
// - each output buffer i is an image pool of its own, tied to i by RegisterVp9DecoderBuffer; the player reads the
//   pool's size at +0x20 / +0x22 (u16 width, height), which InitializeDecoderImagePool takes from the preference
//   (MakeDecodeImagePreference, SDK code: +8 u16 width - 1, +10 u16 height - 1);
// - it acquires an output buffer before it submits input (its wrapper aborts on any failure there): Acquire reserves
//   the buffer the next shown picture goes to and returns a fence (NativeSyncHandle, which the caller zeroed; the
//   host writes a token in its first word); the player waits for it through nn::syncpt::sdk::RequestSyncPointEvent,
//   signalled when SubmitVp9DecoderInputBuffer has decoded a picture into that buffer (at once if it already has);
// - a submission with no reserved buffer to decode into answers "not ready" (the wrapper's retry code 0x76);
// - the picture is read with ReadDecoderOutputImageNv12 (Y plane, then interleaved UV, each with the caller's pitch).
//   GetDecoderImagePoolNativeImageHandle (the player's GPU path) has no image yet and returns 0.
// libvpx is BSD-3-Clause and already linked for ov_movie.c.
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include <vpx/vp8dx.h>
#include <vpx/vpx_decoder.h>
#include <dav1d/dav1d.h>

#include "host.h"
#include "platform/platform.h"

enum { R_NOT_READY = 0x1c266f };   // (result & 0x3fffff) - 0x1c2000 == 0x66f: "try again" for the game's wrapper
// QUEUED: packets the decoder takes ahead of the buffers for their pictures, as Eglantine's video session does
// (nx2_gsv.h, INx2VideoSession::MaxQueuedInputs); a submission past them answers "not ready".
enum { SLOTS = 16, DECODERS = 4, WAITERS = 4, QUEUED = 8 };
enum { S_FREE, S_WAIT, S_FILLED };   // registered; acquired with no picture yet; acquired holding a picture
enum { FENCE_TAG = 0xc0de0000u };    // fence token: tag | decoder << 8 | buffer

// TOTK_TRACE=codec: a line for each decoder call that moves a buffer or a picture, to follow a player that stops.
#define TRACE(...)                                                                                                   \
    do {                                                                                                             \
        if (rt_trace & RT_TRACE_CODEC) rt_log("codec: " __VA_ARGS__);                                                \
    } while (0)

#define LOG_FIRST(...)                                                                                               \
    do {                                                                                                             \
        static volatile int32_t logged;                                                                              \
        if (!__atomic_exchange_n(&logged, 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED)) rt_log(__VA_ARGS__);                                 \
    } while (0)

typedef struct {
    uint64_t pool;     // guest VideoDecoderImagePoolType registered for this index; 0: not registered
    int state;
    uint32_t seq;      // acquisition order: pictures fill the oldest waiting buffer
    uint64_t waiter[WAITERS];   // guest system events of sync point events requested before the picture came
    uint16_t w, h;
    int64_t pts;       // nanoseconds (nn::TimeSpan)
    int eos;
    uint8_t *nv12;     // w*h luma, then cw*ch interleaved UV pairs
} Slot;

// A packet submitted while no buffer was reserved for its picture, decoded once one is (ov_vp9_acquire).
typedef struct { uint8_t *data; size_t size; int64_t pts; int end; } Packet;

typedef struct {
    uint64_t key;      // guest Vp9DecoderType; 0: unused
    vpx_codec_ctx_t vpx;
    int vpx_ok;
    int av1;           // 1: AV1 through dav1d (Switch 2 movies); 0: VP9 through libvpx
    Dav1dContext *dav;
    uint32_t seq;
    Slot slot[SLOTS];
    Slot last;         // the newest picture, for packets that show none
    Packet queue[QUEUED];
    int qhead, qn;
} Dec;

static Dec decs[DECODERS];
static PlatMutex lock = PLAT_MUTEX_INIT;   // every decoder call; held across a decode (one 960x540 frame, a few ms)

static Dec *dec_of(uint64_t key) {
    for (int i = 0; i < DECODERS; i++)
        if (decs[i].key == key) return &decs[i];
    return NULL;
}

static uint32_t cw(uint16_t w) { return (w + 1u) / 2; }
static uint32_t ch(uint16_t h) { return (h + 1u) / 2; }

// Copies a decoded I420 picture into s as NV12.
static void put_picture(Slot *s, const vpx_image_t *img) {
    uint16_t w = (uint16_t)img->d_w, h = (uint16_t)img->d_h;
    if (!s->nv12 || s->w != w || s->h != h) {
        free(s->nv12);
        s->nv12 = malloc((size_t)w * h + 2 * (size_t)cw(w) * ch(h));
        if (!s->nv12) rt_fatal("codec: out of memory for a %ux%u picture", w, h);
        s->w = w, s->h = h;
    }
    for (uint32_t y = 0; y < h; y++) memcpy(s->nv12 + (size_t)y * w, img->planes[0] + (size_t)y * img->stride[0], w);
    uint8_t *uv = s->nv12 + (size_t)w * h;
    for (uint32_t y = 0; y < ch(h); y++) {
        const uint8_t *u = img->planes[1] + (size_t)y * img->stride[1], *v = img->planes[2] + (size_t)y * img->stride[2];
        uint8_t *o = uv + (size_t)y * 2 * cw(w);
        for (uint32_t x = 0; x < cw(w); x++) o[2 * x] = u[x], o[2 * x + 1] = v[x];
    }
}

static void queue_drop(Dec *d);
static void dec_free(Dec *d) {
    if (d->vpx_ok) vpx_codec_destroy(&d->vpx);
    if (d->dav) dav1d_close(&d->dav);
    for (int i = 0; i < SLOTS; i++) free(d->slot[i].nv12);
    free(d->last.nv12);
    queue_drop(d);
    memset(d, 0, sizeof *d);
}

// Copies a decoded dav1d picture (any layout, 8 to 16 bit) into s as 8-bit NV12.
static void put_picture_av1(Slot *s, const Dav1dPicture *p) {
    uint16_t w = (uint16_t)p->p.w, h = (uint16_t)p->p.h;
    if (!s->nv12 || s->w != w || s->h != h) {
        free(s->nv12);
        s->nv12 = malloc((size_t)w * h + 2 * (size_t)cw(w) * ch(h));
        if (!s->nv12) rt_fatal("codec: out of memory for a %ux%u picture", w, h);
        s->w = w, s->h = h;
    }
    int sh = p->p.bpc > 8 ? p->p.bpc - 8 : 0, wide = p->p.bpc > 8;
#define PX(pl, st, x, y)                                                                                             \
    (wide ? (uint8_t)(((const uint16_t *)((const uint8_t *)(p->data[pl]) + (ptrdiff_t)(y) * (st)))[x] >> sh)        \
          : ((const uint8_t *)(p->data[pl]) + (ptrdiff_t)(y) * (st))[x])
    ptrdiff_t ys = p->stride[0], cs = p->stride[1];
    for (uint32_t y = 0; y < h; y++)
        for (uint32_t x = 0; x < w; x++) s->nv12[(size_t)y * w + x] = PX(0, ys, x, y);
    uint8_t *uv = s->nv12 + (size_t)w * h;
    int lay = p->p.layout;   // I400 0, I420 1, I422 2, I444 3
    for (uint32_t y = 0; y < ch(h); y++)
        for (uint32_t x = 0; x < cw(w); x++) {
            uint8_t *o = uv + (size_t)y * 2 * cw(w) + 2 * x;
            if (lay == DAV1D_PIXEL_LAYOUT_I400) o[0] = o[1] = 128;
            else {
                uint32_t sx = lay == DAV1D_PIXEL_LAYOUT_I444 ? 2 * x : x, sy = lay == DAV1D_PIXEL_LAYOUT_I420 ? y : 2 * y;
                if (sy >= h) sy = h - 1;
                o[0] = PX(1, cs, sx, sy), o[1] = PX(2, cs, sx, sy);
            }
        }
#undef PX
}

static void copy_slot(Slot *to, const Slot *from) {
    if (!from->nv12) return;
    size_t n = (size_t)from->w * from->h + 2 * (size_t)cw(from->w) * ch(from->h);
    if (!to->nv12 || to->w != from->w || to->h != from->h) {
        free(to->nv12);
        if (!(to->nv12 = malloc(n))) rt_fatal("codec: out of memory for a picture");
        to->w = from->w, to->h = from->h;
    }
    memcpy(to->nv12, from->nv12, n);
}

static void queue_drop(Dec *d) {
    for (int i = 0; i < d->qn; i++) free(d->queue[(d->qhead + i) % QUEUED].data);
    d->qhead = d->qn = 0;
}

// The oldest reserved buffer still waiting for a picture: pictures fill buffers in acquisition order.
static Slot *oldest_wait(Dec *d) {
    Slot *s = NULL;
    for (int i = 0; i < SLOTS; i++)
        if (d->slot[i].state == S_WAIT && (!s || (int32_t)(d->slot[i].seq - s->seq) < 0)) s = &d->slot[i];
    return s;
}

// Decodes one packet into the waiting buffer s (lock held). A packet that shows nothing leaves s waiting, except the
// last one: the player then gets the previous picture (or black) marked as the end. Returns the number of events to
// signal, stored in wake.
static int decode_into(Dec *d, Slot *s, const uint8_t *data, size_t size, int64_t pts, int end, uint64_t wake[WAITERS]) {
    const vpx_image_t *img = NULL, *f;
    Dav1dPicture pic = {0};
    int have_pic = 0;
    if (d->av1 && d->dav && data && size) {
        Dav1dData dd = {0};
        uint8_t *buf = dav1d_data_create(&dd, size);
        if (buf) {
            memcpy(buf, data, size);
            for (;;) {
                int r = dav1d_send_data(d->dav, &dd);
                if (r < 0 && r != DAV1D_ERR(EAGAIN)) {
                    LOG_FIRST("codec: AV1 packet of %zu bytes failed (%d)", size, r);
                    break;
                }
                Dav1dPicture q = {0};
                while (dav1d_get_picture(d->dav, &q) == 0) {
                    if (have_pic) dav1d_picture_unref(&pic);
                    pic = q, have_pic = 1;
                    memset(&q, 0, sizeof q);
                }
                if (!dd.sz) break;
            }
            dav1d_data_unref(&dd);
        }
    }
    if (d->vpx_ok && data && size) {
        if (vpx_codec_decode(&d->vpx, data, (unsigned)size, NULL, 0) != VPX_CODEC_OK)
            LOG_FIRST("codec: VP9 packet of %zu bytes failed: %s", size, vpx_codec_error_detail(&d->vpx));
        vpx_codec_iter_t it = NULL;
        while ((f = vpx_codec_get_frame(&d->vpx, &it))) img = f;   // a superframe shows at most one; keep the last
    }
    int filled = 1;
    if (have_pic) put_picture_av1(s, &pic), copy_slot(&d->last, s), dav1d_picture_unref(&pic);
    else if (img) put_picture(s, img), copy_slot(&d->last, s);
    else if (end && d->last.nv12) copy_slot(s, &d->last);
    else if (end) {
        vpx_image_t black = {.d_w = 16, .d_h = 16};
        static uint8_t y[16 * 16], uv[8 * 8];
        if (!uv[0]) memset(y, 16, sizeof y), memset(uv, 128, sizeof uv);
        black.planes[0] = y, black.planes[1] = black.planes[2] = uv, black.stride[0] = 16, black.stride[1] = black.stride[2] = 8;
        put_picture(s, &black);
    } else filled = 0;
    TRACE("decode %zu bytes pts %lld%s: buffer %d %s", size, (long long)pts, end ? " end" : "", (int)(s - d->slot),
          filled ? "filled" : "still waiting (no picture shown)");
    LOG_FIRST("codec: first VP9 packet: %zu bytes, picture %ux%u", size, s->w, s->h);
    int n = 0;
    if (filled) {
        s->state = S_FILLED, s->pts = pts, s->eos = end;
        for (int k = 0; k < WAITERS; k++)
            if (s->waiter[k]) wake[n++] = s->waiter[k];
        memset(s->waiter, 0, sizeof s->waiter);
    }
    return n;
}

// Result nn::codec::video::Initialize(), Finalize(): nothing to open on the host
static void ov_video_init(Cpu *c) { ret_x(c, 0); }
static void ov_video_fini(Cpu *c) { ret_x(c, 0); }
static void ov_aac_ctor(Cpu *c) { ret_x(c, arg_x(c, 0)); }
static void ov_aac_zero(Cpu *c) { ret_x(c, 0); }
static void ov_aac_value(Cpu *c) { ret_x(c, 0); }

static void vp9_init(Cpu *c, uint64_t key, unsigned w, unsigned h, int av1, int vp8) {
    plat_mutex_lock(&lock);
    Dec *d = dec_of(key);
    if (!d) d = dec_of(0);
    if (!d) rt_fatal("codec: more than %d VP9 decoders", DECODERS);
    dec_free(d);
    d->key = key;
    d->av1 = av1;
    int ok;
    if (av1) {
        Dav1dSettings st;
        dav1d_default_settings(&st);
        st.n_threads = 1, st.max_frame_delay = 1;   // a picture per packet, no frame-thread delay
        ok = dav1d_open(&d->dav, &st) == 0;
        if (!ok) d->dav = NULL;
    } else {
        vpx_codec_dec_cfg_t cfg = {.threads = 2, .w = w, .h = h};
        ok = d->vpx_ok = vpx_codec_dec_init(&d->vpx, vp8 ? vpx_codec_vp8_dx() : vpx_codec_vp9_dx(), &cfg, 0) == VPX_CODEC_OK;
    }
    plat_mutex_unlock(&lock);
    rt_log("codec: %s decoder %#llx %ux%u on the host (%s%s)", av1 ? "AV1" : "VP9", (unsigned long long)key, w, h,
           av1 ? "dav1d" : "libvpx", ok ? "" : " failed to start: pictures stay black");
    ret_x(c, 0);
}
// Result InitializeVp9Decoder(Vp9DecoderType *, void *work, size_t, size_t, u16 w, u16 h, u32, input, output fmt)
static void ov_vp9_init(Cpu *c) { vp9_init(c, arg_x(c, 0), arg_x(c, 4) & 0xffff, arg_x(c, 5) & 0xffff, 0, 0); }
// Result Initialize{Vp9,Av1}DecoderByTransferMemory(Type *, void *work, size_t, size_t, u16 w, u16 h, u32, in, out, mode)
static void ov_vp9_init_tm(Cpu *c) { vp9_init(c, arg_x(c, 0), arg_x(c, 4) & 0xffff, arg_x(c, 5) & 0xffff, 0, 0); }
static void ov_av1_init_tm(Cpu *c) { vp9_init(c, arg_x(c, 0), arg_x(c, 4) & 0xffff, arg_x(c, 5) & 0xffff, 1, 0); }
// Result Initialize{Vp9,Av1}DecoderByRemoteMemory(Type *, size_t, u16 w, u16 h, u32, in, out, mode)
static void ov_vp9_init_rm(Cpu *c) { vp9_init(c, arg_x(c, 0), arg_x(c, 2) & 0xffff, arg_x(c, 3) & 0xffff, 0, 0); }
static void ov_av1_init_rm(Cpu *c) { vp9_init(c, arg_x(c, 0), arg_x(c, 2) & 0xffff, arg_x(c, 3) & 0xffff, 1, 0); }
static void ov_vp8_init_tm(Cpu *c) { vp9_init(c, arg_x(c, 0), arg_x(c, 4) & 0xffff, arg_x(c, 5) & 0xffff, 0, 1); }
static void ov_vp8_init_rm(Cpu *c) { vp9_init(c, arg_x(c, 0), arg_x(c, 2) & 0xffff, arg_x(c, 3) & 0xffff, 0, 1); }
// Result InitializeVp9Decoder(Vp9DecoderType *, size_t, size_t, u16 w, u16 h, u32, input, output fmt)
static void ov_vp9_init_nowork(Cpu *c) { vp9_init(c, arg_x(c, 0), arg_x(c, 3) & 0xffff, arg_x(c, 4) & 0xffff, 0, 0); }

// SDK 20's image preference is an indirect 0x20-byte return.  The SDK stores width-1 and height-1 at +8/+10;
// ov_pool_init consumes those fields to report the guest-visible image dimensions.
static void ov_make_image_preference(Cpu *c) {
    uint8_t *out = (uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)c->x[8];   // AAPCS64 indirect result register, not stack argument 8
    if (out) {
        memset(out, 0, 0x20);
        uint16_t w = (uint16_t)(arg_x(c, 0) ? arg_x(c, 0) - 1 : 0);
        uint16_t h = (uint16_t)(arg_x(c, 1) ? arg_x(c, 1) - 1 : 0);
        memcpy(out + 8, &w, sizeof w);
        memcpy(out + 10, &h, sizeof h);
        out[0] = (uint8_t)arg_x(c, 2);
        out[1] = (uint8_t)arg_x(c, 3);
    }
    ret_x(c, 0);
}

// The AV1 intro requests NV12.  RGBA variants are kept off the console IPC path; black is a safe fallback if another
// movie selects one of them before a host conversion path is needed.
static void ov_read_rgba(Cpu *c) {
    uint8_t *out = arg_p(c, 6);
    size_t size = arg_x(c, 8);
    if (out && size <= 64u * 1024u * 1024u) memset(out, 0, size);
    ret_x(c, 0);
}

static void ov_h264_unsupported(Cpu *c) { ret_x(c, 0x1c0001u); }

// Result FinalizeVp9Decoder(Vp9DecoderType *)
static void ov_vp9_fini(Cpu *c) {
    plat_mutex_lock(&lock);
    Dec *d = dec_of(arg_x(c, 0));
    if (d) dec_free(d);
    plat_mutex_unlock(&lock);
    ret_x(c, 0);
}

// Result FlushVp9Decoder(Vp9DecoderType *): outputs not handed over yet are dropped
static void ov_vp9_flush(Cpu *c) {
    plat_mutex_lock(&lock);
    Dec *d = dec_of(arg_x(c, 0));
    if (d)
        for (int i = 0; i < SLOTS; i++)
            if (d->slot[i].state == S_FILLED) d->slot[i].state = S_WAIT;   // still reserved; its picture is dropped
    if (d) queue_drop(d);   // and so are the packets not decoded yet
    plat_mutex_unlock(&lock);
    TRACE("flush");
    ret_x(c, 0);
}

// Result Start/StopVp9Decoder(Vp9DecoderType *), FinalizeDecoderImagePool(pool): nothing to do
static void ov_ok(Cpu *c) { ret_x(c, 0); }

// Result RegisterVp9DecoderBuffer(Vp9DecoderType *, u32 index, VideoDecoderImagePoolType *, u32)
static void ov_vp9_register(Cpu *c) {
    uint32_t i = (uint32_t)arg_x(c, 1);
    plat_mutex_lock(&lock);
    Dec *d = dec_of(arg_x(c, 0));
    if (d && i < SLOTS) d->slot[i].pool = arg_x(c, 2), d->slot[i].state = S_FREE;
    plat_mutex_unlock(&lock);
    if (!d || i >= SLOTS) rt_log("codec: RegisterVp9DecoderBuffer index %u of an unknown decoder or past %d", i, SLOTS);
    ret_x(c, 0);
}

// Result InitializeDecoderImagePool(pool, void *, size_t, const VideoDecoderImagePreference &, u32, CodecMode): the
// size the player reads back at +0x20 / +0x22
static void ov_pool_init(Cpu *c) {
    uint8_t *pool = arg_p(c, 0);
    const uint8_t *pref = arg_p(c, 3);
    uint16_t w, h;
    memcpy(&w, pref + 8, 2), memcpy(&h, pref + 10, 2);
    w++, h++;
    memcpy(pool + 0x20, &w, 2), memcpy(pool + 0x22, &h, 2);
    ret_x(c, 0);
}

// Result CalculateDecoderImagePoolBuffer(size_t *size, size_t *align, const preference &, u32 count),
// CalculateVp9DecoderWorkBuffer(size_t *size, size_t *align, size_t, u16 w, u16 h): the buffers hold nothing on the
// host (the pictures are host memory), so one page each
static void ov_calc_size(Cpu *c) {
    *(uint64_t *)arg_p(c, 0) = 0x1000;
    *(uint64_t *)arg_p(c, 1) = 0x1000;
    ret_x(c, 0);
}

// One manual-clear guest SystemEventType per decoder/event object. A SyncPointEventType is itself the storage passed to
// CreateSyncPointEvent; the decoder's submission-ready event has no guest storage, so allocate one for it.
static struct { uint64_t key, ev; } event_tab[64];
static int event_n;
static PlatMutex event_lock = PLAT_MUTEX_INIT;
static uint64_t event_at(Cpu *c, uint64_t key, uint64_t storage) {
    plat_mutex_lock(&event_lock);
    uint64_t ev = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < event_n && !ev; i++)
        if (event_tab[i].key == key) ev = event_tab[i].ev;
    if (!ev) {
        if (event_n == 64) rt_fatal("codec: more than 64 decoder and sync point objects");
        ev = storage;
        event_tab[event_n].key = key, event_tab[event_n++].ev = ev;
    }
    plat_mutex_unlock(&event_lock);
    kern_bind_system_event(c, ev, 0);
    return ev;
}
static uint64_t event_for(Cpu *c, uint64_t key) {
    plat_mutex_lock(&event_lock);
    uint64_t ev = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < event_n && !ev; i++)
        if (event_tab[i].key == key) ev = event_tab[i].ev;
    plat_mutex_unlock(&event_lock);
    if (!ev) ev = event_at(c, key, (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)mem_kernel_alloc(0x100, 16));
    else kern_bind_system_event(c, ev, 0);
    return ev;
}

static void codec_signal_event(Cpu *c, uint64_t ev) {
    static uint64_t signal;
    if (!signal && !(signal = ldr_symbol("_ZN2nn2os17SignalSystemEventEPNS0_15SystemEventTypeE")))
        rt_fatal("codec: nn::os::SignalSystemEvent is not loaded");
    rt_call(c, signal, 1, ev);
}

// Result GetVp9DecoderSubmissionReadyEvent(nn::os::SystemEventType **out, Vp9DecoderType *): signalled while the
// decoder can take a packet, which is when an output buffer is reserved for its picture. The player clears it after a
// submission comes back not ready, so AcquireVp9DecoderOutputBuffer signals it again (ov_vp9_acquire).
static void ov_vp9_ready_event(Cpu *c) {
    uint64_t *out = arg_p(c, 0), dec = arg_x(c, 1);
    uint64_t ev = event_for(c, dec);
    codec_signal_event(c, ev);
    *out = ev;
    TRACE("submission-ready event %#llx handed out (signalled)", (unsigned long long)ev);
    ret_x(c, 0);
}

// Result SubmitVp9DecoderInputBuffer(u64 *id, Vp9DecoderType *, const void *data, size_t size, TimeSpan pts, bool end):
// decoded at once into the oldest waiting buffer, else queued for the next one reserved; "not ready" once QUEUED
// packets wait. After the end of a guide movie the player flushes and starts over with the buffers it still holds,
// submitting its third packet before it releases one: without the queue that packet was refused, nothing released a
// buffer again, and the window kept the movie's first picture, a flat yellow card.
static void ov_vp9_submit(Cpu *c) {
    uint64_t *id = arg_p(c, 0);
    const uint8_t *data = arg_p(c, 2);
    size_t size = arg_x(c, 3);
    int64_t pts = (int64_t)arg_x(c, 4);
    int end = (int)(arg_x(c, 5) & 1);
    plat_mutex_lock(&lock);
    Dec *d = dec_of(arg_x(c, 1));
    Slot *s = d && !d->qn ? oldest_wait(d) : NULL;
    if (!s) {
        int queued = d && d->qn < QUEUED;
        if (queued) {
            Packet *q = &d->queue[(d->qhead + d->qn++) % QUEUED];
            *q = (Packet){size ? malloc(size) : NULL, size, pts, end};
            if (size && !q->data) rt_fatal("codec: out of memory for a %zu-byte packet", size);
            if (size) memcpy(q->data, data, size);
            if (id) *id = d->seq;
        }
        int waiting = d ? d->qn : 0;
        plat_mutex_unlock(&lock);
        TRACE("submit %zu bytes pts %lld%s: %s (%d queued)", size, (long long)pts, end ? " end" : "",
              queued ? "queued for the next reserved buffer" : "not ready", waiting);
        ret_x(c, queued ? 0 : R_NOT_READY);
        return;
    }
    uint64_t wake[WAITERS];
    int n = decode_into(d, s, data, size, pts, end, wake);
    if (id) *id = d->seq;
    plat_mutex_unlock(&lock);
    for (int k = 0; k < n; k++) codec_signal_event(c, wake[k]);
    ret_x(c, 0);
}

// Result AcquireVp9DecoderOutputBuffer(u32 *index, NativeSyncHandle *fence, Vp9DecoderType *): reserves a free buffer
// for the next picture, decodes queued packets into the waiting buffers; the fence carries the token
// RequestSyncPointEvent waits on
static void ov_vp9_acquire(Cpu *c) {
    uint32_t *index = arg_p(c, 0), *fence = arg_p(c, 1);
    uint64_t key = arg_x(c, 2);
    uint64_t wake[SLOTS * WAITERS];
    int n = 0;
    plat_mutex_lock(&lock);
    Dec *d = dec_of(key);
    int got = -1;
    for (int i = 0; d && i < SLOTS && got < 0; i++)
        if (d->slot[i].pool && d->slot[i].state == S_FREE) got = i;
    if (got >= 0) {
        Slot *s = &d->slot[got];
        s->state = S_WAIT, s->seq = d->seq++, s->eos = 0;
        memset(s->waiter, 0, sizeof s->waiter);
        *index = (uint32_t)got;
        if (fence) *fence = FENCE_TAG | (uint32_t)(d - decs) << 8 | (uint32_t)got;
        Slot *w;
        while (d->qn && (w = oldest_wait(d)) && n <= SLOTS * WAITERS - WAITERS) {
            Packet q = d->queue[d->qhead];
            d->qhead = (d->qhead + 1) % QUEUED, d->qn--;
            n += decode_into(d, w, q.data, q.size, q.pts, q.end, wake + n);
            free(q.data);
        }
    }
    plat_mutex_unlock(&lock);
    if (got < 0) rt_log("codec: AcquireVp9DecoderOutputBuffer with every registered buffer reserved");
    else TRACE("acquire: buffer %d", got);
    for (int k = 0; k < n; k++) codec_signal_event(c, wake[k]);
    // A reserved buffer lets the next packet in: wake a player that waits for the submission-ready event after a not
    // ready submission. Without this, the tutorial's guide movies stopped at their second picture.
    if (got >= 0) codec_signal_event(c, event_for(c, key));
    ret_x(c, got < 0 ? R_NOT_READY : 0);
}

// Result ReleaseVp9DecoderOutputBuffer(Vp9DecoderType *, u32 index, NativeSyncHandle)
static void ov_vp9_release(Cpu *c) {
    uint32_t i = (uint32_t)arg_x(c, 1);
    plat_mutex_lock(&lock);
    Dec *d = dec_of(arg_x(c, 0));
    if (d && i < SLOTS && d->slot[i].state != S_FREE) d->slot[i].state = S_FREE;
    plat_mutex_unlock(&lock);
    TRACE("release: buffer %u", i);
    ret_x(c, 0);
}

// Result GetVp9DecoderOutputBufferProperties(u16 *w, u16 *h, u16 *, u16 *, nn::movie::ColorSpace *, TimeSpan *pts,
// bool *end, Vp9DecoderType *, u32 index). The two unnamed u16 get the picture size too (aligned or display size).
static void ov_vp9_props(Cpu *c) {
    uint32_t i = (uint32_t)arg_x(c, 8);
    plat_mutex_lock(&lock);
    Dec *d = dec_of(arg_x(c, 7));
    Slot s = d && i < SLOTS ? d->slot[i] : (Slot){0};
    plat_mutex_unlock(&lock);
    for (int k = 0; k < 4; k++) {
        uint16_t *p = arg_p(c, k);
        if (p) *p = k & 1 ? s.h : s.w;
    }
    LOG_FIRST("codec: output properties: %ux%u", s.w, s.h);
    if (arg_p(c, 4)) *(uint32_t *)arg_p(c, 4) = 0;
    if (arg_p(c, 5)) *(int64_t *)arg_p(c, 5) = s.pts;
    if (arg_p(c, 6)) *(uint8_t *)arg_p(c, 6) = (uint8_t)s.eos;
    ret_x(c, d ? 0 : R_NOT_READY);
}

// Result ReadDecoderOutputImageNv12(const VideoDecoderImagePoolType *, u32 image, u16 x, u16 y, u16 w, u16 h,
// void *luma, size_t luma_pitch, size_t luma_size, void *chroma, size_t chroma_pitch, size_t chroma_size)
static void ov_read_nv12(Cpu *c) {
    uint64_t pool = arg_x(c, 0);
    uint32_t x0 = arg_x(c, 2) & 0xffff, y0 = arg_x(c, 3) & 0xffff, w = arg_x(c, 4) & 0xffff, h = arg_x(c, 5) & 0xffff;
    uint8_t *ly = arg_p(c, 6), *luv = arg_p(c, 9);
    size_t yp = arg_x(c, 7), ys = arg_x(c, 8), uvp = arg_x(c, 10), uvs = arg_x(c, 11);
    plat_mutex_lock(&lock);
    const Slot *s = NULL;
    for (int k = 0; k < DECODERS && !s; k++)
        for (int i = 0; decs[k].key && i < SLOTS && !s; i++)
            if (decs[k].slot[i].pool == pool && decs[k].slot[i].nv12) s = &decs[k].slot[i];
    if (s) {
        uint32_t cx = x0 < s->w ? x0 : s->w, cy = y0 < s->h ? y0 : s->h;
        uint32_t rw = w < s->w - cx ? w : s->w - cx, rh = h < s->h - cy ? h : s->h - cy;
        size_t n = rw < yp ? rw : yp;   // each row stays inside the caller's pitch and buffer
        for (uint32_t r = 0; r < rh && ly && r * yp + n <= ys; r++)
            memcpy(ly + r * yp, s->nv12 + (size_t)(cy + r) * s->w + cx, n);
        const uint8_t *uv = s->nv12 + (size_t)s->w * s->h;
        uint32_t uw = 2 * ((rw + 1) / 2), uh = (rh + 1) / 2, ux = 2 * (cx / 2), uy = cy / 2;
        n = uw < uvp ? uw : uvp;
        for (uint32_t r = 0; r < uh && luv && r * uvp + n <= uvs; r++)
            memcpy(luv + r * uvp, uv + (size_t)(uy + r) * 2 * cw(s->w) + ux, n);
    }
    int64_t pts = s ? s->pts : -1;
    static volatile int32_t image_stats;
    static const int64_t stats_pts[] = {500000000ll, 1000000000ll, 2000000000ll, 5000000000ll, 10000000000ll, 20000000000ll};
    int32_t stat_index = __atomic_load_n(&image_stats, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    if (s && s->nv12 && stat_index < 6 && pts >= stats_pts[stat_index]) {
        uint64_t sum = 0;
        unsigned lo = 255, hi = 0, count = 0;
        size_t pixels = (size_t)s->w * s->h;
        for (size_t i = 0; i < pixels; i += pixels / 1024 ? pixels / 1024 : 1) {
            unsigned yv = s->nv12[i];
            sum += yv;
            if (yv < lo) lo = yv;
            if (yv > hi) hi = yv;
            count++;
        }
        const uint8_t *uv = s->nv12 + pixels;
        uint64_t uv_sum = 0;
        unsigned uv_count = 0;
        size_t chroma = 2 * (size_t)cw(s->w) * ch(s->h);
        for (size_t i = 0; i < chroma; i += chroma / 1024 ? chroma / 1024 : 1) uv_sum += uv[i], uv_count++;
        int32_t sample = __atomic_add_fetch(&image_stats, 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
        rt_log("codec: NV12 sample #%d pts %lld: Y mean %u range %u..%u, U mean %u",
               sample, (long long)pts, count ? (unsigned)(sum / count) : 0, lo, hi,
               uv_count ? (unsigned)(uv_sum / uv_count) : 0);
    }
    plat_mutex_unlock(&lock);
    LOG_FIRST("codec: first NV12 read %ux%u (%s)", w, h, s ? "a decoded picture" : "no picture for this pool");
    TRACE("read pool %#llx: pts %lld", (unsigned long long)pool, (long long)pts);
    ret_x(c, 0);
}

// NativeImageHandle GetDecoderImagePoolNativeImageHandle(const VideoDecoderImagePoolType *, u32): no GPU image
static void ov_pool_image(Cpu *c) {
    LOG_FIRST("codec: GetDecoderImagePoolNativeImageHandle %p #%u: no GPU image (the player's NV12 path is served)",
              arg_p(c, 0), (unsigned)arg_x(c, 1));
    ret_x(c, 0);
}

// ---- nn::syncpt::sdk: GPU sync point events (the decoder's output fences), not in the SDK's loaded modules. Each is a
// guest system event; a request is signalled at once, as the host has no sync point to wait for.
// Result CreateSyncPointEvent(SyncPointEventType *)
static void ov_sp_create(Cpu *c) {
    uint64_t key = arg_x(c, 0);
    event_at(c, key, key);
    ret_x(c, 0);
}
// void InitializeMultiWaitHolder(nn::os::MultiWaitHolderType *, SyncPointEventType *): the system event's holder
static void ov_sp_holder(Cpu *c) {
    static uint64_t init;
    if (!init && !(init = ldr_symbol("_ZN2nn2os25InitializeMultiWaitHolderEPNS0_19MultiWaitHolderTypeEPNS0_15SystemEventTypeE")))
        rt_fatal("codec: nn::os::InitializeMultiWaitHolder(SystemEventType *) is not loaded");
    uint64_t holder = arg_x(c, 0), ev = event_for(c, arg_x(c, 1));
    rt_call(c, init, 2, holder, ev);
}
// bool TryWaitSyncPointEvent(const SyncPointEventType *)
static void ov_sp_trywait(Cpu *c) {
    static uint64_t trywait;
    if (!trywait && !(trywait = ldr_symbol("_ZN2nn2os18TryWaitSystemEventEPNS0_15SystemEventTypeE")))
        rt_fatal("codec: nn::os::TryWaitSystemEvent is not loaded");
    uint64_t ev = event_for(c, arg_x(c, 0));
    ret_x(c, rt_call(c, trywait, 1, ev) & 1);
}
// The host AV1/VP9 decoder completes synchronously before signaling its guest event, so any fence polled by the
// movie event manager is already complete. The SDK implementation otherwise dispatches through the uninitialized
// console sync-point service backend.
static void ov_sp_trywait_handle(Cpu *c) { ret_x(c, 1); }
static void clear_event(Cpu *c, uint64_t ev) {
    static uint64_t clear;
    if (!clear && !(clear = ldr_symbol("_ZN2nn2os16ClearSystemEventEPNS0_15SystemEventTypeE")))
        rt_fatal("codec: nn::os::ClearSystemEvent is not loaded");
    rt_call(c, clear, 1, ev);
}

// void RequestSyncPointEvent(SyncPointEventType *, const SyncPointHandle &): re-arms the event (cleared, as the last
// request may have left it signalled); a decoder fence (FENCE_TAG) fires when its buffer holds a picture, anything
// else at once, as the host has no sync point to wait for
static void ov_sp_request(Cpu *c) {
    const uint32_t *h = arg_p(c, 1);
    uint32_t tok = h ? *h : 0;
    uint64_t ev = event_for(c, arg_x(c, 0));
    clear_event(c, ev);
    int now = 1;
    if ((tok & 0xffff0000u) == FENCE_TAG && (tok >> 8 & 0xff) < DECODERS && (tok & 0xff) < SLOTS) {
        plat_mutex_lock(&lock);
        Slot *s = &decs[tok >> 8 & 0xff].slot[tok & 0xff];
        if (s->state == S_WAIT)
            for (int k = 0; k < WAITERS; k++)
                if (!s->waiter[k] || s->waiter[k] == ev) {
                    s->waiter[k] = ev, now = 0;
                    break;
                }
        plat_mutex_unlock(&lock);
    }
    TRACE("sync point request %#x: %s", tok, now ? "signalled at once" : "waits for its picture");
    if (now) codec_signal_event(c, ev);
}
// void CancelSyncPointEvent(SyncPointEventType *): the request is dropped and the event cleared
static void ov_sp_cancel(Cpu *c) {
    uint64_t ev = event_for(c, arg_x(c, 0));
    plat_mutex_lock(&lock);
    for (int k = 0; k < DECODERS; k++)
        for (int i = 0; i < SLOTS; i++)
            for (int j = 0; j < WAITERS; j++)
                if (decs[k].slot[i].waiter[j] == ev) decs[k].slot[i].waiter[j] = 0;
    plat_mutex_unlock(&lock);
    clear_event(c, ev);
}
// void DestroySyncPointEvent(SyncPointEventType *): the event stays bound for the next Create on the same object
static void ov_sp_nop(Cpu *c) { (void)c; }

// Result Get{Vp9,Av1}DecoderOutputBufferProperties(u16 *w, u16 *h, u16 *, u16 *, TimeSpan *pts, bool *end, Type *, u32 index)
// (Switch 2 SDK 20: no ColorSpace argument)
static void ov_props2(Cpu *c) {
    uint32_t i = (uint32_t)arg_x(c, 7);
    plat_mutex_lock(&lock);
    Dec *d = dec_of(arg_x(c, 6));
    Slot s = d && i < SLOTS ? d->slot[i] : (Slot){0};
    plat_mutex_unlock(&lock);
    for (int k = 0; k < 4; k++) {
        uint16_t *p = arg_p(c, k);
        if (p) *p = k & 1 ? s.h : s.w;
    }
    LOG_FIRST("codec: output properties: %ux%u", s.w, s.h);
    if (arg_p(c, 4)) *(int64_t *)arg_p(c, 4) = s.pts;
    if (arg_p(c, 5)) *(uint8_t *)arg_p(c, 5) = (uint8_t)s.eos;
    ret_x(c, d ? 0 : R_NOT_READY);
}
// SystemEventType *Get{Vp9,Av1}DecoderSubmissionReadyEvent(Type *)
static void ov_ready2(Cpu *c) {
    uint64_t ev = event_for(c, arg_x(c, 0));
    codec_signal_event(c, ev);
    ret_x(c, ev);
}
// Result UnregisterXxxDecoderBuffer(Type *, u32 index)
static void ov_unregister(Cpu *c) {
    uint32_t i = (uint32_t)arg_x(c, 1);
    plat_mutex_lock(&lock);
    Dec *d = dec_of(arg_x(c, 0));
    if (d && i < SLOTS) d->slot[i].pool = 0, d->slot[i].state = S_FREE;
    plat_mutex_unlock(&lock);
    ret_x(c, 0);
}
```

```c
// Adapted from MacNativeGames games/totk/runtime/frontend.m (nn::vi, lines 345-359) and gfx_bridge.c (nv, lines
// 74-86) @ b75be8cf (MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 MacNativeGames contributors). The nvnBootstrapLoader stop takes the place
// of MacNativeGames' NVN entry (third_party/d2r_gfx/gfx/nvn/hle_nvn.c:115-118); no code of it is copied.
// Graphics bring-up:
//   nv::*        record the game's allocator callbacks and graphics work memory (guest addresses) for the NVN layer
//   nn::vi::*    display, layer and native window identities; the vsync event is bound here
//   nvnBootstrapLoader   the end of --boot (rt_boot_event "nvn"); otherwise the synthetic address of an NVN proc (nvn_procs.c)

#define VI_R_INVALID 0xf601u   // MacNativeGames' result for a call on an unknown display or layer

static OvNvState nv;
static PlatMutex lock = PLAT_MUTEX_INIT;

const OvNvState *ov_nv_state(void) { return &nv; }

static void set_allocator(Cpu *c, OvNvAllocator *a) {
    plat_mutex_lock(&lock);
    *a = (OvNvAllocator){arg_x(c, 0), arg_x(c, 1), arg_x(c, 2), arg_x(c, 3)};
    plat_mutex_unlock(&lock);
}

// void nv::SetGraphicsAllocator(AllocateFunction, FreeFunction, ReallocateFunction, void *user)
static void ov_graphics_allocator(Cpu *c) { set_allocator(c, &nv.graphics); }
// void nv::SetGraphicsDevtoolsAllocator(AllocateFunction, FreeFunction, ReallocateFunction, void *user)
static void ov_devtools_allocator(Cpu *c) { set_allocator(c, &nv.devtools); }

// void nv::InitializeGraphics(void *memory, size_t size). TotK hands over a work buffer. the NVN 2 reference title (Switch 2)
// passes (0, 0) and leaves the driver to its allocator callbacks; nothing on the host reads the buffer, so that is fine.
static void ov_initialize_graphics(Cpu *c) {
    uint64_t mem = arg_x(c, 0), size = arg_x(c, 1);
    if (!mem != !size) rt_fatal("nv::InitializeGraphics: work memory %#llx with size %#llx", (unsigned long long)mem,
                                (unsigned long long)size);
    plat_mutex_lock(&lock);
    nv.memory = mem;
    nv.memory_size = size;
    nv.initialized = 1;
    plat_mutex_unlock(&lock);
    rt_log("nv: graphics work memory %#llx+%#llx recorded", (unsigned long long)mem,
           (unsigned long long)size);
}

// void nv::InitCheck(): aborts unless nv::InitializeGraphics ran, and that call is the host's (above), so the SDK's own
// flag is never set. the NVN 2 reference title calls it before nn::codec::video::Initialize when a tutorial guide movie starts.
static void ov_init_check(Cpu *c) { (void)c; }

// ---- nn::vi: the identities are small zeroed blocks in the guest-visible kernel region, in case SDK code reads them
static int vi_ready;
static void *display, *layer, *window;

// void nn::vi::Initialize()
static void ov_vi_initialize(Cpu *c) {
    (void)c;
    plat_mutex_lock(&lock);
    if (!display) {
        display = mem_kernel_alloc(64, 16);
        layer = mem_kernel_alloc(64, 16);
        window = mem_kernel_alloc(64, 16);
    }
    vi_ready = 1;
    plat_mutex_unlock(&lock);
}

static int vi_up(void) {
    plat_mutex_lock_shared(&lock);
    int r = vi_ready;
    plat_mutex_unlock_shared(&lock);
    return r;
}

// Result nn::vi::OpenDefaultDisplay(Display **out)
static void ov_open_display(Cpu *c) {
    void **out = arg_p(c, 0);
    if (!out || !vi_up()) { ret_x(c, VI_R_INVALID); return; }
    *out = display;
    ret_x(c, 0);
}

// Result nn::vi::CreateLayer(Layer **out, Display *display)
static void ov_create_layer(Cpu *c) {
    void **out = arg_p(c, 0);
    if (!out || !vi_up() || arg_p(c, 1) != display) { ret_x(c, VI_R_INVALID); return; }
    *out = layer;
    ret_x(c, 0);
}

// Result nn::vi::GetNativeWindow(void **out, Layer *layer): a placeholder the NVN layer recognises
static void ov_native_window(Cpu *c) {
    void **out = arg_p(c, 0);
    if (!out || !vi_up() || arg_p(c, 1) != layer) { ret_x(c, VI_R_INVALID); return; }
    *out = window;
    ret_x(c, 0);
}

// Result nn::vi::GetDisplayVsyncEvent(os::SystemEventType *event, Display *display): auto-clear system event
static void ov_vsync_event(Cpu *c) {
    uint64_t ev = arg_x(c, 0);
    if (!ev || !vi_up() || arg_p(c, 1) != display) { ret_x(c, VI_R_INVALID); return; }
    kern_bind_system_event(c, ev, 1);
    gfx_vsync_bind(ev);
    ret_x(c, 0);
}

// ---- Switch 2 vi calls (the NVN 2 reference title): the host presents SDR with a fixed swap interval and no VRR.

// void *nvnBootstrapLoader(const char *name): the first NVN call
static void ov_nvn_bootstrap(Cpu *c) {
    const char *name = arg_p(c, 0);
    if (!name) name = "(null)";
    static int32_t first = 1;
    if (rt_config()->boot && plat_xchg32(&first, 0)) rt_boot_event("nvn", c, name);   // ends --boot; returns
                                                                                                // when --seconds goes on
    ret_x(c, nvn_proc_address(name));
}

// registration runs at start-up instead of through boot.c.
```

```c
// Adapted from MacNativeGames games/totk/runtime/input.c and hid_feedback.c @ b75be8cf (MIT, Copyright (c) 2026
// MacNativeGames contributors).
// nn::hid overrides: one connected controller fed by input_poll (gamepad and keyboard,
// runtime/input_win.c; nothing pressed with TOTK_INPUT=none). Docked (default) it is a full-key controller as player 1 (id 0, style bit 0); with
// TOTK_OPERATION_MODE=handheld it is the handheld controller (id 0x20, style bit 1) and player 1 is not connected,
// which is the controller the game reads in that mode. Mouse and keyboard report no input. The controller has two
// vibration devices (left, right) played on the gamepad's motors (TOTK_RUMBLE=0: none) and a six-axis sensor fed by
// the gamepad's gyro and accelerometer (TOTK_MOTION=0, live: reads at rest). State layouts follow libnx HID.
#include <math.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "cfg.h"
#include "host.h"
#include "input.h"
#include "ov.h"
#include "platform/platform.h"

typedef struct { int64_t sampling; uint64_t buttons; int32_t lx, ly, rx, ry; uint32_t attributes, pad; } NpadState;
typedef struct { int64_t sampling; int32_t x, y, dx, dy, wx, wy; uint32_t buttons, attributes; } MouseState;
typedef struct { int64_t sampling; uint32_t modifiers, attributes; uint64_t keys[4]; } KeyboardState;
typedef struct { int8_t players; uint8_t pad[3]; uint32_t selected; } ControllerSupportResult;
_Static_assert(sizeof(NpadState) == 40 && sizeof(MouseState) == 40 && sizeof(KeyboardState) == 48, "hid state ABI");
_Static_assert(sizeof(ControllerSupportResult) == 8, "controller support result ABI");

enum { STYLE_FULL_KEY = 1, STYLE_HANDHELD = 2, ATTR_CONNECTED = 1 };

static PlatMutex lock = PLAT_MUTEX_INIT;
static uint32_t styles = STYLE_FULL_KEY;
static int enabled, allowed = 1, mouse_ready, keyboard_ready;
static int64_t sample;

static uint32_t pad_id(void) { return ov_handheld() ? 0x20u : 0u; }
static uint32_t pad_style(void) { return ov_handheld() ? STYLE_HANDHELD : STYLE_FULL_KEY; }

static const uint32_t *need_id(Cpu *c, int i, const char *fn) {
    const uint32_t *id = arg_p(c, i);
    if (!id) rt_fatal("nn::hid::%s: null controller id", fn);
    return id;
}

// void InitializeNpad()
static void ov_initialize_npad(Cpu *c) {
    (void)c;
    plat_mutex_lock(&lock);
    enabled = 1;
    plat_mutex_unlock(&lock);
    rt_log("hid: controllers initialized (one connected %s controller)",
           ov_handheld() ? "handheld" : "full-key");
}

// void SetSupportedNpadIdType(const NpadIdType *ids, size_t count)
static void ov_supported_ids(Cpu *c) {
    const uint32_t *ids = arg_p(c, 0);
    uint64_t n = arg_x(c, 1);
    if (n > 10 || (!ids && n)) rt_fatal("nn::hid::SetSupportedNpadIdType: invalid id list (%llu ids)", (unsigned long long)n);
    int ok = 0;
    for (uint64_t i = 0; i < n; i++) ok |= ids[i] == pad_id();
    plat_mutex_lock(&lock);
    allowed = ok;
    plat_mutex_unlock(&lock);
}

// void SetSupportedNpadStyleSet(NpadStyleSet styles)
static void ov_supported_styles(Cpu *c) {
    plat_mutex_lock(&lock);
    styles = (uint32_t)arg_x(c, 0);
    plat_mutex_unlock(&lock);
}

// NpadStyleSet GetNpadStyleSet(const NpadIdType &id)
static void ov_style_set(Cpu *c) {
    uint32_t id = *need_id(c, 0, "GetNpadStyleSet");
    plat_mutex_lock_shared(&lock);
    uint32_t v = enabled && allowed && id == pad_id() ? styles & pad_style() : 0;
    plat_mutex_unlock_shared(&lock);
    ret_x(c, v);
}

// int GetNpadStates(<State> *out, int count, const NpadIdType &id): the newest state only. want: the style of the
// overload, 0 for the Joy-Con overloads (never connected).
static void npad_states(Cpu *c, uint32_t want) {
    NpadState *out = arg_p(c, 0);
    int max = (int)arg_x(c, 1);
    uint32_t id = *need_id(c, 2, "GetNpadStates");
    if (max <= 0) { ret_x(c, 0); return; }
    if (!out) rt_fatal("nn::hid::GetNpadStates: null output");
    plat_mutex_lock(&lock);
    NpadState s = {.sampling = ++sample};
    int live = want && enabled && allowed && id == pad_id() && want == pad_style() && (styles & want);
    plat_mutex_unlock(&lock);
    if (live) {
        s.attributes = ATTR_CONNECTED;
        input_poll(&s.buttons, &s.lx, &s.ly, &s.rx, &s.ry);
    }
    *out = s;
    ret_x(c, 1);
}
static void ov_states_full_key(Cpu *c) { npad_states(c, STYLE_FULL_KEY); }
static void ov_states_handheld(Cpu *c) { npad_states(c, STYLE_HANDHELD); }
static void ov_states_joycon(Cpu *c) { npad_states(c, 0); }

// void SetNpadJoyHoldType(NpadJoyHoldType type)
static void ov_hold_type(Cpu *c) {
    int64_t t = (int32_t)arg_x(c, 0);
    if (t < 0 || t > 1) rt_fatal("nn::hid::SetNpadJoyHoldType: invalid hold type %lld", (long long)t);
}

// void DisconnectNpad(const NpadIdType &id): only the controller in use (handheld mode disconnects player 1)
static void ov_disconnect(Cpu *c) {
    uint32_t id = *need_id(c, 0, "DisconnectNpad");
    if (id != pad_id()) return;
    plat_mutex_lock(&lock);
    allowed = 0;
    plat_mutex_unlock(&lock);
}

// Result ShowControllerSupport(ControllerSupportResultInfo *out, const ControllerSupportArg &arg): the one controller
// is already connected, so the applet returns at once with one player on it.
static void ov_controller_support(Cpu *c) {
    ControllerSupportResult *out = arg_p(c, 0);
    if (out) *out = (ControllerSupportResult){.players = 1, .selected = pad_id()};
    ret_x(c, 0);
}

static void ov_initialize_mouse(Cpu *c) {
    (void)c;
    plat_mutex_lock(&lock);
    mouse_ready = 1;
    plat_mutex_unlock(&lock);
}

static void ov_initialize_keyboard(Cpu *c) {
    (void)c;
    plat_mutex_lock(&lock);
    keyboard_ready = 1;
    plat_mutex_unlock(&lock);
}

// int GetMouseStates(MouseState *out, int count): a mouse that is not connected
static void ov_mouse_states(Cpu *c) {
    MouseState *out = arg_p(c, 0);
    int max = (int)arg_x(c, 1);
    if (max <= 0) { ret_x(c, 0); return; }
    if (!out) rt_fatal("nn::hid::GetMouseStates: null output");
    plat_mutex_lock(&lock);
    if (!mouse_ready) rt_fatal("nn::hid::GetMouseStates before InitializeMouse");
    *out = (MouseState){.sampling = ++sample};
    plat_mutex_unlock(&lock);
    ret_x(c, 1);
}

// void GetKeyboardState(KeyboardState *out): a keyboard with no key down
static void ov_keyboard_state(Cpu *c) {
    KeyboardState *out = arg_p(c, 0);
    if (!out) rt_fatal("nn::hid::GetKeyboardState: null output");
    plat_mutex_lock(&lock);
    if (!keyboard_ready) rt_fatal("nn::hid::GetKeyboardState before InitializeKeyboard");
    *out = (KeyboardState){.sampling = ++sample};
    plat_mutex_unlock(&lock);
}

// ---- vibration and six-axis sensor (MacNativeGames hid_feedback.c)
// Handles are the SDK's (nn::hid::utility, sdk+0x4a6e00 and sdk+0x4a6ab0): byte 0 the style index (3 full-key,
// 4 handheld), byte 1 the controller id, byte 2 the device (vibration 0 left / 1 right, six-axis 2). Every call under
// the public functions goes through nn::hid::detail (sdk's PLT), answered here instead of by the hid service, including
// the batches VibrationTarget queues through detail::EnqueueVibrationValue into detail::SendVibrationValues.
// VibrationValue {amplitude low, frequency low, amplitude high, frequency high}: 0..1 and Hz, neutral 0/160/0/320.
typedef struct { float amp_low, freq_low, amp_high, freq_high; } VibrationValue;
typedef struct { uint32_t type, position; } VibrationDeviceInfo;   // type 1 linear resonant actuator; position 1 left, 2 right
_Static_assert(sizeof(VibrationValue) == 16 && sizeof(VibrationDeviceInfo) == 8, "vibration ABI");

enum { STYLE_INDEX_FULL_KEY = 3, STYLE_INDEX_HANDHELD = 4, SIX_AXIS_DEVICE = 2, RUMBLE_MS = 250 };
#define RUMBLE_STALE_NS 250000000ull     // a side the game has not updated for 250 ms is silent
#define RUMBLE_REFRESH_NS 50000000ull    // an unchanged value is sent again every 50 ms (its 250 ms start over)
#define RUMBLE_MIN_GAP_NS 10000000ull    // a changed value at most every 10 ms (the game streams every few ms)
static const VibrationValue vib_neutral = {0, 160, 0, 320};

static int env_zero(const char *name) {
    const char *e = cfg_get(name);
    return e && !strcmp(e, "0");
}

static void once(volatile int32_t *flag, const char *fmt, uint32_t v) {
    if (!plat_xchg32(flag, 1)) rt_log(fmt, v);
}

// TOTK_RUMBLE_STRENGTH (percent, 0..300, default 130; 0 = off) and TOTK_RUMBLE_CURVE (exponent on the amplitude, 0.2..1.5,
// default 0.6). HD rumble is strong at low amplitude, an ERM motor hardly turns there, so weak values are lifted by the
// curve (0.1 -> 0.25) and the strength scales the result (saturating at 65535; 0.66 and up reach full drive at 130 %).
// Both are live settings (the menu): read again whenever cfg_version changes.
static float rumble_strength = 1.3f, rumble_curve = 0.6f;
static volatile int32_t rumble_cfg_logged;
static unsigned rumble_cfg_seen = ~0u;
static float cfg_float(const char *name, float lo, float hi) {
    double v = cfg_double(name);
    return (float)(v < lo ? lo : v > hi ? hi : v);
}
static void rumble_cfg(void) {
    unsigned v = cfg_version();
    if (v == rumble_cfg_seen) return;
    rumble_cfg_seen = v;
    rumble_strength = cfg_float("TOTK_RUMBLE_STRENGTH", 0, 300) / 100;
    rumble_curve = cfg_float("TOTK_RUMBLE_CURVE", 0.2f, 1.5f);
    int trig = input_rumble_triggers_enabled();
    if (!plat_xchg32(&rumble_cfg_logged, 1))
        rt_log("hid: rumble strength %.0f%%, curve %.2f, triggers %s", rumble_strength * 100, rumble_curve, trig ? "on" : "off");
}
static uint16_t motor(float a) { return rumble_motor(a, rumble_curve, rumble_strength); }

static uint32_t pad_style_index(void) { return ov_handheld() ? STYLE_INDEX_HANDHELD : STYLE_INDEX_FULL_KEY; }

// The SDK's id check (utility functions): players 1-8, other (0x10) and handheld (0x20); the public functions abort
// on another id.
static uint32_t handle_id(Cpu *c, const char *fn) {
    uint32_t id = *need_id(c, 2, fn);
    if (id >= 8 && id != 0x10 && id != 0x20) rt_fatal("nn::hid::%s: invalid controller id %#x", fn, id);
    return id;
}

// int GetVibrationDeviceHandles(VibrationDeviceHandle *out, int count, const NpadIdType &id, NpadStyleSet style):
// utility::GetVibrationDeviceHandles' table, the first style bit in its order; none with TOTK_RUMBLE=0.
static void ov_vibration_handles(Cpu *c) {
    uint32_t *out = arg_p(c, 0), style = (uint32_t)arg_x(c, 3);
    int max = (int)arg_x(c, 1);
    uint32_t id = handle_id(c, "GetVibrationDeviceHandles");
    if (!out || max <= 0 || __builtin_popcount(style) != 1)
        rt_fatal("nn::hid::GetVibrationDeviceHandles: invalid arguments (count %d, styles %#x)", max, style);
    static volatile int32_t asked;
    rumble_cfg();
    // strength 0 keeps the devices (silent), so the menu can turn rumble up again
    if (env_zero("TOTK_RUMBLE")) { once(&asked, "hid: no vibration devices (TOTK_RUMBLE=%u)", 0); ret_x(c, 0); return; }
    static const struct { uint8_t bit, n; uint32_t base; } t[] = {
        {0, 2, 0x3}, {1, 2, 0x4}, {2, 2, 0x5}, {3, 1, 0x6}, {4, 1, 0x10007}, {5, 1, 0x8}, {10, 1, 0xd}, {8, 2, 0x4},
        {30, 2, 0x21}, {29, 2, 0x20}};
    int n = 0;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof t / sizeof *t && !n; i++) {
        if (!(style >> t[i].bit & 1)) continue;
        n = t[i].n < max ? t[i].n : max;
        for (int k = 0; k < n; k++) out[k] = (t[i].base | id << 8) + ((uint32_t)k << 16);
    }
    once(&asked, "hid: the game asked for its vibration devices (first handle %#x)", n ? out[0] : 0);
    ret_x(c, (uint64_t)n);
}

// int GetSixAxisSensorHandles(SixAxisSensorHandle *out, int count, const NpadIdType &id, NpadStyleSet style):
// utility::GetSixAxisSensorHandle's order (one sensor per style, two for the Joy-Con pair). Also with TOTK_MOTION=0: the
// sensor then reads at rest (six_fill), so the menu can turn motion on while the game runs.
static void ov_six_axis_handles(Cpu *c) {
    uint32_t *out = arg_p(c, 0), style = (uint32_t)arg_x(c, 3);
    int max = (int)arg_x(c, 1);
    uint32_t id = handle_id(c, "GetSixAxisSensorHandles");
    if (!out || max <= 0) rt_fatal("nn::hid::GetSixAxisSensorHandles: invalid arguments (count %d)", max);
    static volatile int32_t asked;
    uint32_t base = 0, n = 1;
    if (style & 1) base = 0x20003;
    else if (style & 2) base = 0x20004;
    else if (style & 4) base = 0x5, n = 2;
    else if (style & 8) base = 0x6;
    else if (style & 0x10) base = 0x10007;
    else if (style & 0x20) base = 0x20003;
    else if (style & 0xe80) n = 0;
    else if (style & 0x100) base = 0x20004;
    else if ((style & 0x60000040) == 0x40) base = 0x20003;
    else n = 0;
    if (n > (uint32_t)max) n = (uint32_t)max;
    for (uint32_t k = 0; k < n; k++) out[k] = (base | id << 8) + (k << 16);
    once(&asked, "hid: the game asked for its six-axis sensor (first handle %#x)", n ? out[0] : 0);
    ret_x(c, n);
}

static const uint32_t *need_handle(const void *p, const char *fn) {
    if (!p) rt_fatal("nn::hid::detail::%s: null handle", fn);
    return p;
}

// The vibration device (0 left, 1 right) a handle names on the connected controller, or -1 (logged once).
static int vibration_side(const uint32_t *h, const char *fn) {
    uint32_t v = *need_handle(h, fn), dev = v >> 16 & 0xff;
    if ((v & 0xff) == pad_style_index() && (v >> 8 & 0xff) == pad_id() && dev < 2) return (int)dev;
    static volatile int32_t warned;
    once(&warned, "hid: vibration call for handle %#x, not a device of the connected controller: ignored", v);
    return -1;
}

static PlatMutex vib_lock = PLAT_MUTEX_INIT;
static VibrationValue vib_last[2] = {{0, 160, 0, 320}, {0, 160, 0, 320}};   // vib_lock
static uint64_t vib_at[2], sent_at;                                          // vib_lock
static uint16_t sent_low, sent_high;                                         // vib_lock
static int vib_allowed = 1;                                                  // vib_lock: PermitVibration

static float clamp01(float v) { return v > 0 ? (v < 1 ? v : 1) : 0; }   // NaN -> 0
// Share of a band at f Hz that goes to the light (high-frequency, right) motor: none at 160 Hz and below (the low band's
// neutral frequency), all at 320 Hz and above (the high band's), log scale between.
static float light_share(float f) { return f > 160 ? (f < 320 ? log2f(f / 160) : 1) : 0; }

// Switch HD rumble -> SDL_RumbleGamepad. Each side's two bands split by frequency between the heavy (low) and the light
// (high) motor (light_share) and add up as energy per motor (root of the summed squares); the stronger side drives each
// motor. A side the game has not updated for 250 ms is silent. Each send lasts 250 ms and is renewed every 50 ms while
// the game streams, so the pad stops by itself when the game stops sending (pause, freeze). Under vib_lock.
static void rumble_update(uint64_t now) {
    float heavy = 0, light = 0;
    rumble_cfg();
    for (int s = 0; s < 2 && vib_allowed; s++) {
        if (!vib_at[s] || now - vib_at[s] > RUMBLE_STALE_NS) continue;
        const VibrationValue *v = &vib_last[s];
        float al = clamp01(v->amp_low), ah = clamp01(v->amp_high), sl = light_share(v->freq_low), sh = light_share(v->freq_high);
        float h = sqrtf(al * (1 - sl) * al * (1 - sl) + ah * (1 - sh) * ah * (1 - sh));
        float l = sqrtf(al * sl * al * sl + ah * sh * ah * sh);
        if (h > heavy) heavy = h;
        if (l > light) light = l;
    }
    uint16_t lo = motor(clamp01(heavy)), hi = motor(clamp01(light));
    int changed = lo != sent_low || hi != sent_high, on = lo || hi;
    if (changed ? on && now - sent_at < RUMBLE_MIN_GAP_NS : !on || now - sent_at < RUMBLE_REFRESH_NS) return;
    input_rumble(lo, hi, on ? RUMBLE_MS : 0);
    sent_low = lo, sent_high = hi, sent_at = now;
}

static void play(int side, const VibrationValue *v) {
    if (!v) rt_fatal("nn::hid::detail::SendVibrationValue: null value");
    if (side < 0) return;
    VibrationValue c = *v;
    if (!isfinite(c.amp_low) || !isfinite(c.amp_high) || !isfinite(c.freq_low) || !isfinite(c.freq_high)) c = vib_neutral;
    static volatile int32_t first, first_on;
    if (!plat_xchg32(&first, 1))
        rt_log("hid: first vibration value from the game: %s %.2f@%.0f Hz %.2f@%.0f Hz", side ? "right" : "left",
               (double)c.amp_low, (double)c.freq_low, (double)c.amp_high, (double)c.freq_high);
    if ((c.amp_low > 0.01f || c.amp_high > 0.01f) && !plat_xchg32(&first_on, 1))
        rt_log("hid: first non-zero vibration from the game: %s %.2f@%.0f Hz %.2f@%.0f Hz", side ? "right" : "left",
               (double)c.amp_low, (double)c.freq_low, (double)c.amp_high, (double)c.freq_high);
    uint64_t now = kern_now_ns();
    plat_mutex_lock(&vib_lock);
    vib_last[side] = c;
    vib_at[side] = now;
    rumble_update(now);
    plat_mutex_unlock(&vib_lock);
}

// Result detail::InitializeVibrationDevice(const VibrationDeviceHandle &)
static void ov_vib_init(Cpu *c) {
    static volatile int32_t logged;
    const uint32_t *h = arg_p(c, 0);
    if (vibration_side(h, "InitializeVibrationDevice") >= 0)
        once(&logged, "hid: the game initialized its vibration devices (handle %#x)", *h);
    ret_x(c, 0);
}

// Result detail::SendVibrationValue(const VibrationDeviceHandle &, const VibrationValue &)
static void ov_vib_send(Cpu *c) {
    play(vibration_side(arg_p(c, 0), "SendVibrationValue"), arg_p(c, 1));
    ret_x(c, 0);
}

// Result detail::SendVibrationValues(const VibrationDeviceHandle *, const VibrationValue *, int count)
static void ov_vib_send_many(Cpu *c) {
    const uint32_t *h = arg_p(c, 0);
    const VibrationValue *v = arg_p(c, 1);
    int n = (int)arg_x(c, 2);
    if (n < 0 || (n && (!h || !v))) rt_fatal("nn::hid::detail::SendVibrationValues: invalid batch (%d values)", n);
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) play(vibration_side(&h[i], "SendVibrationValues"), &v[i]);
    ret_x(c, 0);
}

// Result detail::GetActualVibrationValue(VibrationValue *out, const VibrationDeviceHandle &): the last value sent
static void ov_vib_actual(Cpu *c) {
    VibrationValue *out = arg_p(c, 0);
    if (!out) rt_fatal("nn::hid::detail::GetActualVibrationValue: null output");
    int side = vibration_side(arg_p(c, 1), "GetActualVibrationValue");
    VibrationValue v = vib_neutral;
    plat_mutex_lock_shared(&vib_lock);
    if (side >= 0) v = vib_last[side];
    plat_mutex_unlock_shared(&vib_lock);
    *out = v;
    ret_x(c, 0);
}

// Result detail::GetVibrationDeviceInfo(VibrationDeviceInfo *out, const VibrationDeviceHandle &)
static void ov_vib_info(Cpu *c) {
    VibrationDeviceInfo *out = arg_p(c, 0);
    if (!out) rt_fatal("nn::hid::detail::GetVibrationDeviceInfo: null output");
    int side = vibration_side(arg_p(c, 1), "GetVibrationDeviceInfo");
    *out = side >= 0 ? (VibrationDeviceInfo){1, (uint32_t)side + 1} : (VibrationDeviceInfo){0, 0};
    ret_x(c, 0);
}

// Result detail::IsVibrationDeviceMounted(bool *out, const VibrationDeviceHandle &)
static void ov_vib_mounted(Cpu *c) {
    uint8_t *out = arg_p(c, 0);
    if (!out) rt_fatal("nn::hid::detail::IsVibrationDeviceMounted: null output");
    *out = vibration_side(arg_p(c, 1), "IsVibrationDeviceMounted") >= 0;
    ret_x(c, 0);
}

// Result detail::IsVibrationPermitted(bool *out)
static void ov_vib_permitted(Cpu *c) {
    uint8_t *out = arg_p(c, 0);
    if (!out) rt_fatal("nn::hid::detail::IsVibrationPermitted: null output");
    plat_mutex_lock_shared(&vib_lock);
    *out = (uint8_t)vib_allowed;
    plat_mutex_unlock_shared(&vib_lock);
    ret_x(c, 0);
}

// Result detail::PermitVibration(bool): off silences the gamepad at once
static void ov_vib_permit(Cpu *c) {
    int on = (arg_x(c, 0) & 0xff) != 0;
    plat_mutex_lock(&vib_lock);
    vib_allowed = on;
    rumble_update(kern_now_ns());
    plat_mutex_unlock(&vib_lock);
    ret_x(c, 0);
}

static volatile int32_t six_running;   // StartSixAxisSensor .. StopSixAxisSensor

static int six_axis_ours(const uint32_t *h, const char *fn) {
    uint32_t v = *need_handle(h, fn);
    if ((v & 0xff) == pad_style_index() && (v >> 8 & 0xff) == pad_id() && (v >> 16 & 0xff) == SIX_AXIS_DEVICE) return 1;
    static volatile int32_t warned;
    once(&warned, "hid: six-axis call for handle %#x, not the connected controller's sensor: reads at rest", v);
    return 0;
}

// Result detail::StartSixAxisSensor(const SixAxisSensorHandle &): angle and direction start over
static void ov_six_start(Cpu *c) {
    const uint32_t *h = arg_p(c, 0);
    if (six_axis_ours(h, "StartSixAxisSensor")) {
        static volatile int32_t logged;
        once(&logged, "hid: the game started the six-axis sensor (handle %#x)", *h);
        motion_restart(motion_global());
        input_motion_start();
        plat_xchg32(&six_running, 1);
    }
    ret_x(c, 0);
}

// Result detail::StopSixAxisSensor(const SixAxisSensorHandle &)
static void ov_six_stop(Cpu *c) {
    if (six_axis_ours(arg_p(c, 0), "StopSixAxisSensor")) plat_xchg32(&six_running, 0);
    ret_x(c, 0);
}

// All max entries, newest first: the game reads all 16 it asks for and ignores the count (main+0x2a268e0). A short
// history repeats its oldest sample. No motion (sensor not started, no gamepad, one without a gyro, TOTK_MOTION=0):
// a controller lying still, not marked connected.
static int six_fill(MotionState *s, int max, const uint32_t *h, const char *fn) {
    if (max <= 0) return 0;
    if (!s) rt_fatal("nn::hid::detail::%s: null output", fn);
    int live = six_axis_ours(h, fn) && six_running && input_motion_enabled();
    int n = live ? motion_read(motion_global(), s, max, kern_now_ns()) : 0;
    if (!n) {
        static const MotionState rest = {.acc = {0, 0, -1}, .dir = {1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1}};
        for (int i = 0; i < max; i++) s[i] = rest;
    } else
        for (int i = n; i < max; i++) s[i] = s[n - 1];
    static volatile int32_t first_rest, first_live;
    if (!n && six_running) once(&first_rest, "hid: six-axis read with no motion samples: at rest (%u states)", (uint32_t)max);
    if (n) once(&first_live, "hid: first six-axis read with live motion (%u samples)", (uint32_t)n);
    return max;
}

// Result detail::GetSixAxisSensorStates(int *count, SixAxisSensorState *out, int max, const SixAxisSensorHandle &)
static void ov_six_states(Cpu *c) {
    int32_t *count = arg_p(c, 0);
    if (!count) rt_fatal("nn::hid::detail::GetSixAxisSensorStates: null count");
    *count = six_fill(arg_p(c, 1), (int)arg_x(c, 2), arg_p(c, 3), "GetSixAxisSensorStates");
    ret_x(c, 0);
}

// Result detail::GetSixAxisSensorState(SixAxisSensorState *out, const SixAxisSensorHandle &)
static void ov_six_state(Cpu *c) {
    six_fill(arg_p(c, 0), 1, arg_p(c, 1), "GetSixAxisSensorState");
    ret_x(c, 0);
}

// ---- Switch 2 SDK (the NVN 2 reference title): public names for what TotK's SDK had under nn::hid::detail, and the
// touch screen and Joy-Con assignment calls TotK never made.

// int GetSixAxisSensorStates(SixAxisSensorState *out, int count, const SixAxisSensorHandle &): the count is returned
static void ov_six_states_public(Cpu *c) {
    ret_x(c, (uint64_t)(int64_t)six_fill(arg_p(c, 0), (int)arg_x(c, 1), arg_p(c, 2), "GetSixAxisSensorStates"));
}

// void InitializeTouchScreen(): there is no touch screen on the host
static void ov_touch_init(Cpu *c) {
    static volatile int32_t logged;
    (void)c;
    once(&logged, "hid: the game initialized the touch screen (none on this host)", 0);
}

// Touch screen states: the host has no touch screen, so state queries return 0 touches with increasing sampling numbers.
static volatile int64_t g_touch_sampling;

// void GetTouchScreenState<1>(TouchScreenState<1> *out): sampling number, then a count of 0 touches
static void ov_touch_state1(Cpu *c) {
    uint8_t *out = arg_p(c, 0);
    if (!out) rt_fatal("nn::hid::GetTouchScreenState: null output");
    memset(out, 0, 0x38);   // int64 sampling number, int32 count, int32 reserved, one 0x28-byte TouchState
    int64_t n = __atomic_add_fetch(&g_touch_sampling, 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    memcpy(out, &n, 8);
}

static void ov_touch_state1_detail(Cpu *c) {
    uint8_t *out = arg_p(c, 0);
    if (!out) { ret_x(c, 0x802); return; }
    memset(out, 0, 0x38);
    int64_t n = __atomic_add_fetch(&g_touch_sampling, 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    memcpy(out, &n, 8);
    ret_x(c, 0);
}

static void ov_touch_states1_public(Cpu *c) {
    uint8_t *out = arg_p(c, 0);
    int max = (int)arg_x(c, 1);
    if (!out || max <= 0) { ret_x(c, 0); return; }
    int count = max > 1 ? 1 : max;
    memset(out, 0, (size_t)count * 0x38);
    int64_t n = __atomic_add_fetch(&g_touch_sampling, (int64_t)count, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        int64_t sn = n - count + i + 1;
        memcpy(out + i * 0x38, &sn, 8);
    }
    ret_x(c, (uint64_t)(int64_t)count);
}

static void ov_touch_state16(Cpu *c) {
    uint8_t *out = arg_p(c, 0);
    if (!out) rt_fatal("nn::hid::GetTouchScreenState: null output");
    memset(out, 0, 0x290);
    int64_t n = __atomic_add_fetch(&g_touch_sampling, 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    memcpy(out, &n, 8);
}

static void ov_touch_state16_detail(Cpu *c) {
    uint8_t *out = arg_p(c, 0);
    if (!out) { ret_x(c, 0x802); return; }
    memset(out, 0, 0x290);
    int64_t n = __atomic_add_fetch(&g_touch_sampling, 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    memcpy(out, &n, 8);
    ret_x(c, 0);
}

static void ov_touch_states16_public(Cpu *c) {
    uint8_t *out = arg_p(c, 0);
    int max = (int)arg_x(c, 1);
    if (!out || max <= 0) { ret_x(c, 0); return; }
    int count = max > 16 ? 16 : max;
    memset(out, 0, (size_t)count * 0x290);
    int64_t n = __atomic_add_fetch(&g_touch_sampling, (int64_t)count, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        int64_t sn = n - count + i + 1;
        memcpy(out + i * 0x290, &sn, 8);
    }
    ret_x(c, (uint64_t)(int64_t)count);
}

static void ov_touch_states16_detail(Cpu *c) {
    int32_t *out_count = arg_p(c, 0);
    uint8_t *out = arg_p(c, 1);
    int max = (int)arg_x(c, 2);
    if (out_count) *out_count = 0;
    if (!out || max <= 0) { ret_x(c, 0); return; }
    int count = max > 16 ? 16 : max;
    memset(out, 0, (size_t)count * 0x290);
    int64_t n = __atomic_add_fetch(&g_touch_sampling, (int64_t)count, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        int64_t sn = n - count + i + 1;
        memcpy(out + i * 0x290, &sn, 8);
    }
    if (out_count) *out_count = count;
    ret_x(c, 0);
}

// void SetNpadJoyAssignmentModeDual(const NpadIdType &), SetNpadJoyAssignmentModeSingle(const NpadIdType &,
// NpadJoyDeviceType), Result MergeSingleJoyAsDualJoy(const NpadIdType &, const NpadIdType &): the host's one pad is
// always a full controller, so the assignment mode changes nothing
static void ov_joy_assignment(Cpu *c) { ret_x(c, 0); }
static void ov_hid_noop(Cpu *c) { (void)c; }
static void ov_hid_zero(Cpu *c) { ret_x(c, 0); }
static void ov_nmouse_types(Cpu *c) {
    uint32_t *out = arg_p(c, 0);
    if (out) *out = 0;
```
