```h
// Between perf.c (frame timing, always built) and the OS's sampling profiler (prof_win.c on Windows).
#pragma once
#include <stdint.h>

extern volatile uint32_t prof_render_tid;   // the thread that presents (perf_present)
extern volatile uint32_t prof_main_tid;     // the guest main thread (perf_main_thread)
extern volatile uint32_t prof_replay_tid;   // the asynchronous replay (perf_replay_thread): its waits hold up the frame too

// The sampler; perf.c's weak versions do nothing.
int prof_sampler_start(void);               // TOTK_PROFILE: starts sampling; 1 when it runs
void prof_sampler_write(void);              // writes the profile once (prof_write)
void prof_sampler_frame(uint64_t frame, uint64_t now, uint64_t d);   // every present; d: the interval, 0 on the first

```

`runtime/prof_win.c`:

```c
// Sampling profiler (TOTK_PROFILE=<path>) and per-frame timing (TOTK_TRACE=perf). tools/prof_report.py reads the profile.
// A host thread wakes every 1 ms and, for every other thread, suspends it, reads Rip and resumes it. The sampler never
// allocates or takes a lock between SuspendThread and ResumeThread and never runs guest code. The profile is text:
//   totk-prof 1 / base <hex> / period_us / samples N / thread <tid> <samples> <in-exe samples> / module <base> <size> <path> /
//   rip <hex> <count> (the top PROF_TOP Rips) / stack <count> <rip> <caller> ... (TOTK_PROFILE_RENDER or
//   TOTK_PROFILE_CHAINS only, the top PROF_STACKS call chains)
// With TOTK_PROFILE_RENDER (the render thread) or TOTK_PROFILE_CHAINS=1 (every thread, chains of all threads summed: for
// short frame ranges, as each sample copies a stack) the sampler also copies up to STK_COPY bytes of the suspended
// thread's stack and, after
// ResumeThread, unwinds the copy with the .pdata tables (RtlVirtualUnwind), so it takes no lock while the thread is
// suspended. The unwind stops at the first frame outside the copy; deeper callers are cut.
// TOTK_PROFILE_SLOW=<ms> keeps every thread's chains of the last half second in a ring (a thread outside the exe, mostly
// waiting, copies 8 KiB of stack, one in it STK_COPY; a thread that ran no cycle since its previous sample is not
// suspended and repeats its previous chain; a sample that took over 2 ms to stop its thread, which happens while the
// thread is in a long kernel call, is written as `tstall <tid> <ms into the window> <ms stopping> <rip>...` with the
// chain where the thread stopped) and, after a present at least <ms> after the previous one, writes
// that interval's samples (plus the 20 ms before) to <TOTK_PROFILE>.f<frame>: the profile format, one `stack 1` line per
// sample, and `tstack <tid> <ms into the window> <rip>...` lines that keep the thread and the time. At most 64 dumps.
#include <windows.h>
#include <psapi.h>
#include <tlhelp32.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "cfg.h"
#include "flight.h"
#include "gfx.h"
#include "host.h"
#include "perfmon.h"
#include "prof.h"

#define render_tid prof_render_tid
#define main_tid prof_main_tid
#define replay_tid prof_replay_tid

#define PROF_SLOTS (1u << 16)   // Rip hash table, open addressing; a full table drops new Rips
#define PROF_TOP 4000           // more than the 200 asked for: the report sums per function
#define PROF_THREADS 512
#define STK_SLOTS (1u << 15)      // call-chain hash table, open addressing; a full table drops new chains
#define PROF_STACKS 6000
#define STK_COPY (64u << 10)      // stack bytes copied per sample
#define STK_SLACK (64u << 10)     // zeros after the copy: a frame reaching past it reads zeros, and a zero Rip ends the chain

typedef struct { uint64_t rip, n; } RipCount;
#define PROF_DEPTH 24             // frames kept per call chain, the sampled Rip first
// cycles, depth, last: TOTK_PROFILE_SLOW only, the thread's cycle count and chain at its previous sample
typedef struct { DWORD tid; HANDLE h; uint64_t n, in_exe, cycles; uint32_t depth; uint64_t last[PROF_DEPTH]; } ThreadSlot;

static RipCount table[PROF_SLOTS];
typedef struct { uint64_t hash, n; uint32_t depth; uint64_t rip[PROF_DEPTH]; } StackCount;
static StackCount stacks[STK_SLOTS];
static uint64_t stacks_dropped;
static uint8_t stk_buf[STK_COPY + STK_SLACK] __attribute__((aligned(16)));   // the slack is never written
static ThreadSlot threads[PROF_THREADS];
static int n_threads;
static uint64_t total, dropped;
static const char *out_path;
static HANDLE sampler;
static volatile LONG stop, written;
static uintptr_t exe_lo, exe_hi;
static int only_render;             // TOTK_PROFILE_RENDER=1: sample the render thread only
static int only_main;               // TOTK_PROFILE_MAIN=1: sample the guest main thread only
static int chains;                  // call chains are kept: TOTK_PROFILE_RENDER or TOTK_PROFILE_CHAINS
static volatile uint64_t cur_frame; // last presented frame
static uint64_t frame_lo, frame_hi; // TOTK_PROFILE_FRAMES=<lo>-<hi>: sample only while presents lo..hi-1 are pending
static int64_t world_lo, world_hi;  // TOTK_PROFILE_FRAMES=w<lo>-<hi>: only while the world clock is in [lo, hi) s (us)

#define SLOW_RING (1u << 15)        // TOTK_PROFILE_SLOW: about 0.5 s of samples of every thread
#define SLOW_DUMPS 64
typedef struct { uint64_t t; DWORD tid; uint32_t depth; uint64_t rip[PROF_DEPTH]; } Sample;
static Sample ring[SLOW_RING];
static uint64_t ring_n;
#define STALL_RING 1024
static Sample stalls[STALL_RING];   // t: when the stop began; rip[PROF_DEPTH - 1] holds the stop's ns
static uint64_t stall_n;
static uint64_t slow_ns;            // TOTK_PROFILE_SLOW in ns, 0 off
static volatile LONG64 dump_lo, dump_hi, dump_frame;   // the render thread asks for a window, the sampler writes it

static void count_rip(uint64_t rip) {
    uint32_t i = (uint32_t)((rip * 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15ull) >> 48);
    for (uint32_t k = 0; k < 64; k++, i = (i + 1) & (PROF_SLOTS - 1)) {
        if (table[i].rip == rip || !table[i].rip) {
            table[i].rip = rip;
            table[i].n++;
            return;
        }
    }
    dropped++;
}

static void count_stack(const uint64_t *rip, uint32_t depth) {
    uint64_t h = 0xcbf29ce484222325ull;
    for (uint32_t d = 0; d < depth; d++) h = (h ^ rip[d]) * 0x100000001b3ull;
    h |= 1;   // 0 marks a free slot
    uint32_t i = (uint32_t)(h >> 49);
    for (uint32_t k = 0; k < 64; k++, i = (i + 1) & (STK_SLOTS - 1)) {
        StackCount *s = &stacks[i];
        if (!s->hash) {
            s->hash = h, s->depth = depth;
            memcpy(s->rip, rip, depth * sizeof *rip);
        } else if (s->hash != h || s->depth != depth || memcmp(s->rip, rip, depth * sizeof *rip)) {
            continue;
        }
        s->n++;
        return;
    }
    stacks_dropped++;
}

// Unwinds the stack copied to stk_buf from real address lo (n bytes). Registers that point into the copied range are
// moved into the copy, so frame-pointer frames read the copy too. Returns the number of frames.
static uint32_t unwind_copy(CONTEXT *c, uintptr_t lo, size_t n, uint64_t *rip) {
    uintptr_t buf = (uintptr_t)stk_buf, end = buf + n;
    DWORD64 *regs[] = {&c->Rbx, &c->Rbp, &c->Rsi, &c->Rdi, &c->R12, &c->R13, &c->R14, &c->R15};
    for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof regs / sizeof *regs; i++)
        if (*regs[i] >= lo && *regs[i] < lo + n) *regs[i] = *regs[i] - lo + buf;
    c->Rsp = buf;
    uint32_t d = 0;
    while (d < PROF_DEPTH && c->Rip && c->Rsp >= buf && c->Rsp + 8 <= end) {
        rip[d++] = c->Rip;
        DWORD64 base;
        PRUNTIME_FUNCTION f = RtlLookupFunctionEntry(c->Rip, &base, NULL);
        if (f) {
            void *hd;
            DWORD64 est;
            RtlVirtualUnwind(UNW_FLAG_NHANDLER, base, c->Rip, f, c, &hd, &est, NULL);
        } else {   // a leaf function: the return address is on top
            c->Rip = *(DWORD64 *)c->Rsp;
            c->Rsp += 8;
        }
    }
    return d;
}

// Re-lists the process's threads: keeps the handle of a thread seen before, opens new ones, closes the gone ones.
static void refresh_threads(DWORD self) {
    HANDLE snap = CreateToolhelp32Snapshot(TH32CS_SNAPTHREAD, 0);
    if (snap == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) return;
    static ThreadSlot next[PROF_THREADS];
    int n = 0;
    THREADENTRY32 te = {.dwSize = sizeof te};
    DWORD pid = GetCurrentProcessId();
    for (BOOL ok = Thread32First(snap, &te); ok; ok = Thread32Next(snap, &te)) {
        if (te.th32OwnerProcessID != pid || te.th32ThreadID == self || n == PROF_THREADS) continue;
        ThreadSlot *old = NULL;
        for (int i = 0; i < n_threads; i++)
            if (threads[i].tid == te.th32ThreadID) old = &threads[i];
        if (old) {
            next[n++] = *old;
            old->h = NULL;
        } else {
            HANDLE h = OpenThread(THREAD_SUSPEND_RESUME | THREAD_GET_CONTEXT | THREAD_QUERY_INFORMATION, FALSE, te.th32ThreadID);
            if (h) next[n++] = (ThreadSlot){.tid = te.th32ThreadID, .h = h};
        }
    }
    CloseHandle(snap);
    for (int i = 0; i < n_threads; i++)
        if (threads[i].h) CloseHandle(threads[i].h);   // exited; its counts are lost with the slot
    memcpy(threads, next, sizeof(ThreadSlot) * n);
    n_threads = n;
}

static void write_modules(FILE *f) {
    HMODULE mods[1024];
    DWORD need = 0;
    if (!EnumProcessModules(GetCurrentProcess(), mods, sizeof mods, &need)) return;
    for (DWORD i = 0; i < need / sizeof(HMODULE) && i < 1024; i++) {
        MODULEINFO mi;
        char path[MAX_PATH];
        if (GetModuleInformation(GetCurrentProcess(), mods[i], &mi, sizeof mi) && GetModuleFileNameA(mods[i], path, sizeof path))
            fprintf(f, "module %llx %lx %s\n", (unsigned long long)(uintptr_t)mi.lpBaseOfDll, mi.SizeOfImage, path);
    }
}

// The sampler, between ticks: the samples of the window the render thread asked for.
static void slow_dump(void) {
    uint64_t lo = (uint64_t)dump_lo, hi = (uint64_t)dump_hi, frame = (uint64_t)dump_frame;
    static int dumps;
    char path[1100];
    snprintf(path, sizeof path, "%s.f%llu", out_path, (unsigned long long)frame);
    FILE *f = dumps < SLOW_DUMPS ? fopen(path, "w") : NULL;
    if (f) {
        dumps++;
        fprintf(f, "totk-prof 1\nbase %llx\nperiod_us 1000\nframe %llu interval_ms %.1f\nmain %u render %u replay %u\n",
                (unsigned long long)(uintptr_t)GetModuleHandleW(NULL), (unsigned long long)frame, (hi - lo) / 1e6 - 20,
                main_tid, render_tid, replay_tid);
        write_modules(f);
        uint64_t first = ring_n > SLOW_RING ? ring_n - SLOW_RING : 0;
        for (int pass = 0; pass < 2; pass++)
            for (uint64_t k = first; k < ring_n; k++) {
                const Sample *s = &ring[k & (SLOW_RING - 1)];
                if (s->t < lo || s->t > hi) continue;
                if (pass) fprintf(f, "tstack %lu %.1f", s->tid, (s->t - lo) / 1e6);
                else fprintf(f, "stack 1");
                for (uint32_t d = 0; d < s->depth; d++) fprintf(f, " %llx", (unsigned long long)s->rip[d]);
                fputc('\n', f);
            }
        for (uint64_t k = stall_n > STALL_RING ? stall_n - STALL_RING : 0; k < stall_n; k++) {
            const Sample *s = &stalls[k & (STALL_RING - 1)];
            if (s->t + s->rip[PROF_DEPTH - 1] < lo || s->t > hi) continue;
            fprintf(f, "tstall %lu %.1f %.1f", s->tid, ((double)s->t - (double)lo) / 1e6, s->rip[PROF_DEPTH - 1] / 1e6);
            for (uint32_t d = 0; d < s->depth; d++) fprintf(f, " %llx", (unsigned long long)s->rip[d]);
            fputc('\n', f);
        }
        fclose(f);
        rt_log("prof: slow frame %llu (%.1f ms) -> %s", (unsigned long long)frame, (hi - lo) / 1e6 - 20, path);
    }
    InterlockedExchange64(&dump_hi, 0);
}

// TOTK_PROFILE_FRAMES: 1 while the present or world-clock range holds (always without one). It bounds the sampling and
// the TOTK_PROFILE_SLOW dumps alike, so the 64 dumps are not spent on the slow frames of the boot.
static int in_window(void) {
    if (frame_hi && (cur_frame < frame_lo || cur_frame >= frame_hi)) return 0;
    if (world_hi) {   // -1 before the world clock starts
        int64_t w = frame_step_world_us();
        if (w < world_lo || w >= world_hi) return 0;
    }
    return 1;
}

static DWORD WINAPI sampler_main(void *arg) {
    (void)arg;
    DWORD self = GetCurrentThreadId();
    SetThreadPriority(GetCurrentThread(), THREAD_PRIORITY_TIME_CRITICAL);
    HANDLE timer = CreateWaitableTimerExW(NULL, NULL, CREATE_WAITABLE_TIMER_HIGH_RESOLUTION, TIMER_ALL_ACCESS);
    static CONTEXT ctx __attribute__((aligned(16)));
    for (unsigned tick = 0; !stop; tick++) {
        if (timer) {
            LARGE_INTEGER due = {.QuadPart = -10000};   // 1 ms
            SetWaitableTimer(timer, &due, 0, NULL, NULL, FALSE);
            WaitForSingleObject(timer, 10);
        } else {
            Sleep(1);
        }
        if (tick % 64 == 0) refresh_threads(self);
        if (dump_hi) slow_dump();
        if (!in_window()) continue;
        uint64_t now = slow_ns ? kern_now_ns() : 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < n_threads; i++) {
            ThreadSlot *t = &threads[i];
            if ((only_render && t->tid != render_tid) || (only_main && t->tid != main_tid)) continue;
            uint64_t cyc = 0;
            if (slow_ns && t->depth && QueryThreadCycleTime(t->h, &cyc) && cyc == t->cycles) {   // still waiting
                Sample *s = &ring[ring_n++ & (SLOW_RING - 1)];
                s->t = now, s->tid = t->tid, s->depth = t->depth;
                memcpy(s->rip, t->last, t->depth * sizeof *t->last);
                continue;
            }
            ctx.ContextFlags = chains ? CONTEXT_CONTROL | CONTEXT_INTEGER : CONTEXT_CONTROL;
            uint64_t stop0 = slow_ns ? kern_now_ns() : 0;
            if (SuspendThread(t->h) == (DWORD)-1) continue;
            BOOL ok = GetThreadContext(t->h, &ctx);   // returns once the thread has stopped in user mode
            uint64_t stop_ns = slow_ns ? kern_now_ns() - stop0 : 0;
            size_t n = 0;
            MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION mb;
            // a thread stopped between its sub rsp and the stack probe has Rsp in the guard page: touching it would fault
            if (ok && chains && VirtualQuery((void *)ctx.Rsp, &mb, sizeof mb) && mb.State == MEM_COMMIT &&
                !(mb.Protect & (PAGE_GUARD | PAGE_NOACCESS))) {
                n = (uintptr_t)mb.BaseAddress + mb.RegionSize - ctx.Rsp;   // the committed stack above Rsp
                size_t cap = slow_ns && (ctx.Rip < exe_lo || ctx.Rip >= exe_hi) ? 8u << 10 : STK_COPY;
                if (n > cap) n = cap;
                memcpy(stk_buf, (void *)ctx.Rsp, n);
            }
            ResumeThread(t->h);
            if (!ok) continue;
            count_rip(ctx.Rip);
            uint64_t chain[PROF_DEPTH] = {ctx.Rip};
            uint32_t d = n ? unwind_copy(&ctx, ctx.Rsp, n, chain) : 0;
            if (d) count_stack(chain, d);
            if (slow_ns) {
                Sample *s = &ring[ring_n++ & (SLOW_RING - 1)];
                s->t = now, s->tid = t->tid, s->depth = d ? d : 1;
                memcpy(s->rip, chain, s->depth * sizeof *chain);
                if (stop_ns > 2000000) {
                    Sample *w = &stalls[stall_n++ & (STALL_RING - 1)];
                    *w = *s;
                    w->t = stop0;
                    if (w->depth > PROF_DEPTH - 1) w->depth = PROF_DEPTH - 1;
                    w->rip[PROF_DEPTH - 1] = stop_ns;
                }
                QueryThreadCycleTime(t->h, &t->cycles);   // after ResumeThread: the cycles the sample itself cost
                t->depth = s->depth;
                memcpy(t->last, chain, s->depth * sizeof *chain);
            }
            total++;
            t->n++;
            if (ctx.Rip >= exe_lo && ctx.Rip < exe_hi) t->in_exe++;
        }
    }
    return 0;
}

static int cmp_desc(const void *a, const void *b) {
    uint64_t x = ((const RipCount *)a)->n, y = ((const RipCount *)b)->n;
    return (x < y) - (x > y);
}

static int cmp_stack_desc(const void *a, const void *b) {
    uint64_t x = ((const StackCount *)a)->n, y = ((const StackCount *)b)->n;
    return (x < y) - (x > y);
}

void prof_sampler_write(void) {
    if (!out_path || InterlockedExchange(&written, 1)) return;
    InterlockedExchange(&stop, 1);
    if (WaitForSingleObject(sampler, 2000) != WAIT_OBJECT_0) return;   // sampler stuck: no half-written counts
    FILE *f = fopen(out_path, "w");
    if (!f) {
        rt_log("prof: cannot write %s", out_path);
        return;
    }
    fprintf(f, "totk-prof 1\nbase %llx\nperiod_us 1000\nsamples %llu\ndropped %llu\n", (unsigned long long)(uintptr_t)GetModuleHandleW(NULL),
            (unsigned long long)total, (unsigned long long)dropped);
    for (int i = 0; i < n_threads; i++)
        fprintf(f, "thread %lu %llu %llu\n", threads[i].tid, (unsigned long long)threads[i].n, (unsigned long long)threads[i].in_exe);
    write_modules(f);
    int cnt = 0;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < PROF_SLOTS; i++)
        if (table[i].rip) table[cnt++] = table[i];
    qsort(table, cnt, sizeof *table, cmp_desc);
    for (int i = 0; i < cnt && i < PROF_TOP; i++) fprintf(f, "rip %llx %llu\n", (unsigned long long)table[i].rip, (unsigned long long)table[i].n);
    int ns = 0;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < STK_SLOTS; i++)
        if (stacks[i].hash) stacks[ns++] = stacks[i];
    qsort(stacks, ns, sizeof *stacks, cmp_stack_desc);
    for (int i = 0; i < ns && i < PROF_STACKS; i++) {
        fprintf(f, "stack %llu", (unsigned long long)stacks[i].n);
        for (uint32_t d = 0; d < stacks[i].depth; d++) fprintf(f, " %llx", (unsigned long long)stacks[i].rip[d]);
        fputc('\n', f);
    }
    if (stacks_dropped) fprintf(f, "stacks_dropped %llu\n", (unsigned long long)stacks_dropped);
    fclose(f);
    rt_log("prof: %llu samples, %d Rips -> %s", (unsigned long long)total, cnt, out_path);
}

int prof_sampler_start(void) {
    out_path = cfg_get("TOTK_PROFILE");
    if (!out_path || !*out_path) {
        out_path = NULL;
        return 0;
    }
    only_render = cfg_get("TOTK_PROFILE_RENDER") != NULL;
    only_main = !only_render && cfg_get("TOTK_PROFILE_MAIN") != NULL;
    const char *ch = cfg_get("TOTK_PROFILE_CHAINS");
    const char *sl = cfg_get("TOTK_PROFILE_SLOW");
    slow_ns = sl && atoi(sl) > 0 ? (uint64_t)atoi(sl) * 1000000ull : 0;
    chains = only_render || only_main || slow_ns || (ch && *ch && strcmp(ch, "0"));
    const char *fr = cfg_get("TOTK_PROFILE_FRAMES");
    double wl, wh;
    if (fr && fr[0] == 'w' && sscanf(fr + 1, "%lf-%lf", &wl, &wh) == 2 && wl >= 0 && wl < wh)
        world_lo = (int64_t)(wl * 1e6), world_hi = (int64_t)(wh * 1e6);
    else if (fr && sscanf(fr, "%llu-%llu", (unsigned long long *)&frame_lo, (unsigned long long *)&frame_hi) != 2) frame_hi = 0;
    MODULEINFO mi;
    if (GetModuleInformation(GetCurrentProcess(), GetModuleHandleW(NULL), &mi, sizeof mi)) {
        exe_lo = (uintptr_t)mi.lpBaseOfDll;
        exe_hi = exe_lo + mi.SizeOfImage;
    }
    sampler = CreateThread(NULL, 0, sampler_main, NULL, 0, NULL);
    if (!sampler) {
        rt_log("prof: cannot start the sampler (error %lu)", GetLastError());
        out_path = NULL;
        return 0;
    }
    return 1;
}

// perf_present, every present: the frame the sampler's TOTK_PROFILE_FRAMES window counts, and a TOTK_PROFILE_SLOW
// dump of a present at least slow_ns after the previous one (d 0 on the first present).
void prof_sampler_frame(uint64_t frame, uint64_t now, uint64_t d) {
    cur_frame = frame;
    if (slow_ns && d >= slow_ns && !dump_hi && in_window()) {
        dump_lo = (LONG64)(now - d - 20000000ull);
        dump_frame = (LONG64)frame;
        InterlockedExchange64(&dump_hi, (LONG64)now);
    }
}
```

`runtime/rdoc.c`:

```c
// RenderDoc in-app capture (debug tool). TOTK_RDOC=<frame>[,<frame>...] captures those presented frames; TOTK_RDOC_DIR is the
// output directory (default build/captures); TOTK_RDOC_DLL overrides the library's path (renderdoc.dll, librenderdoc.so).
// Only the API fields used are declared here (layout of RENDERDOC_API_1_4_1, renderdoc_app.h, MIT), so no RenderDoc header
// is vendored.
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "cfg.h"
#include "host.h"
#include "vk.h"
#include "platform/platform.h"

#define RDOC_API_1_4_1 10401
#define RDOC_MAX_FRAMES 64

typedef struct {
    void *GetAPIVersion;
    uint32_t (*SetCaptureOptionU32)(int opt, uint32_t val);
    void *fn2_10[9];    // SetCaptureOptionF32 .. UnloadCrashHandler
    void (*SetCaptureFilePathTemplate)(const char *);
    void *GetCaptureFilePathTemplate;
    uint32_t (*GetNumCaptures)(void);
    uint32_t (*GetCapture)(uint32_t idx, char *filename, uint32_t *pathlength, uint64_t *timestamp);
    void *TriggerCapture, *IsTargetControlConnected, *LaunchReplayUI, *SetActiveWindow;
    void (*StartFrameCapture)(void *device, void *window);
    uint32_t (*IsFrameCapturing)(void);
    uint32_t (*EndFrameCapture)(void *device, void *window);
} RdocApi;

static RdocApi *api;
static uint64_t targets[RDOC_MAX_FRAMES];
static int n_targets;
static int capturing;

int rdoc_active(void) { return api != NULL; }

void rdoc_init(void) {
    const char *e = cfg_get("TOTK_RDOC");
    if (!e || !*e) return;
    for (const char *p = e; *p && n_targets < RDOC_MAX_FRAMES;) {
        char *end;
        unsigned long long v = strtoull(p, &end, 10);
        if (end == p) break;
        targets[n_targets++] = v;
        p = *end == ',' ? end + 1 : end;
        if (*end != ',') break;
    }
    if (!n_targets) { rt_log("rdoc: TOTK_RDOC=%s has no frame numbers", e); return; }
    const char *dll = cfg_get("TOTK_RDOC_DLL");
#ifdef _WIN32
    const char *def = "C:/Program Files/RenderDoc/renderdoc.dll";
#else
    const char *def = "librenderdoc.so";
#endif
    void *m = plat_lib_open(dll && *dll ? dll : def);
    if (!m) { rt_log("rdoc: cannot load %s; set TOTK_RDOC_DLL", dll && *dll ? dll : def); return; }
    int (*get_api)(int, void **) = (int (*)(int, void **))plat_lib_sym(m, "RENDERDOC_GetAPI");
    void *a = NULL;
    if (!get_api || get_api(RDOC_API_1_4_1, &a) != 1 || !a) { rt_log("rdoc: RENDERDOC_GetAPI(1.4.1) failed"); return; }
    api = a;
    // Option ids of eRENDERDOC_CaptureOption: 8 RefAllResources, 9 SaveAllInitials, 12 AllowUnsupportedVendorExtensions.
    // The back end imports guest pages with VK_EXT_external_memory_host, which RenderDoc hides unless 12 is set.
    rt_log("rdoc: AllowUnsupportedVendorExtensions -> %u", api->SetCaptureOptionU32(12, 1));
    api->SetCaptureOptionU32(8, 1);
    api->SetCaptureOptionU32(9, 1);
    const char *dir = cfg_get("TOTK_RDOC_DIR");
    char full[PLAT_PATH_MAX], tmpl[PLAT_PATH_MAX + 16];
    if (!plat_full_path(dir && *dir ? dir : "build/captures", full, sizeof full)) return;
    plat_file_mkdir_p(full);
    snprintf(tmpl, sizeof tmpl, "%s/totk", full);
    api->SetCaptureFilePathTemplate(tmpl);
    rt_log("rdoc: ready, %d frame(s), captures %s", n_targets, full);
}

// Called by vk_be_present after frame `frame` was queued and the present drained. A capture of frame N starts after frame N-1's
// present finished and ends after frame N's present, so it holds frame N's submits and its blit/present.
void rdoc_after_present(uint64_t frame) {
    if (!api) return;
    if (capturing) {
        api->EndFrameCapture(NULL, NULL);
        capturing = 0;
        char path[PLAT_PATH_MAX];
        uint32_t len = sizeof path, n = api->GetNumCaptures();
        if (n && api->GetCapture(n - 1, path, &len, NULL)) rt_log("rdoc: frame %llu captured: %s", (unsigned long long)frame, path);
        else rt_log("rdoc: frame %llu capture failed", (unsigned long long)frame);
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n_targets; i++)
        if (targets[i] == frame + 1) { api->StartFrameCapture(NULL, NULL); capturing = 1; rt_log("rdoc: capture of frame %llu started", (unsigned long long)(frame + 1)); }
}
```

`runtime/resolution.c`:

```c
// Game resolution: the size the game composes its frame in (its output: canvas, UI and swapchain) and the size of its
// 3D scene, above the shipped 1920x1080 and 1600x900. The game does the rendering itself, as with the community
// resolution mods (UltraCam, Visual Fixes): the patch sets output and scene (recomp/patches-v121.txt,
// patches-v143.txt; MacNativeGames games/totk/runtime/game_patches.c and game_patches_v143.c, MIT, Copyright (c) 2026
// MacNativeGames contributors) make the game read both sizes from the patch page, and the texture heap that holds the
// output- and scene-sized render targets grows with them.
//
// Settings, read at start: TOTK_OUTPUT_RES = <w>x<h> (default 1920x1080, the game's own), TOTK_RENDER_SCALE = the
// scene's size relative to the output: "game" (default, 5/6, the game's 1600x900 at 1080p) or a percentage; above 100
// the game supersamples its scene, which smooths edges (anti-aliasing) at the cost of GPU time. The game's own final
// pass (FSR 1 EASU) scales the scene to the output; the present scales the output to the window (vk_fsr.c).
//
// Patch page: +16 the scene size {w, h} as floats, +32 the output size and +48 the swapchain size as {w, h} in one
// 64-bit word, +40 the renderer (1.2.1) or display configuration (1.4.3) the patched code stores there.
// +56 the camera's aspect ratio as a float when the output is not 16:9 (set aspect), +60 the field-of-view factor
// (set fov, res_fov_live).
// 1.4.3 scales the scene it reads by output width / 1920 (a 2560x1440 output renders its 1600x900 scene at 2128x1200;
// MacNativeGames measured the same), so its page holds the wanted size divided by that factor and the game's 5/6 needs
// no scene patch. 1.2.1 renders the size it reads (1600x900 on a 2560x1440 output): its page holds the wanted size, and
// the scene set is on whenever the output differs from 1920x1080.
//
// Heap: agl's DynamicTextureAllocator is one fixed heap, "DynamicTextureAllocatorMem" in
// System/HeapSize/Product.Nin_NX_NVN.HeapDef.byml.zs (113664 KiB, carved from "Graphics", 201728 KiB). At 2560x1440
// the shipped size runs out at the title screen. Both heaps grow by the same amount: the shipped size times the output's
// pixel ratio above 1920x1080 plus the scene's above 1600x900 (MacNativeGames' measurement: a 3440x1440 canvas with a
// 4620x1935 scene crashed at +258 MiB and loaded at +400 MiB; this formula gives +750 MiB there). romfs.c serves the
// rewritten table (res_heapdef_build) in place of the original; memory.c adds the amount to the application pool, so
// no other heap shrinks. Without the rewritten table (a RomFS that lacks it, a format this code does not know) the
// patch sets stay off and the game keeps its own sizes.
#include <math.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <zstd.h>

#include "cfg.h"
#include "host.h"

#define BASE_W 1920
#define BASE_H 1080
#define SCENE_W 1600
#define SCENE_H 900
#define DTA_KIB 113664u      // DynamicTextureAllocatorMem, shipped
#define SCENE_MAX 4096       // per side, as MacNativeGames' TOTK_RENDER_RES

static struct {
    int decided;
    unsigned ow, oh, sw, sh;   // output and scene
    int scene_set;             // the scene differs from the game's 5/6 of the output
    int heapdef_ok;            // romfs.c serves the grown HeapDef
    int on;                    // res_init switched the patch sets on
} R;

static void decide(void) {
    static char last_out[64] = {0};
    static char last_scale[64] = {0};

    const char *o = cfg_value("TOTK_OUTPUT_RES");
    const char *s = cfg_value("TOTK_RENDER_SCALE");
    if (!o) o = "1920x1080";
    if (!s) s = "game";

    if (R.decided && !strcmp(o, last_out) && !strcmp(s, last_scale))
        return;
    R.decided = 1;
    snprintf(last_out, sizeof last_out, "%s", o);
    snprintf(last_scale, sizeof last_scale, "%s", s);

    R.ow = BASE_W;
    R.oh = BASE_H;
    unsigned w = 0, h = 0;
    char tail;
    if (sscanf(o, "%ux%u%c", &w, &h, &tail) == 2 && w >= 1280 && h >= 720 && w <= 7680 && h <= 4320) {
        R.ow = w & ~1u;
        R.oh = h & ~1u;
    } else {
        rt_log("resolution: TOTK_OUTPUT_RES=%s is not <width>x<height> in 1280x720..7680x4320; 1920x1080", o);
    }

    double k = 5.0 / 6.0;
    if (strcmp(s, "game")) {
        char *end;
        double pct = strtod(s, &end);
        if (end != s && !*end && pct >= 25 && pct <= 400) {
            k = pct / 100.0;
            R.scene_set = 1;
        } else {
            rt_log("resolution: TOTK_RENDER_SCALE=%s is not game or a percentage 25..400; using game", s);
        }
    }
    double sw = R.ow * k, sh = R.oh * k;
    double fit = fmin(1.0, fmin(SCENE_MAX / sw, SCENE_MAX / sh));
    if (fit < 1.0) R.scene_set = 1;
    R.sw = (unsigned)(sw * fit + 0.5) & ~1u;
    R.sh = (unsigned)(sh * fit + 0.5) & ~1u;
}

static int bigger(void) {
    decide();
    return R.ow != BASE_W || R.oh != BASE_H || R.scene_set;
}

uint64_t res_heap_extra_kib(void) {
    if (!bigger()) return 0;
    double grow = fmax(0.0, (double)R.ow * R.oh / (BASE_W * BASE_H) - 1.0) +
                  fmax(0.0, (double)R.sw * R.sh / (SCENE_W * SCENE_H) - 1.0);
    if (grow <= 0) return 0;
    return (uint64_t)ceil(DTA_KIB * (1.0 + grow) / 1024.0) * 1024 - DTA_KIB;
}

uint64_t res_heap_extra_bytes(void) { return ((res_heap_extra_kib() << 10) + 0x1fffff) & ~0x1fffffull; }

// ---- the HeapDef table. BYML version 2..7, little endian ("YB"): a hash node is {u8 0xC1, u24 count} and count
// entries {u24 key index, u8 type, u32 value}; an int (type 0xD1) is stored in the entry, so a size changes in place.
typedef struct { uint8_t *p; size_t n; uint32_t keys; } Byml;

static int u32_at(const Byml *b, size_t off, uint32_t *v) {
    if (off + 4 > b->n) return 0;
    memcpy(v, b->p + off, 4);
    return 1;
}

static const char *key_name(const Byml *b, uint32_t k) {
    uint32_t head, at;
    if (!u32_at(b, b->keys, &head) || (head & 0xff) != 0xc2 || k >= head >> 8 || !u32_at(b, b->keys + 4 + 4 * k, &at) ||
        b->keys + at >= b->n || !memchr(b->p + b->keys + at, 0, b->n - b->keys - at))
        return NULL;
    return (const char *)b->p + b->keys + at;
}

// The offset of the value of hash node `node`'s entry `name`, which must have type `type`; 0 when there is none.
static size_t field(const Byml *b, uint32_t node, const char *name, uint8_t type) {
    uint32_t head;
    if (!u32_at(b, node, &head) || (head & 0xff) != 0xc1) return 0;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < head >> 8; i++) {
        uint32_t e;
        if (!u32_at(b, node + 4 + 8 * (size_t)i, &e)) return 0;
        const char *k = key_name(b, e & 0xffffff);
        if (k && !strcmp(k, name)) return e >> 24 == type ? node + 8 + 8 * (size_t)i : 0;
    }
    return 0;
}

static size_t heap_size_field(const Byml *b, uint32_t heaps, const char *heap) {
    size_t at = field(b, heaps, heap, 0xc1);
    uint32_t node;
    return at && u32_at(b, at, &node) ? field(b, node, "Size", 0xd1) : 0;
}

int res_heapdef_build(const void *in, size_t n, void **out, size_t *out_n) {
    uint64_t extra = res_heap_extra_kib();
    *out = NULL;
    if (!extra) return 0;
    if (ZSTD_getDictID_fromFrame(in, n)) {
        rt_log("resolution: the HeapDef table needs a zstd dictionary; the game keeps its own resolution");
        return 0;
    }
    unsigned long long raw = ZSTD_getFrameContentSize(in, n);
    if (raw == ZSTD_CONTENTSIZE_UNKNOWN || raw == ZSTD_CONTENTSIZE_ERROR || raw > (64u << 20)) {
        rt_log("resolution: the HeapDef table is not a zstd frame with a size; the game keeps its own resolution");
        return 0;
    }
    Byml b = {malloc((size_t)raw), (size_t)raw, 0};
    if (!b.p) return 0;
    size_t got = ZSTD_decompress(b.p, b.n, in, n);
    uint32_t root, heaps = 0;
    uint16_t ver = 0;
    if (!ZSTD_isError(got) && got == b.n && b.n >= 16) memcpy(&ver, b.p + 2, 2);
    size_t heaps_at = 0, dta_at = 0, gfx_at = 0;
    if (ver >= 2 && ver <= 7 && !memcmp(b.p, "YB", 2) && u32_at(&b, 4, &b.keys) && u32_at(&b, 12, &root) &&
        (heaps_at = field(&b, root, "Heaps", 0xc1)) && u32_at(&b, heaps_at, &heaps)) {
        dta_at = heap_size_field(&b, heaps, "DynamicTextureAllocatorMem");
        gfx_at = heap_size_field(&b, heaps, "Graphics");
    }
    if (!dta_at || !gfx_at) {
        rt_log("resolution: the HeapDef table has no DynamicTextureAllocatorMem / Graphics sizes; the game keeps its own "
               "resolution");
        free(b.p);
        return 0;
    }
    int32_t dta, gfx;
    memcpy(&dta, b.p + dta_at, 4);
    memcpy(&gfx, b.p + gfx_at, 4);
    int32_t dta2 = dta + (int32_t)extra, gfx2 = gfx + (int32_t)extra;
    memcpy(b.p + dta_at, &dta2, 4);
    memcpy(b.p + gfx_at, &gfx2, 4);
    size_t cap = ZSTD_compressBound(b.n);
    void *z = malloc(cap);
    size_t zn = z ? ZSTD_compress(z, cap, b.p, b.n, 9) : 0;
    free(b.p);
    if (!z || ZSTD_isError(zn)) {
        free(z);
        return 0;
    }
    *out = z;
    *out_n = zn;
    rt_log("resolution: HeapDef DynamicTextureAllocatorMem %d -> %d KiB, Graphics %d -> %d KiB", dta, dta2, gfx, gfx2);
    return 1;
}

void res_heapdef_served(void) { R.heapdef_ok = 1; }

// ---- start: the patch page and the sets
static uint64_t pack(unsigned w, unsigned h) { return (uint64_t)h << 32 | w; }

void res_init(void) {
    if (!bigger()) {
        rt_log("resolution: the game's own (output 1920x1080, scene 1600x900)");
        return;
    }
    int output = rt_patch_set("output"), scene = rt_patch_set("scene");
    if (output < 0 || scene < 0) {
        rt_log("resolution: the generated C has no output and scene patch sets; the game keeps its own resolution");
        return;
    }
    fs_init();   // romfs.c serves the grown HeapDef from here on (res_heapdef_served)
    if (res_heap_extra_kib() && !R.heapdef_ok) {   // sizes at or below the shipped ones fit the shipped heaps
        rt_log("resolution: no grown HeapDef table; the game keeps its own resolution");
        return;
    }
    uint8_t *page = rt_patch_page();
    double k = RT_V143 ? (double)R.ow / BASE_W : 1.0;   // 1.4.3's own scaling of the scene with the output width
    int scene_on = R.scene_set || (!RT_V143 && (R.ow != BASE_W || R.oh != BASE_H));
    float sc[2] = {(float)(R.sw / k), (float)(R.sh / k)};
    uint64_t out = pack(R.ow, R.oh), none = 0;
    memcpy(page + 16, sc, sizeof sc);
    memcpy(page + 32, &out, 8);
    memcpy(page + 40, &none, 8);
    memcpy(page + 48, &out, 8);
    rt_patch_switch(output, R.ow != BASE_W || R.oh != BASE_H);
    rt_patch_switch(scene, scene_on);
    R.on = 1;
    // Another shape than 16:9 (more than 1% off): the camera takes the output's ratio (recomp/patches-v121.txt and
    // patches-v143.txt, set aspect), so a 21:9 output shows more of the world at the sides instead of a stretched 16:9 view. The HUD's layouts
    // for that shape come from romfs-patches-<w>x<h> (romfs.c overlay_init, tools/make_romfs_patches.py --aspect).
    double ratio = (double)R.ow / R.oh, game = (double)BASE_W / BASE_H;
    int aspect = rt_patch_set("aspect");
    if (!res_is_16x9(R.ow, R.oh)) {
        if (aspect < 0) {
            rt_log("resolution: output %ux%u is not 16:9 and this game version has no camera aspect patch; the view "
                   "is stretched", R.ow, R.oh);
        } else {
            float r = (float)ratio;
            memcpy(page + 56, &r, sizeof r);
            rt_patch_switch(aspect, 1);
            rt_log("resolution: camera aspect ratio %.4f (16:9 is %.4f)", ratio, game);
        }
    } else {
        rt_patch_switch(aspect, 0);   // the page holds no ratio
    }
    rt_log("resolution: output %ux%u, scene %ux%u%s; texture heap +%llu KiB", R.ow, R.oh, R.sw, R.sh,
           scene_on ? "" : " (the game's own 5/6 of the output)", (unsigned long long)res_heap_extra_kib());
}

// 16:9 within 1% (1366x768 counts): the shape the game's own layouts and camera are made for.
int res_is_16x9(unsigned w, unsigned h) {
    double rel = ((double)w / h) / ((double)BASE_W / BASE_H);
    return rel >= 0.99 && rel <= 1.01;
}

// The game resolution asks for a romfs-patches-<w>x<h> overlay: it is not 16:9 and the game version has the camera
// aspect patch (set aspect); the UI layouts of another shape only fit a camera that follows the same shape.
int res_wants_wide_overlay(const unsigned out[2]) {
    return !res_is_16x9(out[0], out[1]) && rt_patch_set("aspect") >= 0;
}

// Field of view (TOTK_FOV, percent of the game's own, 70..140, live): the camera's vertical view angle times the
// factor on page +60 (recomp/patches-v143.txt, set fov). The horizontal angle follows through the aspect ratio. 100
// switches the set off, so the camera code is the game's own. Runs on a settings change (gfx_present.c
// window_settings_live), the first time at the first present.
#define FOV_MIN 70
#define FOV_MAX 140
void res_fov_live(void) {
    static int set = -2, shown = 100;
    if (set == -2) set = rt_patch_set("fov");
    int pct = cfg_int("TOTK_FOV");
    pct = pct < FOV_MIN ? FOV_MIN : pct > FOV_MAX ? FOV_MAX : pct;
    if (pct == shown) return;
    shown = pct;
    if (set < 0) {
        rt_log("resolution: this game version has no field-of-view patch; TOTK_FOV=%d does nothing", pct);
        return;
    }
    float k = pct / 100.0f;
    memcpy((uint8_t *)rt_patch_page() + 60, &k, sizeof k);   // before the switch: a site that sees it on reads k
    rt_patch_switch(set, pct != 100);
    rt_log("resolution: field of view %d%% of the game's", pct);
}

void res_wanted(unsigned out[2]) {
    decide();
    out[0] = R.ow, out[1] = R.oh;
}

void res_sizes(unsigned out[2], unsigned scene[2]) {
    decide();
    out[0] = R.ow ? R.ow : BASE_W;
    out[1] = R.oh ? R.oh : BASE_H;
    scene[0] = R.sw ? R.sw : SCENE_W;
    scene[1] = R.sh ? R.sh : SCENE_H;
}

```

`runtime/romfs.c`:

```c
// Adapted from MacNativeGames games/totk/runtime/romfs.c @ b75be8cf (MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 MacNativeGames
// contributors).
// Read-only game RomFS backed by the player's extracted image.
//
// Input: <romfs>/romfs.bin (rt_config()->romfs), whose six IVFC levels and SHA-256 tools/extract.py verified, and
// romfs-index.bin next to totk.exe (TOTK_ROMFS_INDEX overrides), which tools/romfs_index.py wrote together with
// romfs_config.h. fs_init checks the index's SHA-256 and layout and the image size. The full 17 GB hash runs only with
// TOTK_ROMFS_VERIFY=full; a proof file (.romfs-verified-v1 next to the index, or in TOTK_ROMFS_PROOF_DIR) keyed by
// the file's volume, file id, size and times skips it on later starts, TOTK_ROMFS_VERIFY=force ignores the proof.
//
// Reads are positional (platform.h plat_file_pread), so threads read the image in parallel without a file-pointer
// lock. TOTK_ROMFS_MMAP=1 maps the image instead.
//
// Overlays: files listed in a directory's manifest.tsv are served in place of the originals. Each line names a RomFS
// path, the overlay's size and SHA-256 and the original's SHA-256 ("-" adds a file the RomFS lacks; it is numbered
// after the RomFS's own files, file_count + k in path order). The directories, in this order: TOTK_ROMFS_PATCHES and
// TOTK_ROMFS_MODS; unset or "0" = none. A missing path, a size or hash mismatch or a changed original stops the start.
// An overlay file is opened when the game opens it; its identity (volume, file id, size, last write) is kept from the
// start check, and an open that finds another file there stops the game.
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "cfg.h"
#include "fs.h"
#include "host.h"
#include "romfs_config.h"
#include "romfs_path.h"
#include "platform/platform.h"
#include "sha256.h"

#define NH 65536                     // RomFS handle slots
#define READ_CHUNK (64u << 20)       // largest single read
#define HASH_CHUNK (8u << 20)
#define ADDED UINT64_MAX             // an added overlay file's index until overlay_init numbers it

typedef struct { uint64_t offset, size; uint32_t name, len; } Entry;
_Static_assert(sizeof(Entry) == 24, "index entry layout");

typedef struct { uint32_t volume, pad; uint64_t file_id, size, write_time, create_time; } Identity;   // no padding
typedef struct { uint64_t index, size; char *path, *name; Identity id; } Overlay;

static uint8_t *index_bytes;
static size_t index_size;
static uint64_t file_count, strings_offset;
static PlatFile *image;
static const uint8_t *image_map;
static char image_file[2048];
static char index_dir[2048];         // the directory of romfs-index.bin: the proof file's default place
static char mount_name[32];
static char mount_names[8][32];
static int mount_count;
static PlatMutex lock = PLAT_MUTEX_INIT;
static uint64_t handles[NH];         // file index + 1; 0 is free
static uint32_t handle_ovl[NH];      // overlay slot + 1 of an open handle, 0 = original
static PlatFile *handle_file[NH];    // the handle's open overlay file, when handle_ovl is set
static Overlay *overlays;            // sorted by RomFS index after overlay_init
static size_t noverlay, overlay_cap;
static char **added;                 // RomFS paths of the added files, sorted; added[k] is index file_count + k
static size_t nadded;

static void need(int c, const char *m) {
    if (!c) rt_fatal("RomFS: %s", m);
}

static Entry entry(uint64_t i) {
    Entry e;
    memcpy(&e, index_bytes + 24 + i * 24, 24);
    return e;
}
static const char *entry_name(Entry e) { return (const char *)index_bytes + strings_offset + e.name; }

static double now_s(void) { return (double)plat_now_ns() / 1e9; }

// ---- positional reads
// Bytes read at off (0 at or past the end of the file), -1 on an I/O error.

// A file read writes guest memory from the kernel's I/O path, which GetWriteWatch does not report: stamp the pages so
// textures and GPU mirrors over the buffer re-read them (MKW streams each terrain layer from disk into one ASTC staging
// texture; without this all 68 layers were copied from the first, mostly empty, upload: black road/ground).
void vk_guest_written(uint64_t addr, uint64_t size);
static int64_t read_at(PlatFile *f, void *buf, uint32_t n, uint64_t off) {
    mem_thaw((uintptr_t)buf, n);   // the kernel's write would fail on a frozen page instead of faulting
    int64_t got = plat_file_pread(f, buf, n, off);
    if (got > 0) vk_guest_written((uintptr_t)buf, (uint64_t)got);
    if (got == -2)   // a read-only page in the buffer: a frozen region missed its thaw
        rt_log("RomFS: read of %u bytes into %p refused: the buffer is not writable", n, buf);
    return got < 0 ? -1 : got;
}

static PlatFile *open_read(const char *path) { return plat_file_open(path); }

static Identity identity_of(PlatFile *f) {
    PlatFileId i;
    need(plat_file_id(f, &i), "file information");
    return (Identity){(uint32_t)i.volume, 0, i.file_id, i.size, i.write_time, i.create_time};
}

// ---- SHA-256 over a file range, streaming
static void hex32(const uint8_t d[32], char out[65]) {
    for (int i = 0; i < 32; i++) snprintf(out + 2 * i, 3, "%02x", d[i]);
}

static void sha_range(PlatFile *f, uint64_t offset, uint64_t size, char hex[65], int progress) {
    Sha256 h;
    sha256_init(&h);
    uint8_t *buf = malloc(HASH_CHUNK);
    need(buf != NULL, "hash buffer");
    double t0 = now_s();
    for (uint64_t done = 0; done < size;) {
        uint32_t want = size - done > HASH_CHUNK ? HASH_CHUNK : (uint32_t)(size - done);
        int64_t n = read_at(f, buf, want, offset + done);
        need(n > 0, "read of hash input");
        sha256_update(&h, buf, (size_t)n);
        done += (uint64_t)n;
        if (progress && (done % (2ull << 30) < (uint64_t)n || done == size))
            rt_log("RomFS: hashed %.1f of %.1f GiB (%.0f MiB/s)", done / 1073741824.0, size / 1073741824.0,
                   done / 1048576.0 / (now_s() - t0 + 1e-9));
    }
    uint8_t d[32];
    sha256_final(&h, d);
    free(buf);
    hex32(d, hex);
}

// ---- full image verification with a proof file
typedef struct { char magic[16], sha256[65]; uint8_t pad[7]; Identity id; } RomfsProof;

static void verify_image(const char *dir) {
    const char *mode = cfg_get("TOTK_ROMFS_VERIFY");
    if (!mode || (strcmp(mode, "full") && strcmp(mode, "force"))) return;
    const char *pdir = cfg_get("TOTK_ROMFS_PROOF_DIR");
    if (pdir && *pdir) dir = pdir;
    RomfsProof want = {0}, saved;
    memcpy(want.magic, "TOTKRFS-PROOF-1", 16);
    memcpy(want.sha256, ROMFS_IMAGE_SHA256, sizeof ROMFS_IMAGE_SHA256 < 65 ? sizeof ROMFS_IMAGE_SHA256 : 65);
    want.id = identity_of(image);
    char path[2100];
    need(snprintf(path, sizeof path, "%s/.romfs-verified-v1", dir) < (int)sizeof path, "proof path");
    if (strcmp(mode, "force")) {
        PlatFile *p = open_read(path);
        if (p) {
            int ok = plat_file_pread(p, &saved, sizeof saved, 0) == sizeof saved;
            plat_file_close(p);
            if (ok && !memcmp(&saved, &want, sizeof want)) {
                rt_log("RomFS unchanged since its full SHA-256 check (%s)", path);
                return;
            }
        }
    }
    rt_log("RomFS: verifying the SHA-256 of %s (%llu bytes)", image_file, (unsigned long long)want.id.size);
    char hex[65];
    sha_range(image, 0, want.id.size, hex, 1);
    if (strcmp(hex, ROMFS_IMAGE_SHA256))
        rt_fatal("RomFS image %s has SHA-256 %s, the extraction recorded %s (extract it again)", image_file, hex,
                 ROMFS_IMAGE_SHA256);
    Identity after = identity_of(image);
    need(!memcmp(&after, &want.id, sizeof after), "image changed during verification");
    plat_file_write_atomic(path, &want, sizeof want);
    rt_log("RomFS: image SHA-256 ok");
}

// ---- index lookup
static uint64_t lower(const char *name) {
    uint64_t lo = 0, hi = file_count;
    while (lo < hi) {
        uint64_t m = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
        if (strcmp(entry_name(entry(m)), name) < 0) lo = m + 1;
        else hi = m;
    }
    return lo;
}

static size_t added_lower(const char *p) {
    size_t lo = 0, hi = nadded;
    while (lo < hi) {
        size_t m = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
        if (strcmp(added[m], p) < 0) lo = m + 1;
        else hi = m;
    }
    return lo;
}

// The index of RomFS path p (an added file: file_count + k), or UINT64_MAX.
static uint64_t file_index(const char *p) {
    uint64_t i = lower(p);
    if (i < file_count && !strcmp(p, entry_name(entry(i)))) return i;
    size_t k = added_lower(p);
    return k < nadded && !strcmp(added[k], p) ? file_count + k : UINT64_MAX;
}

// 1 when a RomFS file or an added one lies under folder (a path ending in '/').
static int folder_exists(const char *folder) {
    size_t n = strlen(folder);
    uint64_t i = lower(folder);
    if (i < file_count && !strncmp(entry_name(entry(i)), folder, n)) return 1;
    size_t k = added_lower(folder);
    return k < nadded && !strncmp(added[k], folder, n);
}

// The overlay slot + 1 that replaces RomFS file i, or 0.
static uint32_t overlay_slot(uint64_t i) {
    size_t lo = 0, hi = noverlay;
    while (lo < hi) {
        size_t m = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
        if (overlays[m].index < i) lo = m + 1;
        else hi = m;
    }
    return lo < noverlay && overlays[lo].index == i ? (uint32_t)(lo + 1) : 0;
}

// ---- overlays
// Loads and checks one overlay folder. A failed check stops the game, except with optional set (the Xbox prompts
// folder): the folder is dropped, the reason logged, and 0 returned. Returns 1 when the folder is loaded or has no
// manifest.
static int overlay_load(const char *dir, int optional) {
#define BAD(...) do { if (!optional) rt_fatal(__VA_ARGS__); rt_log(__VA_ARGS__); goto bad; } while (0)
    char path[2100];
    need(snprintf(path, sizeof path, "%s/manifest.tsv", dir) < (int)sizeof path, "overlay path");
    FILE *m = fopen(path, "rb");
    if (!m) {
        rt_log("RomFS overlay: none (%s)", path);
        return 1;
    }
    char line[8192];
    size_t first = noverlay;
    uint64_t hashed = 0;
    double t0 = now_s();
    while (fgets(line, sizeof line, m)) {
        if (line[0] == '#' || line[0] == '\n' || line[0] == '\r') continue;
        char name[4096], sha[65], orig[65], hex[65];
        unsigned long long size = 0;
        need(sscanf(line, "%4095[^\t]\t%llu\t%64[0-9a-f]\t%64[0-9a-f-]", name, &size, sha, orig) == 4 &&
             strlen(sha) == 64 && (strlen(orig) == 64 || !strcmp(orig, "-")), "overlay manifest line");
        need(romfs_path_valid_relative(name), "overlay path");
        uint64_t i = lower(name);
        int known = i < file_count && !strcmp(entry_name(entry(i)), name), add = !strcmp(orig, "-");
        if (!known && !add)
            BAD("RomFS overlay: %s/manifest.tsv names %s, which the RomFS lacks; a new file has \"-\" as its "
                "original's SHA-256", dir, name);
        if (known && add)
            BAD("RomFS overlay: %s/manifest.tsv adds %s, which the RomFS already has; give its original's SHA-256",
                dir, name);
        Entry e = {0};
        if (known) {
            e = entry(i);
            sha_range(image, e.offset, e.size, hex, 0);
            if (strcmp(hex, orig)) BAD("RomFS overlay: the original of %s has SHA-256 %s, %s/manifest.tsv says %s",
                                       name, hex, dir, orig);
        } else {
            i = ADDED;
        }
        char file[8200];
        need(snprintf(file, sizeof file, "%s/%s", dir, name) < (int)sizeof file, "overlay file path");
        PlatFile *f = open_read(file);
        if (!f) BAD("RomFS overlay: %s missing", file);
        Identity id = identity_of(f);
        if (id.size != size) {
            plat_file_close(f);
            BAD("RomFS overlay: %s has %llu bytes, its manifest says %llu", file, (unsigned long long)id.size, size);
        }
        sha_range(f, 0, size, hex, 0);
        plat_file_close(f);
        if (strcmp(hex, sha)) BAD("RomFS overlay: %s has SHA-256 %s, its manifest says %s", file, hex, sha);
        hashed += e.size + size;
        if (noverlay == overlay_cap) {
            overlay_cap = overlay_cap ? overlay_cap * 2 : 16;
            overlays = realloc(overlays, overlay_cap * sizeof *overlays);
            need(overlays != NULL, "overlay table");
        }
        char *copy = strdup(file), *rel = strdup(name);
        need(copy && rel, "overlay path copy");
        overlays[noverlay++] = (Overlay){i, size, copy, rel, id};
        if (noverlay - first <= 16)
            rt_log("RomFS overlay: %s (%llu bytes) %s", name, size, add ? "is added" : "replaces the original");
    }
    fclose(m);
    if (noverlay - first > 16) rt_log("RomFS overlay: %zu files from %s (%zu not listed)", noverlay - first, dir,
                                      noverlay - first - 16);
    if (noverlay > first) rt_log("RomFS overlay: %s checked, %zu files, %.1f MiB hashed in %.2f s", dir,
                                 noverlay - first, hashed / 1048576.0, now_s() - t0);
    return 1;
bad:
    fclose(m);
    for (size_t k = first; k < noverlay; k++) {
        free((void *)overlays[k].path);
        free((void *)overlays[k].name);
    }
    noverlay = first;
    return 0;
#undef BAD
}

static int overlay_order(const void *a, const void *b) {
    uint64_t x = ((const Overlay *)a)->index, y = ((const Overlay *)b)->index;
    return (x > y) - (x < y);
}

static int added_order(const void *a, const void *b) {
    return strcmp((*(Overlay *const *)a)->name, (*(Overlay *const *)b)->name);
}

// Number the added files in path order after the RomFS's own (file_count + k); two overlays adding one path stop.
static void added_init(void) {
    Overlay **list = NULL;
    for (size_t k = 0; k < noverlay; k++)
        if (overlays[k].index == ADDED) {
            list = realloc(list, (nadded + 1) * sizeof *list);
            need(list != NULL, "added files");
            list[nadded++] = &overlays[k];
        }
    if (!nadded) return;
    qsort(list, nadded, sizeof *list, added_order);
    added = malloc(nadded * sizeof *added);
    need(added != NULL, "added files");
    for (size_t k = 0; k < nadded; k++) {
        if (k && !strcmp(list[k]->name, list[k - 1]->name))
            rt_fatal("RomFS overlay: %s and %s both add %s", list[k - 1]->path, list[k]->path, list[k]->name);
        list[k]->index = file_count + k;
        added[k] = list[k]->name;
    }
    free(list);
    rt_log("RomFS overlay: %zu files added to the RomFS", nadded);
}

// The HeapDef table a bigger game resolution needs (resolution.c): its texture heap and that heap's parent grow. The
// base is an overlay that replaces the table (a mod's heap sizes stay), else the RomFS original; the grown table is
// written to <profile>/resolution/ and served in the base's place.
#define HEAPDEF "System/HeapSize/Product.Nin_NX_NVN.HeapDef.byml.zs"
static void heapdef_overlay(void) {
    if (!res_heap_extra_kib()) return;
    uint64_t i = lower(HEAPDEF);
    if (i >= file_count || strcmp(entry_name(entry(i)), HEAPDEF)) {
        rt_log("RomFS: %s missing; the game keeps its own resolution", HEAPDEF);
        return;
    }
    Overlay *base = NULL;
    for (size_t k = 0; k < noverlay; k++)
        if (overlays[k].index == i) base = &overlays[k];
    PlatFile *f = base ? open_read(base->path) : image;
    uint64_t off = base ? 0 : entry(i).offset, n = base ? base->size : entry(i).size;
    void *in = n && n < (16u << 20) && f ? malloc((size_t)n) : NULL;
    int ok = in && read_at(f, in, (uint32_t)n, off) == (int64_t)n;
    if (base && f) plat_file_close(f);
    void *out = NULL;
    size_t out_n = 0;
    ok = ok && res_heapdef_build(in, (size_t)n, &out, &out_n);
    free(in);
    if (!ok) return;
    char dir[2100], file[2200];
    need(snprintf(dir, sizeof dir, "%s/resolution", rt_config()->profile) < (int)sizeof dir, "resolution path");
    need(snprintf(file, sizeof file, "%s/Product.Nin_NX_NVN.HeapDef.byml.zs", dir) < (int)sizeof file, "resolution path");
    plat_file_mkdir_p(dir);
    ok = plat_file_write(file, out, out_n);
    free(out);
    PlatFile *r = ok ? open_read(file) : NULL;
    if (!r) {
        rt_log("RomFS: cannot write %s; the game keeps its own resolution", file);
        return;
    }
    Identity id = identity_of(r);
    plat_file_close(r);
    char *copy = strdup(file);
    need(copy != NULL, "overlay path copy");
    if (base) {
        free(base->path);
        base->path = copy;
        base->size = out_n;
        base->id = id;
    } else {
        if (noverlay == overlay_cap) {
            overlay_cap = overlay_cap ? overlay_cap * 2 : 16;
            overlays = realloc(overlays, overlay_cap * sizeof *overlays);
            need(overlays != NULL, "overlay table");
        }
        char *rel = strdup(HEAPDEF);
        need(rel != NULL, "overlay path copy");
        overlays[noverlay++] = (Overlay){i, out_n, copy, rel, id};
    }
    rt_log("RomFS overlay: %s (%zu bytes, grown heaps) replaces %s", file, out_n, base ? "the mod's table" : "the original");
    res_heapdef_served();
}

static int xbox_prompts_ready;    // romfs-patches-xbox/manifest.tsv was next to romfs-index.bin at start
static int xbox_prompts_active;   // and overlay_init loaded it

int romfs_xbox_prompts_ready(void) { return xbox_prompts_ready; }
int romfs_xbox_prompts_active(void) { return xbox_prompts_active; }

static void overlay_init(void) {
    // TOTK_ROMFS_PATCHES unset: romfs-patches next to romfs-index.bin if it has a manifest (tools/make_romfs_patches.py).
    // A game resolution that is not 16:9 takes romfs-patches-<w>x<h> instead when it is there: the same overlay with
    // the UI laid out for that shape (make_romfs_patches.py --aspect), when the game version has the camera aspect patch
    // the layout goes with (res_wants_wide_overlay).
    // With pad_layout = xbox_prompts, romfs-patches-xbox in its place: the same patches with the A/B and X/Y prompts
    // swapped (make_romfs_patches.py --xbox-prompts). The game reads the archives once at boot, so the prompts stay
    // until restart even though the layout itself changes live. Each folder replaces romfs-patches as a whole and the
    // setup builds no wide folder with Xbox prompts, so a wide game resolution keeps the Switch prompts.
    char def[2100], xbox[2100];
    const char *patches = cfg_get("TOTK_ROMFS_PATCHES");
    int wide = 0;
    unsigned out[2];
    res_wanted(out);
    if (!patches && res_wants_wide_overlay(out)) {
        if (snprintf(def, sizeof def, "%s/romfs-patches-%ux%u/manifest.tsv", index_dir, out[0], out[1]) < (int)sizeof def &&
            plat_file_exists(def)) {
            def[strlen(def) - strlen("/manifest.tsv")] = 0;
            patches = def, wide = 1;
        } else {
            rt_log("RomFS overlay: no romfs-patches-%ux%u for this game resolution, the UI keeps its 16:9 layout "
                   "(tools/make_romfs_patches.py --aspect %ux%u)", out[0], out[1], out[0], out[1]);
        }
    }
    xbox_prompts_ready =
        snprintf(xbox, sizeof xbox, "%s/romfs-patches-xbox/manifest.tsv", index_dir) < (int)sizeof xbox &&
        plat_file_exists(xbox);
    int want_xbox = !strcasecmp(cfg_value("TOTK_PAD_LAYOUT"), "xbox_prompts");
    if (!patches && want_xbox && xbox_prompts_ready) {
        xbox[strlen(xbox) - strlen("/manifest.tsv")] = 0;
        xbox_prompts_active = overlay_load(xbox, 1);
        if (xbox_prompts_active) rt_log("RomFS overlay: Xbox button prompts (%s)", xbox);
        else rt_log("RomFS overlay: %s failed its check (run the setup again); romfs-patches loads instead", xbox);
    } else if (want_xbox) {
        rt_log("RomFS overlay: pad_layout = xbox_prompts, but %s; Switch prompts stay",
               wide      ? "the game resolution takes the wide UI layout"
               : patches ? "TOTK_ROMFS_PATCHES is set"
                         : "romfs-patches-xbox has no manifest.tsv (run the setup again)");
    }
    if (!patches && !xbox_prompts_active && snprintf(def, sizeof def, "%s/romfs-patches/manifest.tsv", index_dir) < (int)sizeof def &&
        plat_file_exists(def)) {
        def[strlen(def) - strlen("/manifest.tsv")] = 0;
        patches = def;
    }
    const char *dirs[2] = {patches, cfg_get("TOTK_ROMFS_MODS")};
    for (int i = 0; i < 2; i++)
        if (dirs[i] && *dirs[i] && strcmp(dirs[i], "0")) overlay_load(dirs[i], 0);
    heapdef_overlay();
    added_init();
    if (noverlay) qsort(overlays, noverlay, sizeof *overlays, overlay_order);
    for (size_t k = 1; k < noverlay; k++)
        if (overlays[k].index == overlays[k - 1].index)
            rt_fatal("RomFS overlay: %s and %s replace the same file %s", overlays[k - 1].path, overlays[k].path,
                     overlays[k].name);
}

// ---- start
// romfs-index.bin next to totk.exe, or TOTK_ROMFS_INDEX.
static void index_path(char *out, size_t cap) {
    const char *e = cfg_get("TOTK_ROMFS_INDEX");
    if (e && *e) {
        need(snprintf(out, cap, "%s", e) < (int)cap, "index path");
        return;
    }
    need(plat_exe_path(out, cap), "executable path");
    char *sep = plat_last_sep(out);
    size_t k = sep ? (size_t)(sep - out) + 1 : 0;
    need(k + 16 < cap, "executable path");
    strcpy(out + k, "romfs-index.bin");
}

static void load_index(void) {
    char path[2100];
    index_path(path, sizeof path);
    snprintf(index_dir, sizeof index_dir, "%s", path);
    char *sep = plat_last_sep(index_dir);
    if (sep) *sep = 0;
    else strcpy(index_dir, ".");
    uint64_t sz = 0;
    index_bytes = plat_file_read(path, &sz);
    if (!index_bytes) rt_fatal("RomFS index %s missing (tools/build_game.py writes it next to totk.exe)", path);
    need(sz >= 24 && sz < (128 << 20), "index size");
    index_size = (size_t)sz;
    uint8_t d[32];
    char hex[65];
    rt_sha256(index_bytes, index_size, d);
    hex32(d, hex);
    if (strcmp(hex, ROMFS_INDEX_SHA256))
        rt_fatal("RomFS index %s has SHA-256 %s, this build expects %s (rebuild with tools/build_game.py)", path, hex,
                 ROMFS_INDEX_SHA256);
    need(!memcmp(index_bytes, "TOTKRFS1", 8), "index format");
    memcpy(&file_count, index_bytes + 8, 8);
    memcpy(&strings_offset, index_bytes + 16, 8);
    need(file_count == ROMFS_FILE_COUNT && file_count < 1000000 && strings_offset == 24 + file_count * 24 &&
         strings_offset < index_size, "index layout");
    const char *previous = NULL;
    for (uint64_t i = 0; i < file_count; i++) {
        Entry e = entry(i);
        need(e.offset <= ROMFS_IMAGE_SIZE && e.size <= ROMFS_IMAGE_SIZE - e.offset, "file bounds");
        need(e.name < index_size - strings_offset && e.len > 1 && e.len <= index_size - strings_offset - e.name,
             "name bounds");
        const char *name = entry_name(e);
        need(name[e.len - 1] == 0 && strlen(name) == e.len - 1 && (!previous || strcmp(previous, name) < 0),
             "sorted paths");
        previous = name;
    }
    rt_log("RomFS index %s: SHA-256 ok, %llu files, %zu bytes", path, (unsigned long long)file_count, index_size);
}

static void init_once(void *param) {
    (void)param;
#ifdef ROMFS_MISSING
    rt_fatal("this build has no RomFS: tools/build_game.py found no index.json in its --romfs directory");
#else
    double t0 = now_s();
    load_index();
    const char *dir = rt_config()->romfs;
    need(snprintf(image_file, sizeof image_file, "%s/romfs.bin", dir) < (int)sizeof image_file, "image path");
    image = open_read(image_file);
    if (!image) rt_fatal("RomFS image %s missing; put romfs.bin into the romfs folder next to totk or set TOTK_ROMFS",
                         image_file);
    PlatFileId sz;
    need(plat_file_id(image, &sz), "image size");
    if (sz.size != ROMFS_IMAGE_SIZE)
        rt_fatal("RomFS image %s has %llu bytes, the index was built for %llu", image_file,
                 (unsigned long long)sz.size, (unsigned long long)ROMFS_IMAGE_SIZE);
    rt_log("RomFS image %s: size ok (%llu bytes)", image_file, (unsigned long long)ROMFS_IMAGE_SIZE);
    verify_image(index_dir);
    const char *mm = cfg_get("TOTK_ROMFS_MMAP");
    if (mm && strcmp(mm, "0")) {
        const void *v = plat_file_map(image);
        if (v) {
            image_map = v;
            rt_log("RomFS: mapped read path enabled");
        } else {
            rt_log("RomFS: mapping failed; using positional reads");
        }
    }
    overlay_init();
    rt_log("RomFS ready: %llu files, %zu overlays, %zu added, %.2f s", (unsigned long long)file_count, noverlay,
           nadded, now_s() - t0);
#endif
    return;
}

void fs_init(void) {
    static PlatOnce once = PLAT_ONCE_INIT;
    plat_once(&once, init_once, NULL);
}

// ---- the RomFS interface (fs.h)
void fs_trace(const char *what, const char *path) {
    static double t0;
    if (!(rt_trace & RT_TRACE_FS)) return;
    if (!t0) t0 = now_s();
    rt_log("fs %8.3f %s %s", now_s() - t0, what, path ? path : "(null)");
}

uint64_t romfs_file_count(void) { return file_count; }

const char *romfs_entry(uint64_t i, uint64_t *offset, uint64_t *size) {
    if (i >= file_count) return NULL;
    Entry e = entry(i);
    if (offset) *offset = e.offset;
    if (size) *size = e.size;
    return entry_name(e);
}

const char *romfs_image_path(void) { return image_file; }

size_t romfs_overlay_count(void) { return noverlay; }

const char *romfs_overlay(size_t k, const char **file, uint64_t *size, int *is_added) {
    if (k >= noverlay) return NULL;
    *file = overlays[k].path;
    *size = overlays[k].size;
    *is_added = overlays[k].index >= file_count;
    return overlays[k].name;
}

static const char *romfs_find_mount(const char *path, size_t *mlen_out) {
    if (!path) return NULL;
    for (int i = 0; i < mount_count; i++) {
        size_t n = strlen(mount_names[i]);
        if (n && !strncmp(path, mount_names[i], n) && path[n] == ':') {
            if (mlen_out) *mlen_out = n;
            return mount_names[i];
        }
    }
    return NULL;
}

int romfs_owns(const char *path) {
    return romfs_find_mount(path, NULL) != NULL;
}

int romfs_handle(uint64_t h) { return h > ROMFS_HANDLE_BASE && h < ROMFS_HANDLE_BASE + NH; }

uint32_t romfs_mount(const char *name) {
    fs_init();
    if (!name || !romfs_path_valid_relative(name) || strlen(name) >= sizeof mount_name || strchr(name, '/') ||
        strchr(name, ':'))
        return FS_R_INVALID;
    plat_mutex_lock(&lock);
    if (!*mount_name) strcpy(mount_name, name);
    int found = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < mount_count; i++)
        if (!strcmp(mount_names[i], name)) found = 1;
    if (!found && mount_count < 8) strcpy(mount_names[mount_count++], name);
    plat_mutex_unlock(&lock);
    rt_log("fs mount %s: -> RomFS", name);
    return 0;
}

uint32_t romfs_open(uint64_t *out, const char *path, int mode) {
    fs_trace("rom", path);
    if (!out || mode != FS_OPEN_READ) return FS_R_UNSUPPORTED_OPEN;
    const char *mname = romfs_find_mount(path, NULL);
    const char *p = mname ? romfs_path_relative(mname, path) : NULL;
    if (!p) return FS_R_PATH_NOT_FOUND;
    uint64_t i = file_index(p);
    if (i == UINT64_MAX) return FS_R_PATH_NOT_FOUND;
    uint32_t ov = overlay_slot(i);
    PlatFile *f = NULL;
    if (ov) {
        const Overlay *o = &overlays[ov - 1];
        f = open_read(o->path);
        Identity id;
        if (f) id = identity_of(f);
        if (!f || memcmp(&id, &o->id, sizeof id))
            rt_fatal("RomFS overlay %s is missing or changed since the start check (restart the game)", o->path);
    }
    plat_mutex_lock(&lock);
    for (unsigned j = 1; j < NH; j++)
        if (!handles[j]) {
            handles[j] = i + 1;
            handle_ovl[j] = ov;
            handle_file[j] = f;
            *out = ROMFS_HANDLE_BASE + j;
            plat_mutex_unlock(&lock);
            return 0;
        }
    plat_mutex_unlock(&lock);
    rt_fatal("RomFS file handle table full (%d)", NH);
}

// The handle's index row (an added file's is empty: its bytes are all in its overlay), and where its bytes come from:
// the overlay file, or the original's range of the image.
static int handle_source(uint64_t h, PlatFile **f, uint64_t *base, uint64_t *size) {
    if (!romfs_handle(h)) return 0;
    uint64_t j = h - ROMFS_HANDLE_BASE;
    plat_mutex_lock_shared(&lock);
    uint64_t i = handles[j];
    uint32_t ov = handle_ovl[j];
    PlatFile *of = handle_file[j];
    plat_mutex_unlock_shared(&lock);
    if (!i) return 0;
    if (ov) {
        *f = of;
        *base = 0;
        *size = overlays[ov - 1].size;
    } else {
        Entry e = entry(i - 1);
        *f = image;
        *base = e.offset;
        *size = e.size;
    }
    return 1;
}

uint32_t romfs_read(uint64_t *out, uint64_t h, int64_t offset, void *buffer, uint64_t size) {
    PlatFile *f;
    uint64_t base, fsize;
    if (!out || offset < 0 || !handle_source(h, &f, &base, &fsize)) return FS_R_INVALID;
    if ((uint64_t)offset > fsize || (!buffer && size)) return FS_R_INVALID;
    uint64_t n = size < fsize - (uint64_t)offset ? size : fsize - (uint64_t)offset, done = 0;
    if (f == image && image_map) {
        memcpy(buffer, image_map + base + (uint64_t)offset, (size_t)n);
        done = n;
    }
    while (done < n) {
        uint32_t chunk = n - done > READ_CHUNK ? READ_CHUNK : (uint32_t)(n - done);
        int64_t r = read_at(f, (uint8_t *)buffer + done, chunk, base + (uint64_t)offset + done);
        if (r <= 0) rt_fatal("RomFS read failure at %#llx", (unsigned long long)(base + offset + done));
        done += (uint64_t)r;
    }
    *out = done;
    return 0;
}

uint32_t romfs_size(int64_t *out, uint64_t h) {
    PlatFile *f;
    uint64_t base, size;
    if (!out || !handle_source(h, &f, &base, &size)) return FS_R_INVALID;
    *out = (int64_t)size;
    return 0;
}

void romfs_close(uint64_t h) {
    PlatFile *f;
    uint64_t base, size;
    if (!handle_source(h, &f, &base, &size))
        rt_fatal("RomFS: close of invalid file handle %#llx", (unsigned long long)h);
    uint64_t j = h - ROMFS_HANDLE_BASE;
    plat_mutex_lock(&lock);
    PlatFile *of = handle_ovl[j] ? handle_file[j] : NULL;
    handles[j] = 0;
    handle_ovl[j] = 0;
    handle_file[j] = NULL;
    plat_mutex_unlock(&lock);
    if (of) plat_file_close(of);
}

uint32_t romfs_entry_type(int *out, const char *path) {
    if (!out) return FS_R_INVALID;
    const char *mname = romfs_find_mount(path, NULL);
    const char *p = mname ? romfs_path_relative(mname, path) : NULL;
    if (!p) return FS_R_PATH_NOT_FOUND;
    if (file_index(p) != UINT64_MAX) {
        *out = FS_ENTRY_FILE;
        return 0;
    }
    char dir[4096];
    if (snprintf(dir, sizeof dir, "%s/", p) >= (int)sizeof dir) return FS_R_INVALID;
    if (folder_exists(dir)) {
        *out = FS_ENTRY_DIRECTORY;
        return 0;
    }
    return FS_R_PATH_NOT_FOUND;
}

int romfs_list_dir(const char *path, int (*cb)(const char *name, int kind, uint64_t size, void *ctx), void *ctx) {
    size_t mlen = 0;
    const char *mname = romfs_find_mount(path, &mlen);
    if (!mname || path[mlen] != ':' || path[mlen + 1] != '/') return PLAT_FS_NOT_FOUND;
    const char *rel = path + mlen + 2;
    while (*rel == '/') rel++;
    char prefix[4096];
    size_t plen = 0;
    if (*rel) {
        if (!romfs_path_valid_relative(rel)) return PLAT_FS_NOT_FOUND;
        int n = snprintf(prefix, sizeof prefix, "%s/", rel);
        if (n < 0 || n >= (int)sizeof prefix) return PLAT_FS_NOT_FOUND;
        plen = (size_t)n;
        if (!folder_exists(prefix)) return PLAT_FS_NOT_FOUND;
    } else {
        prefix[0] = 0;
    }
    char last_dir[769] = "";
    size_t last_dlen = 0;
    uint64_t i = plen ? lower(prefix) : 0;
    for (; i < file_count; i++) {
        Entry e = entry(i);
        const char *name = entry_name(e);
        if (plen && strncmp(name, prefix, plen)) break;
        const char *rest = name + plen;
        const char *slash = strchr(rest, '/');
        if (slash) {
            size_t dlen = (size_t)(slash - rest);
            if (dlen > 0 && dlen < sizeof last_dir &&
                (dlen != last_dlen || memcmp(rest, last_dir, dlen))) {
                memcpy(last_dir, rest, dlen);
                last_dir[dlen] = 0;
                last_dlen = dlen;
                if (!cb(last_dir, PLAT_FS_DIR, 0, ctx)) break;
            }
        } else {
            uint32_t ov = overlay_slot(i);
            uint64_t sz = ov ? overlays[ov - 1].size : e.size;
            if (!cb(rest, PLAT_FS_FILE, sz, ctx)) break;
        }
    }
    return PLAT_FS_OK;
}

// ---- overrides
// nn::Result nn::fs::MountRom(const char *name, void *cache, size_t cache_size)
static void ov_mount_rom(Cpu *c) { ret_x(c, romfs_mount(arg_p(c, 0))); }
// nn::Result nn::fs::QueryMountRomCacheSize(size_t *out): no cache needed, the host reads the image directly
static void ov_query_cache(Cpu *c) {
    uint64_t *out = arg_p(c, 0);
    if (out) *out = 0;
    ret_x(c, out ? 0 : FS_R_INVALID);
}
// void nn::fs::InitializeForApplication(): SDK-internal; opens the index instead of the fs service session
static void ov_initialize(Cpu *c) {
    (void)c;
    fs_init();
}

HOST_OVERRIDE("_ZN2nn2fs8MountRomEPKcPvm", ov_mount_rom);
HOST_OVERRIDE("_ZN2nn2fs8MountRomEPKc", ov_mount_rom);
HOST_OVERRIDE("_ZN2nn2fs22QueryMountRomCacheSizeEPm", ov_query_cache);
HOST_OVERRIDE("_ZN2nn2fs24InitializeForApplicationEv", ov_initialize);
```

`runtime/romfs_path.h`:

```h
// From MacNativeGames games/totk/runtime/romfs_path.h @ b75be8cf (MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 MacNativeGames
// contributors).
// RomFS path validation shared by the runtime (romfs.c) and its probe (fs_host.c probe_fs).
#pragma once
#include <stddef.h>
#include <string.h>

// A RomFS-relative path: non-empty, no leading '/', no '\', no empty, "." or ".." component.
static inline int romfs_path_valid_relative(const char *path) {
    if (!path || !*path || *path == '/' || strchr(path, '\\')) return 0;
    for (const char *part = path; *part;) {
        const char *end = strchr(part, '/');
        size_t size = end ? (size_t)(end - part) : strlen(part);
        if (!size || (size == 1 && part[0] == '.') || (size == 2 && part[0] == '.' && part[1] == '.')) return 0;
        if (!end) break;
        part = end + 1;
    }
    return 1;
}

// "<mount>:/<path>" -> "<path>", or NULL. Audio stream requests join a mount root and a leading-slash resource,
// producing "content://Sound/...": repeated root separators are skipped; traversal, backslashes and empty interior
// components are still rejected.
static inline const char *romfs_path_relative(const char *mount, const char *path) {
    if (!mount || !*mount || !path) return NULL;
    size_t size = strlen(mount);
    if (strncmp(path, mount, size) || path[size] != ':' || path[size + 1] != '/') return NULL;
    path += size + 2;
    while (*path == '/') ++path;
    return romfs_path_valid_relative(path) ? path : NULL;
}
```

`runtime/sha256.c`:

```c
// SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4). The block function has two forms: one on the x86 SHA extensions (SHA-NI: Intel since Ice Lake
// and Goldmont, AMD since Zen), which hashes the RomFS image at about the speed of a disk read, and portable C for CPUs
// without them. sha256_selftest in the probes compares both against the FIPS test vectors.
#include "sha256.h"

#include <string.h>

#if defined(__x86_64__)
#include <immintrin.h>
#endif

static const uint32_t K[64] = {
    0x428a2f98, 0x71374491, 0xb5c0fbcf, 0xe9b5dba5, 0x3956c25b, 0x59f111f1, 0x923f82a4, 0xab1c5ed5,
    0xd807aa98, 0x12835b01, 0x243185be, 0x550c7dc3, 0x72be5d74, 0x80deb1fe, 0x9bdc06a7, 0xc19bf174,
    0xe49b69c1, 0xefbe4786, 0x0fc19dc6, 0x240ca1cc, 0x2de92c6f, 0x4a7484aa, 0x5cb0a9dc, 0x76f988da,
    0x983e5152, 0xa831c66d, 0xb00327c8, 0xbf597fc7, 0xc6e00bf3, 0xd5a79147, 0x06ca6351, 0x14292967,
    0x27b70a85, 0x2e1b2138, 0x4d2c6dfc, 0x53380d13, 0x650a7354, 0x766a0abb, 0x81c2c92e, 0x92722c85,
    0xa2bfe8a1, 0xa81a664b, 0xc24b8b70, 0xc76c51a3, 0xd192e819, 0xd6990624, 0xf40e3585, 0x106aa070,
    0x19a4c116, 0x1e376c08, 0x2748774c, 0x34b0bcb5, 0x391c0cb3, 0x4ed8aa4a, 0x5b9cca4f, 0x682e6ff3,
    0x748f82ee, 0x78a5636f, 0x84c87814, 0x8cc70208, 0x90befffa, 0xa4506ceb, 0xbef9a3f7, 0xc67178f2,
};

static inline uint32_t ror(uint32_t x, int n) { return x >> n | x << (32 - n); }

static void blocks_c(uint32_t h[8], const uint8_t *p, size_t n) {
    for (; n; n--, p += 64) {
        uint32_t w[64];
        for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++)
            w[i] = (uint32_t)p[4 * i] << 24 | (uint32_t)p[4 * i + 1] << 16 | (uint32_t)p[4 * i + 2] << 8 | p[4 * i + 3];
        for (int i = 16; i < 64; i++) {
            uint32_t s0 = ror(w[i - 15], 7) ^ ror(w[i - 15], 18) ^ w[i - 15] >> 3;
            uint32_t s1 = ror(w[i - 2], 17) ^ ror(w[i - 2], 19) ^ w[i - 2] >> 10;
            w[i] = w[i - 16] + s0 + w[i - 7] + s1;
        }
        uint32_t a = h[0], b = h[1], c = h[2], d = h[3], e = h[4], f = h[5], g = h[6], k = h[7];
        for (int i = 0; i < 64; i++) {
            uint32_t t1 = k + (ror(e, 6) ^ ror(e, 11) ^ ror(e, 25)) + ((e & f) ^ (~e & g)) + K[i] + w[i];
            uint32_t t2 = (ror(a, 2) ^ ror(a, 13) ^ ror(a, 22)) + ((a & b) ^ (a & c) ^ (b & c));
            k = g, g = f, f = e, e = d + t1, d = c, c = b, b = a, a = t1 + t2;
        }
        h[0] += a, h[1] += b, h[2] += c, h[3] += d, h[4] += e, h[5] += f, h[6] += g, h[7] += k;
    }
}

#if defined(__x86_64__)
// The state lives in two registers as the SHA instructions want it: ABEF and CDGH. Each group of four rounds adds the
// round constants to four message words and runs sha256rnds2 twice; the message schedule for words 16..63 is
// msg2(msg1(W[t-16..], W[t-12..]) + W[t-7..], W[t-4..]).
__attribute__((target("sha,sse4.1"))) static void blocks_ni(uint32_t h[8], const uint8_t *p, size_t n) {
    const __m128i bswap = _mm_set_epi64x(0x0c0d0e0f08090a0bull, 0x0405060700010203ull);
    __m128i t = _mm_shuffle_epi32(_mm_loadu_si128((const __m128i *)&h[0]), 0xb1);   // CDAB
    __m128i s1 = _mm_shuffle_epi32(_mm_loadu_si128((const __m128i *)&h[4]), 0x1b);  // EFGH
    __m128i s0 = _mm_alignr_epi8(t, s1, 8);                                          // ABEF
    s1 = _mm_blend_epi16(s1, t, 0xf0);                                               // CDGH
    for (; n; n--, p += 64) {
        __m128i a0 = s0, c0 = s1, m[4];
        for (int g = 0; g < 16; g++) {
            __m128i *w = &m[g & 3];
            if (g < 4) *w = _mm_shuffle_epi8(_mm_loadu_si128((const __m128i *)(p + 16 * g)), bswap);
            else
                *w = _mm_sha256msg2_epu32(_mm_add_epi32(_mm_sha256msg1_epu32(*w, m[(g + 1) & 3]),
                                                        _mm_alignr_epi8(m[(g + 3) & 3], m[(g + 2) & 3], 4)),
                                          m[(g + 3) & 3]);
            __m128i k = _mm_add_epi32(*w, _mm_loadu_si128((const __m128i *)&K[4 * g]));
            s1 = _mm_sha256rnds2_epu32(s1, s0, k);
            s0 = _mm_sha256rnds2_epu32(s0, s1, _mm_shuffle_epi32(k, 0x0e));
        }
        s0 = _mm_add_epi32(s0, a0);
        s1 = _mm_add_epi32(s1, c0);
    }
    t = _mm_shuffle_epi32(s0, 0x1b);                  // FEBA
    s1 = _mm_shuffle_epi32(s1, 0xb1);                 // DCHG
    _mm_storeu_si128((__m128i *)&h[0], _mm_blend_epi16(t, s1, 0xf0));   // DCBA
    _mm_storeu_si128((__m128i *)&h[4], _mm_alignr_epi8(s1, t, 8));      // HGFE
}
#endif

static void blocks(uint32_t h[8], const uint8_t *p, size_t n) {
#if defined(__x86_64__)
    static int ni = -1;
    if (ni < 0) ni = __builtin_cpu_supports("sha") && __builtin_cpu_supports("sse4.1");
    if (ni) return blocks_ni(h, p, n);
#endif
    blocks_c(h, p, n);
}

void sha256_init(Sha256 *s) {
    static const uint32_t iv[8] = {0x6a09e667, 0xbb67ae85, 0x3c6ef372, 0xa54ff53a,
                                   0x510e527f, 0x9b05688c, 0x1f83d9ab, 0x5be0cd19};
    memcpy(s->h, iv, sizeof iv);
    s->bytes = 0;
    s->used = 0;
}

void sha256_update(Sha256 *s, const void *data, size_t n) {
    const uint8_t *p = data;
    s->bytes += n;
    if (s->used) {
        size_t k = 64 - s->used < n ? 64 - s->used : n;
        memcpy(s->buf + s->used, p, k);
        s->used += (uint32_t)k, p += k, n -= k;
        if (s->used < 64) return;
        blocks(s->h, s->buf, 1);
        s->used = 0;
    }
    if (n >= 64) {
        blocks(s->h, p, n / 64);
        p += n & ~(size_t)63, n &= 63;
    }
    memcpy(s->buf, p, n);
    s->used = (uint32_t)n;
}

void sha256_final(Sha256 *s, uint8_t out[32]) {
    uint64_t bits = s->bytes * 8;
    uint8_t pad[72] = {0x80};
    size_t k = (s->used < 56 ? 56 : 120) - s->used;
    for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) pad[k + i] = (uint8_t)(bits >> (56 - 8 * i));
    sha256_update(s, pad, k + 8);
    for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++)
        out[4 * i] = (uint8_t)(s->h[i] >> 24), out[4 * i + 1] = (uint8_t)(s->h[i] >> 16),
        out[4 * i + 2] = (uint8_t)(s->h[i] >> 8), out[4 * i + 3] = (uint8_t)s->h[i];
}

void sha256(const void *data, size_t n, uint8_t out[32]) {
    Sha256 s;
    sha256_init(&s);
    sha256_update(&s, data, n);
    sha256_final(&s, out);
}
```

`runtime/sha256.h`:

```h
// SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4), streaming. Uses the x86 SHA extensions when the CPU has them, portable C otherwise.
#pragma once
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>

typedef struct {
    uint32_t h[8];
    uint64_t bytes;      // message bytes so far
    uint8_t buf[64];     // a partial block
    uint32_t used;
} Sha256;

void sha256_init(Sha256 *s);
void sha256_update(Sha256 *s, const void *data, size_t n);
void sha256_final(Sha256 *s, uint8_t out[32]);
```
