`tools/make_romfs_patches.py`:

```py
# Adapted from MacNativeGames games/totk/scripts/make_romfs_patches.py @ ebe621d (MIT, Copyright (c) 2026
# MacNativeGames contributors).
"""Build the 60 fps RomFS overlay for TotK 1.1.1, 1.2.1 or 1.4.3 (runtime/romfs.c, TOTK_ROMFS_PATCHES).

UI/LayoutArchive/Common.Product.<110 or 140>.Nin_NX_NVN.blarc.zs: the weapon / shield / material quick menus capture the game
picture for their background when the panes C_CaptureBG_00, C_CaptureClearBG_00 and P_CaptureClearBG_00 become
visible at animation frame 1.0 (anim/ShortCutBG_00_In.bflan), AutoBuilder the same with C_CaptureBG_00
(anim/AutoBuilder_00_In.bflan). UI animations advance 0.5 frames per game frame at 60 fps, so the capture lands after
the world stopped drawing and the background can be black. The visibility keys move to frame 0.0: the live world is
captured at once (upstream checked weapon, shield, material and ability wheel at 60 fps, and 30 fps).
The game-over flow fix of the same upstream script is 1.0.0 only (1.1.1, 1.2.1 and 1.4.3 run DmF_SY_GameOver.110) and is
left out.

--aspect <w>x<h> (a game resolution of another shape than 16:9, such as 3440x1440 or 1280x800) also lays the UI out
for that shape (tools/ultrawide_layout.py): menus keep their 16:9 proportions in the middle, full-screen backgrounds
cover the screen and the HUD moves to the screen's corners (wider) or its top and bottom edges (narrower). totk.exe
loads that overlay from romfs-patches-<w>x<h> when the game resolution is that size (runtime/romfs.c overlay_init);
the camera's side of it is the patch set aspect (recomp/patches-v121.txt, patches-v143.txt).

--xbox-prompts: the same overlay with the A and B, and the X and Y button prompts swapped, for pad_layout = xbox_prompts
(runtime/romfs.c overlay_init loads romfs-patches-xbox in place of romfs-patches). That layout plays an Xbox pad by
position, as nintendo does: the button that does Switch A is labelled B, and the prompts then name the label. Built from
the game's own images and glyphs, nothing added:
- the action prompt (blyt/DoCommand_00.bflyt) draws the letter images Nt_KeyTexA/B/X/Y_00 of timg/__Combined.bntx in
  the Common archive: their image data is swapped (same format, size and tiling). Around it, a diamond names the
  other face buttons with one-letter text panes (T_B_00, T_X_00, ...). The game fills them from the messages of the
  same name in LayoutMsg/DoCommand_00.msbt of each Mals/<language> archive, over the layout's own text: both have
  their letters swapped the same way. The diamond's shape (Nt_KeyBtnSubBase*) shows the button's position, which
  stays right.
- every other prompt is text: the button glyphs U+E040 A, U+E041 B, U+E042 X, U+E043 Y of scft/External.bfotf, the
  same font in each Font/Font*.Nin_NX_NVN.bfarc.zs. Their CFF outlines and horizontal metrics are swapped.

Input: build/extracted/<version>/romfs (romfs.bin and index.json, verified by tools/extract.py). Output:
build/<version>/romfs-patches/<path> by default (romfs-patches-xbox with --xbox-prompts), and <out>/manifest.tsv (path, size, SHA-256 of the overlay, SHA-256 of the original). Run with .venv-py314.
"""
import argparse
import compression.zstd as zstd
import hashlib
import importlib.util
import json
import re
import struct
from pathlib import Path

root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
ap.add_argument('--version', choices=('v111', 'v121', 'v143'), default='v121')
ap.add_argument('--romfs', type=Path, help='default build/extracted/<version>/romfs')
ap.add_argument('--out', type=Path,
                help='default build/<version>/romfs-patches (romfs-patches-xbox with --xbox-prompts)')
ap.add_argument('--aspect', help='<w>x<h> of a game resolution of another shape than 16:9: also lay the UI out for it')
ap.add_argument('--xbox-prompts', action='store_true', help='swap the A/B and X/Y button prompts as well')
args = ap.parse_args()
args.romfs = args.romfs or root / 'build/extracted' / args.version / 'romfs'
args.out = args.out or root / 'build' / args.version / ('romfs-patches-xbox' if args.xbox_prompts else 'romfs-patches')
index = json.loads((args.romfs / 'index.json').read_text())
assert index['status'] == 'pass'
files = {f['path']: f for f in index['files']}


def sarc_nodes(data):
    """(name, node offset, absolute start, end) of every SARC member, in SFAT order."""
    assert data[:4] == b'SARC' and data[6:8] == b'\xff\xfe'
    header, size, start = struct.unpack_from('<HxxII', data, 4)
    assert size == len(data) and data[header:header + 4] == b'SFAT'
    count = struct.unpack_from('<H', data, header + 6)[0]
    names = header + 12 + count * 16
    assert data[names:names + 4] == b'SFNT'
    names += 8
    out = []
    for i in range(count):
        node = header + 12 + i * 16
        _, attribute, lo, hi = struct.unpack_from('<4I', data, node)
        offset = names + (attribute & 0xffffff) * 4
        out.append((data[offset:data.index(0, offset, start)].decode(), node, start + lo, start + hi))
    return out


def sarc_members(data):
    """name -> (absolute start, end) of every SARC member."""
    return {name: (lo, hi) for name, _, lo, hi in sarc_nodes(data)}


def flvi_keys(data, base):
    """(pane name, absolute key offset, keys) of every FLVI (visibility) step track in the BFLAN at data[base:]."""
    assert data[base:base + 4] == b'FLAN' and data[base + 4:base + 6] == b'\xff\xfe'
    pos, out = base + 0x14, []
    for _ in range(struct.unpack_from('<H', data, base + 0x10)[0]):
        magic, size = data[pos:pos + 4], struct.unpack_from('<I', data, pos + 4)[0]
        if magic == b'pai1':
            count, table = struct.unpack_from('<H', data, pos + 14)[0], pos + struct.unpack_from('<I', data, pos + 16)[0]
            for e in range(count):
                eo = pos + struct.unpack_from('<I', data, table + 4 * e)[0]
                name = data[eo:eo + 28].split(b'\0')[0].decode()
                for t in range(data[eo + 28]):
                    to = eo + struct.unpack_from('<I', data, eo + 32 + 4 * t)[0]
                    if data[to:to + 4] != b'FLVI':
                        continue
                    for g in range(data[to + 4]):
                        go = to + struct.unpack_from('<I', data, to + 8 + 4 * g)[0]
                        assert data[go + 2] == 1, 'visibility tracks are step curves'
                        ko = go + struct.unpack_from('<I', data, go + 8)[0]
                        keys = [struct.unpack_from('<fH', data, ko + 8 * k)
                                for k in range(struct.unpack_from('<H', data, go + 4)[0])]
                        out.append((name, ko, keys))
        pos += size
    return out


def bntx_swap(data, base, pairs):
    """Swap the image data of each (name, name) pair of textures in the BNTX at data[base:] (names without the ^
    suffix). Both of a pair must have the same header from flags to layout (format, size, tiling, mips) and image
    size, so the bytes of one are a valid image of the other."""
    assert data[base:base + 4] == b'BNTX' and data[base + 0x20:base + 0x24] == b'NX  '
    count, table = struct.unpack_from('<IQ', data, base + 0x24)
    found = {}
    for k in range(count):
        info = base + struct.unpack_from('<Q', data, base + table + 8 * k)[0]
        assert data[info:info + 4] == b'BRTI'
        name = base + struct.unpack_from('<Q', data, info + 0x60)[0]
        name = data[name + 2:name + 2 + struct.unpack_from('<H', data, name)[0]].decode().split('^')[0]
        mips = base + struct.unpack_from('<Q', data, info + 0x70)[0]
        shape = bytes(data[info + 0x10:info + 0x3c]) + bytes(data[info + 0x50:info + 0x54])
        start, size = base + struct.unpack_from('<Q', data, mips)[0], struct.unpack_from('<I', data, info + 0x50)[0]
        found[name] = (shape, start, size)
    for a, b in pairs:
        assert a in found and b in found, f'{a} or {b} missing from the texture list'
        (shape_a, at_a, size), (shape_b, at_b, _) = found[a], found[b]
        assert shape_a == shape_b, f'{a} and {b} differ in format, size or tiling'
        data[at_a:at_a + size], data[at_b:at_b + size] = data[at_b:at_b + size], data[at_a:at_a + size]


def bflyt_letters(data, base, end, swap):
    """Swap the text of the one-letter text panes T_<letter>_<n> (A, B, X or Y) in the BFLYT at data[base:end] by
    swap (letter -> letter); the names of the panes changed. Same length (one UTF-16 letter and its terminator)."""
    assert data[base:base + 4] == b'FLYT'
    pos, changed = base + struct.unpack_from('<H', data, base + 6)[0], []
    while pos + 8 <= end:
        magic, size = data[pos:pos + 4], struct.unpack_from('<I', data, pos + 4)[0]
        if magic == b'txt1':
            name = data[pos + 12:pos + 36].split(b'\0')[0].decode()
            length = struct.unpack_from('<H', data, pos + 0x56)[0]
            at = pos + struct.unpack_from('<I', data, pos + 0x64)[0]
            letter = data[at:at + 2].decode('utf-16-le') if length == 4 and at > pos else ''
            if letter in swap and re.fullmatch(r'T_[ABXY]_\d+', name):
                data[at:at + 2] = swap[letter].encode('utf-16-le')
                changed.append(name)
        if not size:
            break
        pos += size
    return changed


def msbt_letters(data, swap):
    """Swap the one-letter messages labelled T_<letter>_<n> (A, B, X or Y) in the UTF-16 MSBT data (a bytearray) by
    swap; the labels changed. The game sets a layout's text panes from the messages of the same name in
    Mals/<language>/LayoutMsg/<layout>.msbt, over the text stored in the layout."""
    assert data[:8] == b'MsgStdBn' and data[0x0c] == 1, 'not a UTF-16 MSBT'
    sections, pos = {}, 0x20
    for _ in range(struct.unpack_from('<H', data, 0x0e)[0]):
        size = struct.unpack_from('<I', data, pos + 4)[0]
        sections[bytes(data[pos:pos + 4])] = (pos + 16, size)
        pos = (pos + 16 + size + 15) & ~15
    labels, (base, _) = {}, sections[b'LBL1']
    for g in range(struct.unpack_from('<I', data, base)[0]):
        count, at = struct.unpack_from('<II', data, base + 4 + 8 * g)
        at += base
        for _ in range(count):
            length = data[at]
            labels[struct.unpack_from('<I', data, at + 1 + length)[0]] = data[at + 1:at + 1 + length].decode()
            at += 1 + length + 4
    (base, size), changed = sections[b'TXT2'], []
    count = struct.unpack_from('<I', data, base)[0]
    offsets = list(struct.unpack_from(f'<{count}I', data, base + 4)) + [size]
    for i in range(count):
        at, length = base + offsets[i], offsets[i + 1] - offsets[i]
        letter = data[at:at + 2].decode('utf-16-le') if length == 4 else ''
        if letter in swap and re.fullmatch(r'T_[ABXY]_\d+', labels.get(i, '')):
            data[at:at + 2] = swap[letter].encode('utf-16-le')
            changed.append(labels[i])
    return changed


def cff_index(data, pos):
    """([(start, end)] of every item, offSize, end) of the CFF INDEX at data[pos:]."""
    count = struct.unpack_from('>H', data, pos)[0]
    if not count:
        return [], 0, pos + 2
    size = data[pos + 2]
    offsets = [int.from_bytes(data[pos + 3 + i * size:pos + 3 + (i + 1) * size], 'big') for i in range(count + 1)]
    first = pos + 2 + (count + 1) * size
    return [(first + offsets[i], first + offsets[i + 1]) for i in range(count)], size, first + offsets[-1]


def cff_charstrings(data, cff):
    """The offset (from the CFF table) of the CharStrings INDEX: operator 17 of the Top DICT. CID-keyed fonts (ROS,
    operator 12 30) are refused: their glyphs can use different private dictionaries."""
    _, _, pos = cff_index(data, cff + data[cff + 2])       # Name INDEX after the header
    top, _, _ = cff_index(data, pos)
    (pos, end), operands, found = top[0], [], None
    while pos < end:
        b = data[pos]
        if b <= 21:
            op = (12, data[pos + 1]) if b == 12 else b
            pos += 2 if b == 12 else 1
            assert op != (12, 30), 'CID-keyed CFF'
            if op == 17:
                found = operands[-1]
            operands = []
        elif b == 28:
            operands.append(struct.unpack_from('>h', data, pos + 1)[0]); pos += 3
        elif b == 29:
            operands.append(struct.unpack_from('>i', data, pos + 1)[0]); pos += 5
        elif b == 30:                                    # real number: nibbles up to an 0xf
            pos += 1
            while data[pos] & 0x0f != 0x0f and data[pos] & 0xf0 != 0xf0:
                pos += 1
            pos += 1
            operands.append(0)
        elif b <= 246:
            operands.append(b - 139); pos += 1
        elif b <= 250:
            operands.append((b - 247) * 256 + data[pos + 1] + 108); pos += 2
        else:
            operands.append(-(b - 251) * 256 - data[pos + 1] - 108); pos += 2
    assert found is not None, 'no CharStrings in the Top DICT'
    return found


def otf_glyph(data, cmap, code):
    """The glyph id of a code point in the format 4 (platform 3 encoding 1) subtable of the cmap at data[cmap:]."""
    for k in range(struct.unpack_from('>H', data, cmap + 2)[0]):
        platform, encoding, offset = struct.unpack_from('>HHI', data, cmap + 4 + 8 * k)
        p = cmap + offset
        if (platform, encoding) != (3, 1) or struct.unpack_from('>H', data, p)[0] != 4:
            continue
        seg = struct.unpack_from('>H', data, p + 6)[0] // 2
        for s in range(seg):
            end = struct.unpack_from('>H', data, p + 14 + 2 * s)[0]
            start = struct.unpack_from('>H', data, p + 16 + 2 * seg + 2 * s)[0]
            if not start <= code <= end:
                continue
            delta = struct.unpack_from('>h', data, p + 16 + 4 * seg + 2 * s)[0]
            at = p + 16 + 6 * seg + 2 * s
            ro = struct.unpack_from('>H', data, at)[0]
            glyph = code if not ro else struct.unpack_from('>H', data, at + ro + 2 * (code - start))[0]
            return (glyph + delta) & 0xffff if glyph else 0
    raise AssertionError(f'U+{code:04X} is not in the font')


def otf_checksum(data):
    data = bytes(data) + bytes(-len(data) % 4)
    return sum(struct.unpack(f'>{len(data) // 4}I', data)) & 0xffffffff


def bfotf_swap(data, pairs):
    """The BFOTF data with the glyphs of each (code point, code point) pair swapped: CFF outlines and horizontal
    metrics, then the table checksums. A BFOTF is an OpenType font after an 8-byte header; from offset 4 on, every
    4-byte word is XORed with one key, which the size field gives away (it holds the font's length)."""
    key = bytes(x ^ y for x, y in zip(data[4:8], struct.pack('>I', len(data) - 8)))
    plain = bytearray(data[:4]) + bytearray(x ^ key[i % 4] for i, x in enumerate(data[4:]))
    font = plain[8:]
    assert font[:4] == b'OTTO', 'not a CFF OpenType font'
    tables = {}
    for k in range(struct.unpack_from('>H', font, 4)[0]):
        tag, _, offset, length = struct.unpack_from('>4sIII', font, 12 + 16 * k)
        tables[tag] = (12 + 16 * k, offset, length)
    cff = tables[b'CFF '][1]
    strings, size, end = cff_index(font, cff + cff_charstrings(font, cff))
    hmtx, metrics = tables[b'hmtx'][1], struct.unpack_from('>H', font, tables[b'hhea'][1] + 34)[0]
    order = list(range(len(strings)))
    for a, b in pairs:
        ga, gb = otf_glyph(font, tables[b'cmap'][1], a), otf_glyph(font, tables[b'cmap'][1], b)
        assert 0 < ga < len(strings) and 0 < gb < len(strings) and ga < metrics and gb < metrics, (a, b, ga, gb)
        order[ga], order[gb] = order[gb], order[ga]
        ma, mb = hmtx + 4 * ga, hmtx + 4 * gb
        font[ma:ma + 4], font[mb:mb + 4] = font[mb:mb + 4], font[ma:ma + 4]
    # The CharStrings INDEX again with the items in the new order: the same length, so nothing after it moves.
    body = b''.join(bytes(font[slice(*strings[g])]) for g in order)
    first = strings[0][0]
    assert first + len(body) == end
    font[first:end] = body
    at, base = first - (len(strings) + 1) * size, 1   # the offset array ends where the first item starts
    for i, g in enumerate(order + [None]):
        font[at + i * size:at + (i + 1) * size] = base.to_bytes(size, 'big')
        if g is not None:
            base += strings[g][1] - strings[g][0]
    head = tables[b'head'][1]
    struct.pack_into('>I', font, head + 8, 0)
    for entry, offset, length in tables.values():
        struct.pack_into('>I', font, entry + 4, otf_checksum(font[offset:offset + length]))
    struct.pack_into('>I', font, head + 8, (0xb1b0afba - otf_checksum(font)) & 0xffffffff)
    plain[8:] = font
    return bytes(plain[:4]) + bytes(x ^ key[i % 4] for i, x in enumerate(plain[4:]))


def sarc_replace(data, new):
    """The SARC data with the members named in new (name -> bytes) replaced. The header, SFAT and SFNT stay; the
    members are laid out again in their old order, each at an offset with at least the alignment its old one had."""
    start = struct.unpack_from('<I', data, 12)[0]
    out = bytearray(data[:start])
    for name, node, lo, hi in sorted(sarc_nodes(data), key=lambda n: n[2]):
        align = min(lo & -lo, 0x2000) if lo else 0x2000
        out += bytes(-len(out) % align)
        body = new.get(name, data[lo:hi])
        struct.pack_into('<II', out, node + 8, len(out) - start, len(out) - start + len(body))
        out += body
    struct.pack_into('<I', out, 8, len(out))
    return bytes(out)


COMMON = {'v111': '110', 'v121': '110', 'v143': '140'}   # the version in the name of each game's Common archive
ARCHIVE = f'UI/LayoutArchive/Common.Product.{COMMON[args.version]}.Nin_NX_NVN.blarc.zs'
MEMBERS = {
    'anim/ShortCutBG_00_In.bflan': ('C_CaptureBG_00', 'C_CaptureClearBG_00', 'P_CaptureClearBG_00'),
    'anim/AutoBuilder_00_In.bflan': ('C_CaptureBG_00',),
}
KEY_TEXTURES = (('Nt_KeyTexA_00', 'Nt_KeyTexB_00'), ('Nt_KeyTexX_00', 'Nt_KeyTexY_00'))
KEY_GLYPHS = ((0xE040, 0xE041), (0xE042, 0xE043))   # A B, X Y in scft/External.bfotf
KEY_LETTERS = {'A': 'B', 'B': 'A', 'X': 'Y', 'Y': 'X'}   # the face-button diamond around the action prompt
FONTS = sorted(p for p in files if re.fullmatch(r'Font/Font(_\w+)?\.Nin_NX_NVN\.bfarc\.zs', p))
# The message archive of each language: the newest version in the RomFS (Mals/USen.Product.121.sarc.zs on 1.2.1).
MALS = {}
for p in files:
    m = re.fullmatch(r'Mals/(\w+)\.Product\.(\d+)\.sarc\.zs', p)
    if m and int(m[2]) > MALS.get(m[1], (0, ''))[0]:
        MALS[m[1]] = (int(m[2]), p)
MALS = sorted(p for _, p in MALS.values())
LAYOUT_MSG = 'LayoutMsg/DoCommand_00.msbt'

with (args.romfs / 'romfs.bin').open('rb') as image:
    def read(path):
        f = files[path]
        image.seek(f['offset'])
        b = image.read(f['size'])
        assert len(b) == f['size']
        return b
    dictionaries = {}
    pack = zstd.decompress(read('Pack/ZsDic.pack.zs'))
    for name, (lo, hi) in sarc_members(pack).items():
        d = zstd.ZstdDict(pack[lo:hi])
        dictionaries[d.dict_id] = d
    originals = {path: read(path) for path in [ARCHIVE] + (FONTS + MALS if args.xbox_prompts else [])}
raw = originals[ARCHIVE]
info = zstd.get_frame_info(raw)
dictionary = dictionaries[info.dictionary_id]
original = zstd.decompress(raw, zstd_dict=dictionary)
blarc = bytearray(original)
assert len(blarc) == info.decompressed_size
members = sarc_members(blarc)
patched = {}
for member, panes in MEMBERS.items():
    lo, hi = members[member]
    changed = []
    for name, ko, keys in flvi_keys(blarc, lo):
        if name not in panes:
            continue
        assert [(f, v) for f, v in keys] == [(0.0, 0), (1.0, 1)], (member, name, keys)
        struct.pack_into('<f', blarc, ko + 8, 0.0)
        changed.append(name)
    assert sorted(changed) == sorted(panes), (member, changed)
    patched[member] = changed
layout = []
if args.aspect:
    width, height = (int(v) for v in args.aspect.lower().split('x'))
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('ultrawide_layout', Path(__file__).with_name('ultrawide_layout.py'))
    ultrawide = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(ultrawide)
    layout = ultrawide.apply(blarc, members, width, height)
diff = [i for i in range(len(original)) if original[i] != blarc[i]]
touched = [members[m] for m in (*MEMBERS, *layout)]
assert diff and all(any(lo <= i < hi for lo, hi in touched) for i in diff), diff
outputs = {ARCHIVE: bytes(blarc)}   # RomFS path -> new contents (before compression)
if args.xbox_prompts:
    bntx_swap(blarc, members['timg/__Combined.bntx'][0], KEY_TEXTURES)
    letters = {}
    for member, (lo, hi) in members.items():
        if member.endswith('.bflyt'):
            changed = bflyt_letters(blarc, lo, hi, KEY_LETTERS)
            if changed:
                letters[member] = changed
    assert 'blyt/DoCommand_00.bflyt' in letters, 'no letter panes in blyt/DoCommand_00.bflyt'
    outputs[ARCHIVE] = bytes(blarc)
    assert FONTS, 'no Font/Font*.Nin_NX_NVN.bfarc.zs in the RomFS'
    for path in FONTS:
        frame = zstd.get_frame_info(originals[path])
        bfarc = zstd.decompress(originals[path], zstd_dict=dictionaries.get(frame.dictionary_id))
        lo, hi = sarc_members(bfarc)['scft/External.bfotf']
        outputs[path] = sarc_replace(bfarc, {'scft/External.bfotf': bfotf_swap(bfarc[lo:hi], KEY_GLYPHS)})
    assert MALS, 'no Mals/<language>.Product.<version>.sarc.zs in the RomFS'
    messages = {}
    for path in MALS:
        frame = zstd.get_frame_info(originals[path])
        mals = bytearray(zstd.decompress(originals[path], zstd_dict=dictionaries.get(frame.dictionary_id)))
        lo, hi = sarc_members(mals)[LAYOUT_MSG]
        msbt = bytearray(mals[lo:hi])
        changed = msbt_letters(msbt, KEY_LETTERS)
        assert len(changed) == sum(len(v) for v in letters.values()), (path, changed)
        mals[lo:hi] = msbt
        outputs[path] = bytes(mals)
        messages[path] = len(changed)

lines = []
for path, contents in outputs.items():
    raw = originals[path]
    dictionary = dictionaries.get(zstd.get_frame_info(raw).dictionary_id)
    data = zstd.compress(contents, level=19, zstd_dict=dictionary)
    assert zstd.decompress(data, zstd_dict=dictionary) == contents
    assert zstd.get_frame_info(data).dictionary_id == zstd.get_frame_info(raw).dictionary_id
    target = args.out / path
    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    target.write_bytes(data)
    lines.append('\t'.join([path, str(len(data)), hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest(), hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()]))
(args.out / 'manifest.tsv').write_text('# path\tsize\tsha256\toriginal_sha256 (tools/make_romfs_patches.py)\n'
                                       + ''.join(line + '\n' for line in lines))
print(json.dumps(dict(status='pass', path=ARCHIVE, members=patched, changed_bytes=len(diff),
                      ultrawide_layout=dict(aspect=args.aspect, members=len(layout)) if args.aspect else None,
                      xbox_prompts=dict(textures=KEY_TEXTURES, letters=letters, messages=messages, fonts=FONTS)
                      if args.xbox_prompts else None)))

```

`tools/mkw_cli.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Mario Kart World Windows recomp research driver (local game data only).

Stages: input audit -> local version lock -> ARM64 lift -> optional RomFS pack
-> incremental native build -> bounded boot experiment and diagnostic report.
This tool does not claim that a generated executable is playable.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import mkw_probe

BUILD_ID = 'mkw180'
TARGET_VERSION = '1.8.0'
UPDATE_BUILD_NUMBER = 917504
EXPECTED_TITLE = '0400C3F00006E000'
# Public 1.0.0 reference module IDs from kartnative's game-specific profile.
# NSO0 stores a 32-byte ID at header offset 0x40; the published value is 16 bytes.
# Different genuine revisions may have different IDs, so experimental overrides must be explicit.
KNOWN_BASE_MODULE_IDS = {
    'main': '9e244438c3d8ef1c703a6a85ef99c4f0',
    'subsdk0': 'd39a7a3d44530bb61b35690e5b0383d5',
    'sdk': '90ebba182862b9ecdc21fcb87b999012',
}


def nso_module_id(path: Path) -> str:
    with path.open('rb') as f:
        hdr = f.read(0x60)
    if len(hdr) < 0x60 or hdr[:4] != b'NSO0':
        raise ValueError(f'{path}: missing NSO0 header or module ID')
    return hdr[0x40:0x50].hex()


def check_module_ids(exefs: Path) -> tuple[bool, dict]:
    actual = {name: nso_module_id(exefs / name) for name in KNOWN_BASE_MODULE_IDS}
    return all(actual[name] == wanted for name, wanted in KNOWN_BASE_MODULE_IDS.items()), actual
MODULE_PATTERN = re.compile(r'^(?:main|sdk|subsdk\d+)$')
ERROR_PATTERNS = [
    ('game identity / loader', (r'wrong title', r'loader:', r'cannot read', r'NPDM', r'\bhash\b', r'module .*not loaded')),
    ('guest startup / constructors', (r'no DT_INIT', r'constructor', r'init::Start', r'not exported', r'fn ptr', r'could not resolve symbol')),
    ('Horizon / IPC', (r'unknown (?:svc|service)', r'ipc:', r'unsupported (?:svc|command)', r'kernel:', r'unknown port')),
    ('graphics / NVN', (r'NVN', r'vulkan', r'shader', r'pipeline', r'vk_', r'GPU')),
    ('memory / scheduling', (r'memory commit', r'virtual memory', r'allocation failed', r'deadlock', r'thread')),
]
MILESTONES = [
    ('module-load', [r'loader:.*loaded', r'ldr:.*loaded', r'modules linked']),
    ('main-thread', [r'boot: Switch2 NPDM main', r'boot: ENTER nn::init::Start']),
    ('guest-initialization', [r'boot: ENTER .* DT_INIT', r'boot: DT_INIT .*state=2']),
    ('first-nvn-call', [r'boot: Switch2 FIRST_NVNCALL']),
    ('first-present', [r'presented \(nvn calls', r'boot: frames \d+ presented']),
]


def sha256(path: Path) -> str:
    dig = hashlib.sha256()
    with path.open('rb') as f:
        for block in iter(lambda: f.read(8 << 20), b''):
            dig.update(block)
    return dig.hexdigest()


def add_common(ap):
    ap.add_argument('--repo', type=Path, required=True, help='mkw-recomp source checkout')
    ap.add_argument('--dump', type=Path, required=True, help='Extracted Mario Kart World update directory with exefs/ and romfs/')


def paths(args):
    repo = args.repo.resolve()
    exefs, romfs = mkw_probe.locate(args.dump.resolve())
    if not (repo / 'tools' / 'build_game.py').is_file() or not (repo / 'recomp' / 'gen.py').is_file():
        raise ValueError(f'{repo} is not an mkw-recomp source checkout')
    npdm = mkw_probe.npdm(exefs / 'main.npdm')
    if npdm['title_id'] != EXPECTED_TITLE:
        raise ValueError(f'Unexpected program ID {npdm["title_id"]}, need {EXPECTED_TITLE}')
    for required in ('main', 'sdk', 'subsdk0'):
        if not (exefs / required).is_file():
            raise ValueError(f'Missing MKW module {exefs / required}')
    names = [name for name in ['main'] + [f'subsdk{i}' for i in range(10)] + ['sdk']
             if (exefs / name).is_file()]
    return repo, exefs, romfs, names


def python_of(repo: Path) -> str:
    candidates = [repo / '.venv' / 'Scripts' / 'python.exe', repo / '.venv' / 'bin' / 'python']
    for f in candidates:
        if f.is_file():
            return str(f)
    return sys.executable


def local_hash_path(repo: Path) -> Path:
    return repo / 'build' / 'mkw-local' / 'expected-mkw180.json'


def create_lock(exefs: Path, dest: Path, attestation: bool, allow_unknown_ids=False) -> dict:
    if not attestation:
        raise ValueError('Update 1.8.0 is not proven by the program ID. Use --i-confirm-update-180 only when the supplied dump is the 1.8.0 update.')
    # There are no verified public 1.8.0 module IDs pinned in this devkit.
    # Reject a complete match to the known 1.0.0 IDs, but NEVER claim that
    # a non-match proves 1.8.0. SHA-256 values below are a LOCAL consistency lock.
    known_ids, base_ids = check_module_ids(exefs)
    if known_ids:
        raise ValueError('ExeFS matches the known base 1.0.0 module IDs. This is not evidence of a 1.8.0 update.')
    module_ids = {p.name: nso_module_id(p) for p in exefs.iterdir()
                  if p.is_file() and MODULE_PATTERN.fullmatch(p.name)}
    files = sorted([p for p in exefs.iterdir() if p.is_file() and not p.name.startswith('.')], key=lambda p: p.name)
    allowed = {'rtld', 'main.npdm'} | {n for n in [p.name for p in files] if MODULE_PATTERN.fullmatch(n)}
    unknown = [p.name for p in files if p.name not in allowed]
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(f'Unexpected ExeFS files: {unknown}')
    expected = {
        '_comment': ('Mario Kart World LOCAL user-supplied standalone update claimed to be 1.8.0. '
                     'Version and completeness are NOT independently verified. SHA-256 locks input consistency only.'),
        'title_id': EXPECTED_TITLE,
        'display_version': TARGET_VERSION,
        'update_build_number_claimed': UPDATE_BUILD_NUMBER,
        'version_verified': False,
        'matches_known_base_100_ids': known_ids,
        'module_ids': module_ids,
        'mkw_version_attested_not_verified': True,
        'exefs_sha256': {p.name: sha256(p) for p in files},
    }
    dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if dest.is_file():
        old = json.loads(dest.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
        if old.get('exefs_sha256') != expected['exefs_sha256']:
            raise ValueError('Local version-lock hashes changed. Refusing overwrite; check game version or dump integrity.')
    else:
        dest.write_text(json.dumps(expected, indent=2) + '\n', encoding='utf-8')
    return expected


def validate_lock(exefs: Path, lock: Path) -> None:
    if not lock.is_file():
        raise ValueError(f'Missing {lock}; run `prepare --i-confirm-update-180` first')
    expected = json.loads(lock.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
    for name, wanted in expected['exefs_sha256'].items():
        file = exefs / name
        if not file.is_file() or sha256(file) != wanted:
            raise ValueError(f'Input changed from local version lock: {file}')


def command(argv: list[str], cwd: Path, dry_run=False) -> None:
    display = ' '.join('"'+a+'"' if ' ' in a else a for a in argv)
    print(f'[{cwd}] $ {display}', flush=True)
    if dry_run:
        return
    result = subprocess.run(argv, cwd=cwd, check=False)
    if result.returncode:
        raise RuntimeError(f'Command failed with exit code {result.returncode}: {argv[1]}')


def do_prepare(args):
    repo, exefs, romfs, modules = paths(args)
    if romfs is None or not romfs.is_dir() or not any(romfs.iterdir()):
        raise ValueError('No non-empty RomFS directory found; an update-only dump must include all required game assets.')
    info = create_lock(exefs, local_hash_path(repo), args.i_confirm_update_180)
    output = {'program_id': EXPECTED_TITLE, 'version_claimed': TARGET_VERSION,
              'update_build_number_claimed': UPDATE_BUILD_NUMBER,
              'version_verified': False, 'module_ids': info['module_ids'],
              'exefs': str(exefs),
              'romfs': str(romfs) if romfs else None,
              'modules': modules, 'hashes': info['exefs_sha256']}
    report = repo / 'build' / 'mkw-local' / 'input.json'
    report.write_text(json.dumps(output, indent=2) + '\n', encoding='utf-8')
    print(f'PREPARED: {report}\nLocal SHA-256 lock created. Claimed update: {TARGET_VERSION} (not independently verified). Modules: {", ".join(modules)}')


def do_xlate(args):
    repo = args.repo.resolve()
    source = repo/'tools'/'build_xlate.py'
    if not source.is_file():
        raise ValueError(f'Missing translator build script: {source}')
    # A child of the repository build tree, so NuGet discovery sees it for
    # build/xlate/xlate and build/xlate/ryujinx projects. No global NuGet edits.
    config = repo/'build'/'xlate'/'NuGet.Config'
    contents = ("<?xml version=\"1.0\" encoding=\"utf-8\"?>\n"
                "<configuration>\n  <packageSources>\n    <clear />\n"
                "    <add key=\"nuget.org\" value=\"https://api.nuget.org/v3/index.json\" />\n"
                "  </packageSources>\n  <auditSources>\n    <clear />\n"
                "    <add key=\"nuget.org\" value=\"https://api.nuget.org/v3/index.json\" />\n"
                "  </auditSources>\n</configuration>\n")
    if config.exists() and config.read_text(encoding='utf-8') != contents:
        raise ValueError(f'Refusing to overwrite a different local NuGet config: {config}')
    if args.dry_run:
        print(f'Would write project-local NuGet sources to: {config}')
    else:
        config.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        config.write_text(contents, encoding='utf-8')
    command([python_of(repo), str(source)], repo, args.dry_run)


def do_generate(args):
    repo, exefs, _, modules = paths(args)
    validate_lock(exefs, local_hash_path(repo))
    cmd = [python_of(repo), str(repo/'recomp'/'gen.py'), '--exefs', str(exefs),
           '--out', str(repo/'generated'/BUILD_ID), '--modules', ','.join(modules)]
    if args.jobs:
        cmd += ['--jobs', str(args.jobs)]
    if args.limit:
        cmd += ['--limit', str(args.limit)]
        print('NOTE: --limit generates a partial CPU test, never a bootable game.', flush=True)
    command(cmd, repo, args.dry_run)
    if not args.dry_run:
        marker = repo/'generated'/BUILD_ID/'.mkw_partial'
        if args.limit:
            marker.write_text(f'Partial test generation with --limit {args.limit}; not a boot build.\n', encoding='utf-8')
        elif marker.exists():
            marker.unlink()
        if not args.limit:
            command([python_of(repo), str(repo/'tools'/'mkw_generated_overlays.py'),
                     '--repo', str(repo), '--exefs', str(exefs)], repo)


def do_pack(args):
    repo, _, romfs, _ = paths(args)
    if romfs is None:
        raise ValueError('No extracted RomFS found')
    packed = repo/'build'/'extracted'/BUILD_ID/'romfs'
    if (romfs/'romfs.bin').is_file() and (romfs/'index.json').is_file():
        print('Already packed. Use this folder with --romfs in build_game.py:')
        print(romfs)
        return
    if (packed/'romfs.bin').is_file() and (packed/'index.json').is_file() and not args.force:
        print(f'Reusing packed RomFS: {packed} (use --force to repack after changes)')
        return
    command([python_of(repo), str(repo/'tools'/'pack_romfs.py'), '--dir', str(romfs),
             '--out', str(packed)], repo, args.dry_run)


def chosen_romfs(repo: Path, romfs: Path | None) -> Path:
    selection = repo/'build'/'mkw-local'/'selected-romfs.json'
    if selection.is_file():
        spec = json.loads(selection.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
        folder = Path(spec['path'])
        if not (folder/'index.json').is_file():
            raise ValueError(f'Selected RomFS disappeared: {folder}; rebuild')
        if spec['backend'] == 'mkw-loose-v1' and not (folder/'loose-root.txt').is_file():
            raise ValueError(f'Selected loose RomFS root missing: {folder}; rebuild')
        if spec['backend'] != 'mkw-loose-v1' and not (folder/'romfs.bin').is_file():
            raise ValueError(f'Selected packed RomFS image missing: {folder}; rebuild')
        return folder
    if romfs and (romfs/'index.json').is_file() and (romfs/'romfs.bin').is_file():
        return romfs
    # MKW builder's new zero-copy mode uses the native runtime's loose backend.
    loose = repo/'build'/'extracted'/BUILD_ID/'romfs-loose'
    if (loose/'index.json').is_file() and (loose/'loose-root.txt').is_file():
        doc = json.loads((loose/'index.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
        if doc.get('backend') == 'mkw-loose-v1' and doc.get('status') == 'inventory-only':
            return loose
    p = repo/'build'/'extracted'/BUILD_ID/'romfs'
    if not (p/'index.json').is_file() or not (p/'romfs.bin').is_file():
        raise ValueError(f'RomFS not indexed at {loose} or packed at {p}; run builder first')
    return p


def do_build(args):
    repo, exefs, romfs, _ = paths(args)
    validate_lock(exefs, local_hash_path(repo))
    gen = repo/'generated'/BUILD_ID/'layout.json'
    if not gen.exists():
        raise ValueError(f'Missing {gen}; run generate first')
    if (gen.parent/'.mkw_partial').exists():
        raise ValueError('Generated code is from --limit partial test; rerun generate without --limit')
    command([python_of(repo), str(repo/'tools'/'mkw_generated_overlays.py'),
             '--repo', str(repo), '--exefs', str(exefs)], repo, args.dry_run)
    build_source = repo/'tools'/'build_game.py'
    # The runtime uses a nonzero rt_game_version for TotK-only constructor
    # and NVN return-address checks. MKW MUST have version 0 to use the
    # generic Switch 2 boot path. Earlier kits erroneously registered 180.
    if "'mkw180': '1.8.0'" in build_source.read_text(encoding='utf-8'):
        raise ValueError('Outdated mkw180=180 registration would activate TotK boot checks. Run tools/mkw_build_version.py --repo <repo> --apply')
    packed = chosen_romfs(repo, romfs)
    exe = repo/'build'/BUILD_ID/('mkw.exe' if os.name=='nt' else 'mkw')
    cmd = [python_of(repo), str(repo/'tools'/'build_game.py'), '--version', BUILD_ID,
           '--expected', str(local_hash_path(repo)), '--exefs', str(exefs),
           '--romfs', str(packed)]
    if args.jobs:
        cmd += ['--jobs', str(args.jobs)]
    if args.dry_run:
        print(f'Expected local executable: {exe}')
    command(cmd, repo, args.dry_run)
    if not args.dry_run:
        print(f'BUILT: {exe}\nNOTE: a successful link does not establish Mario Kart World boot compatibility.')


def analyze_text(log: str) -> dict:
    stages = {name: any(re.search(p, log, re.I) for p in patterns) for name, patterns in MILESTONES}
    fatals = [line.strip() for line in log.splitlines()
              if re.search(r'\bFATAL\b|\bfatal:|\bERROR\b|unsupported|not implemented', line, re.I)]
    categories = {group: [line for line in fatals if any(re.search(p, line, re.I) for p in patterns)]
                  for group, patterns in ERROR_PATTERNS}
    category = next((group for group, matches in categories.items() if matches), 'unclassified') if fatals else 'none'
    if stages['first-nvn-call']:
        level = 'M2 early graphics reached; NOT title-screen boot'
    elif stages['guest-initialization']:
        level = 'guest constructors started; boot not established'
    elif stages['main-thread']:
        level = 'main thread initialized; boot not established'
    elif stages['module-load']:
        level = 'modules linked; boot not established'
    else:
        level = 'no boot milestone proved'
    return {'stages': stages, 'boot_evidence': level, 'fatal_count': len(fatals),
            'first_fatals': fatals[:25], 'likely_category': category,
            'title_screen_seen': False, 'note': 'A text log cannot verify a rendered title screen.'}


def do_analyze(args):
    log = args.log.resolve()
    if not log.is_file():
        raise ValueError(f'Log missing: {log}')
    result = analyze_text(log.read_text(encoding='utf-8',errors='replace'))
    output = args.out or log.with_suffix('.summary.json')
    output.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + '\n', encoding='utf-8')
    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))
    print(f'SUMMARY: {output}')


def do_run(args):
    repo, exefs, romfs, _ = paths(args)
    exe = repo/'build'/BUILD_ID/('mkw.exe' if os.name=='nt' else 'mkw')
    if not exe.is_file():
        raise ValueError(f'No executable found at {exe}; build first')
    lock = local_hash_path(repo)
    validate_lock(exefs, lock)
    packed = chosen_romfs(repo, romfs)
    mode = {'selftest': '--selftest', 'services': '--probe-services',
            'boot': '--boot', 'game': None, 'first-frame': None}[args.mode]
    cmd = [str(exe), '--exefs', str(exefs), '--romfs', str(packed),
           '--profile', str(repo/'build'/'profile-mkw180')]
    if mode:
        cmd.append(mode)
    env = os.environ.copy()
    env['MKW_BOOT_TRACE'] = '1'
    # An earlier diagnostic run must not leak its first-NVN stop into a game run.
    env.pop('MKW_STOP_ON_NVN', None)
    if args.mode == 'boot':
        env['MKW_STOP_ON_NVN'] = '1'
    env['TOTK_NATIVE_GS'] = '1'
    env['TOTK_ASTC'] = 'gpu'
    env['TOTK_ASTC_BC'] = '1'
    env['TOTK_MEMORY'] = 'auto'
    # Memory pool from the base 1.0.0 research is NOT imposed on the unverified 1.8.0 update.
    # Allow explicit testing when users have measured the update's requirements.
    if args.app_pool:
        env['TOTK_APP_POOL'] = args.app_pool
    if args.gpu:
        env['TOTK_GPU'] = args.gpu
    env['TOTK_TRACE'] = args.trace
    report_dir = repo/'build'/'mkw-local'/'runs'
    report_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    label = time.strftime('%Y%m%d_%H%M%S')+'_'+args.mode
    log = report_dir/(label+'.log')
    shot_dir = report_dir/(label+'_guest_frames')
    if args.mode == 'first-frame':
        shot_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
        # These screenshots come from rt_frame_presented, not a fake host splash.
        # Use several frames because some runtimes count from zero.
        env['TOTK_SHOTS'] = '0-8:1'
        env['TOTK_SHOTS_DIR'] = str(shot_dir)
    print('RUN:', ' '.join(cmd), '\nLOG:', log, flush=True)
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    timed_out = False
    captured = None
    stopped_after_capture = False
    # Stream potentially huge host traces to a file, not to process memory.
    with log.open('w', encoding='utf-8') as output:
        proc = subprocess.Popen(cmd, cwd=repo, env=env, stdout=output, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
        if args.mode == 'first-frame':
            # A real guest-presented image may take >80s to appear.
            deadline = time.monotonic() + args.timeout
            while time.monotonic() < deadline and proc.poll() is None:
                candidates = sorted(shot_dir.glob('f*.png'))
                for file in candidates:
                    if file.stat().st_size >= 64:
                        with file.open('rb') as png:
                            start = png.read(8)
                            png.seek(-12, os.SEEK_END)
                            end = png.read(12)
                        if start == b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n' and end[4:8] == b'IEND':
                            captured = file
                            break
                if captured:
                    # Diagnostic-only capture: don't report a successful game exit.
                    time.sleep(0.5)
                    proc.terminate()
                    try:
                        proc.wait(timeout=5)
                    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                        proc.kill()
                        proc.wait()
                    stopped_after_capture = True
                    break
                time.sleep(0.25)
            if proc.poll() is None:
                timed_out = True
                proc.kill()
                proc.wait()
                rc = None
            else:
                rc = proc.returncode
        else:
            try:
                rc = proc.wait(timeout=None if args.timeout <= 0 else args.timeout)
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                timed_out = True
                proc.kill()
                proc.wait()
                rc = None
    # Avoid loading a multi-gigabyte trace into memory. Keep head + tail.
    with log.open('rb') as stream:
        beginning = stream.read(2 << 20)
        if log.stat().st_size > 5 << 20:
            stream.seek(-3 << 20, 2)
            ending = stream.read(3 << 20)
            data = (beginning + b'\n[... log truncated for summary ...]\n' + ending).decode('utf-8', 'replace')
        else:
            data = (beginning + stream.read()).decode('utf-8', 'replace')
    # The game's own logfile might contain diagnostics not sent to the console.
    game_log = repo/'build'/BUILD_ID/'logs'/'totk.log'
    if game_log.is_file() and game_log.stat().st_mtime >= time.time() - (time.monotonic() - t0) - 5:
        with game_log.open('rb') as g:
            if game_log.stat().st_size > 3 << 20:
                g.seek(-3 << 20, 2)
            data += '\n[game log]\n' + g.read().decode('utf-8', 'replace')
    report = analyze_text(data)
    report.update({'exit_code': rc, 'timed_out': timed_out, 'elapsed_s': round(time.monotonic()-t0,2),
                   'mode': args.mode, 'log': str(log),
                   'first_guest_frame_png': str(captured) if captured else None,
                   'first_guest_frame_captured': bool(captured),
                   'stopped_for_diagnostic': stopped_after_capture})
    log.with_suffix('.json').write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2)+'\n', encoding='utf-8')
    print('\n'.join(data.splitlines()[-45:]))
    print(f'\nRESULT: {report["boot_evidence"]}; first fatal: {(report["first_fatals"] or ["none"])[0]}')
    if captured:
        print(f'ACTUAL GUEST FRAME SAVED: {captured}')
        print('This proves one frame was presented, not that a title/loading screen is correct.')
    print('Timing:', 'timeout' if timed_out else f'exit code {rc}', 'in', report['elapsed_s'],'seconds')
    if timed_out:
        print('TIMEOUT: not automatically a successful boot, inspect the game log.')
    return 0 if (captured and stopped_after_capture) or (rc == 0 and not timed_out) else 3


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest='cmd', required=True)
    p = sub.add_parser('prepare', help='Confirm identity and pin hashes of a locally supplied dump')
    add_common(p)
    p.add_argument('--i-confirm-update-180', action='store_true', help='Attest input is a 1.8.0 update; does not establish dump completeness')
    p.set_defaults(fn=do_prepare)
    p = sub.add_parser('xlate', help='Build shader translator with project-local nuget.org config')
    p.add_argument('--repo', type=Path, required=True)
    p.add_argument('--dry-run', action='store_true')
    p.set_defaults(fn=do_xlate)
    p = sub.add_parser('generate', help='Lift local ARM64 modules using the gen.py of this checkout')
    add_common(p)
    p.add_argument('--jobs', type=int)
    p.add_argument('--limit', type=int, default=0)
    p.add_argument('--dry-run', action='store_true')
    p.set_defaults(fn=do_generate)
    p = sub.add_parser('pack', help='Create the packed RomFS image, unless already present')
    add_common(p)
    p.add_argument('--force', action='store_true')
    p.add_argument('--dry-run', action='store_true')
    p.set_defaults(fn=do_pack)
    p = sub.add_parser('build', help='Build local Windows executable incrementally')
    add_common(p)
    p.add_argument('--jobs', type=int, default=4)
    p.add_argument('--dry-run', action='store_true')
    p.set_defaults(fn=do_build)
    p = sub.add_parser('run', help='Bounded host/boot experiment, never claims title screen')
    add_common(p)
    p.add_argument('--mode', choices=['selftest','services','boot','first-frame','game'], default='boot')
    p.add_argument('--timeout', type=int, default=240)
    p.add_argument('--gpu', choices=['null','vulkan'], default=None)
    p.add_argument('--trace', default='ipc,svc')
    p.add_argument('--app-pool', help='Optional research override of TOTK_APP_POOL for this child process (e.g. 0x...)')
    p.set_defaults(fn=do_run)
    p = sub.add_parser('analyze-log', help='Summarize failure stage of an existing Windows log')
    p.add_argument('--log', type=Path, required=True)
    p.add_argument('--out', type=Path)
    p.set_defaults(fn=do_analyze)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        ret = args.fn(args)
        return ret if isinstance(ret, int) else 0
    except (ValueError, OSError, RuntimeError) as e:
        print('ERROR:', e, file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

if __name__ == '__main__':
    raise SystemExit(main())
```

`tools/mkw_expected.py`:

```py
"""Write tools/data/expected-<name>.json for a Mario Kart World ExeFS: hashes and title id only, no game data.

    .venv\\Scripts\\python tools\\mkw_expected.py --exefs build\\extracted\\mkw180\\exefs --name mkw180 --display 1.8.0
"""
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import struct
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


def title_id(npdm):
    """Program id from the ACI0 block of main.npdm."""
    data = npdm.read_bytes()
    if data[:4] != b'META':
        raise SystemExit(f'{npdm}: not an NPDM')
    off, size = struct.unpack_from('<II', data, 0x70)
    aci = data[off:off + size]
    if aci[:4] != b'ACI0':
        raise SystemExit(f'{npdm}: no ACI0 block')
    return f'{struct.unpack_from("<Q", aci, 0x10)[0]:016X}'


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument('--exefs', type=Path, required=True)
    ap.add_argument('--name', required=True, help='build version name, e.g. mkw180')
    ap.add_argument('--display', required=True, help='display version, e.g. 1.8.0')
    args = ap.parse_args()
    files = sorted(p for p in args.exefs.iterdir() if p.is_file() and not p.name.startswith('.'))
    out = {
        '_comment': f'Mario Kart World {args.display} ExeFS. Hashes only; no game data.',
        'title_id': title_id(args.exefs / 'main.npdm'),
        'display_version': args.display,
        'exefs_sha256': {p.name: hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest() for p in files},
    }
    dst = ROOT / 'tools' / 'data' / f'expected-{args.name}.json'
    dst.write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=2) + '\n', encoding='utf-8')
    print(dst, out['title_id'], ', '.join(out['exefs_sha256']))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```

`tools/mkw_generated_overlays.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Apply the required MKW 1.8.0 heap-observer wrappers to freshly lifted C."""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import re
from pathlib import Path

MARKER = 'MKW_GENERATED_OVERLAYS_M15_26'
MAIN_SHA256 = '29040941362bf30175134a580a06fff7ffb8bb27e9cfed60d9ace9e9e2d982fe'
SDK_SHA256 = 'acdc4a29bb809955d6a680f3f8515e0bd1d6eb1028e6a38182f00dea08c309bd'
FUNCTIONS = {
    0x70003E3550: 'primary_alloc',
    0x70001A58A0: 'dealloc',
    0x70003F24C0: 'region_vfunc',
    0x70003F17A0: 'region_direct',
    0x7000805830: 'region_string',
}


def digest(path: Path) -> str:
    value = hashlib.sha256()
    with path.open('rb') as stream:
        for block in iter(lambda: stream.read(8 << 20), b''):
            value.update(block)
    return value.hexdigest()


def verify_exefs(exefs: Path) -> None:
    for name, expected in (('main', MAIN_SHA256), ('sdk', SDK_SHA256)):
        path = exefs / name
        if not path.is_file() or digest(path) != expected:
            raise ValueError(f'{name}: expected the audited MKW 1.8.0 module')


def definition(address: int) -> re.Pattern[str]:
    return re.compile(r'\bvoid\s+f_' + f'{address:x}' + r'\s*\(Cpu\s*\*c\)\s*\{')


def locate(repo: Path) -> dict[Path, list[tuple[int, str]]]:
    root = repo / 'generated' / 'mkw180' / 'main'
    if not root.is_dir():
        raise ValueError(f'generated main module is missing: {root}')
    result: dict[Path, list[tuple[int, str]]] = {}
    found = {address: [] for address in FUNCTIONS}
    patterns = {address: definition(address) for address in FUNCTIONS}
    for path in root.glob('main_*.c'):
        source = path.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
        for address, pattern in patterns.items():
            if pattern.search(source):
                found[address].append(path)
    for address, matches in found.items():
        if len(matches) != 1:
            raise ValueError(f'expected one lifted definition for {address:#x}; found {len(matches)}')
        result.setdefault(matches[0], []).append((address, FUNCTIONS[address]))
    return result


def wrapper(address: int, kind: str, original: str) -> str:
    if kind == 'primary_alloc':
        body = '''
    uint64_t mkw_size = c->x[0];
    uint64_t mkw_owner = c->x[1];
    uint64_t mkw_align = c->x[2];
    ORIGINAL(c);
    mkw_heap_owner_record(c->x[0], mkw_owner, mkw_size, mkw_align);'''
    elif kind == 'dealloc':
        body = '''
    uint64_t mkw_pointer = c->x[1];
    mkw_heap_owner_discard(mkw_pointer);
    ORIGINAL(c);'''
    else:
        if kind == 'region_vfunc':
            requested, owner, size = 1, 0, 'mkw_requested'
        elif kind == 'region_direct':
            requested, owner, size = 0, 1, 'mkw_requested'
        elif kind == 'region_string':
            requested, owner, size = 0, 1, '(mkw_requested <= UINT64_MAX - 16u ? mkw_requested + 16u : mkw_requested)'
        else:
            raise ValueError('unknown generated overlay kind')
        body = f'''
    uint64_t mkw_requested = c->x[{requested}];
    uint64_t mkw_owner = c->x[{owner}];
    int32_t mkw_signed_align = (int32_t)c->x[2];
    uint64_t mkw_align = mkw_signed_align < 0
        ? (uint64_t)(-(int64_t)mkw_signed_align)
        : (uint64_t)mkw_signed_align;
    ORIGINAL(c);
    mkw_heap_owner_record(c->x[0], mkw_owner, {size}, mkw_align);'''
    body = body.replace('ORIGINAL', original)
    return f'''\n/* {MARKER}: observe the unmodified lifted allocator. */
void f_{address:x}(Cpu *c) {{{body}
}}
'''


def patch_chunk(source: str, entries: list[tuple[int, str]]) -> str:
    if MARKER in source:
        raise ValueError('partially or previously overlaid generated source')
    declarations = ('#include "cpu.h"\n'
                    'extern void mkw_heap_owner_record(uint64_t, uint64_t, uint64_t, uint64_t);\n'
                    'extern void mkw_heap_owner_discard(uint64_t);')
    if source.count('#include "cpu.h"') != 1:
        raise ValueError('unexpected generated source header')
    source = source.replace('#include "cpu.h"', declarations, 1)
    for address, kind in entries:
        pattern = definition(address)
        matches = list(pattern.finditer(source))
        if len(matches) != 1:
            raise ValueError(f'lifted function {address:#x} is missing or ambiguous')
        match = matches[0]
        original = f'mkw_original_{kind}_{address:x}'
        renamed = match.group(0).replace('void', 'static void', 1).replace(f'f_{address:x}', original, 1)
        source = source[:match.start()] + renamed + source[match.end():]
        source += wrapper(address, kind, original)
    return source


def apply(repo: Path, exefs: Path) -> dict:
    verify_exefs(exefs)
    state = repo / 'build' / 'mkw-local' / 'generated-overlays.json'
    if state.is_file():
        record = json.loads(state.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
        for name, expected in record.get('files', {}).items():
            path = repo / name
            if not path.is_file() or digest(path) != expected:
                raise ValueError(f'generated overlay changed after installation: {name}')
        return record
    located = locate(repo)
    outputs = {path: patch_chunk(path.read_text(encoding='utf-8'), entries)
               for path, entries in located.items()}
    for path, output in outputs.items():
        path.write_text(output, encoding='utf-8', newline='\n')
    record = {
        'marker': MARKER,
        'files': {path.relative_to(repo).as_posix(): digest(path) for path in outputs},
        'functions': [f'{address:#x}' for address in FUNCTIONS],
    }
    state.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    state.write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2) + '\n', encoding='utf-8')
    return record


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    parser.add_argument('--repo', type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--exefs', type=Path, required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    try:
        record = apply(args.repo.resolve(), args.exefs.resolve())
        print(f'{MARKER}: {len(record["functions"])} functions in {len(record["files"])} chunks')
    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError, UnicodeError) as error:
        parser.exit(2, f'ERROR: {error}\n')
    return 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    raise SystemExit(main())

```

`tools/mkw_pack_romfs.py`:

```py
"""Pack an extracted RomFS directory into the flat image and index.json the runtime reads (runtime/romfs.c).

Dumps of Switch 2 games often come as a folder of loose files. The runtime only needs one image file and the offset
and size of each file in it (tools/romfs_index.py), so the files are concatenated in path order, each aligned to 16
bytes. Dot files the dump tool leaves (".listing") are skipped. The output is game data: it goes under build/.

    .venv\\Scripts\\python tools\\mkw_pack_romfs.py --dir <dump>\\romfs --out build\\extracted\\mkw180\\romfs

Standard library only.
"""
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

ALIGN = 16
CHUNK = 8 << 20


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument('--dir', type=Path, required=True, help='extracted RomFS root')
    ap.add_argument('--out', type=Path, required=True, help='folder for romfs.bin and index.json')
    args = ap.parse_args()
    root = args.dir.resolve()
    files = []
    for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(root):
        dirnames.sort()
        for name in filenames:
            if not name.startswith('.'):
                p = Path(dirpath) / name
                files.append((p.relative_to(root).as_posix(), p))
    files.sort(key=lambda e: e[0].encode())
    args.out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    image = args.out / 'romfs.bin'
    sha = hashlib.sha256()
    entries, off, t0 = [], 0, time.time()
    with open(image, 'wb') as dst:
        for i, (rel, p) in enumerate(files):
            pad = -off % ALIGN
            if pad:
                dst.write(b'\0' * pad)
                sha.update(b'\0' * pad)
                off += pad
            size = 0
            with open(p, 'rb') as src:
                while chunk := src.read(CHUNK):
                    dst.write(chunk)
                    sha.update(chunk)
                    size += len(chunk)
            entries.append({'path': rel, 'offset': off, 'size': size})
            off += size
    total_bytes = off
    index = {
        'format_version': 1,
        'image_sha256': sha.hexdigest(),
        'image_size': total_bytes,
        'files': entries,
    }
    index_path = args.out / 'index.json'
    index_path.write_text(json.dumps(index, indent=2) + '\n', encoding='utf-8')
    dt = time.time() - t0
    rate = (total_bytes / (1 << 20)) / dt if dt > 0 else 0
    print(f'mkw_pack_romfs: {len(entries)} files, {total_bytes / (1 << 20):.1f} MiB in {dt:.1f}s ({rate:.1f} MiB/s) -> {args.out}')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

```

`tools/mkw_probe.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Mario Kart World recompilation input audit (no game assets or keys included).

Read-only input validation for a decrypted ExeFS/RomFS dump. Generates an
informational JSON report. It does NOT recompile, extract, decrypt, or certify
that a dump is version 1.0.0. Standard library only.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

EXPECTED_TITLE = 0x0400C3F00006E000
EXPECTED_NAME = 'Mario Kart World'
MODULE = re.compile(r'^(?:main|sdk|rtld|subsdk[0-9]+)$')


def byte_size(size: int) -> str:
    for unit in ('B', 'KiB', 'MiB', 'GiB', 'TiB'):
        if size < 1024 or unit == 'TiB':
            return f'{size:.1f} {unit}'
        size /= 1024
    return '?'


def digest(path: Path, bufsize: int = 8 * 1024 * 1024) -> str:
    sha = hashlib.sha256()
    with path.open('rb') as f:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(bufsize), b''):
            sha.update(chunk)
    return sha.hexdigest()


def npdm(path: Path) -> dict:
    with path.open('rb') as f:
        # ACID may be larger, but the ACI0 header only needs 0x40 bytes.
        header = f.read(0x80)
        file_size = path.stat().st_size
        if len(header) < 0x80 or header[:4] != b'META':
            raise ValueError('main.npdm does not begin with a valid META header')
        aci_off, aci_size = struct.unpack_from('<II', header, 0x70)
        if aci_off < 0x80 or aci_size < 0x40 or aci_off + aci_size > file_size:
            raise ValueError('invalid ACI0 offset/size in main.npdm')
        f.seek(aci_off)
        aci = f.read(0x40)
        if aci[:4] != b'ACI0':
            raise ValueError('main.npdm points to a missing ACI0 block')
        title_id = struct.unpack_from('<Q', aci, 0x10)[0]
        name = header[0x20:0x30].split(b'\x00', 1)[0].decode('ascii', 'replace')
        return {
            'magic': 'META', 'aci0_magic': 'ACI0',
            'title_id': f'{title_id:016X}',
            'is_mario_kart_world': title_id == EXPECTED_TITLE,
            'process_name': name, 'npdm_meta_version': struct.unpack_from('<I', header, 0x18)[0],
            'main_thread_core': header[0x0F],
        }


def locate(dump: Path) -> tuple[Path, Path | None]:
    if dump.is_file():
        if dump.suffix.lower() == '.nup':
            raise ValueError('NUP container supplied. Extract your own game into exefs/ and romfs/ first; this tool is an audit, not a NUP decryptor.')
        raise ValueError('Expected a directory containing exefs/ and romfs/, not a file')
    # Prioritize a complete standalone update over a stale/empty base folder.
    # Some NUP extractors create empty base/exefs when only update content exists.
    candidates = [
        dump / 'updates' / '917504',
        dump / '917504',
        dump,
        dump / 'base',
    ]
    if dump.name.lower() == 'exefs':
        candidates.insert(0, dump.parent)
    for root in candidates:
        exefs = root / 'exefs'
        if (exefs / 'main.npdm').is_file() and (exefs / 'main').is_file():
            romfs = root / 'romfs'
            return exefs, romfs if romfs.is_dir() else None
    raise ValueError('Could not locate exefs/; try --dump H:\\Switch2\\MarioKartWorld\\updates\\917504')


def inspect_exefs(exefs: Path, hash_files: bool) -> tuple[list[dict], list[str]]:
    errors = []
    result = []
    for filename in ('main.npdm', 'main', 'sdk'):
        if not (exefs / filename).is_file():
            errors.append(f'Missing required ExeFS file: {filename}')
    for p in sorted(exefs.iterdir(), key=lambda p: p.name):
        if not p.is_file() or (p.name != 'main.npdm' and not MODULE.fullmatch(p.name)):
            continue
        st = p.stat()
        info = {'name': p.name, 'bytes': st.st_size}
        if p.name != 'main.npdm':
            with p.open('rb') as f:
                magic = f.read(4)
            # This is a warning only: Switch2 variants have evolved.
            info['magic_hex'] = magic.hex()
            info['nso0_magic'] = magic == b'NSO0'
            if not info['nso0_magic']:
                errors.append(f'{p.name} does not start with NSO0; may be unsupported or damaged')
        if hash_files:
            info['sha256'] = digest(p)
        result.append(info)
    return result, errors


def scan_romfs(romfs: Path | None, enumerate_files: bool) -> dict:
    if romfs is None:
        return {'present': False, 'scanned': False}
    result = {'present': True, 'path': str(romfs), 'scanned': enumerate_files}
    if enumerate_files:
        count = total = 0
        for parent, dirs, names in os.walk(romfs):
            dirs.sort()
            for name in names:
                if name.startswith('.'):
                    continue
                p = Path(parent, name)
                if p.is_file():
                    count += 1
                    total += p.stat().st_size
        result.update({'file_count': count, 'total_file_bytes': total})
    return result


def run_probe(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    dump = args.dump.expanduser().resolve()
    try:
        exefs, romfs = locate(dump)
    except ValueError as e:
        print(f'ERROR: {e}', file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    errors: list[str] = []
    npdm_record: dict | None = None
    try:
        npdm_record = npdm(exefs / 'main.npdm')
        if not npdm_record['is_mario_kart_world']:
            errors.append(f"Wrong title ID: {npdm_record['title_id']} (need {EXPECTED_TITLE:016X})")
    except (ValueError, OSError) as e:
        errors.append(str(e))
    modules, module_errors = inspect_exefs(exefs, args.sha256)
    errors.extend(module_errors)
    asset_info = scan_romfs(romfs, args.scan_romfs)
    if not asset_info['present']:
        errors.append('Missing RomFS folder')
    report = {
        'tool': 'mkw_probe', 'schema_version': 1,
        'game': EXPECTED_NAME, 'target_program_id': f'{EXPECTED_TITLE:016X}',
        'target_version_claimed': '1.8.0',
        'version_verified': False,
        'version_note': 'The NPDM title ID does not prove the update version or completeness. Current 1.8.0 module IDs are not independently pinned in this kit.',
        'exefs': str(exefs), 'npdm': npdm_record, 'modules': modules,
        'romfs': asset_info, 'errors': errors, 'input_layout_valid': len(errors) == 0,
        'seconds': round(time.monotonic() - t0, 3),
        'next_step': 'Establish version-specific module hashes and a game-specific code generation profile. This probe does not produce a playable EXE.'
    }
    args.report.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    args.report.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding='utf-8')
    print(f'Game:       {EXPECTED_NAME}')
    print(f'ExeFS:      {exefs}')
    print(f'RomFS:      {romfs or "MISSING"}')
    print(f'Program ID: {npdm_record["title_id"] if npdm_record else "unavailable"}')
    print('Modules:    ' + ', '.join(x['name'] for x in modules))
    for m in modules:
        print(f"  {m['name']:12s} {byte_size(m['bytes']):>12s}" + (f" sha256={m['sha256']}" if 'sha256' in m else ''))
    if asset_info.get('scanned'):
        print(f"RomFS:      {asset_info['file_count']:,} files, {byte_size(asset_info['total_file_bytes'])}")
    print('Version:    not verified (hash baseline needed)')
    print(f'Report:     {args.report}')
    if errors:
        print('INPUT PROBLEMS:', file=sys.stderr)
        for error in errors:
            print(f'  - {error}', file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    print('PASS: game identity and extracted directory layout. This is NOT a recompilation or full data integrity test.')
    return 0


def run_tools(_: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    candidates = [
        ('Python', [sys.executable, '--version']),
        ('Git', ['git', '--version']),
        ('.NET 10+', ['dotnet', '--list-sdks']),
        ('MSYS2 Clang', [r'C:\msys64\ucrt64\bin\clang.exe', '--version']),
        ('MSYS2 Ninja', [r'C:\msys64\ucrt64\bin\ninja.exe', '--version']),
    ]
    missing = False
    for label, cmd in candidates:
        found = bool(shutil.which(cmd[0]) or Path(cmd[0]).is_file())
        if not found:
            print(f'[MISSING] {label}: {cmd[0]}')
            missing = True
            continue
        try:
            res = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10)
            lines = (res.stdout + res.stderr).splitlines()
            msg = lines[0] if lines else '(no output)'
            if label == '.NET 10+':
                found = any(x.strip().startswith('10.') for x in lines)
            print(f'[{"PASS" if found else "MISSING"}] {label}: {msg}')
            if not found:
                missing = True
        except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired) as e:
            print(f'[ERROR] {label}: {e}')
            missing = True
    return 2 if missing else 0


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest='command', required=True)
    p = sub.add_parser('probe', help='Read-only Mario Kart World ExeFS/RomFS validation')
    p.add_argument('--dump', required=True, type=Path, help='Game root, updates/917504/, or exefs/ directory')
    p.add_argument('--report', type=Path, default=Path('mkw-input-report.json'))
    p.add_argument('--sha256', action='store_true', help='Compute full hashes for each ExeFS module; slower')
    p.add_argument('--scan-romfs', action='store_true', help='Count RomFS files and their sizes; slower on HDD')
    p.set_defaults(fn=run_probe)
    t = sub.add_parser('tools', help='Check prerequisites without installing/changing anything')
    t.set_defaults(fn=run_tools)
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    return args.fn(args)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    raise SystemExit(main())
```

`tools/mkw_select_romfs.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Select an existing user-created packed RomFS without copying or hashing it."""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    parser.add_argument('--repo', type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--packed', type=Path, required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    repo = args.repo.resolve()
    packed = args.packed.resolve()
    image = packed / 'romfs.bin'
    index = packed / 'index.json'
    if not image.is_file() or not index.is_file():
        parser.error(f'{packed} must contain romfs.bin and index.json')
    manifest = json.loads(index.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
    if manifest.get('status') != 'pass' or manifest.get('romfs_size') != image.stat().st_size:
        parser.error('packed RomFS index is incomplete or does not match the image size')
    output = repo / 'build' / 'mkw-local' / 'selected-romfs.json'
    output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    output.write_text(json.dumps({'path': str(packed), 'backend': 'packed'}, indent=2) + '\n', encoding='utf-8')
    print(f'Selected existing packed RomFS: {packed}')
    return 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    raise SystemExit(main())
```

```txt
// ---- the window (Switch 2 system settings look, ui/theme.h): a title bar, the category list on the left (L / R or
// Q / E step it, a click picks one), the page with its help box on the right, and a footer with the controller hints and
// "Continue" / "Quit game". B on the gamepad and Esc close it.

// A round button glyph with its letter (the footer hints).
static void hint_glyph(ImDrawList *dl, ImVec2 c, float rad, const char *letter) {
    using namespace mkw_theme;
    dl->AddCircleFilled(c, rad, kText);
    ImFont *font = ImGui::GetFont();
    float fs = rad * 1.25f;
    ImVec2 ts = font->CalcTextSizeA(fs, FLT_MAX, 0, letter);
    dl->AddText(font, fs, ImVec2(c.x - ts.x * 0.5f, c.y - ts.y * 0.5f), kHeader, letter);
}

// A pill glyph (L, R) for the category switch.
static float hint_pill(ImDrawList *dl, ImVec2 p, float h, const char *letter) {
    using namespace mkw_theme;
    ImFont *font = ImGui::GetFont();
    float fs = h * 0.62f;
    ImVec2 ts = font->CalcTextSizeA(fs, FLT_MAX, 0, letter);
    float w = ts.x + h * 0.9f;
    dl->AddRectFilled(p, ImVec2(p.x + w, p.y + h), kText, h * 0.5f);
    dl->AddText(font, fs, ImVec2(p.x + (w - ts.x) * 0.5f, p.y + (h - ts.y) * 0.5f), kHeader, letter);
    return w;
}

static void layout_menu(uint32_t w, uint32_t h, float scale) {
    using namespace mkw_theme;
    ImGui::GetBackgroundDrawList()->AddRectFilled(ImVec2(0, 0), ImVec2((float)w, (float)h), kBackdrop);
    float ww = fminf(w * 0.86f, 1500 * scale), wh = fminf(h * 0.88f, 880 * scale);
    ImGui::SetNextWindowPos(ImVec2(w * 0.5f, h * 0.5f), ImGuiCond_Always, ImVec2(0.5f, 0.5f));
    ImGui::SetNextWindowSize(ImVec2(ww, wh), ImGuiCond_Always);
    ImGui::PushStyleVar(ImGuiStyleVar_WindowPadding, ImVec2(0, 0));
    ImGui::Begin("##menu", nullptr, ImGuiWindowFlags_NoDecoration | ImGuiWindowFlags_NoMove |
                                        ImGuiWindowFlags_NoSavedSettings | ImGuiWindowFlags_NoScrollWithMouse);
    ImGui::PopStyleVar();
    ImDrawList *dl = ImGui::GetWindowDrawList();
    ImFont *font = ImGui::GetFont();
    const ImGuiStyle &st = ImGui::GetStyle();
    ImVec2 o = ImGui::GetWindowPos();
    float W = ImGui::GetWindowWidth(), H = ImGui::GetWindowHeight(), fs = ImGui::GetFontSize();
    float pad = 30 * scale, rounding = st.WindowRounding;
    float head_h = floorf(fs * 3.1f), foot_h = floorf(fs * 3.3f), side_w = floorf(fminf(W * 0.26f, 380 * scale));
    float body_y = o.y + head_h, body_h = H - head_h - foot_h;

    // title bar: an accent bar, "Mario Kart World", the page title, and the version on the right
    dl->AddRectFilled(o, ImVec2(o.x + W, o.y + head_h), kHeader, rounding, ImDrawFlags_RoundCornersTop);
    dl->AddLine(ImVec2(o.x, o.y + head_h - 0.5f), ImVec2(o.x + W, o.y + head_h - 0.5f), kDivider, 1.0f);
    float tfs = fs * 1.3f, ty = o.y + (head_h - tfs) * 0.5f;
    dl->AddRectFilled(ImVec2(o.x + pad, o.y + head_h * 0.27f), ImVec2(o.x + pad + 6 * scale, o.y + head_h * 0.73f),
                      kAccent, 3 * scale);
    float tx = o.x + pad + 20 * scale;
    const char *brand = "Mario Kart World";
    dl->AddText(font, tfs, ImVec2(tx, ty), kText, brand);
    tx += font->CalcTextSizeA(tfs, FLT_MAX, 0, brand).x + 14 * scale;
    dl->AddText(font, fs, ImVec2(tx, o.y + (head_h - fs) * 0.5f + fs * 0.08f), kTextSoft, menu_text(UI_MENU_TITLE));
    char version[96];
    const char *game = "1.8.0";   // this project builds the 1.8.0 update (tools/mkw_cli.py prepare --i-confirm-update-180)
    char gbuf[16];
    if (rt_game_version) {
        snprintf(gbuf, sizeof gbuf, "%d.%d.%d", rt_game_version / 100, rt_game_version / 10 % 10, rt_game_version % 10);
        game = gbuf;
    }
    snprintf(version, sizeof version, menu_text(UI_MENU_VERSION), rt_port_version, game);
    float vw = font->CalcTextSizeA(fs * 0.85f, FLT_MAX, 0, version).x;
    dl->AddText(font, fs * 0.85f, ImVec2(o.x + W - pad - vw, o.y + (head_h - fs * 0.85f) * 0.5f), kTextDim, version);

    // category list
    dl->AddRectFilled(ImVec2(o.x, body_y), ImVec2(o.x + side_w, body_y + body_h), kSidebar);
    dl->AddLine(ImVec2(o.x + side_w - 0.5f, body_y), ImVec2(o.x + side_w - 0.5f, body_y + body_h), kDivider, 1.0f);
    int step = g_modal || binds_modal()                                                                  ? 0
             : ImGui::IsKeyPressed(ImGuiKey_GamepadR1, false) || ImGui::IsKeyPressed(ImGuiKey_E, false) ? 1
             : ImGui::IsKeyPressed(ImGuiKey_GamepadL1, false) || ImGui::IsKeyPressed(ImGuiKey_Q, false) ? -1
                                                                                                         : 0;
    if (step) g_tab_request = (g_tab + step + TAB_COUNT) % TAB_COUNT;
    float ih = floorf(fs * 2.4f), ix = o.x + 14 * scale, iw = side_w - 28 * scale, iy = body_y + 18 * scale;
    for (int k = 0; k < TAB_COUNT; k++) {
        ImVec2 a(ix, iy + k * (ih + 6 * scale)), b(ix + iw, a.y + ih);
        ImGui::SetCursorScreenPos(a);
        ImGui::PushID(k);
        // not in the D-pad navigation (L / R switch pages); the mouse picks one
        if (ImGui::InvisibleButton("##cat", ImVec2(iw, ih)) && !g_modal && !binds_modal()) g_tab_request = k;
        bool hov = ImGui::IsItemHovered();
        ImGui::PopID();
        bool sel = k == (g_tab_request >= 0 ? g_tab_request : g_tab);
        if (sel) {
            dl->AddRectFilled(a, b, kRowSel, 8 * scale);
            dl->AddRectFilled(ImVec2(a.x + 8 * scale, a.y + ih * 0.22f), ImVec2(a.x + 13 * scale, b.y - ih * 0.22f),
                              kAccent, 3 * scale);
        } else if (hov) {
            dl->AddRectFilled(a, b, kRowHover, 8 * scale);
        }
        dl->AddText(ImVec2(a.x + 26 * scale, a.y + (ih - fs) * 0.5f), sel ? kAccentText : kText, menu_text(kTabNames[k]));
    }
    // L / R under the list: the controller's page switch
    {
        float ph = fs * 1.1f, py = body_y + body_h - ph - 20 * scale, px = ix + 12 * scale;
        px += hint_pill(dl, ImVec2(px, py), ph, "L") + 8 * scale;
        hint_pill(dl, ImVec2(px, py), ph, "R");
    }
    if (g_tab_request >= 0) {
        g_tab = g_tab_request;
        g_focus_page = g_tab_request;   // the new page's first row takes the cursor
        g_tab_request = -1;
    }

    // the page: a direct NavFlattened child of this window (option_rows.cpp), so the D-pad moves between its rows and
    // the footer buttons without a second child level in between
    ImGui::SetCursorScreenPos(ImVec2(o.x + side_w + pad, body_y + pad * 0.7f));
    if (g_focus_page == g_tab) {
        opt_focus_first();
        g_focus_page = -1;
    }
    opt_reserve_bottom(foot_h + pad * 0.5f);
    opt_reserve_right(pad);
    switch (g_tab) {
    case TAB_DISPLAY: tab_display(scale); break;
    case TAB_SOUND: tab_sound(scale); break;
    case TAB_CONTROLS: tab_controls(scale); break;
    case TAB_SYSTEM: tab_system(scale); break;
    case TAB_ADVANCED: tab_advanced(scale); break;
    }

    // footer: the hints (or the save failure) on the left, "Continue" and "Quit game" on the right
    float fy = o.y + H - foot_h;
    dl->AddRectFilled(ImVec2(o.x, fy), ImVec2(o.x + W, o.y + H), kHeader, rounding, ImDrawFlags_RoundCornersBottom);
    dl->AddLine(ImVec2(o.x, fy + 0.5f), ImVec2(o.x + W, fy + 0.5f), kDivider, 1.0f);

            {"A", UI_MENU_HINT_OK}, {"B", UI_MENU_HINT_BACK}};
        for (const auto &e : hints) {
            hint_glyph(dl, ImVec2(hx + rad, cy), rad, e.glyph);
            hx += rad * 2 + 8 * scale;

    if (!was_modal && (ImGui::IsKeyPressed(ImGuiKey_Escape, false) || ImGui::IsKeyPressed(ImGuiKey_GamepadFaceRight, false)))
        set_open(0);
    ImGui::End();
}
```
