`tools/shader_list.py`:

```py
"""The MacNativeGames shared shader list (refs/MacNativeGames games/totk/assets/shader_list.tsv, MIT; docs/shader-list.md
there) as our tools read it: every row of one revision, plus the V rows of every older revision that it dropped.

MacNativeGames prunes V rows its own runtime no longer needs: default variants, which its seed translates for every
shader (1.4.3 on 2026-10-22, 1.0.0 to 1.2.1 on 2026-10-25), and variants that differ only in vertex input or colour
output types (2026-10-26). Our answers (runtime/gfx_shader.c) still tell those apart, so a dropped row names a variant
our play meets: at 1340bee the list alone has 134 rows of 1.4.3 shaders, its history 24,839, and of 1.2.1 6,771 and
25,238. A row no draw asks for costs one translation. No copy of the list goes into the repository.
"""
import subprocess
import sys

PATH = 'games/totk/assets/shader_list.tsv'


def git(repo, *args):
    return subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(repo), *args], check=True, capture_output=True, encoding='utf-8').stdout


def history(repo, rev='origin/HEAD'):
    """rev's list, then each V row of an older revision that no newer one has, newest first."""
    if git(repo, 'rev-parse', '--is-shallow-repository').strip() == 'true':
        # a shallow clone has rev's list only: preparing from it skips most variants and shows only as stutter in play
        sys.exit(f'{repo} is a shallow clone without the shader list\'s history; run tools/fetch_refs.sh')
    lines = git(repo, 'show', f'{rev}:{PATH}').splitlines()
    seen = set(lines)
    for h in git(repo, 'log', '--format=%H', rev, '--', PATH).split()[1:]:
        for line in git(repo, 'show', f'{h}:{PATH}').splitlines():
            if line.startswith('V\t') and line not in seen:
                seen.add(line)
                lines.append(line)
    return '\n'.join(lines) + '\n'
```

`tools/spin_waits.py`:

```py
# Adapted from nxnative dm/tools/patch_nso.py @ 6d34984 (MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 seedds): the spin wait search
# ("Spin waits": spin_rw, spin_kind, spin_rmw, spin_lock, spin_store, spin_quick, spin_region, spin_region1).
"""Find the spin waits of the ExeFS modules and print them as `spin` lines of a patch table (recomp/patches.py).

Usage: spin_waits.py --exefs build/extracted/v143/exefs --patches recomp/patches-v143.txt [--modules main,subsdk0,sdk]

A guest loop that polls memory until another thread changes it fills only its own core on the Switch, where a better
thread pinned there preempts it. Here it holds one of the three virtual cores (runtime/kernel.c) and a host core, and
when the poll takes and releases a lock on every pass, two pollers hand the lock's cache line between their cores so
that the thread whose item it is rarely wins its exclusive store (nxnative 6d34984: Breath of the Wild's job queue,
main+0xef62dc, CPU frames of 30-210 ms every 1-10 s). The generator sends the back-edges of such loops through
rt_spin_gate (runtime/kernel.c kern_spin_gate), which slows the poll down and hands the virtual core to a waiting
thread once the loop has polled for a while.

A loop counts only when it provably cannot leave by itself. From its head T every path back to T (the region R,
within SPIN_WIN bytes after T) runs loads, register and flag arithmetic, direct branches and barriers; no call, SVC,
system register or event wait; nothing live at T is written in R. Allowed besides: an exclusive add of a constant
that every path back to T undoes on the same address, a spin lock taken and released on the same address on every
path, a test loop on a word inside R, and at most SPIN_STORES stores of registers R never writes (fixed values to
fixed addresses, so the passes repeat after a few). Sites of the patch table are kept out of regions.

Runs on the development machine (capstone); the table it prints is checked in, so the installer's generator needs
no disassembler.
"""
import argparse
import re
import struct
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from capstone import CS_ARCH_ARM64, CS_MODE_ARM, Cs
from capstone.arm64 import ARM64_OP_IMM, ARM64_OP_MEM, ARM64_OP_REG

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / 'recomp'))

import patches  # noqa: E402
from layout import layout  # noqa: E402
from nso import Nso  # noqa: E402

SPIN_WIN = 512   # bytes from a backward branch back to its target
SPIN_TOPS = {0x16, 0x17, 0x54, 0x34, 0x35, 0xB4, 0xB5, 0x36, 0x37, 0xB6, 0xB7}   # b, b.cond, cbz/cbnz, tbz/tbnz
SPIN_PATHS, SPIN_STEPS, SPIN_STORES = 256, 4096, 4   # complete paths back to T; search steps; stores in a region
SPIN_LSE = ('ldadd', 'ldclr', 'ldeor', 'ldset', 'ldsmax', 'ldsmin', 'ldumax', 'ldumin')
SPIN_BAD = {'bl', 'blr', 'br', 'ret', 'eret', 'svc', 'hvc', 'smc', 'brk', 'hlt', 'udf', 'mrs', 'msr', 'sys', 'sysl',
            'wfe', 'wfi', 'sev', 'sevl', 'clrex', 'dc', 'ic', 'at', 'tlbi', 'drps', 'dcps1', 'dcps2', 'dcps3', 'blraa',
            'blrab', 'blraaz', 'blrabz', 'braa', 'brab', 'braaz', 'brabz', 'retaa', 'retab', 'eretaa', 'eretab'}
# Words that end every path through them by their encoding alone: bl; br / blr / ret; svc / brk; stores (immediate,
# unscaled, pre / post-index, register offset, vector); stp / stnp; LSE atomics. Exclusive stores and pre / post-index
# loads are left to the full check.
SPIN_STOP = ((0xFC000000, 0x94000000), (0xFE000000, 0xD6000000), (0xFF000000, 0xD4000000), (0x3FC00000, 0x39000000),
             (0x3FC00000, 0x3D000000), (0x3FC00000, 0x3D800000), (0x3FE00000, 0x38000000), (0x3FE00C00, 0x38200800),
             (0x3FE00000, 0x3C000000), (0x3FE00000, 0x3C800000), (0x3A400000, 0x28000000), (0x3F200C00, 0x38200000))


class SpinNo(Exception):
    pass


def norm(n):
    """w / x views as x<n>, vector views as v<n>, zero registers as None."""
    n = {'fp': 'x29', 'lr': 'x30', 'wsp': 'sp'}.get(n, n)
    if n in ('wzr', 'xzr'):
        return None
    m = re.fullmatch(r'[wx](\d+)', n)
    if m:
        return 'x' + m.group(1)
    m = re.fullmatch(r'[bhsdqv](\d+)', n)
    return 'v' + m.group(1) if m else n


class Search:
    """The spin waits of one module image. touched: image offsets no region may contain (patch sites)."""

    def __init__(self, img, text_end, touched):
        self.img, self.text_end, self.touched = img, text_end, touched
        self.md = Cs(CS_ARCH_ARM64, CS_MODE_ARM)
        self.md.detail = True
        self.dec = {}

    def ins(self, a):
        if a not in self.dec:
            self.dec[a] = next(self.md.disasm(bytes(self.img[a:a + 4]), a), None) if 0 <= a < self.text_end else None
        return self.dec[a]

    def word(self, a):
        return struct.unpack_from('<I', self.img, a)[0]

    def candidates(self):
        """{loop head: [backward branches to it]}, branches at most SPIN_WIN bytes back."""
        cand = {}
        for o in range(0, self.text_end, 4):
            w = self.word(o)
            t = w >> 24
            if t not in SPIN_TOPS:
                continue
            if t in (0x16, 0x17):
                d = ((w & 0x3FFFFFF) - (1 << 26)) * 4
            elif t & 0x7E == 0x36:
                d = (((w >> 5) & 0x3FFF) - (1 << 14)) * 4 if w & 0x40000 else 4
            elif t == 0x54:
                d = (((w >> 5) & 0x7FFFF) - (1 << 19)) * 4 if w & 0x800000 and not w & 0x10 else 4
            else:
                d = (((w >> 5) & 0x7FFFF) - (1 << 19)) * 4 if w & 0x800000 else 4
            if -SPIN_WIN <= d <= 0:
                cand.setdefault(o + d, []).append(o)
        return cand

    @staticmethod
    def rw(ins):
        """(registers read, registers written). Capstone lists a compare's first operand as written and the flags as
        read by cbz / tbz, and leaves out the destination of adds, so every register operand counts as well: operand 0
        written and the others read, or for a load all of them written."""
        m = ins.mnemonic
        regs = [norm(ins.reg_name(o.reg)) for o in ins.operands if o.type == ARM64_OP_REG]
        ops = set(regs) - {None}
        if m in ('cbz', 'cbnz', 'tbz', 'tbnz'):
            return ops, set()
        if m.startswith('b.'):
            return {'nzcv'}, set()
        if m == 'b':
            return set(), set()
        if m in ('cmp', 'cmn', 'tst', 'fcmp', 'fcmpe'):
            return ops, {'nzcv'}
        if m in ('ccmp', 'ccmn', 'fccmp', 'fccmpe'):
            return ops | {'nzcv'}, {'nzcv'}
        r, w = ins.regs_access()
        r = {norm(ins.reg_name(x)) for x in r} - {None}
        w = {norm(ins.reg_name(x)) for x in w} - {None}
        if m.startswith(('ld', 'prfm', 'prfum')):
            return r, w | ops
        return r | (set(regs[1:]) - {None}), w | (set(regs[:1]) - {None})

    @staticmethod
    def kind(ins):
        """'br' direct branch, 'pc' adr / adrp, 'ok' a load or register / flag arithmetic, None anything else."""
        if ins is None:
            return None
        m = ins.mnemonic
        if m in ('b', 'cbz', 'cbnz', 'tbz', 'tbnz') or m.startswith('b.'):
            return 'br'
        if m in ('adr', 'adrp'):
            return 'pc'
        if m in SPIN_BAD or m.startswith(('st', 'cas', 'swp') + SPIN_LSE):
            return None
        mem = any(o.type == ARM64_OP_MEM for o in ins.operands)
        if m.startswith(('ld', 'prfm', 'prfum')):
            return 'ok' if mem else None   # no memory operand: a pc-relative literal load
        return None if mem else 'ok'

    def rmw(self, a):
        """ld(a)xr wA,[xN]; add|sub wB,wA,#k; st(l)xr wS,wB,[xN]; cbnz wS,<the load> at a -> (xN, +-k, registers
        written, the four instructions), or None."""
        l = [self.ins(a + 4 * i) for i in range(4)]
        if (None in l or l[0].mnemonic not in ('ldxr', 'ldaxr') or l[1].mnemonic not in ('add', 'sub')
                or l[2].mnemonic not in ('stxr', 'stlxr') or l[3].mnemonic != 'cbnz'):
            return None
        r = lambda x, i: x.reg_name(x.operands[i].reg)
        if len(l[1].operands) != 3 or l[1].operands[2].type != ARM64_OP_IMM or 'lsl' in l[1].op_str:
            return None
        base = l[0].operands[1].mem
        if base.disp or base.index or l[2].operands[2].mem.base != base.base or l[2].operands[2].mem.disp:
            return None
        if r(l[1], 1) != r(l[0], 0) or r(l[2], 1) != r(l[1], 0) or r(l[3], 0) != r(l[2], 0) or l[3].operands[1].imm != a:
            return None
        k = l[1].operands[2].imm * (1 if l[1].mnemonic == 'add' else -1)
        return norm(l[0].reg_name(base.base)), k, {norm(r(l[0], 0)), norm(r(l[1], 0)), norm(r(l[2], 0))} - {None}, l

    def lock(self, a):
        """An exclusive spin lock sequence or a test loop entered at a -> (kind, xN, its instructions, how many come
        before a, how many from a on, registers read, registers written):
          'acq'  ld(a)xr wA,[xN]; cbz wA,+16; clrex; b <the load>; st(l)xr wS,wK,[xN]; cbnz wS,<the load>
          'rel'  clrex; ld(a)xr wA,[xN]; cmp wA,#k; b.ne <the clrex>; st(l)xr wS,wzr,[xN]; cbnz wS,<the load>
                 (entered at the load), or stlr wzr,[xN]
          'tst'  ldr|ldrb|ldrh wA,[xN{,#imm}]; cmp wA,#k; b.eq|b.ne <the load>"""
        l = [self.ins(a + 4 * i) for i in range(6)]
        if l[0] is None:
            return None
        r = lambda x, i: x.reg_name(x.operands[i].reg)
        plain = lambda x, i: x.operands[i].type == ARM64_OP_MEM and not x.operands[i].mem.index and not x.operands[i].mem.disp
        m0 = l[0].mnemonic
        if m0 in ('ldxr', 'ldaxr') and None not in l and r(l[0], 0).startswith('w') and plain(l[0], 1):
            base = l[0].operands[1].mem.base
            bn = norm(l[0].reg_name(base))
            if (l[1].mnemonic == 'cbz' and r(l[1], 0) == r(l[0], 0) and l[1].operands[1].imm == a + 16
                    and l[2].mnemonic == 'clrex' and l[3].mnemonic == 'b' and l[3].operands[0].imm == a
                    and l[4].mnemonic in ('stxr', 'stlxr') and plain(l[4], 2) and l[4].operands[2].mem.base == base
                    and r(l[4], 1) not in ('wzr', 'xzr')
                    and l[5].mnemonic == 'cbnz' and r(l[5], 0) == r(l[4], 0) and l[5].operands[1].imm == a):
                return 'acq', bn, l, 0, 6, {bn, norm(r(l[4], 1))}, {norm(r(l[0], 0)), norm(r(l[4], 0))}
            p = self.ins(a - 4)
            if (p is not None and p.mnemonic == 'clrex' and l[1].mnemonic == 'cmp' and r(l[1], 0) == r(l[0], 0)
                    and l[1].operands[1].type == ARM64_OP_IMM and l[2].mnemonic == 'b.ne'
                    and l[2].operands[0].imm == a - 4 and l[3].mnemonic in ('stxr', 'stlxr') and r(l[3], 1) == 'wzr'
                    and plain(l[3], 2) and l[3].operands[2].mem.base == base and l[4].mnemonic == 'cbnz'
                    and r(l[4], 0) == r(l[3], 0) and l[4].operands[1].imm == a):
                return 'rel', bn, [p] + l[:5], 1, 5, {bn}, {norm(r(l[0], 0)), norm(r(l[3], 0)), 'nzcv'}
        if m0 == 'stlr' and len(l[0].operands) == 2 and r(l[0], 0) in ('wzr', 'xzr') and plain(l[0], 1):
            return 'rel', norm(l[0].reg_name(l[0].operands[1].mem.base)), l[:1], 0, 1, {norm(l[0].reg_name(l[0].operands[1].mem.base))}, set()
        if (m0 in ('ldr', 'ldrb', 'ldrh') and None not in l[:3] and len(l[0].operands) == 2 and r(l[0], 0).startswith('w')
                and l[0].operands[1].type == ARM64_OP_MEM and not l[0].operands[1].mem.index and not l[0].writeback
                and l[1].mnemonic == 'cmp' and r(l[1], 0) == r(l[0], 0) and l[1].operands[1].type == ARM64_OP_IMM
                and l[2].mnemonic in ('b.eq', 'b.ne') and l[2].operands[0].imm == a):
            bn = norm(l[0].reg_name(l[0].operands[1].mem.base))
            return 'tst', bn, l[:3], 0, 3, {bn}, {norm(r(l[0], 0)), 'nzcv'}
        return None

    @staticmethod
    def store(ins):
        """str / strb / strh / stur / sturb / sturh of a w register or zr to [xN{,#imm}] (no writeback, no register
        offset) -> (value register or None for zr, base register), or None."""
        if (ins is None or ins.mnemonic not in ('str', 'strb', 'strh', 'stur', 'sturb', 'sturh') or ins.writeback
                or len(ins.operands) != 2):
            return None
        v, o = ins.operands
        if v.type != ARM64_OP_REG or o.type != ARM64_OP_MEM or o.mem.index:
            return None
        vn = ins.reg_name(v.reg)
        if not (vn.startswith('w') or vn == 'xzr'):
            return None
        return norm(vn), norm(ins.reg_name(o.mem.base))

    def quick(self, T, hi):
        """A back-edge to T can be reached from T without passing a word of SPIN_STOP (only such heads get the full
        check, which decodes)."""
        seen, todo = set(), [T]
        while todo:
            a = todo.pop()
            if a in seen or not T <= a <= hi:
                continue
            seen.add(a)
            w = self.word(a)
            t = w >> 24
            if 0x14 <= t <= 0x17:
                succ = (a + (((w & 0x3FFFFFF) ^ 0x2000000) - 0x2000000) * 4,)
            elif t == 0x54 or t & 0x7E == 0x34:
                succ = (a + ((((w >> 5) & 0x7FFFF) ^ 0x40000) - 0x40000) * 4, a + 4)
            elif t & 0x7E == 0x36:
                succ = (a + ((((w >> 5) & 0x3FFF) ^ 0x2000) - 0x2000) * 4, a + 4)
            elif any(w & m == v for m, v in SPIN_STOP) and not (
                    w & 0xBFC00000 in (0xB9000000, 0x39000000, 0x79000000)
                    or w & 0xBFE00C00 in (0xB8000000, 0x38000000, 0x78000000)):
                continue   # str / strb / strh (immediate, unscaled) may store the same on every pass
            else:
                succ = (a + 4,)
            if T in succ:
                return True
            todo.extend(succ)
        return False

    def region(self, T, bes):
        """The spin wait with head T (bes: the backward branches to T) -> dict, or None. A store whose value or
        address a pass changes is no part of a region: the paths through it are dropped and the region is found again
        without them. The region without stores is taken instead when the wider one does not cover its back-edges."""
        ban, g = set(), None
        for _ in range(8):
            g = self.region1(T, bes, ban, True)
            if not isinstance(g, set):
                break
            ban |= g
        old = self.region1(T, bes, set(), False)
        return g if isinstance(g, dict) and (not old or old['valid'] <= g['valid']) else old

    def region1(self, T, bes, ban, stores):
        hi = max(bes)
        if not self.quick(T, hi):
            return None
        nodes, back, bad, inner = {}, set(), set(), set()
        todo = [T]
        while todo:
            a = todo.pop()
            if a in nodes or a in bad:
                continue
            if a in ban:
                bad.add(a)
                continue
            rmw = self.rmw(a) if a + 12 <= hi and self.word(a) & 0x3FE00000 == 0x08400000 else None   # ldxr / ldaxr
            lk = None if rmw else self.lock(a)
            if lk and lk[0] == 'tst' and a == T:
                lk = None   # the region's own test loop
            if rmw:
                n = {'kind': 'rmw', 'base': rmw[0], 'k': rmw[1], 'ins': rmw[3], 'uses': {rmw[0]}, 'defs': rmw[2],
                     'succ': [a + 16]}
            elif lk:
                n = {'kind': lk[0], 'base': lk[1], 'k': {'acq': 1, 'rel': -1, 'tst': 0}[lk[0]], 'ins': lk[2],
                     'pre': lk[3], 'uses': lk[5], 'defs': lk[6], 'succ': [a + 4 * lk[4]]}
            elif stores and self.store(self.ins(a)):
                x = self.ins(a)
                st = self.store(x)
                n = {'kind': 'stc', 'st': st, 'ins': [x], 'uses': {st[1]} | ({st[0]} - {None}), 'defs': set(),
                     'succ': [a + 4]}
            else:
                x = self.ins(a)
                k = self.kind(x)
                if k is None:
                    bad.add(a)
                    continue
                if k == 'br':
                    t = x.operands[-1].imm
                    succ = [t] if x.mnemonic == 'b' else [t, a + 4]
                else:
                    succ = [a + 4]
                n = {'kind': k, 'ins': [x], 'succ': succ}
            pre = n.get('pre', 0)
            if any(a + 4 * (i - pre) in self.touched for i in range(len(n['ins']))):
                bad.add(a)
                continue
            nodes[a] = n
            if n['kind'] == 'rmw':
                inner |= {a + 4, a + 8, a + 12}
            if n['kind'] in ('acq', 'rel', 'tst'):
                inner |= {a + 4 * (i - pre) for i in range(len(n['ins']))} - {a}
            for s in n['succ']:
                if s == T:
                    back.add(a)
                elif T < s <= hi:
                    todo.append(s)
        if not back or inner & set(nodes) or any(s in inner for n in nodes.values() for s in n['succ']):
            return None

        def prune(ends):
            keep, more = set(ends), True
            while more:
                more = False
                for a, n in nodes.items():
                    if a not in keep and any(s in keep and s != T for s in n['succ']):
                        keep.add(a)
                        more = True
            return keep

        R = prune(back)
        for a in R:
            if 'uses' not in nodes[a]:
                nodes[a]['uses'], nodes[a]['defs'] = self.rw(nodes[a]['ins'][0])
        # Every path from T to a back-edge: no inner cycle, and the exclusive adds on each address (a register between
        # two writes to it) sum to 0; a lock is taken at most once and released after it.
        bad_back, cnt = set(), [0, 0]

        def walk(a, onpath, ver, delta):
            cnt[1] += 1
            if cnt[1] > SPIN_STEPS:
                raise SpinNo
            n = nodes[a]
            if n['kind'] in ('rmw', 'acq', 'rel'):
                key = (n['kind'] != 'rmw', n['base'], ver.get(n['base'], 0))
                delta = dict(delta)
                delta[key] = delta.get(key, 0) + n['k']
                if n['kind'] != 'rmw' and not 0 <= delta[key] <= 1:
                    raise SpinNo
            if n['defs']:
                ver = dict(ver)
                ver.update({r: ver.get(r, 0) + 1 for r in n['defs']})
            for s in n['succ']:
                if s == T:
                    cnt[0] += 1
                    if cnt[0] > SPIN_PATHS:
                        raise SpinNo
                    if any(delta.values()):
                        bad_back.add(a)
                elif s in R:
                    if s in onpath:
                        raise SpinNo
                    walk(s, onpath | {s}, ver, delta)

        try:
            walk(T, {T}, {}, {})
        except (SpinNo, RecursionError):
            return None
        valid = back - bad_back
        if not valid:
            return None
        R = prune(valid)
        # No state carried from one pass to the next: nothing live at T is written in R.
        live, more = {a: set() for a in R}, True
        while more:
            more = False
            for a in sorted(R, reverse=True):
                n, out = nodes[a], set()
                for s in n['succ']:
                    if s == T:
                        out |= live[T] if a in valid else set()
                    elif s in R:
                        out |= live[s]
                new = n['uses'] | (out - n['defs'])
                if new != live[a]:
                    live[a] = new
                    more = True
        defs = set().union(*(nodes[a]['defs'] for a in R))
        if any(nodes[a]['kind'] == 'stc' for a in R) and not any(
                nodes[a]['kind'] in ('rmw', 'acq', 'rel', 'tst') or nodes[a]['ins'][0].mnemonic.startswith('ld')
                for a in R):
            return None   # stores and nothing polled
        vary = {a for a in R if nodes[a]['kind'] == 'stc' and nodes[a]['uses'] & defs}
        if vary:
            return vary
        if sum(nodes[a]['kind'] == 'stc' for a in R) > SPIN_STORES:
            return None
        if live[T] & defs:
            return None
        kinds = sorted({nodes[a]['kind'] for a in R} & {'rmw', 'acq', 'rel', 'tst', 'stc'})
        return {'T': T, 'R': sorted(R), 'valid': valid, 'size': sum(len(nodes[a]['ins']) for a in R), 'kinds': kinds}

    def all(self):
        return [g for g in (self.region(T, bes) for T, bes in sorted(self.candidates().items())) if g]


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument('--exefs', type=Path, required=True)
    ap.add_argument('--patches', type=Path, help='patch table whose sites stay out of regions')
    ap.add_argument('--modules', default='main,subsdk0,sdk')
    args = ap.parse_args()
    sys.setrecursionlimit(20000)
    mods = layout(args.exefs)
    table = patches.load(args.patches, mods) if args.patches else patches.Table()
    for name in args.modules.split(','):
        n = Nso(str(args.exefs / name))
        img = bytes(n.image)
        touched = set(table.sites.get(name, {}))
        found = Search(img, n.text[0] + n.text[1], touched).all()
        print(f'# {name}: {len(found)} spin waits')
        for g in found:
            bes = ' '.join(f'{b:x}' for b in sorted(g['valid']))
            what = ', '.join(g['kinds']) or 'loads'
            print(f'spin {name} {g["T"]:x} {bes}   # {g["size"]} instructions; {what}')
        print(f'{name}: {len(found)} spin waits', file=sys.stderr)
    return 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())
```

```py
"""The game's UI layouts for a canvas of another shape than 16:9 (output_res = 3440x1440 or 1280x800 in totk.ini),

The game lays its UI out on a 1920x1080 grid and maps that grid onto the canvas, so on a 21:9 canvas every layout comes
out 34% too wide and on a 16:10 one 11% too tall. Here each layout's root pane is scaled back to 16:9 on the stretched
axis (scale x = 16/9 over the aspect when wider, scale y = the aspect over 16/9 when narrower), backgrounds that must
cover the whole screen are stretched back, and the HUD's parts move out to the screen's corners (wider) or its top and
bottom edges (narrower). The pane list and the distances are the ones the community TOTK-Ultrawide mod for emulators
found for 1.0.0 .. 1.2.1 (GPL; only those values are taken, no code; THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). This is an independent
implementation, checked against 1.2.1's Common.Product.110 and 1.4.3's Common.Product.140: every pane is found by name
and every pane field and animation key holds the value the edit expects before it is written.
"""

            ('MessageLog_01', 'P_Capture_00', 'y', h),
            ('PaExtraStaminaGauge_00', 'N_BasePattern_00', 'y', h), ('PaExtraStaminaGauge_00', 'N_GaugeMainPattern_00', 'y', h),
            ('Pouch_00', 'N_Info_00', 'y', -h), ('Pouch_00', 'Pa_ExtraStamina_00', 'y', -h),
            ('ShopMenu_00', 'A_AlignGuide_00', 'y', -(477 + h)),
            *[(layout, 'N_SystemBG_00', 'y', -h) for layout in ('SystemActionGuide_00',) + SYSTEM_MENUS],
            ('SystemLoadList_00', 'Pa_Guide_00', 'y', -(474 + h)), ('SystemOption_00', 'A_Guide_00', 'y', -(474 + h))]
    return out

# BFLAN animation targets: FLPA (pane SRT) translate y, FLTS (texture SRT) scale y
FLPA_Y, FLTS_SY = 1, 4

def anim_keys(blarc, lo, pane, tag, target):
    """The absolute offsets of each key (frame, value, slope: 12 bytes) of the hermite curves of one pane, animation
    tag (b'FLPA', b'FLTS') and target in the BFLAN at blarc[lo:], one list per curve. Found by walking the pai1 section,
    so they hold in any version whose animation has that curve."""
    if blarc[lo:lo + 4] != b'FLAN': raise SystemExit(f'{lo:#x}: not a BFLAN')
    pos, out = lo + struct.unpack_from('<H', blarc, lo + 6)[0], []
    for _ in range(struct.unpack_from('<H', blarc, lo + 0x10)[0]):
        magic, size = bytes(blarc[pos:pos + 4]), struct.unpack_from('<I', blarc, pos + 4)[0]
        if magic == b'pai1':
            table = pos + struct.unpack_from('<I', blarc, pos + 16)[0]
            for e in range(struct.unpack_from('<H', blarc, pos + 14)[0]):
                eo = pos + struct.unpack_from('<I', blarc, table + 4 * e)[0]
                if bytes(blarc[eo:eo + 28]).split(b'\0')[0].decode() != pane: continue
                for t in range(blarc[eo + 28]):
                    to = eo + struct.unpack_from('<I', blarc, eo + 32 + 4 * t)[0]
                    if bytes(blarc[to:to + 4]) != tag: continue
                    for g in range(blarc[to + 4]):
                        go = to + struct.unpack_from('<I', blarc, to + 8 + 4 * g)[0]
                        if blarc[go + 1] != target: continue
                        if blarc[go + 2] != 2: raise SystemExit(f'{pane}: a {tag.decode()} curve that is not hermite')
                        keys = go + struct.unpack_from('<I', blarc, go + 8)[0]
                        out.append([keys + 12 * i for i in range(struct.unpack_from('<H', blarc, go + 4)[0])])
        pos += size
    return out

def tall_anim(blarc, members, k, changed):
    """The animation keys that hold positions or zooms on the screen's height, for a canvas narrower than 16:9."""
    h = 540 * (1 / k - 1)
    get = lambda at: struct.unpack_from('<f', blarc, at)[0]
    put = lambda at, v: struct.pack_into('<f', blarc, at, v)
    def anim(name):
        member = f'anim/{name}.bflan'
        if member not in members: raise SystemExit(f'{name}: no animation {member} in the archive')
        changed.add(member)
        return members[member][0]
    # The minimap's four cut panes slide in on straight lines from 0 at frame 0 to y -360, the bottom of a 16:9 layout
    # (hermite keys: the first one's slope is the end point); the end point moves with the screen's edge.
    lo = anim('AppMap_00_MiniMap')
    for pane in ('N_Cut_00', 'N_Cut_01', 'N_Cut_02', 'N_Cut_03'):
        curves = anim_keys(blarc, lo, pane, b'FLPA', FLPA_Y)
        if len(curves) != 1 or len(curves[0]) != 2: raise SystemExit(f'AppMap_00_MiniMap {pane}: {len(curves)} y curves')
        k0, k1 = curves[0]
        if not (get(k0) == 0 and get(k0 + 4) == 0 and abs(get(k0 + 8) + 360) < 1e-3 and get(k1) == 1 and
                abs(get(k1 + 4) + 360) < 1e-3 and get(k1 + 8) == 0):
            raise SystemExit(f'AppMap_00_MiniMap {pane}: not a line from 0 to y -360')
        put(k0 + 8, -(360 + h)), put(k1 + 4, -(360 + h))
    # The large place name of a discovery holds its height (285, then 260) in flat keys; they move to the top edge.
    curves = anim_keys(blarc, anim('Location_00_IsDiscovery'), 'N_Large_00', b'FLPA', FLPA_Y)
    values = [get(key + 4) for keys in curves for key in keys]
    if len(curves) != 1 or values != [285, 285, 260]: raise SystemExit(f'Location_00_IsDiscovery N_Large_00: keys {values}')
    for key in curves[0]: put(key + 4, get(key + 4) + h)
    # The dragon's tears map icon zooms its picture to 1.08 and 1.28 in flat keys; on the stretched axis by 1 / k more.
    curves = anim_keys(blarc, anim('PaMapIconDragonTears_00_Zoom'), 'P_Geoglyph_00', b'FLTS', FLTS_SY)
    values = [round(get(key + 4), 4) for keys in curves for key in keys]
    if len(curves) != 1 or values != [1.08, 1.28]: raise SystemExit(f'PaMapIconDragonTears_00_Zoom P_Geoglyph_00: keys {values}')
    for key in curves[0]: put(key + 4, get(key + 4) / k)

def anim_edits(k, hud_corner):
    """(animation, byte offset, value the game ships, new value): floats inside BFLAN key tables."""
    w = 960 * (1 / k - 1)
    out = [('PaMapIconDragonTears_00_Zoom', 288, 1.08, 1.08 / k), ('PaMapIconDragonTears_00_Zoom', 300, 1.28, 1.28 / k)]
    if hud_corner:   # the minimap's slide-in keys end at x 765, the right edge of a 16:9 layout
        out += [('AppMap_00_MiniMap', o, 765.0, 765 + w) for o in (872, 880, 1628, 1636, 3264, 3272, 3468, 3476)]
    return out

def panes(blarc, lo, hi):
    """pane name -> absolute section offset, first occurrence, for the BFLYT at blarc[lo:hi]."""
    assert blarc[lo:lo + 4] == b'FLYT', 'not a BFLYT'
    head, count = struct.unpack_from('<H', blarc, lo + 6)[0], struct.unpack_from('<H', blarc, lo + 0x10)[0]
    pos, out = lo + head, {}
    for _ in range(count):
        magic, size = bytes(blarc[pos:pos + 4]), struct.unpack_from('<I', blarc, pos + 4)[0]
        if magic in PANE_MAGICS:
            out.setdefault(bytes(blarc[pos + 12:pos + 36]).split(b'\0')[0].decode(), pos)
        pos += size
    assert pos <= hi
    return out

def find_pane(found, layout, name):
    """The pane of that exact name (a version that renamed it stops the script)."""
    if name not in found: raise SystemExit(f'{layout}: no pane {name}')
    return found[name]

def apply(blarc, members, width, height, hud_corner=True):
    """Edits blarc (bytearray) in place for a width x height canvas of another shape than 16:9. Returns the members it
    changed. hud_corner (wider canvases): the HUD goes to the screen's corners; a narrower one always has it at the
    top and bottom edges."""
    wide = width / height > 16 / 9
    k = (16 / 9) / (width / height) if wide else (width / height) / (16 / 9)
    assert k < 1, 'only for canvases of another shape than 16:9'
    root_scale = 'scale_x' if wide else 'scale_y'
    changed, layouts = set(), {}
    unknown = sorted(n for n in KEEP_ROOT if f'blyt/{n}.bflyt' not in members)
    if unknown: raise SystemExit(f'KEEP_ROOT names no layout: {unknown}')
    def pane_offset(layout, pane):
        member = f'blyt/{layout}.bflyt'
        if member not in members: raise SystemExit(f'{layout}: no layout {member} in the archive')
        if member not in layouts: layouts[member] = panes(blarc, *members[member])
        changed.add(member)
        return find_pane(layouts[member], layout, pane)
    for member in sorted(m for m in members if m.startswith('blyt/') and m.endswith('.bflyt')):
        if member[5:-6] in KEEP_ROOT: continue
        at = pane_offset(member[5:-6], 'RootPane') + FIELD[root_scale]
        have = struct.unpack_from('<f', blarc, at)[0]
        if abs(have - 1.0) > 1e-3: raise SystemExit(f'{member[5:-6]} RootPane {root_scale}: {have}, expected 1.0')
        struct.pack_into('<f', blarc, at, k)
    # Every edit's value at k = 1 is the value the game ships (a scale of 1, the 16:9 position): checked before writing,
    # so a version with other numbers stops here instead of getting wrong positions. OFF moves a pane away: not checked.
    table = zip(edits(k, hud_corner), edits(1.0, hud_corner)) if wide else zip(tall_edits(k), tall_edits(1.0))
    for (layout, pane, field, value), (_, _, _, shipped) in table:
        at = pane_offset(layout, pane) + FIELD[field]
        have = struct.unpack_from('<f', blarc, at)[0]
        if value != 10000.0 and abs(have - shipped) > 1e-3: raise SystemExit(f'{layout} {pane} {field}: {have}, expected {shipped}')
        struct.pack_into('<f', blarc, at, value)
    if not wide:
        tall_anim(blarc, members, k, changed)
        return sorted(changed)
    for anim, offset, shipped, value in anim_edits(k, hud_corner):
        member = f'anim/{anim}.bflan'
        if member not in members: raise SystemExit(f'{anim}: no animation {member} in the archive')
        lo, hi = members[member]
        if offset + 4 > hi - lo: raise SystemExit(f'{anim}: too short for +{offset}')
        have = struct.unpack_from('<f', blarc, lo + offset)[0]
        if abs(have - shipped) >= 1e-4: raise SystemExit(f'{anim} +{offset}: {have}, expected {shipped}')
        struct.pack_into('<f', blarc, lo + offset, value); changed.add(member)
    return sorted(changed)
```

```md
# MacNativeGames extraction scripts

Unmodified copies from https://github.com/ly05010419/MacNativeGames at `b75be8cfa704df3701e86130c8ced268e79d6b11`, MIT (see `LICENSE`).

| File | Upstream path |
|---|---|
| `extract_exefs.py` | `games/totk/scripts/extract_exefs.py` |
| `extract_romfs.py` | `games/totk/scripts/extract_romfs.py` |
| `extract_update_romfs.py` | `games/totk/scripts/extract_update_romfs.py` |
| `extract_shared_fonts.py` | `games/totk/scripts/extract_shared_fonts.py` |

`tools/data/expected-v*.json` come from `games/totk/assets/` at the same commit.

Keep these files byte-identical to upstream so they can be updated by copying. Windows-specific behaviour lives in `tools/extract.py` and `tools/extract_fonts.py`.
```

`tools/vendor/macnativegames/extract_exefs.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Read an XCI or NSP in place; extract and verify its base or explicitly selected update Program ExeFS.

Supports NCA3, key-area or common-ticket AES-CTR, and hierarchical SHA-256 PFS0.
Keys stay in memory. No RomFS extraction, executable launch, or network calls.
"""
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import struct
import io
from pathlib import Path
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.ciphers import Cipher, algorithms, modes


def require(condition, message):
    if not condition:
        raise ValueError(message)


def decrypt(key, mode, data):
    ctx = Cipher(algorithms.AES(key), mode).decryptor()
    return ctx.update(data) + ctx.finalize()


def read_at(f, offset, length):
    require(0 <= offset and 0 <= length <= 512 * 1024 * 1024, 'Invalid/big read')
    f.seek(offset)
    data = f.read(length)
    require(len(data) == length, 'Truncated input')
    return data


def hfs(f, offset, bound):
    return partition_entries(f, offset, bound, b'HFS0', 64)


def partition_entries(f, offset, bound, magic=b'PFS0', stride=24):
    """Read a bounded PFS0/HFS0 table without loading its file payloads."""
    require(bound >= 16, 'Truncated partition header')
    hdr = read_at(f, offset, 16)
    require(hdr[:4] == magic, f'Expected {magic.decode()}')
    count, strings_size = struct.unpack_from('<II', hdr, 4)
    require(count <= 4096 and strings_size <= 1024 * 1024, 'Invalid partition table')
    size = 16 + count * stride + strings_size
    require(size <= bound, 'Partition table out of bounds')
    raw = read_at(f, offset, size)
    strings = raw[16 + count * stride:]
    entries = []
    names = set()
    for i in range(count):
        off, length, nameoff = struct.unpack_from('<QQI', raw, 16 + i * stride)
        require(nameoff < len(strings), 'Invalid partition filename offset')
        end = strings.find(b'\0', nameoff)
        require(end >= 0, 'Unterminated partition filename')
        name = strings[nameoff:end].decode('utf-8')
        require(name not in ('', '.', '..') and '/' not in name and '\\' not in name, 'Unsafe partition filename')
        require(name not in names, 'Duplicate partition filename')
        names.add(name)
        require(size + off + length <= bound, 'Partition entry out of bounds')
        entries.append((name, offset + size + off, length))
    end = offset + size
    for _, start, length in sorted(entries, key=lambda e: e[1]):
        require(start >= end, 'Overlapping partition entries')
        end = start + length
    return entries


def container_entries(f, size):
    if read_at(f, 0, 4) == b'PFS0':
        return 'nsp', partition_entries(f, 0, size)
    require(size >= 0x138 and read_at(f, 0x100, 4) == b'HEAD', 'Expected an XCI or NSP (PFS0) game file')
    root = struct.unpack('<Q', read_at(f, 0x130, 8))[0]
    partitions = hfs(f, root, size - root)
    secure = [e for e in partitions if e[0] == 'secure']
    require(len(secure) == 1, 'Expected one XCI secure partition')
    return 'xci', hfs(f, secure[0][1], secure[0][2])


def load_keys(path):
    keys = {}
    for number, line in enumerate(path.read_text().splitlines(), 1):
        line = line.split('#', 1)[0].strip()
        if '=' in line:
            name, value = line.split('=', 1)
            try:
                keys[name.strip().lower()] = bytes.fromhex(value.strip())
            except ValueError:
                raise ValueError(f'Invalid key encoding at line {number}') from None
    return keys


def common_tickets(f, entries):
    """Keep encrypted title keys in memory only, as nxnative's NSP importer does.

    Ticket offsets below are relative to the signed body; accept the standard RSA/ECDSA layouts.
    A personalized ticket cannot provide a common title key and is never treated as one.
    """
    tickets = {}
    bodies = {0x10000: 0x240, 0x10001: 0x140, 0x10002: 0x80,
              0x10003: 0x240, 0x10004: 0x140, 0x10005: 0x80}
    for name, offset, size in entries:
        if not name.lower().endswith('.tik'):
            continue
        require(size >= 4, 'Truncated NSP ticket')
        # Switch ticket signature type is little-endian: RSA2048/SHA256 = 04 00 01 00.
        sig = struct.unpack('<I', read_at(f, offset, 4))[0]
        require(sig in bodies, 'Unsupported NSP ticket signature type')
        body = bodies[sig]
        require(size >= body + 0x180, 'Truncated NSP ticket body')
        data = read_at(f, offset + body, 0x180)
        require(data[0x141] == 0, 'Personalized NSP tickets are unsupported; a common ticket is required')
        rights, key = data[0x160:0x170], data[0x40:0x50]
        require(rights not in tickets or tickets[rights] == key, 'Conflicting NSP tickets')
        tickets[rights] = key
    return tickets


def read_nca_header(f, offset, size, keys):
    require(size >= 0xc00, 'Truncated NCA header')
    require('header_key' in keys, 'Missing header_key in prod.keys')
    raw = read_at(f, offset, 0xc00)
    hdr = b''.join(decrypt(keys['header_key'], modes.XTS(i.to_bytes(16, 'big')),
                           raw[i * 512:(i + 1) * 512]) for i in range(6))
    require(hdr[0x200:0x204] == b'NCA3', 'Expected NCA3 (check prod.keys and the game file)')
    require(struct.unpack_from('<Q', hdr, 0x208)[0] == size, 'NCA size does not match container entry')
    for i in range(4):
        start, end = struct.unpack_from('<II', hdr, 0x240 + i * 16)
        require((start == end == 0) or 0xc00 <= start * 512 < end * 512 <= size, 'NCA section out of bounds')
    return hdr


def nca_ctr_key(hdr, keys, tickets):
    generation = max(max(hdr[0x206], hdr[0x220]) - 1, 0)
    rights = hdr[0x230:0x240]
    if rights != bytes(16):
        require(rights in tickets, 'Missing common ticket for rights-managed NCA in the NSP')
        keyname = f'titlekek_{generation:02x}'
        require(keyname in keys, f'Missing {keyname} in prod.keys')
        return decrypt(keys[keyname], modes.ECB(), tickets[rights])
    require(hdr[0x207] < 3, 'Unsupported NCA key area')
    area = ('application', 'ocean', 'system')[hdr[0x207]]
    keyname = f'key_area_key_{area}_{generation:02x}'
    require(keyname in keys, f'Missing {keyname} in prod.keys')
    return decrypt(keys[keyname], modes.ECB(), hdr[0x300:0x340])[32:48]


def nca_inventory(f, entries, keys):
    records = []
    for name, offset, length in entries:
        if not name.lower().endswith('.nca'):
            continue
        hdr = read_nca_header(f, offset, length, keys)
        record = dict(name=name, nca_offset=offset, size=length, content_type=hdr[0x205],
                      title_id=f'{struct.unpack_from("<Q", hdr, 0x210)[0]:016X}')
        records.append((record, hdr))
    return records


def program_nca(records, update=False):
    if update:
        programs = [(r, h) for r, h in records if r["content_type"] == 0]
        require(len(programs) == 1, "Expected one update Program NCA; combined packages are unsupported")
        record, hdr = programs[0]
        require(record["title_id"] == "0100F2C0115B6000", "Update belongs to another game")
        require(any(hdr[0x400 + i*512 + 4] == 4 for i in range(4)), "Expected a BKTR update, not a base game")
        require(all(r["title_id"] in ("0100F2C0115B6000", "0100F2C0115B6800") for r, _ in records), "Mixed-title update package")
        return record, hdr
    # Update Program NCAs can retain the base title ID; their Meta NCA carries the update ID.
    metadata = [r for r, _ in records if r['content_type'] == 1]
    require(len(metadata) <= 1 and all(r['title_id'] == '0100F2C0115B6000' for r in metadata),
            'Expected base game metadata; updates, DLC and combined packages are unsupported')
    programs = [(r, h) for r, h in records if r['content_type'] == 0]
    require(len(programs) == 1, 'Expected one base Program NCA; updates, DLC and combined packages are unsupported')
    record, hdr = programs[0]
    require(record['title_id'] == '0100F2C0115B6000',
            'Expected Tears of the Kingdom base game 1.0.0; updates, DLC and other games are unsupported')
    return record, hdr


def record_offset(record):
    # Read manifests produced before NSP support too.
    return record['nca_offset'] if 'nca_offset' in record else record['xci_offset']


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('game', type=Path, help='base game 1.0.0 (.xci or .nsp)')
    parser.add_argument('--keys', required=True, type=Path)
    parser.add_argument('--update', action='store_true', help='extract update code; caller must verify supported version hashes')
    parser.add_argument('--output', required=True, type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    require(not args.output.exists(), 'Output already exists; choose a new directory')
    keys = load_keys(args.keys)
    with args.game.open('rb') as f:
        kind, entries = container_entries(f, args.game.stat().st_size)
        tickets = common_tickets(f, entries)
        records = nca_inventory(f, entries, keys)
        record, hdr = program_nca(records, update=args.update)
        ctr_key = nca_ctr_key(hdr, keys, tickets)
        for i in range(4):
            start, end = struct.unpack_from('<II', hdr, 0x240 + 16 * i)
            if not start:
                continue
            fs = hdr[0x400 + 512 * i:0x600 + 512 * i]
            require(hashlib.sha256(fs).digest() == hdr[0x280 + 32 * i:0x2A0 + 32 * i], 'FS header hash mismatch')
            if fs[2:4] != b'\x01\x02':
                continue
            require(fs[4] == 3, 'Only AES-CTR ExeFS is supported')
            blocksize, levels = struct.unpack_from('<II', fs, 0x28)
            hashoff, hashsize, pfsoff, pfssize = struct.unpack_from('<QQQQ', fs, 0x30)
            secstart, secsize = start * 512, (end - start) * 512
            require(levels == 2 and blocksize > 0 and pfssize <= 512 * 1024 * 1024, 'Unsupported ExeFS hash layout')

            def section_read(relative, size):
                require(relative >= 0 and relative + size <= secsize, 'Section read out of bounds')
                absolute = secstart + relative
                aligned = absolute & ~15
                iv = fs[0x140:0x148][::-1] + (aligned // 16).to_bytes(8, 'big')
                data = read_at(f, record_offset(record) + aligned, size + absolute - aligned)
                return decrypt(ctr_key, modes.CTR(iv), data)[absolute - aligned:]

            hashes = section_read(hashoff, hashsize)
            require(hashlib.sha256(hashes).digest() == fs[8:40], 'ExeFS hash-table mismatch')
            pfs = section_read(pfsoff, pfssize)
            for index, pos in enumerate(range(0, pfssize, blocksize)):
                expected = hashes[index * 32:(index + 1) * 32]
                require(hashlib.sha256(pfs[pos:pos + blocksize]).digest() == expected,
                        f'ExeFS block hash mismatch: {index}')
            files = [(name, pfs[off:off + size]) for name, off, size in
                     partition_entries(io.BytesIO(pfs), 0, len(pfs))]
            require(any(name == 'main.npdm' for name, _ in files), 'PFS0 is not ExeFS')
            args.output.mkdir(parents=True)
            extracted = []
            for name, data in files:
                (args.output / name).write_bytes(data)
                extracted.append({'name': name, 'size': len(data), 'sha256': hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()})
            manifest = {'source': str(args.game.resolve()), 'source_size': args.game.stat().st_size,
                        'source_mtime_ns': args.game.stat().st_mtime_ns, 'container': kind,
                        'nca_inventory': [r for r, _ in records], 'program': record, 'section_index': i,
                        'integrity': 'FS header, ExeFS hash table, and every ExeFS data block verified; RSA signatures not checked',
                        'files': extracted}
            (args.output.parent / 'extraction-manifest.json').write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2) + '\n')
            print(json.dumps({'integrity': manifest['integrity'], 'files': extracted}, indent=2))
            return
        raise ValueError('No ExeFS section found')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

```

`tools/vendor/macnativegames/extract_romfs.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Verify all six IVFC levels, stream a local RomFS image, and index its files."""
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import struct
from pathlib import Path
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.ciphers import modes
from extract_exefs import (decrypt, read_at, require, load_keys, container_entries, common_tickets,
                           nca_inventory, program_nca, nca_ctr_key, record_offset)

def main():
    parser=argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('--keys',type=Path,required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--manifest',type=Path,default=Path('extracted/v0/extraction-manifest.json'))
    parser.add_argument('--output',type=Path,default=Path('extracted/v0/romfs'))
    args=parser.parse_args(); require(not args.output.exists(),'Output already exists')
    manifest=json.loads(args.manifest.read_text());record=manifest['program'];keys=load_keys(args.keys)
    source=Path(manifest['source']);require(source.stat().st_size==manifest['source_size'],'Source size changed')
    with source.open('rb') as f:
        _,entries=container_entries(f,source.stat().st_size)
        actual,hdr=program_nca(nca_inventory(f,entries,keys))
        require(actual['name']==record['name'] and actual['size']==record['size'] and
                record_offset(actual)==record_offset(record),'Source Program NCA changed; extract ExeFS again')
        ctr_key=nca_ctr_key(hdr,keys,common_tickets(f,entries))
        for i in range(4):
            start,end=struct.unpack_from('<II',hdr,0x240+i*16)
            if not start:continue
            fs=hdr[0x400+512*i:0x600+512*i]
            require(hashlib.sha256(fs).digest()==hdr[0x280+32*i:0x2a0+32*i],'FS header hash')
            if fs[2:5]!=bytes([0,3,3]):continue
            require(fs[8:12]==b'IVFC' and struct.unpack_from('<III',fs,12)==(0x20000,32,7),'Unsupported IVFC layout')
            levels=[struct.unpack_from('<QQII',fs,0x18+j*24) for j in range(6)]
            def read(relative,size):
                require(0<=relative<=relative+size<=(end-start)*512,'Section bounds')
                absolute=start*512+relative;aligned=absolute&~15;skip=absolute-aligned
                iv=fs[0x140:0x148][::-1]+(aligned//16).to_bytes(8,'big')
                return decrypt(ctr_key,modes.CTR(iv),read_at(f,record_offset(record)+aligned,size+skip))[skip:]
            args.output.mkdir(parents=True);image_path=args.output/'romfs.bin';digest=hashlib.sha256();counts=[]
            parent=fs[0xc8:0xe8]
            with image_path.open('wb') as image:
                for level,(offset,size,power,reserved) in enumerate(levels):
                    require(12<=power<=24 and reserved==0,'IVFC block size');block=1<<power
                    require(len(parent)>=(size+block-1)//block*32,'IVFC parent size')
                    captured=bytearray() if level<5 else None
                    index=0
                    for pos in range(0,size,8*1024*1024):
                        chunk=read(offset+pos,min(8*1024*1024,size-pos))
                        for j in range(0,len(chunk),block):
                            payload=chunk[j:j+block]
                            require(hashlib.sha256(payload+bytes(block-len(payload))).digest()==parent[index*32:index*32+32],f'IVFC level {level} block {index} failed')
                            index+=1
                        if captured is not None:captured.extend(chunk)
                        else:image.write(chunk);digest.update(chunk)
                    counts.append(index)
                    if captured is not None:parent=bytes(captured)
                    print(f'IVFC level {level}: {index} blocks verified',flush=True)
            files=index_romfs(image_path)
            report=dict(status='pass',source_size=source.stat().st_size,program=record['name'],section=i,ivfc_blocks=counts,romfs_size=levels[-1][1],romfs_sha256=digest.hexdigest(),files=files,integrity='FS header and all six IVFC levels verified; RSA signature not checked')
            (args.output/'index.json').write_text(json.dumps(report,indent=2)+'\n')
            print(json.dumps(dict(status='pass',file_count=len(files),size=levels[-1][1],sha256=digest.hexdigest())),flush=True);return
    raise ValueError('No supported RomFS found')

def index_romfs(path):
    with path.open('rb') as f:
        h=struct.unpack('<10Q',read_at(f,0,80));require(h[0]==80,'RomFS header');length=path.stat().st_size
        for off,size in [(h[1],h[2]),(h[3],h[4]),(h[5],h[6]),(h[7],h[8])]:require(off+size<=length,'RomFS table bounds')
        dirs=read_at(f,h[3],h[4]);entries=read_at(f,h[7],h[8]);files=[];seen_dirs=set();seen_files=set();paths=set()
        def name(table,off,n):
            require(off+n<=len(table),'Name bounds');s=table[off:off+n].decode('utf-8');require(s not in ['.','..'] and '/' not in s and '\\' not in s and '\0' not in s,'Unsafe path');return s
        todo=[(0,'')]
        while todo:
            off,parent=todo.pop();require(off not in seen_dirs and off+24<=len(dirs),'Invalid/cyclic directory');seen_dirs.add(off)
            p,sibling,child,file,hash_next,n=struct.unpack_from('<6I',dirs,off);part=name(dirs,off+24,n);prefix=parent+part+'/' if part else parent
            if sibling!=0xffffffff:todo.append((sibling,parent))
            if child!=0xffffffff:todo.append((child,prefix))
            while file!=0xffffffff:
                require(file not in seen_files and file+32<=len(entries),'Invalid/cyclic file');seen_files.add(file)
                p,next_file,data,size,hash_next,n=struct.unpack_from('<IIQQII',entries,file);part=name(entries,file+32,n);require(part!='','Empty file name');filename=prefix+part
                require(filename not in paths and h[9]+data+size<=length,'Duplicate/out-of-bounds file');paths.add(filename)
                files.append(dict(path=filename,offset=h[9]+data,size=size));file=next_file
        return sorted(files,key=lambda item:item['path'])
if __name__=='__main__':main()
```

`tools/vendor/macnativegames/extract_shared_fonts.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Extract the system shared fonts (BFTTF) from firmware data NCAs, verifying the NCA FS header,
all six IVFC levels and each BFTTF header. Fonts stay in the BFTTF form that hardware places in
shared memory; only local copies are written, never printed.

Sources: --xci <game card image> reads the data NCAs from the card's system update partition (a game card carries the
system update it needs, shared fonts included); --firmware reads an unpacked NCA directory. The older --inventory
mode lists the NCAs of an installed firmware."""
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import struct
from pathlib import Path
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.ciphers import modes
from extract_exefs import decrypt, read_at, require, load_keys, hfs, nca_ctr_key
from extract_romfs import index_romfs

FIRMWARE = Path.home() / 'Library/Application Support/Ryujinx/bis/system/Contents/registered'
# nn::pl::SharedFontType -> (system data title, BFTTF file name)
FONTS = [
    (0, 'standard', '0100000000000811', 'nintendo_udsg-r_std_003.bfttf'),
    (1, 'chinese-simplified', '0100000000000814', 'nintendo_udsg-r_org_zh-cn_003.bfttf'),
    (2, 'chinese-simplified-extension', '0100000000000814', 'nintendo_udsg-r_ext_zh-cn_003.bfttf'),
    (3, 'chinese-traditional', '0100000000000813', 'nintendo_udjxh-db_zh-tw_003.bfttf'),
    (4, 'korean', '0100000000000812', 'nintendo_udsg-r_ko_003.bfttf'),
    (5, 'nintendo-extension', '0100000000000810', 'nintendo_ext_003.bfttf'),
]
BFTTF_DECODED_MAGIC = 0x7f9a0218


class Slice:
    """A file seen from a base offset: an NCA inside a game card image reads like a standalone NCA file."""
    def __init__(self, path, base=0):
        self.f, self.base = path.open('rb'), base

    def seek(self, offset, whence=0):
        return self.f.seek(self.base + offset if whence == 0 else offset, whence) - self.base

    def read(self, size=-1):
        return self.f.read(size)

    def __enter__(self):
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *exc):
        self.f.close()


def hfs0_entries(f, offset):
    """(name, absolute offset, size) of each file in the HFS0 partition at offset."""
    length = f.seek(0, 2)
    return hfs(f, offset, length - offset)


def nca_header(f, keys):
    raw = read_at(f, 0, 0xc00)
    return b''.join(decrypt(keys['header_key'], modes.XTS(i.to_bytes(16, 'big')), raw[i * 512:(i + 1) * 512]) for i in range(6))


def xci_data_ncas(xci, keys):
    """title ID -> offset of each data NCA in the card's system update partition."""
    found = {}
    with xci.open('rb') as f:
        require(read_at(f, 0x100, 4) == b'HEAD', 'Not a game card image (XCI)')
        root = struct.unpack('<Q', read_at(f, 0x130, 8))[0]
        update = [e for e in hfs0_entries(f, root) if e[0] == 'update']
        require(update, 'The game card image has no system update partition')
        for name, offset, size in hfs0_entries(f, update[0][1]):
            if not name.endswith('.nca') or name.endswith('.cnmt.nca'):
                continue
            with Slice(xci, offset) as nca:
                hdr = nca_header(nca, keys)
            if hdr[0x200:0x204] == b'NCA3' and hdr[0x205] == 4:   # content type 4: data
                found[f'{struct.unpack_from("<Q", hdr, 0x210)[0]:016x}'] = offset
    return found


def nca_romfs(source, keys, image_path, tickets=None):
    """Write the verified RomFS image of a data NCA (a Path, or a Slice of a game card image) to image_path."""
    with (source if isinstance(source, Slice) else Slice(source)) as f:
        raw = read_at(f, 0, 0xc00)
        hdr = b''.join(decrypt(keys['header_key'], modes.XTS(i.to_bytes(16, 'big')), raw[i * 512:(i + 1) * 512]) for i in range(6))
        require(hdr[0x200:0x204] == b'NCA3', f'Unsupported NCA at {f.base:#x}')
        ctr_key = nca_ctr_key(hdr, keys, tickets or {})
        for i in range(4):
            start, end = struct.unpack_from('<II', hdr, 0x240 + i * 16)
            if not start:
                continue
            fs = hdr[0x400 + 512 * i:0x600 + 512 * i]
            require(hashlib.sha256(fs).digest() == hdr[0x280 + 32 * i:0x2a0 + 32 * i], 'FS header hash')
            if fs[2:5] != bytes([0, 3, 3]):
                continue
            require(fs[8:12] == b'IVFC' and struct.unpack_from('<III', fs, 12) == (0x20000, 32, 7), 'Unsupported IVFC layout')
            levels = [struct.unpack_from('<QQII', fs, 0x18 + j * 24) for j in range(6)]

            def read(relative, size):
                require(0 <= relative <= relative + size <= (end - start) * 512, 'Section bounds')
                absolute = start * 512 + relative
                aligned = absolute & ~15
                skip = absolute - aligned
                iv = fs[0x140:0x148][::-1] + (aligned // 16).to_bytes(8, 'big')
                return decrypt(ctr_key, modes.CTR(iv), read_at(f, aligned, size + skip))[skip:]

            parent = fs[0xc8:0xe8]
            image = bytearray()
            for level, (offset, size, power, reserved) in enumerate(levels):
                require(12 <= power <= 24 and reserved == 0, 'IVFC block size')
                block = 1 << power
                data = read(offset, size)
                for index, j in enumerate(range(0, len(data), block)):
                    payload = data[j:j + block]
                    require(hashlib.sha256(payload + bytes(block - len(payload))).digest() == parent[index * 32:index * 32 + 32], f'IVFC level {level} block {index}')
                parent = data
                if level == 5:
                    image = data
            image_path.write_bytes(image)
            return
    raise ValueError(f'No RomFS in the NCA at {f.base:#x}')


def bfttf_size(data):
    """BFTTF: big-endian words XORed with key = word0 ^ 0x7f9a0218; word1 = font size; payload follows."""
    magic, size = struct.unpack_from('>II', data, 0)
    key = magic ^ BFTTF_DECODED_MAGIC
    decoded = size ^ key
    require(decoded + 8 == len(data), 'BFTTF size does not match file')
    first = struct.unpack_from('>I', data, 8)[0] ^ key
    require(first in (0x00010000, 0x4f54544f), 'BFTTF payload is not a TrueType/OpenType font')
    return decoded


def firmware_data_ncas(folder, keys):
    """Accept an unpacked firmware directory or an installed registered/ directory."""
    require(folder.is_dir(), 'Firmware must be a directory containing NCA files')
    wanted = {title for _, _, title, _ in FONTS}
    found = {}
    for path in sorted(folder.iterdir()):
        if path.is_dir():
            path = path / '00'
        if not path.is_file() or (path.name != '00' and path.suffix.lower() != '.nca'):
            continue
        with path.open('rb') as f:
            hdr = nca_header(f, keys)
        require(hdr[0x200:0x204] == b'NCA3', 'Invalid firmware NCA header (check prod.keys)')
        title = f'{struct.unpack_from("<Q", hdr, 0x210)[0]:016x}'
        if hdr[0x205] == 4 and title in wanted:
            require(title not in found, f'Duplicate shared-font title {title} in firmware')
            found[title] = path
    require(wanted <= found.keys(), 'Firmware is missing shared-font data NCAs: ' + ', '.join(sorted(wanted - found.keys())))
    return found


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('--keys', type=Path, required=True)
    sources = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
    sources.add_argument('--xci', type=Path, help='game card image: take the fonts from its system update partition')
    sources.add_argument('--firmware', type=Path, help='unpacked firmware NCA directory (for NSP builds)')
    parser.add_argument('--inventory', type=Path, default=Path('analysis/firmware-inventory.json'))
    parser.add_argument('--output', type=Path, default=Path('extracted/firmware/shared-fonts'))
    args = parser.parse_args()
    require(not args.output.exists(), 'Output already exists')
    keys = load_keys(args.keys)
    if args.xci:
        card = xci_data_ncas(args.xci, keys)
        missing = sorted({t for _, _, t, _ in FONTS} - card.keys())
        require(not missing, f'Shared font data missing from the card update partition: {", ".join(missing)}')
        source = lambda title: Slice(args.xci, card[title])
    elif args.firmware:
        firmware = firmware_data_ncas(args.firmware, keys)
        source = lambda title: firmware[title]
    else:
        rows = json.loads(args.inventory.read_text())['rows']
        data_nca = {r['title_id']: r['file'] for r in rows if r['content_type'] == 4}
        source = lambda title: (FIRMWARE / data_nca[title] / '00') if (FIRMWARE / data_nca[title]).is_dir() else FIRMWARE / data_nca[title]
    args.output.mkdir(parents=True)
    images = {}
    report = []
    for kind, name, title, filename in FONTS:
        if title not in images:
            image_path = args.output / f'{title}.romfs'
            nca_romfs(source(title), keys, image_path)
            images[title] = (image_path, {e['path']: e for e in index_romfs(image_path)})
        image_path, entries = images[title]
        require(filename in entries, f'{filename} missing in {title}')
        e = entries[filename]
        with image_path.open('rb') as f:
            data = read_at(f, e['offset'], e['size'])
        size = bfttf_size(data)
        out = args.output / f'{kind}-{name}.bfttf'
        out.write_bytes(data)
        report.append(dict(type=kind, name=name, title_id=title, file=filename, bfttf_bytes=len(data), font_bytes=size,
                           sha256=hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()))
    for image_path, _ in images.values():
        image_path.unlink()
    manifest = dict(status='pass', integrity='NCA FS header and six IVFC levels verified per NCA; BFTTF header decodes to an sfnt font; RSA not checked', fonts=report)
    (args.output / 'manifest.json').write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2) + '\n')
    print(json.dumps(dict(status='pass', fonts=[(r['type'], r['font_bytes']) for r in report])))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```

`tools/vendor/macnativegames/extract_update_romfs.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Merge a base XCI/NSP and an update NSP with the pinned hactool BKTR reader.

Temporary common-ticket keys are private files, never arguments or log output.
The caller additionally verifies the resulting image against its known version hash.
"""
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
from extract_exefs import (load_keys, container_entries, common_tickets, nca_inventory,
                           program_nca, record_offset, require)
from extract_romfs import index_romfs

# Lockpick_RCM writes these as 17 bytes: the 16-byte source plus a trailing NUL.
# hactool exits unless the value is exactly 16 bytes, before any BKTR check.
_LOCKPICK_KEK_SOURCE = re.compile(r'(?:mariko_)?master_kek_source_[0-9a-f]{2}\Z')


def copy_range(source, offset, size, target):
    with source.open('rb') as src, target.open('wb') as dst:
        src.seek(offset)
        while size:
            data = src.read(min(size, 8 << 20))
            require(bool(data), 'Truncated NCA')
            dst.write(data)
            size -= len(data)


def hactool_prod_keys(source, target):
    """Copy prod.keys for hactool. The caller's file is left unchanged.

    hactool knows no comments: it reads the rest of a line as the value, so a trailing `# note` makes it exit. The copy
    keeps only the `name = value` lines, read the way load_keys reads them (comments dropped, spaces trimmed).
    A Lockpick trailing NUL on master_kek_source / mariko_master_kek_source is dropped. Any other length is rejected
    without recording the key bytes.
    """
    lines = []
    for number, line in enumerate(Path(source).read_text().splitlines(), 1):
        body = line.split('#', 1)[0]
        if '=' not in body:
            continue
        name, value = (part.strip() for part in body.split('=', 1))
        if _LOCKPICK_KEK_SOURCE.fullmatch(name.lower()) is not None:
            require(re.fullmatch(r'[0-9a-fA-F]+', value) is not None, f'Invalid key encoding at line {number}')
            if len(value) == 34 and value[-2:].lower() == '00':
                value = value[:32]
            require(len(value) == 32, f'{name.lower()} must be 16 bytes')
        lines.append(f'{name} = {value}')
    fd = os.open(target, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL, 0o600)
    with os.fdopen(fd, 'w') as f:
        f.write('\n'.join(lines) + ('\n' if lines else ''))


def merge(base, update, keys_path, hactool, output, *, base_romfs=None):
    require(not output.exists(), 'Output exists')
    keys = load_keys(keys_path)
    inputs = []
    tickets = {}
    sources = ((update, True),) if base_romfs else ((base, False), (update, True))
    for source, is_update in sources:
        with source.open('rb') as f:
            kind, entries = container_entries(f, source.stat().st_size)
            require(not is_update or kind == 'nsp', 'Update must be an NSP')
            found = common_tickets(f, entries)
            for rights, key in found.items():
                require(rights not in tickets or tickets[rights] == key, 'Conflicting common tickets')
                tickets[rights] = key
            record, header = program_nca(nca_inventory(f, entries, keys), update=is_update)
            rights = header[0x230:0x240]
            require(rights == bytes(16) or rights in tickets, 'Missing common ticket')
            inputs.append((source, record, header))
    sections = [i for i in range(4) if inputs[-1][2][0x400+i*512+4] == 4]
    require(len(sections) == 1, 'Expected one BKTR section')
    output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    require(shutil.disk_usage(output.parent).free > inputs[-1][1]['size'] + 18*(1 << 30),
            'Need about 19 GiB free for the temporary update NCA and merged image')
    if base_romfs:
        require(Path(base_romfs).is_file(), 'Previous-version RomFS is missing')
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='update-merge-', dir=output.parent) as tmp:
        tmp = Path(tmp)
        keyfile = tmp/'title.keys'
        fd = os.open(keyfile, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL, 0o600)
        with os.fdopen(fd, 'w') as f:
            for rights, key in tickets.items():
                f.write(f'{rights.hex()} = {key.hex()}\n')
        source, record, _ = inputs[-1]
        copy_range(source, record_offset(record), record['size'], tmp/'update.nca')
        result = tmp/'result'
        result.mkdir()
        base_arg = '--baseromfs='+str(Path(base_romfs).resolve()) if base_romfs else '--basenca='+str(base.resolve())
        environment = dict(os.environ, MNG_TITLE_KEYS=str(keyfile))
        environment.pop('MNG_BASE_RANGE_OFFSET', None); environment.pop('MNG_BASE_RANGE_SIZE', None)
        if not base_romfs:
            environment.update(MNG_BASE_RANGE_OFFSET=str(record_offset(inputs[0][1])),
                               MNG_BASE_RANGE_SIZE=str(inputs[0][1]['size']))
        hactool_keys = tmp/'hactool.keys'
        hactool_prod_keys(keys_path, hactool_keys)
        command = [str(hactool.resolve()), '-x', '-y', '--disablekeywarns', '--suppresskeys',
                   '-k', str(hactool_keys.resolve()), base_arg,
                   f'--section{sections[0]}='+str(result/'romfs.bin'), str(tmp/'update.nca')]
        with (result/'merge.log').open('w') as log:
            code = subprocess.run(command, env=environment,
                                  stdout=log, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT).returncode
        log = (result/'merge.log').read_text()
        # hactool also verifies the NCA's fixed-key and NPDM signatures, which need Nintendo's public keys:
        # without them it always prints those two lines as (FAIL). They are not data failures; the six IVFC
        # levels and the image SHA-256 recorded below decide whether the merge worked.
        unsigned = re.compile(r'\s*(?:Fixed-Key Signature|NPDM Signature) \(FAIL\)')
        checked = '\n'.join(line for line in log.splitlines() if not unsigned.match(line))
        if code or re.search(r'\(FAIL\)|\(INVALID\)|Failed to|Error:', checked):
            # hactool repeats a key it cannot parse ("Key (<value>) must be 32 hex digits!"): keep no long hex in the log
            (output.parent/(output.name+'-failure.log')).write_text(re.sub(r'[0-9A-Fa-f]{32,}', '<hex removed>', log))
        require(code == 0 and not re.search(r'\(FAIL\)|\(INVALID\)|Failed to|Error:', checked), 'BKTR verification failed')
        require(all(re.search(rf'Level {i} \(GOOD\)', log) for i in range(6)), 'Missing verified IVFC levels')
        image = result/'romfs.bin'
        with image.open('rb') as f:
            digest = hashlib.file_digest(f, 'sha256').hexdigest()
        files = index_romfs(image)
        report = dict(status='pass', romfs_size=image.stat().st_size, romfs_sha256=digest,
                      files=files, integrity='BKTR merge; all six IVFC levels verified')
        (result/'index.json').write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2)+'\n')
        result.rename(output)
    print(json.dumps(dict(status='pass', files=len(files), sha256=digest)))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('base', type=Path)
    parser.add_argument('update', type=Path)
    parser.add_argument('--keys', required=True, type=Path)
    parser.add_argument('--hactool', required=True, type=Path)
    parser.add_argument('--base-romfs', type=Path, help='full decrypted base IVFC section, including hash levels (not a raw RomFS image)')
    parser.add_argument('--output', required=True, type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    merge(args.base, args.update, args.keys, args.hactool, args.output, base_romfs=args.base_romfs)
```

```props
  <ItemGroup>
```

```md
# Ryujinx shader translator (vendored subset)

Three projects from Ryujinx 1.3.2, unmodified: `Ryujinx.Graphics.Shader`, `Ryujinx.Common` and `Spv.Generator`.
The shader translation tool in `dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_xlate` references them to translate the original Switch shaders to SPIR-V.
License: MIT, see `LICENSE.txt`. Upstream: <https://github.com/Ryubing>.

Ryujinx 1.3.2 的三个项目，未做修改：`Ryujinx.Graphics.Shader`、`Ryujinx.Common`、`Spv.Generator`。
`dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_xlate` 的着色器翻译工具引用它们，把 Switch 原版着色器翻译成 SPIR-V。许可证 MIT，见 `LICENSE.txt`。
```

`tools/vendor/ryujinx/src/Ryujinx.Common/AsyncWorkQueue.cs`:

```cs
using System;
using System.Collections.Concurrent;
using System.Threading;

namespace Ryujinx.Common
{
    public sealed class AsyncWorkQueue<T> : IDisposable
    {
        private readonly Thread _workerThread;
        private readonly CancellationTokenSource _cts;
        private readonly Action<T> _workerAction;
        private readonly BlockingCollection<T> _queue;

        public bool IsCancellationRequested => _cts.IsCancellationRequested;

        public AsyncWorkQueue(Action<T> callback, string name = null) : this(callback, name, new BlockingCollection<T>())
        {
        }

        public AsyncWorkQueue(Action<T> callback, string name, BlockingCollection<T> collection)
        {
            _cts = new CancellationTokenSource();
            _queue = collection;
            _workerAction = callback;
            _workerThread = new Thread(DoWork)
            {
                Name = name,
                IsBackground = true,
            };
            _workerThread.Start();
        }

        private void DoWork()
        {
            try
            {
                foreach (T item in _queue.GetConsumingEnumerable(_cts.Token))
                {
                    _workerAction(item);
                }
            }
            catch (OperationCanceledException)
            {
            }
        }

        public void Cancel()
        {
            _cts.Cancel();
        }

        public void CancelAfter(int millisecondsDelay)
        {
            _cts.CancelAfter(millisecondsDelay);
        }

        public void CancelAfter(TimeSpan delay)
        {
            _cts.CancelAfter(delay);
        }

        public void Add(T workItem)
        {
            _queue.Add(workItem);
        }

        public void Add(T workItem, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
        {
            _queue.Add(workItem, cancellationToken);
        }

        public bool TryAdd(T workItem)
        {
            return _queue.TryAdd(workItem);
        }

        public bool TryAdd(T workItem, int millisecondsDelay)
        {
            return _queue.TryAdd(workItem, millisecondsDelay);
        }

        public bool TryAdd(T workItem, int millisecondsDelay, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
        {
            return _queue.TryAdd(workItem, millisecondsDelay, cancellationToken);
        }

        public bool TryAdd(T workItem, TimeSpan timeout)
        {
            return _queue.TryAdd(workItem, timeout);
        }

        public void Dispose()
        {
            _queue.CompleteAdding();
            _cts.Cancel();
            _workerThread.Join();

            _queue.Dispose();
            _cts.Dispose();
        }
    }
}
```
